english_verse: and made them work so hard
translation_verse: aŋ ha dʋdɔgɩsɛba a leŋ ba tɩtɩŋ yoŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Ba joŋ dɩɩsɩŋ saanɩŋ arɩ ba tɩntɩŋ-duoruŋ kala ba sɩ kɛnɛ ba bagɩsɩŋ lɛ a fʋgɛba kɩɩ. Bʋa deeŋ kala lɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa bɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nisusuŋ fa.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋla pɩ Hiburu tɩŋŋaa hachagɩraa deemba balɩa: Sɩfɩra arɩ Pʋa,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Dɩ Hiburu tɩŋŋaa haal kala nɛ togilo dɩ ʋ lʋl, má bee na, dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa hambolibie, má kpʋʋ, ka dɩ hantolibie nɛ, ma leŋu.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Ama hachagɩra-la ka fá Wɩa nɛ, ba vɩa Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro niiŋ a bɩ Hiburu tɩŋŋaa hambolibiisi-la kpʋa.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro yɩrɛ hachagɩra-la kɔ ʋ sɩpaaŋ a pɩɛsɛba, “Bɛɛ nɛ ma ŋaa ŋ-la? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma bɩ hambolibiisi-la kpʋa?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ hachagɩra-la bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “Hiburu tɩŋŋaa haalaa bɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa haalaa naga. Hiburu tɩŋŋaa haalaa kɛŋ nyalɩma nɛ woruŋ, dɩ kʋŋ nɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ lʋl, hachagɩraa jaŋ magɛ ŋɩɩ kʋkɔ dɩ ʋ lʋla.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: A tɩŋ hachagɩra-la sɩɩ fá Wɩa a bɩ hambolibiisi-la kpʋa, Wɩa leŋ ba kʋŋkala lʋl biiriŋ, a kɛŋ ba tɩtɩa dɩa nɩaa.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋla pɩ ʋ tinteeŋ nɩaa kala, “Má kɛsɛ Hiburu tɩŋŋaa hambolibiisiŋ kala a yuo hɛ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Naayɩl lɛ, aŋ leŋ hantolibiisiŋ.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala lɛ, Levi doho nɩaa baal kʋbala nɛ jaa Levi doho nɩaa tolo.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Tolo-la kɛŋ luoruŋ a lʋl hambolibie. Ʋ sɩ na dɩ bile zɔmɔ, ʋ joŋu faa chɛnsɩŋ batori.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ama ʋ sɩ na dɩ ʋ bɩra bɩ bile wuo kaa faa, ʋ joŋ sime a taarɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ arɩ keliŋ, a joŋ bile hɛ a kɛŋ kʋa tɔ a kaa mʋ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Naayɩl niiŋ, a joŋo faa yaŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Bii-mulo-la dɩhaala mʋ chɩŋ dɩ-bolii aŋ bibeŋ dɩ ʋ na wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa bile lɛ.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tolo tuu fuo-la dɩ ʋ fo lɩɩŋ, ka ʋ ketiee gʋgɔllɛ fuo-la niiŋ. Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tolo-la sɩ na sime-la fuo-la niiŋ yaŋ tʋɔŋ, ʋ tɩŋ ʋ ketie-la dɔŋɔ dɩ ʋ mʋ joŋ sime-la kɔ.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Ʋ kaa kɔ kuoro tolo-la suri dɩ bie hɛ sime-la tʋɔŋ a yiyel. Ŋɩɩ nɛ bile nisusuŋ kɛnʋ ʋ bʋl, “Hiburu tɩmma-la dɔŋɔ bie nɛ ŋ-la.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ bile dɩhaal-la sɩ chɩna bibeŋ pɩɛsɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tolo-la, “Mɩ mʋ yɩrɛ Hiburu tɩŋŋaa haala-la dɔŋɔ kɔ dɩ ʋ beŋ bile pɩŋ?”

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tolo-la bʋla pɩ haal-la, “Laa bie deeŋ a dɩɛsa pɩmɛ, ka dɩ mɩ timiŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ bile naaŋ laa bile a kaa mʋ dɩa a dɩɛsʋ.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Bile sɩ kʋ waa mʋa, ʋ kaa mʋ pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tolo. Ʋ laa ʋ ŋaa ʋ bie, ʋ hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Mosis, aŋ bʋl, “Mɩ lɩɩsʋ lɩɩŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ.” Mosis fá mʋ Midiaŋ

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Mosis sɩ kʋ waa dɛrɛ, tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala ʋ sii mʋ lee-la ʋ naambiiriŋ sɩ hɛ, a na tɩntɩŋ-duoru-la ba sɩɩ tɩŋ. Ʋ na dɩ Ijipiti tɩmma-la dɔŋɔ ka ŋmoo ʋ naambiiri-la dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ daasɛ leriŋ kala dɩ nʋʋkala bɩ kpaga, ʋ ŋmoo Ijipiti tɩɩna-la a kpʋ a joŋo hugi hagɩlɩ-bumbugulo lɛ.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Ʋ taŋ sɩ pʋla, ʋ lɩɩ a na Hiburu tɩŋŋaa balɩa ka yuo dɔŋɔ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ pɩɛsɛ nɩɩ-la kɩaa sɩ bɩ sɩŋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ ŋmuŋmoo ŋ naambie?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la pɩɛsʋ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ lɩɩsɩŋ dɩ ŋ bibenla a laa la wɩaa jɩjɩŋ? Ŋ bɩɩnɛ dɩ ŋ kpʋmɛ arɩ ŋ sɩ kpʋ Ijipiti tɩɩna-la ŋɩɩ nɛɛ?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ Mosis, ʋ bʋl, “Wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ ŋaa, nɩaa jɩma nɛ.”

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩ nɩa dɩ Mosis kpʋ Ijipiti tɩɩna, ʋ chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ kpʋʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis fá mʋ Midiaŋ tinteeŋ, a mʋ hɔŋ viliŋ sɛmɛ.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Midiaŋ tinteeŋ lɛ, nɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara hɛ nɩmɛ, dɩ ʋ kɛŋ toloo balɩpɛ. Tolie-la kɔ dɩ ba ŋaa lɩɩŋ hɛ ba nyɩmma pʋsʋŋ lɩɩ-nyʋarɩ-kʋa lɛ a pɩ ba nyɩmma pʋsʋŋ.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kʋdaaraa dɔnsʋŋ kʋ kiriba, ama Mosis bɩ sɛyɛ a sii pɛ tolie-la lɛ ba ŋaa lɩɩŋ a pɩ ba nyɩmma pʋsʋŋ.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Tolie-la sɩ mɩɩra mʋ ba nyɩmma Rɛwɛl teeŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ pɩɛsɛba, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ jɩnɩŋ ma kɔ lɩma ŋ-la?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bʋl, “Ijipiti tɩɩna nɛ laala ta kʋdaaraa nɩsɩŋ lɛ aŋ ŋaa lɩɩŋ pɩ la pʋsʋŋ.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba nyɩmma pɩɛsɛba, “Nɩɩ nɛ baal-la hɛ? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma bɩ pɛ kɛnʋ kaa kɔ? Má mʋ yɩrʋ dɩ ʋ kʋ dii kɩaa.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba yɩrɛ Mosis ʋ kɔ. Ʋ sɛɩ arɩ ʋ dɩ Jeturo jaŋ hɔŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jeturo joŋ ʋ tolo Zipora a pɩ Mosis ʋ jaa.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Zipora kɛŋ luoruŋ a lʋl hambolibie, Mosis hɛ bile yɩrɩŋ Gesom, aŋ bʋl, “Mɩ ŋaa nʋhʋɔrʋ nɛ tinteeŋ deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Mosis hɛ Midiaŋ tinteeŋ lɛ ŋɩɩ nɛ halɩɩ, Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro kʋ sʋʋ, ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa ha ŋmuŋmoo niiŋ a tɩŋ yoŋ tɩntɩmɩa-la ba sɩɩ tɩŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa nɩɩ ba yele.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Wɩa sɩ nɩɩ ba yele-la ŋɩɩ, ʋ liise yi nii-la ʋ sɩ hɛ ʋ dɩ Abɩraham, Aɩzɩk arɩ Jekɔb pɛgɛ.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Wɩa na Iziral tɩŋŋaa hɛɛ-la, ba wɩaa chɩlʋ.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis dɩdaa ʋ hɩɩlɩ-baala Jeturo pʋsʋŋ. Jeturo nɛ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Midiaŋ lɛ. Mosis daa pʋsʋ-la a mʋ kieli tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la a mʋ yi Wɩa peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩnaɩ.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Nɩmɛ nɛ Wɩa tɩndaara kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kʋ dagʋ tɩɩ-pugubie sɩ chol nyiŋgeliŋ tʋɔŋ. Mosis na dɩ tɩɩ-pugu-la chol nyiniŋ, ama nyiŋ-la bɩ tɩɩ-pugubie-la ka dii.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis sɩ, “Mɩ jaŋ mʋ kpagɛ a na wʋkpuŋkpere deeŋ, wɩɩ-la sɩ tɩɩ nyiŋ-la chol aŋ bɩ tɩɩ-pugubie-la ka dii.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA sɩ na dɩ Mosis kʋ kpagɛ dɩ ʋ na wɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋaa, Wɩa hɛ tɩɩ-pugubie-la lɛ nɛ aŋ yɩrʋ, “Mosis, Mosis.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis sɛɩ aŋ bʋl, “Na mɩ nɛ ŋ-la.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bʋla pʋ, “Chɩna magɛ ŋɩɩ, pʋpɔ ŋ bɩra sɩ́ sʋrɩsa kʋ kpagɛ. Chaarɛ ŋ nɛntɛŋŋɛɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa tintee-la lɛ ŋ sɩ chɩna ŋaa Wɩa lee nɛ.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bɩra bʋl, “Mɩ nɛ ŋaa ŋ naabalɩmaba Abɩraham, Aɩzɩk arɩ Jekɔb Wɩa.” Mosis sɩ nɩɩ wɩaa deemba, ʋ kɛŋ ʋ sɩaa kaa faa, bɛɛ wɩaa fawʋllʋŋ kɛnʋ nɛ, ʋ bɩ cho dɩ ʋ beŋ Wɩa.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl, “Mɩ na mɩ nɩaa sɩ faasa na hɛɛŋ ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Mɩ nɩɩ ba bunso nɛ a mʋ tɩgɛ ŋɩɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ chaasaa dɔgɩsɛba lɛ. Hɛɛ-la ba sɩɩ na wɩaa chɩl mɩ nɛ.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ kʋ tuu dɩ mɩ laaba ta Ijipiti tɩmma-la nɩsɩŋ lɛ, a lɩɩsɛba tintee-la lɛ a kaa mʋ tintee-la sɩ zɔmɔ a kɛŋ kʋdiilee aŋ pɛ jal ma. Mɩ jaŋ joŋ Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa, Hiti tɩŋŋaa, Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa, Pɛrɛs tɩŋŋaa, Hivi tɩŋŋaa arɩ Jebus tɩŋŋaa tinteyee a pɩba.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Mɩ nɩɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa bunso nɛ a na dɔgɩsɩna-la ma, Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa sɩɩ dɔgɩsɛba.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa mʋ, mɩɩ tɩmɩŋ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ, dɩ ŋ kɛŋ mɩ nɩaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis pɩɛsɛ Wɩa, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ka mɩ dɩ mɩ mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ a wuo kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bʋl, “Mɩ jaŋ chɩŋ ŋ harɩŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ kɛŋ Iziral tɩmma-la kaa kɔ peeliŋ deeŋ nyuŋ dɩ ba chʋɔlɛmɛ daha, ŋɩɩ nɛ jaŋ dagɛ arɩ mɩ-na Wɩa nɛ tɩmɩŋ.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis pɩɛsɛ Wɩa, “Ka dɩ mɩ nɛ mʋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ a bʋla pɩba, ‘Ma nyɩmmaba Wɩa nɛ tɩmmɛ ma teeŋ,’ dɩ ba pɩɛsɛmɛ, ‘Ʋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ bɛɛ?’ Bɛɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ bʋla pɩba?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bɩra bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mʋ bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA, ma naabalɩmaba Abɩraham, Aɩzɩk arɩ Jekɔb Wɩa nɛ tɩmmɛ ma teeŋ. Mɩ yɩrɩŋ nɛ ma TƖƖNA. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma doho nɩaa jaŋ yɩyɩrɛmɛ a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Mʋ a yɩrɛ Iziral nɩhɩasɩŋ kala a hilimi a bʋla pɩba, ‘Ma TƖƖNA Wɩa sɩ ŋaa ma naabalɩma Abɩraham, Aɩzɩk arɩ Jekɔb Wɩa nɛ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kʋ dagɛmɛ a bʋl: Mɩ na ma nɛ, a na ba sɩɩ ŋaama ŋɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ sɩ mɩ jaŋ lɩɩsɛma hɛɛŋ deeŋ lɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a kɛmma mʋ Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa, Hiti tɩŋŋaa, Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa, Pɛrɛs tɩŋŋaa, Hivi tɩŋŋaa arɩ Jebus tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ, tintee-la sɩ sɩma a kɛŋ kɩaa woruŋ.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ bʋl ŋ-la, Iziral nɩhɩasɩ-la jaŋ jegile nɩɩ ŋ teeŋ. Ŋ dɩ ba jaŋ mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, ‘La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa a dagɛla nɛ. Leŋ dɩ la vɛŋ wombiiŋ tapʋlaa batori a jʋʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ tʋɔŋ a kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Ama mɩ jɩma arɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bɩ jaŋ sɛɩ, see dɩ doluŋ nɛ diiu.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ joŋ mɩ doluŋ a fʋgɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa, a ŋaa wʋmagɩlaa Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ, ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma mʋ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa haal kala jaŋ mʋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa haala-la sɩ jʋʋ kpɩkpagɛba dɩɩsɩŋ arɩ haala-la sɩ hɛ ba dɩɩsɩŋ lɛ a pɩɛsa laa sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla kɩaa arɩ gɛnnɩŋ a joŋo laalɛ ba hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ba hantolibiisiŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ ŋaa a laa Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa dʋa kaa viiri.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Wɩa, “Ka dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ bɩ mɩ laa dii, a bɩ wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ bʋla jegile nɩɩ, bɛɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa dɩ ba nɛ sɩ, ‘La TƖƖNA bɩ ʋ tɩtɩa kaa dagɩŋ?’ ”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ ŋ kori ŋɩɩ?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Dantɩga nɛ.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl, “Joŋo lo tinteeŋ.” Mosis joŋo lo tinteeŋ, daa-la bɩrɩmɛ dɩmɩŋ, ʋ fá aŋ leŋu.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mʋ kɛŋ dɩŋ-la bʋbʋɔ-doho lɛ a kaa joŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis mʋ kɛŋ dɩŋ-la bʋbʋɔ-doho lɛ a joŋ, ʋ bɩrɩmɛ dantɩga ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl, “Ŋ-la nɛ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa laa dii arɩ ba naabalɩmaba Abɩraham, Aɩzɩk arɩ Jekɔb Wɩa nɛ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kʋ dagɩŋ.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bɩra bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Joŋ ŋ nɩsɩŋ a hɛ ŋ gɛrɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ.” Mosis joŋo hɛ, ʋ kaa lɩɩsɛ dɩ ʋ keri gbege aŋ pʋllɛ taŋ taŋ.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Joŋ ŋ nɩsɩŋ bɩra hɛ ŋ gɛrɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ.” Ʋ joŋo hɛ, ʋ kaa lɩɩsɛ dɩ ʋ nagɛ ʋ yaraa sɩ nagɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Dɩ wʋmagɩlaa deemba balɩa nɛ ba bɩ laa dii koo a bɩ ŋ teeŋ jegile, ŋaa lɩɩŋ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Naayɩl lɛ a bɩsa ta tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ, ʋ jaŋ bɩrɩmɛ chalɩŋ.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA, “Mɩ TƖƖNA, mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna, mɩ bɩ wʋbʋllʋ ŋaa, a lɩɩ bʋa-la kala lɛ ŋ sɩ suomo bʋl wɩaa mɩ teeŋ arɩ lɛɛlɛ kala. Mɩ nandelimiŋ yuŋŋie arɩ wɩaa bʋlʋŋ.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA pɩɛsʋ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa nuhuobiine niiŋ ʋ kaa bʋl wɩaa? Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa taŋɩŋ? Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa nuhuobiine sɩaa ʋ nɩna koo a leŋ ʋ nyʋlɩmɛ? Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dee bɩ wɩaa deemba kala ka ŋaa?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, mʋ, mɩ jaŋ pɛ ŋ lɛ a dagɩŋ wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ jaŋ bʋl.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Mɩ TƖƖNA, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ mɩɩra tɩŋ nʋʋ dɔŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA Wɩa na baanɩŋ woruŋ Mosis nyuŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Ka ŋ naambie Arɔŋ, Levi tɩɩna-la? Mɩ jɩma ʋ jaŋ wuo bʋl wɩaa woruŋ. Ʋ paala hɛ wombiiŋ lɛ nɛ aa kɔ ŋ teeŋ dɩ ʋ naŋ. Dɩ ʋ nɛ saa naŋ, ʋ tʋɔŋ jaŋ tɔrɛ.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Arɔŋ jaŋ laa ŋ niiŋ wɩaa bʋlaa pɩ nɩalɩŋ, ŋ ma Mosis jaŋ chɩŋ mɩ-na Wɩa naasɩŋ lɛ aa dagʋ wɩɩ-la sɩ maga dɩ ʋ bʋl.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Kɛŋ dantɩga deeŋ ŋ sɩ koro kaa mʋ, ŋ jaŋ kɛnʋ ŋaa wʋmagɩlaa.” Mosis mɩɩra mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis mɩɩra mʋ ʋ hɩɩlɩ-baala Jeturo teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, leŋ dɩ mɩ mɩɩra mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a na mɩ naambiiriŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ha hɛ ba mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jeturo bʋl, “Ŋ jaŋ mʋ woruŋ.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa bʋla pɩ Mosis Midiaŋ tinteeŋ lɛ, “Mɩɩra mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ, nɩalɩŋ kala fa sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ba kpʋŋ sʋba nɛ.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis sii kɛŋ ʋ haala arɩ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ a hɛ kakumo lɛ a mʋmʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ aŋ pɛ joŋ dantɩga-la Wɩa sɩ sɩ ʋ joŋ.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ, ŋaa wʋmagɩla-la kala mɩ sɩ pɩŋ doluŋ dɩ ŋ ŋaa Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ. Ama mɩ jaŋ ŋaa dɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa lɩɩ mʋ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ mʋa, bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa sɩ, ‘Iziral tɩŋŋaa nagɛ mɩ hambolibii bumbuŋ nɛ.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Mɩ bʋla pɩŋ arɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ nanʋala mʋ a na wombiiŋ chʋɔlɛmɛ, ama ŋ vɩa nɛ, ŋɩɩ wɩaa mɩ jaŋ kpʋ ŋ hambolibii bumbuŋ.’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ lɛ nɛ Mosis mʋmʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a mʋ yi lee kʋbala a chʋa nɩmɛ. La TƖƖNA chemu a ŋaa wɩaa nagɛ ʋʋ chɛ ʋ kpʋʋ.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis haala Zipora joŋ tabɩɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ niiŋ a keri ʋ nanʋala peniŋ a kɛŋ chalɩŋ taa Mosis naasɩŋ aŋ bʋl, “Lɛɛlɛ mɩ dɩ ŋ chalɩŋ ŋaa kʋbala nɛ.”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bɩ Mosis kpʋa. Zipora bʋl, “A tɩŋ bile peniŋ keriŋ wɩaa mɩ dɩŋ chalɩŋ ŋaa kʋbala nɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ, “Jʋʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ tʋɔŋ a cheŋ Mosis.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ mʋ chemu Wɩa peeliŋ nyuŋ a guoru.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Mosis bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pʋ a pɩ Arɔŋ, arɩ wʋmagɩla-la kala Wɩa sɩ dagʋ dɩ ʋ ŋaa.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a yɩrɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ a hilimi.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Arɔŋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala Wɩa sɩ bʋla pɩ Mosis a pɩba, ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis ŋaa wʋmagɩla-la Wɩa sɩ dagʋ nɩalɩŋ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ laa dii. Ba sɩ nɩa dɩ La TƖƖNA na ba hɛɛ-la ba sɩɩ na Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a chɩl ba wɩaa, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɛŋ ba nyusuŋ chugili a chʋɔlɛ Wɩa.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la, ‘Pɩ mɩ nɩaa wombiiŋ dɩ ba mʋ a gbiele pɩmɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro pɩɛsɛ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa ma TƖƖNA, aa chɛ dɩ mɩ sɛɩ ʋ niiŋ, a leŋ dɩ ma mʋ? Mɩ bɩ ma TƖƖNA jɩŋ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ bɩra bʋl, “Hiburu tɩŋŋaa Wɩa nɛ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa dagɛla. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, leŋ dɩ la vɛŋ wombiiŋ tapʋlaa batori a jʋʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ tʋɔŋ a kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa. Dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, ʋ jaŋ joŋ nyanyal bɔŋŋɔɔ hɛ la lɛ koo dɩ ʋ kpʋla.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋl, “Lɛɛlɛ nɩalɩŋ yʋga nɛ aŋ ka ma bɩ chɛ dɩ ba faasa tɩŋ.”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ fʋgɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ba tɩtɩŋ yoŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ beŋ tɩntɩmɩa-la,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Lɛɛlɛ má bɩra sɩ́ nɩalɩŋ viri-yaŋ pa dɩ ba hɛ tɩɛrɩŋ lɛ a pɛɛsɛ tiebiee, má leŋ dɩ ba tɩtɩa mʋ chɛ.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Ama, má leŋ dɩ ba pɛɛsɛ tiebiee magɛ ŋɩɩ ba fa sɩ vɛnɛɛ pɛɛsɛ. Ba ŋaa yarɩ-wɩɩ tɩmma nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ba ŋɩŋaa goŋ a bʋl, ‘Má leŋ dɩ la mʋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩ la Wɩa.’

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Má leŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ faasa tɩŋ a kɩɩ ŋɩɩ ba fa sɩɩ tɩŋ, a sɩ́ wombiiŋ na a chɩnaa nɩɩ wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ beŋ tɩntɩmɩa-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ fʋgɛba ba tɩtɩŋ kʋ lɩɩ bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, “Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩ, la bɩra sɩ́ ma viri-yaŋ pa nɛ dɩ ma kaa pɛɛsɛ tiebiee.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Má mʋ chɛ ma tɩtɩa viri-yaŋ, lee-la kala ma sɩ jaŋ naba, ama la bɩ jaŋ keri tɩntɩmɩɩ-la ma sɩ vɛnɛ tɩmaa magɛ ŋɩɩ ta.”

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ pɩsɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala lɛ a gɔllɔ chɩchɛ viri-yaŋ.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ fʋgɛba ba tɩtɩŋ yoŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa bʋl, “Má dɛrɛ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la ma sɩ maga dɩ ma tɩŋ tapʋlɩɩ kala, arɩ la fa sɩ pɩma viri-yaŋ ma tɩmaa magɛ ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ fʋgɛba ba tɩtɩŋ yoŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa ŋmuŋmoo Iziral tɩmma-la ba ma sɩ lɩɩsa dɩ ba bibeŋ tɩntɩnnaa, aŋ pɩɛsɛba, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma bɩ tiebiee pɛɛsɛ jɩnɩŋ a magɛ ŋɩɩ ma sɩ vɛnɛɛ pɛɛsɛ?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩmma-la sɩɩ beŋ tɩntɩnna-la mʋ yele pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ dʋdɔgɩsɛ la ŋ-la?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Ba bɩ la viri-yaŋ pa aŋ kpɩkpɩa la lɛ, ‘Má pɩpɛɛsɛ tiebiee,’ aŋ pɛ vɩvɩɩrɛla. Ŋ nɩaa nɛ ŋaa chei.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋl, “Ma kɛŋ yarɩ-wɩɩŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ma bʋbʋl arɩ mɩ leŋ dɩ ma mʋ a kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Má mɩɩra mʋ ma tɩntɩŋŋaa, nʋʋkala bɩ jaŋ pɩma viri-yaŋ. Ama ma ha maga ma pɛɛsɛ tiebiee magɛ ŋɩɩ ma sɩ vɛnɛɛ pɛɛsɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩmma-la sɩɩ beŋ tɩntɩnna-la jɩŋ arɩ wɩɩŋ jʋʋba nɛ, arɩ ba sɩsɩ, “Má bɩ maga dɩ ma lɩɩsɛ tiebiee magɛ ŋɩɩ ma sɩ vɛnɛɛ pɛɛsɛ a ta.”

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ sii Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ, baa mʋ dɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ hɔnɔ gbɩgbɛrɛba.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ, “La TƖƖNA na wɩɩ-la ma sɩ ŋaa nɛ, ʋ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛma. Ma leŋe Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ bɛrɛla nɛ a joŋ dʋndɔnnʋŋ hɛ la pɛgɛ dɩ ba kpʋla.” Wɩa sɩ ʋ jaŋ laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis sʋl Wɩa a bʋl, “Ou mɩ Tɩɩna, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ joŋ hɛɛŋ deeŋ hɛ nɩaa deemba lɛ? Ŋ-la wɩaa nɛ ŋ tɩmmɛ daha?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Bʋa-la kala lɛ ŋ sɩ tɩmmɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ ŋ yɩrɩŋ lɛ, ʋ dɔgɩsɛ nɩaa deemba nɛ, ka ŋ bɩ wɩɩkala ŋaa dɩ ŋ laaba ta.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Lɛɛlɛ ŋ jaŋ na wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro lɛ. Mɩ jaŋ fʋgʋ dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mʋ. Mɩ jaŋ fʋgʋ dɩ ʋ kiriba dɩ ba lɩɩ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: Mɩ kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa dagɛ Abɩraham, Aɩzɩk arɩ Jekɔb arɩ mɩ nɛ Wɩa doluŋ kala Tɩɩna, ama mɩ bɩ leŋe ba jɩŋ arɩ mɩ yɩrɩŋ nɛ ‘ma TƖƖNA.’

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Mɩ hɛ niiŋ mɩ dɩ ba pɛgɛ nɛ arɩ mɩ jaŋ joŋ Kɛnaŋ tintee-la lɛ ba sɩ hɔnɔ a ŋaa nʋhʋɔra pɩba.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ lɛ, mɩ nɩɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa bunso nɛ, Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa sɩ kɛmba bɩrɩmɛ yosuŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ liise yi nii-la sɩ hɛ mɩ dɩ ba pɛgɛ.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa: ‘Mɩ nɛ ŋaa Wɩa, ma TƖƖNA, mɩ jaŋ lɩɩsɛma hɛɛ-la ma sɩɩ na Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Mɩ jaŋ laama ta arɩ mɩ doluŋ, dɩ ma bɩra sɩ́ yosi ŋaa. Mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ jomma dɩ ma ŋaa mɩ nɩaa, ka dɩ mɩ ŋaa ma Wɩa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma Wɩa, ma TƖƖNA, Wɩa-la sɩ laama ta hɛɛ-la ma fa sɩɩ na Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ kɛmma mʋ tintee-la mɩ sɩ chaasa hɛ niiŋ arɩ mɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩ Abɩraham, Aɩzɩk, arɩ Jekɔb. Mɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩma dɩ ʋ ŋaa ma kʋŋ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Mʋ bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA, “Mɩ sɩ paala bʋl wɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ, ba bɩ jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ, ɛɛ nɛ saa Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro-na jaŋ jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ? Mɩ paala bɩ wɩaa bʋlʋŋ jɩŋ woruŋ.”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ dɩ ba mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ a bʋla pʋ dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ doho nɩaa

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Rubiŋ, Jekɔb bii-hɩaŋ kɛŋ hambolibiisiŋ banɛsɛ nɛ: Hanɔk, Pallu, Hɛzɩrɔŋ arɩ Kaamɩ. Rubiŋ doho nɩaa nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simioŋ ma kɛŋ hambolibiisiŋ balɩdʋ nɛ: Jɛmʋɛl, Jamɩŋ, Ohad, Jakɩŋ, Zoha arɩ Sawʋl. Sawʋl naaŋ ŋaa Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa tolo nɛ. Simioŋ ma doho nɩaa nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Mɛrarɩ ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ Mali arɩ Musi. Levi doho nɩaa nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Iziha ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ: Kora, Nɛfɛg arɩ Zikiri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Ʋzɩɛl ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ Mɩsɩɛl, Ɛlɩzafaŋ arɩ Sɩtɩrɩ.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Arɔŋ nɛ jaa Eliseba, Amɩnadab tolo. Eliseba ŋaa Nasɔŋ dɩhaala nɛ. Nasɔŋ nɛ lʋl Nadab, Abihu, Elieza arɩ Ɩtama.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Kora ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ: Asɛɛ, Ɛlɩkaana arɩ Abɩasaf. Kora doho nɩaa nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Arɔŋ nanʋala Elieza jaa Pʋtɩɛl tolo dɔŋɔ nɛ ʋ lʋl Finihas. Levi doho arɩ ba nɩhɩasɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Arɔŋ arɩ Mosis deeŋ tɩtɩa nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pa, “Má kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa doho doho kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Ba nɛ bɩra bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Wɩa sɩ bʋl wɩɩ-la a pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Wɩa sɩ bʋl wɩaa pɩ Mosis Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: ʋ sɩ, “Mɩ nɛ ŋaa ma Tɩɩna. Mʋ́ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ bʋla pɩŋ a pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Ama Mosis bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA, “Ŋ jɩma mɩ bɩ wɩaa bʋlʋŋ jɩŋ, Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bɩ jaŋ jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Bee na, mɩ ŋaa ŋ nagɛ mɩ-na Wɩa nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ, ka ŋ naambie Arɔŋ ŋaa ŋ wʋlaabʋlla.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Ʋ maga dɩ ŋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ bʋla pɩŋ, dɩ ŋ naambie Arɔŋ ma laa bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: A tɩŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩ bɩ jaŋ jegile nɩɩ ma teeŋ ŋɩɩ, mɩ jaŋ joŋ doluŋ a kɛŋ mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa a lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ba TƖƖNA, dɩ mɩ nɛ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ ba tinteeŋ lɛ arɩ doluŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Dɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro nɛ bʋla arɩ ma ŋaa wʋmagɩl a dagɛ arɩ mɩ-na Wɩa nɛ tɩmma, bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ dɩ ʋ joŋ ʋ dantɩga-la lo Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ, ʋ jaŋ bɩrɩmɛ dɩmɩŋ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ a ŋaa wʋmagɩl-la Wɩa sɩ dagɛba. Arɔŋ joŋ ʋ dantɩga lo Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ sɩpaaŋ, ʋ bɩrɩmɛ dɩmɩŋ.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro yɩrɛ ʋ jaŋ wʋjɩnnaa, vʋgʋraa arɩ ba chichiribee kala, ba ma ŋaa ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa arɩ ba chichiribiŋ.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kʋŋkala joŋ ʋ dantɩga lo ʋ bɩrɩmɛ dɩmɩŋ. Ama Arɔŋ dɩmɩŋ paa ba dɩŋŋaa liŋ.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ ha pɩrɛ, ʋ bɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ teeŋ jegile arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ. Chalɩŋ su Ijipiti tinteeŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ ha pɩra nɛ. Ʋ vɩa dɩ ʋ pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa wombiiŋ dɩ ba mʋ nɛ.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Sii mʋ chemu chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Naayɩl niiŋ. Pɛ joŋ dantɩga-la sɩ bɩrɩmɛ dɩmɩŋ a kori.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ chemu, bʋla pʋ, ‘Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa nɛ tɩmmɛ ŋ teeŋ dɩ mɩ bʋla pɩŋ: Leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mʋ a chʋɔlɛmɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ. Ama faafaa kala a kaa kɔ bʋa deeŋ lɛ ŋ bɩ jegile nɩɩ.

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Wʋmagɩlɩŋ deeŋ nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa dɩ ŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ nʋʋkala Tɩɩna. Dantɩga deeŋ mɩ sɩ koro mɩ jaŋ joŋo ŋmoo fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Naayɩl lɩɩŋ dɩ ʋ bɩrɩmɛ chalɩŋ.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Chenfile-la kala sɩ hɛ fuo-la lɛ jaŋ sʋʋ, dɩ lɩɩ-la sʋsʋɔrɛ. Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa bɩ jaŋ wuo nyʋa lɩɩ-la.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ, dɩ ʋ kɛŋ dantɩga-la sɩ hɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ a kaa liesi Ijipiti tinteeŋ fuonuŋ, vilee arɩ lee na-kala lɩɩŋ sɩ hɛ, ba kala jaŋ bɩrɩmɛ chalɩŋ. Chalɩŋ jaŋ hɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lee na-kala. Kɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ kɛŋ daasɩŋ arɩ chʋrʋŋ ŋaa a hɩhɛ lɩɩŋ jaŋ su arɩ chalɩŋ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ dagɛba. Arɔŋ kɛŋ ʋ dantɩga je Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ kala sɩpaaŋ aŋ ŋmoo fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Naayɩl lɩɩŋ, ʋ bɩrɩmɛ chalɩŋ.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ chenfile-la sɩ hɛ fuo-la lɛ sʋʋ, lɩɩ-la sʋsʋɔrɛ, Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa bɩ lɩɩ-la wuo nyʋa. Chalɩŋ su Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ chichiribee ma ŋaa ŋɩɩ arɩ ba chichiribiŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ wasa dol. Ʋ vɩa dɩ ʋ jegile Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ teeŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Wɩɩŋ deeŋ sɩ ŋaa ma kala, Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bɩ jegile nɩɩ aŋ mɩɩra jʋʋ ʋ kuoru dɩa.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa gɔllɔ lu vilee Naayɩl fuo-la sɛmɛ a chɩchɛ lɩɩŋ ba nyʋa, bɛɛ wɩaa ba fa bɩ fuo-la lɩɩŋ wuo nyʋa.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA sɩ ŋaa Naayɩl fuo-la lɩɩŋ bɩrɩmɛ chalɩŋ ŋɩɩ, ʋ diene a yi tapʋlaa balɩpɛ nɛ.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, ‘Leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ a chʋɔlɛmɛ.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ vɩa dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ ba mʋ, mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ sɔrɔɔ kʋ su Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Naayɩl jaŋ su arɩ sɔrɔɔ, dɩ ba lɩɩ nɩmɛ a jʋʋ ŋ dɩa, ŋ dɩpɩnɩŋ, ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ŋ nɩaa kala dɩɩsɩŋ, ma tabʋʋnʋŋ arɩ ma nɔnnʋŋ kala.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Sɔrɔ-la jaŋ fɩla jɩla sagɛ ŋ lɛ, ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ŋ nɩaa kala lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ dantɩga-la ʋ sɩ koro a kaa zaarɛ fuonuŋ, fuonaasɩŋ arɩ pɩlaa kala sɩ hɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, a leŋ dɩ sɔrɔɔ lɩɩ su Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala.”

english_verse: Aaron obeyed, and suddenly frogs were everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Arɔŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ dagʋ, sɔrɔɔ lɩɩ tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala.

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ chichiribee ma ŋaa ba chichiribiŋ, sɔrɔɔ kʋ lɩɩ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro yɩrɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ a bʋl, “Má sʋl La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ sɔrɔ-la nyɩɩgɛ mɩ dɩ mɩ nɩaa tinteeŋ lɛ, ka dɩ mɩ leŋ dɩ ʋ nɩaa mʋ a kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a dɛnnʋ.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “Mɩ joŋ wɩɩkala hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ dɩ ŋ dagɛ bʋa-la lɛ ŋ sɩ cho dɩ mɩ sʋl Wɩa pɩŋ, ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ŋ nɩaa dɩ sɔrɔ-la lɛl, a lɛl ma dɩɩsɩŋ ma lɛ, aŋ ka kɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ Naayɩl fuo-la lɛ.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋl, “Kʋ sʋl Wɩa pɩmɛ chie.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Mɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ bʋla, dɩ ŋ wuo jɩŋ arɩ Wɩa dɔŋ kala tuo a magɛ La TƖƖNA Wɩa.

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ sɩ ta Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro aŋ lɩɩ, ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis sʋl Wɩa a mʋ tɩgɛ sɔrɔ-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ kaa kʋ hɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA laa Mosis sʋla. Sɔrɔ-la kala sɩ hɛ ba dɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, kaalɩsɩŋ lɛ arɩ bagɩsɩŋ lɛ kala sʋʋ.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Ba hiesi sɔrɔ-la bil puguloo, ba sʋara su tintee-la kala.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Ama Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩ na dɩ sɔrɔ-la sʋba ŋɩɩ, ʋ tʋɔŋ bɩra dol. Ʋ bɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ nɩɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ teeŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ. Dɩnsɩŋ su Ijipiti tinteeŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ ʋ dantɩga-la je a ŋmoo tinteeŋ dɩ kʋŋkɔlʋŋ sii a bɩrɩmɛ dɩnsɩŋ a su Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala.

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Ba ŋaa ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ daga, Arɔŋ kɛŋ ʋ dantɩga-la je a ŋmoo tinteeŋ kʋŋkɔlʋŋ sii a bɩrɩmɛ dɩnsɩŋ a dɩdɩŋ nuhuobiinee arɩ pʋsʋŋ kala, Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala su arɩ dɩnsɩŋ.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ chichiribee ma ŋaa ba chichiribi wɩaa dɩ ba ma leŋ dɩnsɩŋ lɩɩ, ama ba bɩ wuo ŋaa, ka dɩnsɩ-la dɩdɩŋ nuhuobiinee arɩ pʋsʋŋ kala.”

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ chichiribe-la bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “Wɩa nɛ dagɛ ʋ doluŋ ŋɩɩ.” Ama Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ ha pɩrɛ ʋ bɩ jegile nɩɩ ba teeŋ, arɩ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ. Nanchʋɔsʋŋ su Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Sii mʋ cheŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩ yie mʋmʋ fuo-la leriŋ a bʋla pʋ, ‘Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mʋ a wuo dɛnnɛmɛ.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ vɩa, mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ nanchʋɔsʋŋ kʋ ju tɔŋ, a tɔ ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ, a tɔ ŋ nɩaa a jʋʋ su ma dɩɩsɩŋ. Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa dɩɩsɩŋ arɩ ba tinteeŋ kala jaŋ su arɩ nanchʋɔsʋŋ.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA ŋaa ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ daga, a leŋ nanchʋɔ-laalɩŋ kʋ su Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala, Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro dɩa arɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ dɩɩsɩŋ, a chei ba tinteeŋ.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro yɩrɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ a bʋla pɩba, “Má mʋ a kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a dɛnnɛ ma Wɩa tinteeŋ deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Ŋɩɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa, dɩ la nɛ sɩ la kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA Wɩa Ijipiti nɩaa sɩɩŋ lɛ, la jaŋ chei ba kɩsɩŋ lɛ, dɩ ba yagɛla arɩ tabɩaa.

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Ʋ maga la vɛŋ tapʋlaa batori wombiiŋ nɛ a jʋʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ tʋɔŋ, a mʋ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa arɩ ʋ sɩ dagɛla ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋl, “Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma mʋ a kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩ-sʋla pɩ ma TƖƖNA tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ, ama má sɩ́ dɩ-bolii mʋ. Má pɛ sʋl Wɩa pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “Dɩ mɩ nɛ kʋ lɩɩ daha, mɩ jaŋ sʋl La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ chie leŋ dɩ nanchʋɔsʋ-la nyɩɩgɛ ŋ lɛ, ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ŋ nɩaa kala teeŋ. Ama ŋ bɩra bɩ maga dɩ ŋ nyɩsɛla, a pɔ dɩ la sɩ́ mʋ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA.”

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Mosis sii Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ a mʋ sʋl La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA laa Mosis sʋla a leŋ nanchʋɔsʋ-la nyɩɩgɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro lɛ, ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ nɩaa kala teeŋ. Nanchʋɔ-bala ma bɩ ka.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Ama nanchʋɔsʋ-la sɩ mʋa, Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ bɩra dol, ʋ bɩ leŋe nɩalɩŋ mʋ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mʋ a chʋɔlɛmɛ.

english_verse: If you keep refusing,
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ vɩa aŋ ha kɛmba kɩɩ,

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA jaŋ joŋ nyanyalɩŋ hɛ ma pʋsʋ-la kala ma sɩɩ dɩɛsʋ lɛ: ma janɩŋ, ma kakusuŋ, ma bʋntaŋŋaba, ma nɛsɩŋ, ma piesee arɩ ma bʋʋnaa kala.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Ama mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA jaŋ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa pʋsʋŋ pɔrɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ, dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa pʋsʋŋ sɩ́ sʋʋ.’ ”

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA hɛ tapʋlɩɩ-la a bʋl, “Chie nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ tinteeŋ deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, La TƖƖNA ŋaa ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ daga. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa pʋsʋŋ kala sʋʋ, ama Iziral tɩŋŋaa pʋŋ-bala ma bɩ sʋba.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ, “Má ŋaa tʋɔrʋŋ tabʋʋŋ lɛ nɩsɩŋ sɩɩŋ, a kaa mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ, dɩ Mosis joŋo yuo wɩa-nyuŋ.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ bɩrɩmɛ kʋŋkɔlʋŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala lɛ, dɩ mɔpʋllʋŋ ŋmɛrɛ nuhuobiinee arɩ pʋsʋŋ lɛ a yɛrɛ a ŋaa naawɩɩlaa.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba ŋaa tʋɔrʋ-la tabʋʋŋ lɛ a kaa mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ. Mosis joŋo yuo wɩa-nyuŋ, mɔpʋllʋŋ ŋmɛrɛ nuhuobiinee arɩ pʋsʋŋ kala lɛ a yɛrɛ a ŋaa naawɩɩlaa.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ chichiribe-la bɩ wuo pagɩsɛ Mosis mɔpʋllʋ-la-na lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa mɔpʋllʋ-la ŋmɛrɛ chichiribe-la kala lɛ nɛ a nagɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa kala sɩ ŋmɛrɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Ama La TƖƖNA leŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ, ʋ bɩ jegile nɩɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ teeŋ, arɩ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ. Duoŋ-tabɩaa tel Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Sii mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla a chaasa bʋla pʋ, ‘Mɩ-na Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mʋ a chʋɔlʋ.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ-na lɛ dɩ ŋ nɛ vɩa, mɩ jaŋ joŋ mɩ nyanyal bɔŋŋɔɔ kala hɛ ŋ lɛ, ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ŋ nɩaa kala lɛ, dɩ ma jɩŋ arɩ nʋʋkala tuo a magɛmɛ dʋnɩa kala lɛ.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Mɩ kɛŋ doluŋ mɩ fa sɩ jaŋ joŋ nyanyal bɔŋŋɔɔ hɛ ŋ dɩ ŋ nɩaa kala lɛ dɩ ma nyɩɩgɛ tinteeŋ kala lɛ,

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: ama mɩ lemma nɛ, dɩ mɩ dagɛ mɩ doluŋ dɩ mɩ yɩrɩŋ yɩrɛ dʋnɩa sɛmɛ na-kala.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Ŋ ha kɛŋ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ a bɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mʋ,

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: a tɩŋ ŋɩɩ wɩaa, chie bʋa deeŋ lɛ mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ duoŋ-tabɩaa faasa tel Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala lɛ, dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa ha sɩ bɩ na aŋ ka.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩ nʋʋkala dɩ ba kiri ba pʋsʋŋ arɩ kʋŋ na-kala ba sɩ kɛnɛ dɩ-jalɩŋ a hɛ dɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa duoŋ-tabɩaa jaŋ yagɛ nuhuobiinee arɩ pʋsʋ-la kala sɩ hɛ dɩ-jalɩŋ dɩ ba sʋʋ.’ ”

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro nɩhɩasɩ-la dɔnsʋŋ sɩɩ fá Wɩa sɩ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla, fawʋllʋŋ kɛmba, ba kiri ba yosuŋ arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ kala lɩma lɩma ba jʋʋ dɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Ama nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla kaa tɩŋ, leŋ ba yosuŋ arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ kala dɩ-jalɩŋ.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Kɛŋ ŋ nɩsɩŋ je wɩa-nyuŋ, dɩ duoŋ-tabɩaa tel Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala lɛ, a yagɛ nɩaa, pʋsʋŋ arɩ kʋŋ na-kala sɩ nyʋ tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ duoŋ-tabɩaa tele tɔ kʋŋkala nɛ, pʋsʋŋ, nuhuobiinee arɩ kʋŋkala sɩ nyʋ tinteeŋ, tɩɩsɩŋ kala yuori.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ hɛ tintee-la lɛ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Goseŋ dʋndʋŋa lɛ nɛ wɩɩŋ deeŋ bɩ ŋaa.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tɩma yɩrɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ a bʋla pɩba, “Bʋa deeŋ lɛ la ŋaa chei La TƖƖNA nɛ, La TƖƖNA kɩaa sɩma nɛ, mɩ dɩ mɩ nɩaa nɛ bɩ woruŋ ŋaa.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Má sʋl La TƖƖNA pɩla, duoŋ-tabɩaa arɩ duoŋ kpɩa-na-la dɔgɩsɛla yʋgɛ nɛ. Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma mʋ, ma bɩra bɩ maga dɩ ma hɛ daha.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “Dɩ mɩ nɛ lɩɩ tabalɩŋ deeŋ tʋɔŋ, mɩ jaŋ sʋl La TƖƖNA dɩ duoŋ kpɩana-la arɩ duoŋ-tabɩa-la leŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ tɩɩ tinteeŋ kala.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Ama mɩ jɩma arɩ ŋ dɩ ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ ha bɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa ka fá.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Bɔɔ doho kʋbala ba sɩ kaa ŋɩŋaa gɛrɩpɛɛŋ arɩ mɩaa kala chei, bɛɛ wɩaa bʋa-la lɛ dɩ mɩa-la lʋla, tɩa-la ma fɩɩlɛ.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Ama duoŋ-tabɩa-la bɩ mɛmpɛba cheye, bɛɛ wɩaa ba-na fa ha bɩ waa.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Mosis sɩ sii Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ a lɩɩ tabal-la lɛ ʋ sʋl La TƖƖNA, ŋɩɩ nɛ duoŋ-tabɩa-la arɩ duoŋ kpɩa-na-la arɩ duoŋ-la kala leŋ.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩ na dɩ duoŋ-tabɩa-la arɩ duoŋ kpɩa-na-la arɩ duoŋ-la leŋe, ʋ bɩra ŋɩŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ. Ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ kala bɩra kɛŋ tʋɔ-doluŋ.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ ʋ vɩa dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ, arɩ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ pɩ Mosis.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ, mɩ nɛ ŋaa ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ, dɩ mɩ wuo to ŋɩɩ lɛ a ŋaa wʋmagɩlaa ba tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma wuo bʋla pɩ ma biiriŋ arɩ ma nihee ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ wʋrɩgɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa arɩ wʋmagɩla-la mɩ sɩ ŋaa ba tʋɔŋ, dɩ ma wuo jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ma TƖƖNA.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ, a bʋla pʋ, “La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ, ‘Ɛɛ nɛ ŋ chɛ dɩ ŋ vɩa mɩ niiŋ diene magɛ? Leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mʋ a chʋɔlɛmɛ.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ vɩa dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ ba mʋ, mɩ chie jaŋ leŋ dɩ hɔbɔ lɩɩ su ma tinteeŋ kala.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ tɔ tinteeŋ kala, lee bɩ jaŋ ka. Ba jaŋ dii kʋŋ na-kala duoŋ tabɩa-la sɩ bɩ kpʋa, arɩ tɩɩsɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ ma bagɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Hɔbɔ-la jaŋ su ŋ dɩa, ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ dɩɩsɩŋ a su Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa kala dɩɩsɩŋ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ jaŋ ŋaa wʋmagɩl ma nyɩmmaba arɩ ma naabalɩmaba ha sɩ bɩ na aŋ ka ba sɩ sie kala.’ ” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro teeŋ a viiri.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tɩntɩnnaa pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ wɩɩ nɛ baala deeŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ hɛ la lɛ ŋ-la? Leŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ mʋ a zil ba Wɩa, ŋ bɩ na dɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ ka chɛ dɩ ʋ chei?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba yɩrɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ ba mɩɩra kɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ. Ʋ bʋla pɩba, “Má mʋ a zil ma TƖƖNA Wɩa. Ama ma tʋɔŋ kʋbɛɛba nɛ jaŋ mʋ?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “La jaŋ kɛŋ la nɩaa kala mʋ, nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ hambiisiŋ kala a pɛ la pʋsʋŋ kala lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa laa mʋ dɩ la gbieli gbieli-bal nɛ a pɩ La TƖƖNA.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ, “La TƖƖNA jaŋ kɛmma mʋ, ama mɩ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma to kɛŋ ma haalaa arɩ ma biiriŋ a mʋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ naga wʋbɔŋ nɛ ma bɩɩnɛ.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma baalaa dʋndʋŋa nɛ mʋ a zil ma Wɩa arɩ ma sɩɩ chɛ ŋɩɩ.” Ʋ sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ dɛrɛ, ʋ kiri Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ ʋ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Kɛŋ ŋ nɩsɩŋ zaarɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ, dɩ hɔbɔ lɩɩ tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala a dii pɩpaarɩ-la kala duoŋ-tabɩa-la sɩ bɩ kpʋa.”

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ ʋ dantɩga zaarɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, La TƖƖNA leŋ peliŋ lu a lɩɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ wɩɩhɛyɛ arɩ tɩtaŋɩŋ kala, taŋ ka pʋl dɩ pel-la kɛŋ hɔbɔ kɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Hɔbɔ-la faasa yʋgɛ a kʋ tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lee-kala. Hɔbɔ-la doho ha bɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ ŋɩɩ tɔ aŋ ka, ba maachie ma saa bɩra bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ ba tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Ba tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala nɛ ʋ biri, a dii kʋŋ na-kala sɩ nyʋa, tɩɩnɛnɛɛ, pɩpaarɩŋ arɩ kʋŋ na-kala duoŋ-tabɩa-la sɩ bɩ kpʋa.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tɩŋ dɩ ba mʋ kɛŋ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ kɔ lɩma. Ba sɩ kɔ ʋ bʋl, “Mɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ a chei ma dɩ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Mɩɩ sʋlma, má joŋ wɩɩŋ deeŋ mɩ sɩ ŋaa chei a chɛmɛ aŋ sʋl ma TƖƖNA Wɩa dɩ ʋ lɩɩsɛmɛ wʋbɔmʋŋ deeŋ sɩɩ cheimi lɛ.”

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis lɩɩ sʋl La TƖƖNA pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA kɛŋ pel-la bɩrɩmɛ ʋ lu a lɩɩ wɩɩjʋʋlʋŋ a paa hɔbɔ-la kaa mʋ hɛ mʋgʋ-bal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mʋgʋ-fɩaŋ lɛ. Hɔbɔ-la kʋbala ma bɩ ka Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Ama La TƖƖNA ha leŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ, ʋ bɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa wombiiŋ pa dɩ ba mʋ. Birimiŋ tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Kɛŋ ŋ nɩsɩŋ je wɩa-nyuŋ, birimiŋ jaŋ kʋ tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala, dɩ leriŋ biri churu.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ ʋ nɩsɩŋ je wɩa-nyuŋ, birimiŋ kʋ tɔ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala, leriŋ biri lim tapʋlaa batori.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala bɩ ʋ dɔŋɔ ka na, nʋʋ ma bɩ wuo sii lee-la ʋ sɩ hɛ, ŋɩɩ tapʋlaa batori. Ama pʋlʋmʋŋ hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa-na sɩ hɛ lee-la nɛ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro yɩrɛ Mosis a bʋla pʋ, “Ma dɩ ma haalaa arɩ ma biiriŋ kala jaŋ wuo mʋ a zil ma TƖƖNA. Ama má leŋ ma pʋsʋŋ-na.”

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Ʋ maga dɩ ŋ leŋ la kɛŋ la pʋsʋŋ mʋ nɛ a kpʋ a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: La pʋsʋŋ ma maga dɩ ba to la harɩŋ mʋ nɛ. Kʋŋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ ka, ba nɛ la jaŋ kaa zil La TƖƖNA Wɩa. La bɩ jɩŋ pʋna-la la sɩ jaŋ kaa kpʋ zil La TƖƖNA, see dɩ la yi nɩmɛ.”

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bɩra leŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ, ʋ bɩ sɛyɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro kpɩa Mosis lɛ, “Nyɩɩgɛ mɩ sɩpaaŋ, chɛɛ-la mɩ bɩra sɩ jaŋ naŋ mɩ sɩpaaŋ, ŋ jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Mɩ nɩa nɛ, mɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ kɔ ŋ sɩpaaŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mɩ ha jaŋ bɩra joŋ wʋbɔŋ a hɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ nɩaa lɛ, ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ. Dɩ ʋ nɛ saa sɛyɛ, ʋ jaŋ kiri ma kala dɩ ma lɩɩ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ, bʋla pɩ ŋ nɩaa dɩ baalaa mʋ ba nandɔsʋŋ teeŋ, dɩ haalaa ma mʋ ba tanlɔsʋŋ teeŋ a chɩŋ hɔpʋla kpɩɛraa arɩ sɛlɩmɛ kpɩɛraa.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA leŋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa cho Iziral tɩŋŋaa. Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ nɩaa kala joŋ Mosis ʋ ŋaa nɩ-yuŋi.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “La TƖƖNA sɩ ʋ jaŋ gɔllɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala tɩta-siesee.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Hambolibii-bumbuŋ na-kala sɩ hɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ jaŋ sʋʋ, a chɩŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro hambolibii bumbuŋ-la sɩ jaŋ hɔŋ kuoru kpasa lɛ, a kaa tuu yoŋ-haal-la sɩɩ nɔŋ munuŋ nanʋa-hɩaŋ. Ba nɛsɩŋ ma bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ jaŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa jaŋ yele su leriŋ kala, bɛɛ wɩaa wʋdoho deeŋ ha bɩ ba lɛ ŋaa aŋ ka, wɩɩŋ deeŋ dɔŋɔ saa bɩra bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ ʋ ŋaa Ijipiti tinteeŋ kala lɛ.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Ama Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ, vaha ma bɩ jaŋ huosi nʋʋ koo pʋna. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ dabaŋ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ joŋo hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa pɛgɛ.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Ŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ kala jaŋ kʋ kpirimi mɩ sɩpaaŋ, a sʋlmɛ dɩ mɩ dɩ mɩ nɩaa kala viiri. La jaŋ viiri.” Mosis sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ dɛrɛ, ʋ na baanɩŋ woruŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro nyuŋ aŋ lɩɩ viiri.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro bɩ jaŋ jegili ŋ teeŋ, ŋɩɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ ŋaa wʋmagɩlaa yʋgɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ ŋaa wʋmagɩla-la kala nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ, ama La TƖƖNA leŋe Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ nɛ, ʋ bɩ leŋe Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ,

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Chɛnɛ deeŋ nɛ jaŋ ŋaa ma jɩna tʋɔŋ chɛŋ-bumbuŋ.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala, chɛnɛ deeŋ tapʋlaa fii chɛɛŋ, dɩa tɩɩna-kala jaŋ kpʋ pie-bie a pɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ lɩɩsɛ pʋsʋ-la, má beŋ ba nyuŋ a mʋ yi chɛŋ-bumbuŋ-la tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɛsɛ chɛɛŋ, dɩ Iziral tɩɩna-kala kpʋ ʋ pʋna wɩɩ-mul-jʋʋlʋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Dɩɩsɩ-la lɛ ma sɩ jaŋ hɔnɔ chaŋ nammɩa-la, má ŋaa pʋsʋ-la chalɩŋ a taa boiŋ niiŋ sɛsɩŋ arɩ nyuŋ.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋ-la tɩtɩa, má wasɛ nammɩa-la arɩ pɩpaa-haarɩŋ, a kɛŋ boroboro-la sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ a dii.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ nammɩa-la kʋhuoŋ koo kʋchɔɔlʋŋ chaŋ, má wasɛ ba kala, nyusuŋ, naasɩŋ arɩ tʋɔŋ kɩaa kala.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ nammɩa-la chɩna chʋa. Dɩ ʋ nɛ ka dɩ taŋ pʋl, má joŋo nyɩgɛ.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋ-la nɛ ma jaŋ dii kɩalɩŋ: Má vɔɔ ma gɛnnɩŋ arɩ damɛrɩsɩŋ, a hɛ nɛntɛŋŋɛɛ aŋ paa ma dantɩgɩsɩŋ kori a dii kɩalɩŋ lɩma lɩma. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal gbiele nɛ.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋ-la tɩtɩa, mɩ jaŋ gɔllɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a kpʋ ba hambolibii-hɩasɩŋ arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ a leŋ vesi-la kala sɩ hɛ Ijipiti lɛ jɩŋ arɩ ba bɩ kɩaa ŋaa, mɩ nɛ ŋaa ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Chal-la ma sɩ ŋaa taa ma dɩɩsɩŋ jaŋ ŋaa magɩl, dɩ mɩ nɛ kʋ naʋ, mɩ jaŋ kiele bal, wʋbɔŋ kala bɩ jaŋ ŋaa ma lɛ dɩ mɩ nɛ kɔ dɩ mɩ yuo Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: Tapʋlʋŋ deeŋ jaŋ ŋaa magɩl a pɩma, dɩ ma dɩ ma doho nɩaa kala gbieli a liliisi wɩalɩŋ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ ŋaa a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Ma jaŋ dii boroboro-la sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ. Tapʋl-bumbuŋ, má paa sɩ-bʋrʋ-la kala sɩ hɛ ma dɩɩsɩŋ lɛ lɩɩ ta. A lɩɩ tapʋl-bumbuŋ a kaa mʋ tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ, dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ dii kʋdiilii sɩ kɛŋ sɩbʋrʋŋ, má lɩɩsʋ ta Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Tapʋl-bumbuŋ arɩ tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ má hilimi La TƖƖNA yɩrɩŋ lɛ. Tapʋlaa deemba, má sɩ́ tɩntɩmɩɩ kala tɩŋ, see kʋdiile-la ma sɩ jaŋ ŋaa dii.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Ʋ maga dɩ maa gbieli boroboro-la sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ gbiele nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ mɩ kɛŋ ma doho nɩaa kala kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Ma dɩ ma doho nɩaa kala sɩ jaŋ to ma harɩŋ kɔ jaŋ gbigbieli tapʋlʋŋ deeŋ chɛɛŋ a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: A chɩŋ chɛŋ-bumbuŋ tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɛsɛ chɛɛŋ dɩdaanɩŋ a kaa mʋ tapʋlaa mara arɩ kʋbala dɩdaanɩŋ, nʋʋkala maga dɩ ʋ didii boroboro-la sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ nɛ.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Tapʋlaa balɩpɛ-la pɛgɛ, nʋʋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ hɛ ʋ dɩa lɛ. Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ dii kʋŋ sɩ kɛŋ sɩbʋrʋŋ, má lɩɩsʋ ta Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ, dɩ tɩɩna ŋaa Iziral tɩɩna koo nɩwogo.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ kʋŋkala sɩ kɛŋ sɩbʋrʋŋ dii lee na-kala ma sɩ hɛ. Má didii kɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis yɩrɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋhɩasɩŋ hɛ dɔŋɔ a bʋla pɩba, “Má kʋŋkala mʋ lɩma a lɩɩsɛ pie-bel pɔrʋŋ a pɩ ma dɩa nɩaa dɩ ba kpʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal pʋna.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Má chɔl kaku-dɩgɩlɩŋ a kaa yuu pʋna-la ma sɩ kpʋa chalɩŋ sɩ hɛ taasɩ-gbaŋa lɛ a taa ma boiŋ niiree sɛsɩŋ arɩ nyuŋ. Nʋʋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ kʋ lɩɩ ʋ dɩa tʋɔŋ see taŋ pʋla.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
