translation_verse: Dɩ La TƖƖNA nɩɩ gɔllɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ dɩ ʋ kpʋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa, ʋ jaŋ na chal-la sɩ taa ma boiŋ niiree a kiele bal, ʋ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ wʋbɔŋ kala jʋʋma.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ mʋ tintee-la La TƖƖNA sɩ sɩ ʋ jaŋ joŋo pɩma, má tuto wɩɩŋ deeŋ.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Dɩ ma biiriŋ nɛ pɩɛsɛma, arɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma sɩɩ ŋaa ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ bɛɛ,

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: ma jaŋ bʋla pɩba, ‘Ʋ ŋaa dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal gbiele nɛ aa zil La TƖƖNA, ʋ sɩ kieli Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩɩsɩŋ bal Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ aŋ kpʋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa aŋ leŋ la.’ ” Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ tuu kpirimi a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ dagɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ.

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩta-siesee La TƖƖNA kʋ kpʋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa hambolibii bumbumba kala, a chɩŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro hambolibii bumbuŋ lɛ, a kaa mʋʋ yi nɩalɩŋ ba fa sɩ kaa tɔ dɩa hambolibii bumbumba, a pɛ ba pʋsʋŋ kala bii-bumbumba lɛ.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ arɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa kala sii yele su Ijipiti tinteeŋ tɩtaŋɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa dɩa kala tuo Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ nʋʋ sɩ bɩ sʋba.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋ-la Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro yɩrɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ a bʋla pɩba, “Ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sii aŋ leŋ mɩ nɩaa a mʋ zil ma TƖƖNA arɩ ma fa sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Má to kɛsɛ ma piesee, bʋʋnaa arɩ ma nɛsɩŋ a viiri. Dɩ ma nɛ mʋa, ma sʋl Wɩa pɩ mɩ ma.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa yigiba dɩ ba lɩɩ ba tinteeŋ lɛ lɩma, aŋ bʋl, “Ma lɩɩ, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee la kala jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ joŋ ba munnuŋ ba fa sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ hɛ a hɛ gbansɩŋ lɛ a kɛŋ gɛnnɩŋ vɔɔ tɔ a joŋo baasɛ baasɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa wɩɩ-la arɩ ŋɩɩ Mosis fa sɩ bʋla pɩba. Ba sʋl gɛnnɩŋ, hɔpʋla arɩ sɛlɩmɛ kpɩɛraa Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa teeŋ.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA leŋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa lɛɛlɛ zizil Iziral tɩŋŋaa a joŋ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ pɩɛsaa chɛ a pɩba. Iziral tɩŋŋaa to ŋɩɩ lɛ a chʋŋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa dʋa kala viiri.

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɛŋ naasɩŋ lɛ nɛ a lɩɩ Ramesis sɩ hɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a mʋ Sʋkɔf. Ba baalaa dʋndʋŋa yi bʋɩ zɔɔ-balɩdʋ nɛ, ba haalaa arɩ ba biiriŋ bɩ pɛ.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Nɩwogusuŋ yʋga nɛ woruŋ a to ba harɩŋ a pɛ kɛsɛ ba pʋŋ-laalɩŋ: piesee, nɛsɩŋ arɩ bʋʋnaa.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ kiriba ba lɩɩ Ijipiti lɛ ŋɩɩ, ba bɩ chɩnɩŋ na dɩ ba ŋaa kʋdiilee. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba joŋ munnu-la ba sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ hɛ a ŋaa boroboro.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa tapʋlɩɩ nɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa hɔŋ a sɩ́ doŋ pɩŋ a liliisi ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ pɔba. Iziral tɩŋŋaa doho nɩaa maga dɩ baa ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ nɛ a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA Wɩa bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ, “Wombiee deemba nɛ ma jaŋ to a gbieli dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal gbiele. Nɩwogo kala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ pɛ dii.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Yomo kala ma sɩ yɔbɔ, dɩ ma nɛ keri ʋ peniŋ, ʋ jaŋ wuo dii gbiele-la kʋdiilee.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Nʋhʋɔra arɩ pachɩŋ diire-na bɩ kɩalɩŋ wuo dii.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Má dii kɩalɩŋ dɩa tʋɔŋ, má sɩ́ kaa kʋ lɩɩ dɩ-jalɩŋ, má sɩ́ nammɩa-la haŋgbelee ma dɩma yɛrɛ.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala nɛ maga dɩ ba gbieli gbiele deeŋ.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩwogo kala nɛ hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ aa chɛ dɩ ʋ pɛ gbieli mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal gbiele-la, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ keri baala-la kala sɩ hɛ ʋ dɩa lɛ penee nɛ, aŋ-na mʋ pɛ a nagɛ ʋ ma ŋaa Iziral tɩɩna nɛ. Nʋʋkala sɩ bɩ ʋ peniŋ kere bɩ jaŋ wuo dii mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal gbiele kʋdiilee.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Wombiee deemba nɛ maga Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ nɩwogusu-la kala sɩ hɛ ba tʋɔŋ tuto a mʋʋ tɩgɛ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal gbiele-la lɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ dagɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa nɛ La TƖƖNA kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa doho doho kala kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Dɩ Iziral tɩɩna kala nɛ lʋl ʋ hambolibii bumbuŋ, ʋ joŋo pɩmɛ, dɩ pʋna ma nɛ lʋl ʋ bii-bumbuŋ dɩ ʋ ŋaa bele, mɩ nɛ tɩɩʋ.”

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ kɛmma kaa mʋ Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa, Hiti tɩŋŋaa, Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa, Hivi tɩŋŋaa arɩ Jebus tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ, tintee-la sɩ sɩma a kɛŋ kɩaa, ʋ hɛ niiŋ pɩ ma naabalɩmaba arɩ ʋ jaŋ joŋo pɩma, ma jaŋ gbieli gbiele-la chɛnɛ-la tɩtɩa tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma jaŋ dii boroboro-la sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ. Tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ, má gbieli gbiele a zil La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Tapʋlaa deemba balɩpɛ ma jaŋ dii boroboro-la sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ, aŋ paala sɩ́ leŋe dɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ koo boroboro-la sɩ kɛŋ sɩbʋrʋŋ kpagɛ lee-la ma sɩ hɛ.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la má bʋla pɩ ma biiriŋ, ‘Laa gbieli gbiele deeŋ a tɩŋ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ ŋaa pɩla nɛ bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩ kɛnla kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Gbiele deeŋ jaŋ nagɛ magɩl ma nɩsaa lɛ, a nagɛ magɩl ma tilliŋ lɛ dɩ La TƖƖNA niiŋ wɩaa sɩ́ ma niiŋ lɛ lɛl. Ʋ doluŋ nɛ ʋ kaa kɛmma lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Má gbigbieli gbiele deeŋ bʋa deeŋ lɛ jɩna na-kala.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ kɛmma mʋ Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa tintee-la ʋ sɩ hɛ niiŋ pɩ ma naabalɩmaba arɩ ʋ jaŋ joŋo pɩma,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: má joŋ ma hambolibii bumbumba arɩ ma pʋsʋŋ ma kala bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Kakusuŋ bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ, má kɛŋ pie-pɔrɔɔ lenniba. Dɩ ma nɛ bɩ pie-biisiŋ kaa lenni, má mɩlɩmɛ ba baŋŋaa bori. Ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa hambolibii bumbumba maga dɩ ma mɩɩra time laaba.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Maachie dɩ ŋ bie nɛ pɩɛsɩŋ a chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa bʋbʋɔŋ, bʋla pʋ, ‘La TƖƖNA kɛŋ ʋ doluŋ nɛ a kɛnla lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, lee-la la fa sɩ hɛ a ŋaa yosi.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ fa sɩ pɩra ʋ bɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ leŋ la lɩɩ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA kpʋ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa hambolibii bumbumba arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ kala. Ŋ-la nɛ tɩɩ mɩ joŋ mɩ hambolibii bumbumba arɩ mɩ pʋsʋŋ ma kala bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA, ama mɩ hambolibii bumbumba-na mɩ yie time laa nɛ.’

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba saa jaŋ nagɛ magɩlɩŋ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ, a nagɛ magɩl ŋ tile lɛ arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ kɛnla lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ arɩ ʋ doluŋ.” Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩɩ chol mʋgʋ-balɩŋ

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩ ta Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba viiri, Wɩa bɩ ba kaa to wombii-kuu-la sɩ to Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ. Wɩa sɩ, “Dɩ ba nɛ mʋ cheŋ laalɩŋ wombiiŋ lɛ, ba jaŋ wuo bɩrɩmɛ ba tʋɔbɩɩnaa a mɩɩra mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa gollo to tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ a chaasɛ mʋgʋ-bal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mʋgʋ-fɩaŋ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ba laalɛ ba bayuori kɩaa nɛ.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Mosis pɛ paa Josɛf haŋgbelee arɩ Josɛf fa sɩ leŋe Iziral tɩŋŋaa hɛ niiŋ ŋɩɩ. Ʋ fa sɩ, “Wɩa sɛnɛ jaŋ kʋ laama ta. Dɩ ʋ nɛ kʋ laama ta, má pɛ paa mɩ haŋgbelee kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ sii lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sʋkɔf, ba mʋ hɔŋ Ɛtam lɛ nɛ a kpagɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaaŋ-la sɩ nagɛ jebiiŋ a laa ba sɩpaaŋ wɩɩhɛyɛ, arɩ jebii-la sɩ nagɛ nyiniŋ a laa ba sɩpaaŋ tɩtaŋɩŋ bɩ ba harɩŋ mɩɩra.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba mɩɩra mʋ hɔŋ a kpagɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Pɩ-Hahɩrɔf, a hɛ Mɩgɩdɔl arɩ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ pɛgɛ a chaasɛ Baal-Zɛfɔŋ.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro jaŋ bɩɩnɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛlɛ nɛ tintee-la lɛ aa baarɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ ŋaa dɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ, dɩ ʋ lɩɩ kiri ba harɩŋ. Mɩ yɩrɩŋ jaŋ yɩrɛ dɩ mɩ nɛ yuo dii Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala. Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ba TƖƖNA.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro sɩ nɩa arɩ Iziral tɩmma-la fá viiri nɛ, ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ tʋɔbɩɩnaa bɩrɩmɛ. Ba bʋl, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ la ŋaa ŋ-la a leŋ Iziral tɩmma-la sɩ tɩma pɩpɩla fá viiri?”

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA ŋaa Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ, ʋ kiri Iziral tɩŋŋaa harɩŋ, ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɩvɛŋ, ba bɔyɛ bɩ joŋ.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro ja-jɩllaa arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo janɩŋ torukoba kiri a mʋ puuba dɩ ba hɔŋ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ niiŋ, a kpagɛ Pɩ-Hasɩrɔf a chaasɛ Baal-Zɛfɔŋ.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo sɩ mʋʋ kpagɛba, Iziral tɩŋŋaa bee na dɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa nɛ kiri ba harɩŋ kʋkɔ. Fawʋllʋŋ chaasa kɛmba. Ba ŋmoo niiŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ pɛ ba lɛ.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa pɩɛsɛ Mosis, “A tɩŋ leriŋ sɩ tuo dɩ ba hugila Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ wɩaa nɛ tɩɩ ŋ kɛnla kaa kʋ lɩɩ tintee-hɩlɩŋ deeŋ tʋɔŋ dɩ la sʋʋ? Bɛɛ nɛ ŋ ŋaala ŋ-la?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: La bɩ bʋla pɩŋ arɩ ŋ lenla Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ la tɩma pɩpɩbaa? La sɩ jaŋ tɩma pɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa bɩ kpɩa la sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ ta tintee-hɩlɩŋ deeŋ tʋɔŋ?”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ, “Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛmma. Má nyɩrɛ bɔyɛ. Ma jaŋ na ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ jaŋ laama ta jɩnɩŋ. Ijipiti tɩmma-la ma sɩɩ na jɩnɩŋ, ma maachie bɩra bɩ jaŋ naba.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA jaŋ yuo laama, má-na bibeŋ Wɩa lɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ bunso pɩpɩmɛ? Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba vɩvɛŋ, ba sɩ́ chɩŋ.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Kɛŋ ŋ dantɩga-la je a zaarɛ mʋga-la nyuŋ, lɩɩ-la jaŋ pɔɩ balɩa, dɩ Iziral tɩmma-la vɛŋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ mʋga-la tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Ijipiti tɩmma-la tʋɔŋ pɩrɛ dɩ ba kire to ma harɩŋ jʋʋ mʋga-la tʋɔŋ. Nɩmɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ yuo dii Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo, ʋ janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ʋ ja-jɩllaa kala a laa yɩrɩŋ.

english_verse: The Egyptians will know for sure that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Dɩ mɩ nɛ yuo diiba, mɩ yɩrɩŋ jaŋ yɩrɛ, dɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ba TƖƖNA.”

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa tɩndaarʋ-la fa sɩ laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ mɩɩra bala chɩŋ ba harɩŋ, duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaaŋ-la ma fa sɩ nagɛ jebiiŋ ma lɩɩ ba sɩpaaŋ kʋ bala chɩŋ ba harɩŋ.

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: Ʋ kʋ chɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa pɛgɛ a kɛrɛ birimiŋ hɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa lɛ aŋ leŋ pʋlʋmʋŋ hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa leriŋ. Biriŋ-la sɩ hɛ ba pɛgɛ ŋɩɩ, ba kʋŋkala bɩ wuo mʋ kpagɛ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩtaŋ-la kala.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ dantɩga-la sɩ hɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ zaarɛ mʋga-la nyuŋ. La TƖƖNA leŋ pel-duoŋ lɩɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ a lu tɩtaŋ-la kala a ŋaa mʋga-la lɩɩŋ pɔɩ balɩa aŋ ka tintee-hɩlɩŋ.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɛŋ mʋga-la tʋɔŋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ, ka lɩɩ-la nagɛ jebiiŋ ba nadiiŋ arɩ ba nagʋa.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Sɩɩpʋʋraa, La TƖƖNA to duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaaŋ-la sɩ nagɛ jebiiŋ aŋ kɛŋ nyiniŋ lɛ, a na Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoroo a ŋaa ba wɩɩkala vʋgʋmɛ.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Aŋ ka ʋ ŋaa ba janɩŋ torukoba naasɩŋ yuŋ a bɩ wuo vɩvɛŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ijipiti tɩmma-la bʋl, “Má leŋ la fá, aŋ ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa. La TƖƖNA yuola a pɩpɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Kɛŋ ŋ dantɩga-la sɩ hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ tɩɛnɛ a zaarɛ mʋga-la nyuŋ, dɩ lɩɩŋ mɩɩra kʋ tɔ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa arɩ ba janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ba ja-jɩllaa lɛ.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ ʋ nɩsɩŋ zaarɛ mʋga-la lɛ. Chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla mʋga-la mɩɩra kʋ tɔ a nagɛ ʋ nagɩsɩŋ. Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa nɛrɩgɛ dɩ ba laa ba tɩtɩa a bɩ wuo lɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA leŋ lɩɩ-la pɛllɛ paaba.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Lɩɩ-la kʋ tɔ janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ja-jɩlla-la arɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro laalɩyuoroo kala fa sɩ to Iziral tɩmma-la harɩŋ jʋʋ mʋga-la. Ba nɩbala ma bɩ wuo lɩɩ.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Ama Iziral tɩŋŋaa wuo vɛŋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ nɛ mʋga-la tʋɔŋ, aŋ ka lɩɩŋ nagɛ jebiiŋ ba nadiiŋ arɩ ba nagʋa kala.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ La TƖƖNA laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ba na Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa kʋsʋʋnʋŋ sɩ pɩŋ mʋga-la niiŋ kala.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ na tɩntɩŋ-duoru-la La TƖƖNA sɩ tɩma Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa lɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ laa Wɩa arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnna Mosis wɩaa dii.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ deeŋ a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA: “Mɩ jaŋ yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ leŋ ʋ yɩrɩŋ faasa yɩrɛ nɛ. Ʋ yuo dii janɩŋ arɩ ba jɩjɩllaa a jomba yuo hɛ mʋga lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA nɛ ŋaa mɩ doluŋ, mɩ jaŋ yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ aa dagɛ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa. Ʋ nɛ ŋaa mɩ Laataara. Ʋ nɛ ŋaa mɩ Wɩa, mɩ jaŋ dɛnnʋ. Ʋ nɛ ŋaa mɩ nyɩmma Wɩa, mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ʋ yɩrɩŋ yɩrɛ.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA ŋaa bayuoru nɛ, ʋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Ʋ joŋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo yuo hɛ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ lɛ nɛ. Ijipiti kuoro laalɩyuori-kpaŋkpamba kala jʋʋ Mʋgʋ-fɩaŋ.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Lɩɩ-luŋii-la tɔba nɛ, ba tuu lɩɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ a nagɛ tabɩɩŋ.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA, ŋ naduo-la kɛŋ doluŋ woruŋ, ʋ nɛ ŋ kaa ŋmoo ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ pɩsɛ.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Ŋ doluŋ yʋga, ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ yuo dii nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ŋ niiŋ sɛyɛ. Ŋ leŋe ŋ baanɩŋ guu sii nɛ, a diiba a nagɛ nyiniŋ sɩ dii ya-yʋalaa.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Ŋ mɩɩ-boiŋ peliŋ nɛ yigi lɩɩŋ mʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ, ʋ sii chɩŋ a nagɛ kɛrɛ, ka fuo-luŋii-la tʋɔŋ kala hɩl.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ bigisi ba tɩtɩa lɛ a bʋl, ‘La jaŋ kire kɛmba a kpʋba arɩ tokobiee aŋ laa kɩalɩŋ kala la sɩɩ chɛ ba dʋa tʋɔŋ.’

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ŋ wiese hɛ ba lɛ nɛ, mʋgʋ-balɩŋ tɔ ba kala, ba tuu lɩɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ a nagɛ hɔɔ-yuŋuŋ sɩ tuu lɩɩ-balɩŋ.

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Ŋ dagɛba ŋ doluŋ nɛ, tinteeŋ paaba liŋ.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Ŋ chonuŋ sɩ bɩ dɛrɛ wɩaa ŋ jaŋ laa nɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ laata sɩpaaŋ. Ŋ dol-la nɛ ŋ jaŋ kaa kɛmba hɛ ŋ dɩɩ-zɔmʋŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Fawʋllʋŋ jaŋ kɛŋ Ɛdɔm tinteeŋ kuoroo, dɩ Mʋab tinteeŋ babiibalaa ma chichel, dɩ Kɛnaŋ tinteeŋ nɩaa nandaasɩŋ kala yʋɔrɛ.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Fawʋllʋŋ jaŋ chaasa jʋʋba dɩ ba chichel. Ŋ doluŋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ba chɩŋ jim a nagɛ bʋŋ, ka ŋ nɩaa kʋ bal, nɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ laa ta.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Ŋ jaŋ kɛmba jɩla hɛ ŋ peeliŋ nyuŋ, ŋ tɩtɩa dɩhɔnʋŋ, lee-la ŋ sɩ sɩ ŋ jaŋ joŋo pɩba, lee-la ŋ sɩ saa pɩ ŋ tɩtɩa a jʋjʋʋ.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA jaŋ dii kuoruŋ a kaa mʋ wuu.”

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɛŋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ nɛ a lɩɩ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ tʋɔŋ, ama Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro janɩŋ arɩ ʋ janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ja-jɩllaa sɩ mʋ jʋʋ mʋga-la, La TƖƖNA leŋe lɩɩŋ mɩɩra kʋ tɔba nɛ.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Mɩrɩam fa ŋaa Arɔŋ dɩhaala nɛ, a ŋaa Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ. Ʋ sii a joŋ chɩnchɩga. Haalaa dɔnsʋŋ ma sii to ʋ harɩŋ a paa ba chɩnchɩgɩsɩŋ a gʋgʋa.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mɩrɩam ta yɩɩlɩŋ pɩba. Ʋ sɩ, “Má yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA, má leŋ dɩ ʋ yɩrɩŋ yɩrɛ woruŋ. Ʋ joŋ ja-jɩlla arɩ ʋ jaaba kala a yuo hɛ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ.”

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ba sii Mʋgʋ-fɩaŋ-la niiŋ. Ba mʋ jʋʋ Suu tintee-hɩlɩŋ. Ba vɛŋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ tapʋlaa batori aŋ bɩ lɩɩŋ na dɩ ba nyʋa.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kʋ yi lee kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Mara. Ba bɩ lɩɩ-la sɩ hɛ lee-la wuo nyʋa, bɛɛ wɩaa lɩɩ-la hɛyɛ nɛ.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ gʋgʋrɩmɛ wɩaa Mosis teeŋ, aa bʋl, “Nɩɩ nɛ la jaŋ na lɩɩŋ a nyʋa?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bunso pɩ La TƖƖNA. La TƖƖNA dagʋ daaŋ ʋ joŋo yuo hɛ lɩɩ-la lɛ ʋ zɔŋ arɩ nyʋanʋŋ. Nɩmɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA bil wombiee pɩba a magɩsɛba.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ, “Dɩ ma nɛ jaŋ jegile nɩɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩa niiŋ woruŋ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ, a to wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ dagɛma, mɩ bɩ jaŋ joŋ nyanyalɩa-la mɩ sɩ joŋo hɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa lɛ a hɛ ma lɛ. Mɩ nɛ ŋaa ma TƖƖNA, mɩ nɩɩ vaarɛ ma nyanyalaa.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sii Elim lɛ a mʋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Sɩŋ, a hɛ Elim arɩ Sɩnaɩ pɛgɛ. Ba sɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ chɛŋ-lɩa tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɔŋ harɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Ba sɩ hɛ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala gʋgʋrɩmɛ wɩaa Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ teeŋ.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ, “Dɩ la nɛ fa sʋba La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ nɛ kpɩa. Lee-la, la fa yie hɔŋ nɛ a chaŋ nammɩa aŋ dii kʋdiile-la kala la sɩɩ chɛ a vɔgɛ, aŋ ka lɛɛlɛ ma kɛnla kʋ lɩɩ tintee-hɩlɩŋ deeŋ lɛ dɩ la nɩ-daŋ deeŋ kala sʋʋ arɩ losuŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ kʋdiilee lɩɩ wɩa-nyuŋ kʋ tuu a pɩma a nagɛ duonuŋ sɩ yie lɩɩ wɩa-nyuŋ kʋʋ tuu ŋɩɩ. Tapʋlɩɩ na-kala nɩalɩŋ jaŋ lɩɩ paa ba sɩ jaŋ wuo dii magɛ ŋɩɩ. Mɩɩ chɛ dɩ mɩ magɩsɛba a na ba jaŋ to wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ dagɛba koo ba bɩ jaŋ to.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ kʋ yi tapʋl-dʋ chɛɛŋ, ba jaŋ lɩɩ paa kʋdiile-la a magɛ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ yie vɛnɛɛ paa naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩa.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala, “Jɩnɩŋ dɩdaanɩŋ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ kɛmma lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Chie chʋchʋɔŋ ma jaŋ na La TƖƖNA tʋla sɩ nagɛ ŋɩɩ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ nɩɩ ma sɩ gʋrɩmɛ wɩalɩŋ ʋ teeŋ nɛ. La ma nɛ kʋbɛɛba ma gʋgʋrɩmɛ wɩaa la teeŋ?”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bɩra bʋl, “Dɩdaanɩŋ deeŋ La TƖƖNA jaŋ pɩma nammɩa dɩ ma chaŋ. Chie chʋchʋɔŋ ʋ jaŋ pɩma kʋdiilee dɩ ma dii a vɔgɛ. Dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ kɛmma kaa kɔ daha. Ʋ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ ma sɩ gʋrʋma ʋ teeŋ nɛ. La ma nɛ kʋbɛɛba maa gʋrɩmɛ wɩaa la teeŋ? La TƖƖNA teeŋ nɛ maa gʋrɩmɛ.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ, “Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala, dɩ ba kɔ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩɩ gʋrʋmʋ nɛ.”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Arɔŋ sɩ bʋl wɩaa pɩpɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋɩɩ, ba beŋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ dɩɩrɩŋ, a na La TƖƖNA tʋla dɩ ʋ chaanɛ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “Mɩ nɩɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ gʋrɩmɛ wɩalɩŋ nɛ. Bʋla pɩba, ‘Jɩnɩŋ wɩɩ-mul-jʋʋlʋŋ ma jaŋ chaŋ nammɩa, chie chʋchʋɔŋ ma jaŋ dii kʋdiilee a vɔgɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ma TƖƖNA Wɩa.’ ”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ dɩdaanɩŋ, jɩmpɩrɩwɩɩba lɩɩ Wɩa-jaŋ kʋ tuu lee-la ba sɩ hɔnɔ kala, chʋchʋɔŋ nyalɩŋ nyala golli ba dɩhɔnʋŋ kala.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Nyal-la sɩ huoso dɛrɛ, kʋpʋl gulo gulo biisiŋ sɩ nagɛ nɩdɩma nantʋɔrʋŋ tɔ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la kala.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ na kɩaa deemba, ba pɩɛsɛ dɔŋɔ, “Bɛɛ kɩaa ma nɛ ŋ-la?” Bɛɛ wɩaa ba bɩ kɩalɩŋ jɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩba, “Kʋdiile-la La TƖƖNA sɩ joŋo pɩma dɩ ma dii nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Ŋ-la nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl, ‘Nʋʋkala paa magɛ ŋ dɩa nɩaa diiniŋ, dɩ ba kʋŋkala laa kuokuo gbaŋa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ.’ ”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ daga, dɔnsʋŋ paa yʋgɛ, dɔnsʋŋ ma paa muuri.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩba, “Nʋʋkala sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ŋ kɩaa chʋa.”

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Ama ba dɔnsʋŋ bɩ jegile nɩɩ Mosis sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ aŋ leŋ ba kɩaa chʋa. Taŋ ka pʋl dɩ nanchʋɔlaa jʋa, ba suomo sʋsʋɔrɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis na baanɩŋ ba nyuŋ.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Chʋchʋɔ na-kala nʋʋkala yie paa magɛ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ jaŋ dii nɛ. Dɩ wɩa nɛ kʋ haasɛ, kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ paa aŋ ka yie ŋmɩɛrɛ nɛ.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Tapʋl-dʋ chɛɛŋ ba paa kʋdiile-la ba sɩ yie vɛnɛɛ paa tapʋlɩɩ-kala a magɛ ŋɩɩ naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩa, nʋʋkala gbaŋ-bala. Iziral nɩhɩasɩŋ kʋ hɛ duoso pɩ Mosis.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩba, “Ŋ-la nɛ La TƖƖNA dagɛ: ‘Chie ŋaa tapʋl-wiesii nɛ a ŋaa La TƖƖNA tapʋl-zɔŋ. Nʋʋkala wasɛ kɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ jaŋ wasɛ jɩnɩŋ aŋ chɔ kɩalɩŋ ma ŋ sɩ jaŋ chɔ, aŋ joŋ kɩalɩŋ sɩ ka bil dɩ chie.’ ”

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba joŋ kʋdiile-la kʋkaanaa bil arɩ Mosis sɩ dagɛba ŋɩɩ, taŋ pʋl dɩ kʋdiile-la bɩ pʋa, nanchʋɔlaa ma bɩ jʋa.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Má dii kʋdiile-la ma sɩ kɛnɛ jɩnɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa jɩnɩŋ ŋaa tapʋl-wiesii nɛ a pɩ La TƖƖNA, ma bɩ jaŋ na kʋdiilii kala tintee-la lɛ jɩnɩŋ.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Tapʋlaa balɩdʋ pɛgɛ ma jaŋ paa kʋdiilee, tapʋl-pɛɩ-chɛɛŋ ŋaa la chɛ-wiesiŋ nɛ, ma bɩ jaŋ na kʋdiilii kala tapʋlɩɩ-la.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Tapʋl-pɛɩ-la chɛɛŋ nɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ vɩa aŋ lɩɩ dɩ ba paa kʋdiile-la a bɩ kʋŋkala na.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA pɩɛsɛ Mosis, “Ɛɛ nɛ maa chɛ dɩ ma diene magɛ aŋ-na to wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile pɩma arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ dagɛma dɩ ma to?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Má bee na, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA joŋ tapʋl-pɛɩ-la pɩma dɩ ʋ ŋaa ma chɛ-wiesii nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ joŋ tapʋlaa balɩa kʋdiilee pɩma tapʋl-dʋ chɛɛŋ. Nʋʋkala maga dɩ ʋ hɛ dɩa lɛ nɛ tapʋl-pɛɩ-la chɛɛŋ. Nʋʋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ lɩɩ ʋ dɩa lɛ.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nʋʋkala wiesi tapʋl-pɛɩ-la chɛɛŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala kɛŋ kʋdiile-la yɩyɩrɛ ‘mana’. Ʋ ŋaa kʋpʋla nɛ a nagɛ sɛrɛɛ-biee, aŋ ŋaa lɛnlɛŋ a nagɛ munuŋ ba sɩ joŋ tʋʋŋ hɛ a wasɛ.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Ŋ-la nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl, ‘Má magɩsɛ kʋdiile-la gbaŋa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a bil ma doho nɩaa lɛ, dɩ ba wuo sii na kʋdiile-la mɩ fa sɩ joŋo pɩma tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ, bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩ kɛmma kaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ, “Joŋ taga a magɩsɛ ‘mana’ gbaŋa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ hɛ a joŋo bil La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ dɩ la doho nɩaa sii na.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ pɩ Mosis, Mosis leŋ Arɔŋ joŋ taga a magɩsɛ ‘mana-la’ hɛ a joŋo bil Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la sɩpaaŋ dɩ ʋ wuo chɩŋ nɩmɛ dɩ nʋʋkala sɩ́ digu.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala lɩɩ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩŋ a vɛŋ aŋ pɛ hɔnɔ wiesi ŋɩɩ halɩɩ arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ dagɛba ŋɩɩ. Ba mʋ hɔŋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Refidim lɛ, ama lɩɩŋ fa tuo lee-la dɩ nɩalɩŋ nyʋa.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba ŋaa goŋ Mosis teeŋ a bʋl, “Pɩla lɩɩŋ dɩ la nyʋa.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋl, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma ŋɩŋaa goŋ mɩ nyuŋ? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ maa magɩsɛ La TƖƖNA?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Lɩɩ-nyʋasʋŋ sɩ faasa kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ ŋɩɩ, ba ha gʋgʋrɩmɛ wɩaa Mosis teeŋ. Ba sɩ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ kɛnla kaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, dɩ ŋ leŋ lɩɩnyʋasʋŋ kpʋ la dɩ la biiriŋ arɩ la pʋsʋŋ kala dɩ la sʋʋ?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bunso pɩ La TƖƖNA a bʋl, “Bɛɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa pɩ nɩaa deemba? Ba paala ŋaa siri nɛ dɩ ba yagɛmɛ kpʋ arɩ tabɩaa.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Sii laa nɩalɩŋ sɩpaaŋ mʋ a pɛ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋhɩasɩŋ a joŋ ŋ dantɩga-la ŋ sɩ kaa ŋmoo Naayɩl fuo-la a kori.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ gbɛrɩŋ peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩnaɩ bʋŋ-la bʋbʋɔŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋmoo bʋŋ-la arɩ ŋ dantɩga-la, lɩɩŋ jaŋ kʋ lɩɩ dɩ nɩalɩŋ nyʋa.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis ŋaa ŋɩɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋhɩasɩŋ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Ʋ hɛ lee-la yɩrɩŋ Masa arɩ Mɛrɩba a tɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ ŋaa goŋ-la a magɩsɛ La TƖƖNA a bʋl, “La TƖƖNA hɛ la teeŋ nɛ koo ʋ tuo nɛ?” Ba yuo dii Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa sii kɔ dɩ ba yuo Iziral tɩŋŋaa Refidim lɛ.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Josua, “Tʋɔsɛ baala-la dɔnsʋŋ dɩ ma mʋ yuo Amalɛk tɩmma-la. Mɩ chie jaŋ chɩŋ peeliŋ nyuŋ a kori Wɩa dantɩga-la.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Josua ŋaa ŋɩɩ Mosis sɩ dagʋ ba yuo Amalɛk tɩmma-la, ka Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ arɩ Huu jɩl peel-la nyuŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Mosis kɛŋ ʋ nɩsaa je. Ʋ sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo didii Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa, ama dɩ Mosis nɩsaa nɛ kʋ tuu, Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa ma yie yuo didiiba nɛ.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Mosis nɩsaa sɩ kʋ yʋɔrɛ, ba joŋ tabɩɩŋ bil, ʋ hɔŋ ʋ nyuŋ. Ka Arɔŋ arɩ Huu kɛŋ Mosis nɩsaa je, Arɔŋ chɩŋ sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ, Huu ma chɩŋ sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ. Ba kɛŋ Mosis nɩsaa je a chɩŋ ŋɩɩ halɩɩ wɩa tuu jʋʋ.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Josua arɩ ʋ nɩaa yuo dii Amalɛk tɩmma-la.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Ŋmʋnsɛ wɩɩŋ deeŋ hɛ teniŋ tʋɔŋ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ ma sɩ jaŋ vɛnɛɛ liisi a leŋ dɩ Josua nɩɩʋ, arɩ mɩ jaŋ chei Amalɛk dɩ ʋ yɩrɩŋ lɛl dʋnɩa kala lɛ.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis saa Wɩɩsʋllɩ koruŋ a hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ, ‘La TƖƖNA nɛ ŋaa mɩ jɔnjɔŋ ’.

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ, “Mɩ joŋ mɩ yɩɛlaa hɛ La TƖƖNA lɛ nɛ. Ʋ jaŋ yuyuo Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa doho na-kala a kaa mʋ wuu.”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Mosis hɩɩlɩ-baala fa ŋaa ba bʋla pʋ, “Mɩɩ kɔ ŋ teeŋ nɛ, mɩ dɩ ŋ haala arɩ ŋ biiriŋ balɩa.”

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis lɩɩ cheŋ ʋ hɩɩlɩ-baala a tuu kpirimi aŋ guoru, ba chʋɔlɛ dɔŋɔ aŋ jʋʋ lɛbɩŋ.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Mosis bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ ŋaa Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa kala lɛ a tɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa wɩaa a pɩ ʋ hɩɩlɩ-baala. Ʋ bɩra dagɛ hɛɛ-la kala ba sɩ na wombiiŋ lɛ arɩ ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ laaba ta.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ mɩ jɩma arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ kɩɩ vesiŋ kala, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta nɛ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ, nɩalɩŋ fa sɩɩ ŋaa sɩɩ-jʋʋ wɩaa ba lɛ.”

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis hɩɩlɩ-baala Jeturo kɛŋ kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ kɩaa dɔnsʋŋ kɔ dɩ ʋ pɩ Wɩa. Arɔŋ arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋhɩasɩŋ kala kɔ Mosis hɩɩlɩ-baala teeŋ, ba kala dii kɩaa Wɩa sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Ŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ kala jaŋ lɔlɔ ta pɛɩ, tɩntɩmɩɩ-la yʋga, ʋ kɩɩ ŋ dʋndʋŋa tɩmɩŋ nɛ.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, Mosis sii hɔŋ dɩ ʋ laa nɩalɩŋ wɩaa jɩma pɩba. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba chɩna gollu a lɩɩ chʋchʋɔŋ a kaa mʋ dɩdaanɩŋ.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Mosis hɩɩlɩ-baala sɩ na wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ ŋaa pɩ nɩalɩŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ sɩ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ wɩɩ nɛ ŋ ŋaa pɩpɩ ŋ nɩaa ŋ-la? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ dʋndʋŋa laa nɩalɩŋ kala wɩaa a jɩjɩŋ, ka ba kala chɩna golluŋ a lɩɩ chʋchʋɔŋ a kaa mʋ dɩdaanɩŋ?”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pʋ, “Ba kɔ mɩ teeŋ dɩ mɩ dagɛba wɩɩ-la Wɩa sɩɩ chɛ nɛ.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Bʋa na-kala lɛ dɩ ba nɛ kɛŋ kaalɛrɛ, ba yie kaa kɔ mɩ teeŋ nɛ mɩ jɩma pɩba, aŋ dagɛba Wɩa wombie-la arɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ daga.”

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis hɩɩlɩ-baala sɩ, “Wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa, ʋ bʋa lɛ dee ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ dɩ mɩ dagɩŋ wɩɩ, Wɩa jaŋ pɛ ŋ lɛ. Ʋ maga dɩ ŋ nɛ chɩŋ nɩalɩŋ arɩ Wɩa pɛgɛ a laa ba wɩaa kaa mʋ Wɩa sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Dagɛba Wɩa wombie-la arɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ daga. Dagɛba ŋɩɩ ba sɩ maga dɩ baa ŋaa wɩaa, arɩ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ maga dɩ baa tɩŋ ba tɩntɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: Leŋ dɩ nɩaa deemba nɛ laa nɩalɩŋ wɩaa jɩma pɩpɩba bʋa na-kala lɛ, ka wɩalɩŋ sɩ dolie, dɩ ba kaa kɔ ŋ teeŋ, ama wʋbiisi-la na-kala maga dɩ ba bʋlba nɛ ba tɩtɩa lɛ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, wɩalɩŋ bɩra bɩ jaŋ daŋ ŋ dʋndʋŋa nyuŋ.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ dɩ Wɩa sɛɩ, ŋ bɩ jaŋ lɔl ŋ tɩtɩa, ŋ jaŋ wuo wasɛ nɩalɩŋ wɩaa kala pɩba dɩ ba mʋ ba dɩɩsɩŋ arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ.”

english_verse: He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of
translation_verse: Ʋ tʋɔsɛ baalaa sɩ kaasa Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala tʋɔŋ, a leŋ ba ŋaa nɩalɩŋ sɩpaalaaraa, dɔnsʋŋ bibeŋ nɩaa bʋɩba, dɔnsʋŋ zɔlɔba, dɔnsʋŋ mahɩŋ balɩa arɩ fiiba, dɔnsʋŋ ma fiiba.

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Ba laa nɩalɩŋ wɩaa jɩma pɩpɩba bʋa na-kala lɛ. Wɩalɩŋ sɩ dolie kɩɩba, ba yie kaa mʋ Mosis teeŋ nɛ, ama wʋbiisi-la na-kala ba yie jɩmba nɛ ba tɩtɩa lɛ.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ ʋ hɩɩlɩ-baala Jeturo lɩɩ hɛ wombiiŋ lɛ ʋ mʋ ʋ jaŋ.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis jɩl peel-la nyuŋ dɩ ʋ cheŋ Wɩa. La TƖƖNA yɩrʋ peel-la nyuŋ a bʋl, “Ŋ-la nɛ ŋ jaŋ bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Jekɔb doho nɩaa:

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: ‘Ma tɩtɩa na wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ ŋaa Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa lɛ nɛ, arɩ ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ pɔma a nagɛ kachuuŋ sɩ kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ tɔ ʋ biiriŋ a kɛmma kaa kʋ lɩɩ.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ dɩ ma nɛ jaŋ to mɩ niiŋ woruŋ a kɛŋ nii-la sɩ hɛ mɩ dɩ ma pɛgɛ tɩtɩŋ, dʋnɩa nɩaa kala tʋɔŋ, ma jaŋ ŋaa nɩa mɩ sɩ tɩɩ.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ jaŋ ŋaa tintee-la nɩaa sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ a laa nɩaa nyuŋ a tɩma pɩpɩmɛ.’ Wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ jaŋ bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis tuu yɩrɛ nɩalɩŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ kala hɛ dɔŋɔ a bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pʋ a pɩba.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ kala sɛɩ wɩalɩŋ a bʋl, “La jaŋ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis mʋ bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA wɩɩ-la ba sɩ bʋla.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mɩ jaŋ to duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaaŋ-bine tʋɔŋ a kɔ ma teeŋ. Nɩalɩŋ jaŋ nɩɩ dɩ mɩɩ bʋl wɩaa ŋ teeŋ. Dɩ ba nɛ nɩa dɩ mɩɩ bʋl wɩaa ŋ teeŋ, ba jaŋ laaŋ dii bʋa na-kala.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bɩra bʋl wɩɩ-la nɩalɩŋ sɩ bʋla a pɩ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mʋ́ pɩɩsɛ nɩalɩŋ disiniŋ ta jɩnɩŋ arɩ chie, a leŋ dɩ ba chɛsɛ ba gɛnnɩŋ.

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: Má ŋaa siri dɛrɛ chɛ-tori chɛɛŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa chɛɛ-la, mɩ jaŋ kʋ tuu Sɩnaɩ peel-la nyuŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ kala namɛ.

english_verse: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
translation_verse: Tuuri magɩlɩŋ golli peel-la aŋ bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ, dɩ ba pɔ ba sɩ́ magɩl-la kielu a kʋ jɩl peel-la nyuŋ koo ba paala sɩ́ ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ ma kʋ yi. Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ kʋ yi, ʋ maga dɩ ma kpʋʋ.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Dɩ nuhuobiiŋ nɛ koo dɩ pʋna nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ba jaŋ yagɩŋ arɩ tabɩaa koo tosuŋ a kpʋ. Nʋʋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ digu. Ba bɩ jaŋ kɛŋ nɩsaa ŋmobu. Ama dɩ ba nɛ faasa ŋmʋʋ pie-bel-nyile, má mʋ jɩl peel-la nyuŋ.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Mosis sɩ lɩɩ peel-la nyuŋ kʋ tuu nɩalɩŋ teeŋ, ʋ pɩɩsɛ ba disiniŋ ta ka ba chɛsɛ ba gɛnnɩŋ.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ, “Má kɛŋ ma tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ a gbɛrɛ tapʋlaa batori. A lɩɩ jɩnɩŋ a kaa mʋ tapʋlaa batori nʋʋkala pɔ ʋ sɩ́ haal pɩŋ.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Chɛ-tori-la chɛɛŋ chʋchʋɔŋ, taŋ lɩlɩgɩsɛ aŋ pɛ kpɩkpɩa. Duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaaŋ-bine kʋ tɔ peel-la, ka ba nɩɩ banyile sɩ faasa ŋmʋʋ. Nʋʋkala sɩ hɛ ba bugu-la-lɛ chel.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛmba lɩɩ ba bugu-la lɛ a mʋ Wɩa teeŋ peel-la bʋbʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩnaɩ kala tɔ arɩ nyʋɔsʋŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA kʋ tuu ʋ nyuŋ nɛ a nagɛ nyiniŋ, nyʋɔsʋŋ sii jɩjɩl wɩa-nyuŋ dugugu. Peel-la kala faasa zigili.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ faasa ŋmʋʋ banyile-la, Mosis bʋl wɩaa, ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa kpɩa bʋl wɩaa pʋ.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA kʋ tuu Sɩnaɩ peel-la nyuŋ aŋ yɩrɛ Mosis dɩ ʋ kʋ jɩl peel-la nyuŋ, ʋ jɩl.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Tuu bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ dɩ ba pʋpɔ dɩ ba sɩ́ daha kʋ jɩl, a chɩchɛ dɩ ba namɛ. Dɩ ba nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ba jesiŋ jaŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa ma tɩtɩa maga dɩ ba pɩɩsɛ ba disiniŋ ta nɛ aŋ-na kɔ mɩ sɩpaaŋ, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA jaŋ dɔgɩsɛba.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA, “Nɩalɩŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo kʋ jɩl Sɩnaɩ Peeliŋ deeŋ nyuŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ bʋla pɩla arɩ la tuuri magɩlɩŋ a golli peel-la dɩ ʋ ŋaa ŋ-na Wɩa lee.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Tuu kɛŋ Arɔŋ dɩ ma kɔ, ama Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa dɔnsʋŋ arɩ nɩkaana-la sɩ́ fʋgʋsa kʋ jɩl mɩ teeŋ, dɩ ba nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛba.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis tuu bʋl wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pʋ a pɩba.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bʋl wɩaa deemba,

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ chɩŋ dɩ-bolii, ka Mosis mʋ yi biriŋ lim-la tʋɔŋ Wɩa sɩ hɛ. Vesiŋ arɩ korunuŋ

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Mɩ-na nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa. Mɩ nɛ kɛmma kaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, lee-la ma fa sɩ hɛ a ŋaa yosi.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: Ma bɩ maga dɩ ma kɛŋ wɩa kala a pɛ mɩ-na Wɩa lɛ.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: Ma pɔ má sɩ́ tɔŋ kala mɛ a pɩ ma tɩtɩa dɩ ʋ nagɛ wɩa-nyuŋ kʋŋ, koo tinteeŋ nyuŋ kʋŋ, koo lɩɩŋ tʋɔŋ kʋŋ.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: Ama nɩalɩŋ sɩ chomi a tuto mɩ niiriŋ, mɩ jaŋ dagɛ mɩ chonuŋ a pɩba arɩ ba biiriŋ arɩ ba nihee arɩ ba nihi-lɩɛrɛba a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: Ma pɔ má sɩ́ mɩ yɩrɩŋ yɩrʋ pɛɩ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩa jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ nɩɩ-la kala sɩ yɩrɛ mɩ yɩrɩŋ pɛɩ.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: Máa liisi chɛ-wiesii-la wɩaa dɩ ʋ ŋaa tapʋl-zɔŋ a pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Má tɩŋ ma tɩntɩŋŋaa tapʋlaa balɩdʋ pɛgɛ.

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: Ama tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ ŋaa chɛ-wiesii nɛ a pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA. Má sɩ́ tɩntɩmɩɩ kala tɩŋ, ma biiriŋ, ma nʋhʋɔraa, ma pʋsʋŋ arɩ ma dɩa tɩntɩnnaa kala, baalaa arɩ haalaa.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Tapʋlaa balɩdʋ nɛ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA joŋo ŋaa wɩa-nyuŋ arɩ tinteeŋ, mʋgʋ-balaa arɩ kɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ ba lɛ, tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ nɛ mɩ wiesi. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ joŋ chɛ-wiesiŋ deeŋ a wasʋ, a leŋ ʋ ŋaa tapʋl-zɔŋ.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: Má zizil ma naamba arɩ ma nyɩmmaba, dɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA leŋ dɩ ma mɩɩsɩŋ duomi tintee-la lɛ mɩ sɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩma.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ nʋʋ haal chɛ.

english_verse: Do not steal.
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ gaa.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Má pɔ dɩ ma sɩ́ ma dɔnsʋŋ tɩŋŋaa kɩaa hɩɛnʋ: ba dɩɩsɩŋ, ba haalaa, ba dɩa tɩntɩnnaa baalaa koo haalaa, ba nɛsɩŋ koo ba kakusuŋ, koo kʋŋ na-kala ba sɩ kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Má pʋpɔ ma sɩ́ vene kala ŋaa a pɛ mɩ lɛ. Má pʋpɔ ma sɩ́ sɛlɩmɛ koo hɔpʋla kaa libi vene kala aa zilu.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩ na dɩ taŋ lɩgɩsa aŋ kpɩa a nɩɩ ba sɩ ŋmʋʋ nyile a na peel-la sɩ tɔ nyʋɔsʋŋ, fawʋllʋŋ kɛmba ba chichel. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba sʋʋsa mʋ chɩŋ dɩ-bolii,

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: aŋ bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Ŋ tɩtɩa bʋl wɩaa pɩpɩla, la jaŋ jegile nɩɩ. Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ Wɩa nɛ bʋla pɩla, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, la jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩba, “Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛmma, Wɩa kɔ dɩ ʋ magɩsɛma a na nɛ dɩ ma fɩfáʋ a sɩ́ wʋbɔŋ wɩaa ŋaa.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa: Ma tɩtɩa na mɩ sɩ lɩɩ wɩa-nyuŋ kʋ tuu bʋl wɩaa pɩma ŋɩɩ nɛ.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: Má kɛŋ tɩɛrɩŋ saa Wɩɩsʋllɩ koruŋ pɩmɛ. Nɩmɛ nɛ ma jaŋ kɛŋ ma piesee, bʋʋnaa arɩ ma nɛsɩŋ kʋ ŋaa ma kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ ma nii-magɛ dɔŋɔ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩmɛ. Lee na-kala mɩ sɩ dagɛma dɩ ma dɩdɛnnɛmɛ, mɩ jaŋ kɔ lee-la a pɛ ma lɛ.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɩɩ chɛ dɩ ma kɛŋ tabɩaa saa Wɩɩsʋllɩ koruŋ pɩmɛ, má sɩ́ tabɩa-la wasa ta. Dɩ ma nɛ kɛŋ ma tɩntɩnnɩ kʋŋkala chɩchɛ dɩ ma wasɛba, maa birisiba nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: And don't build an altar that requires steps; you might expose yourself when you climb up.
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ lusuŋ-choluŋ hɛ a to jɩjɩl koru-la, dɩ ma nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ma jaŋ kɛŋ ma yarɩ-biree nyɩɩsɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala nɛ ŋmoo ʋ nyɩmma koo ʋ naaŋ, ʋ maga má kpʋʋ nɛ.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩaa nɛ yuo dɔŋɔ, dɩ dɔŋɔ bolimi dɔŋɔ arɩ nɩsɩŋ koo tabɩɩŋ, dɩ ʋ kaa pɩŋ dɩa lɛ,

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: Wombiee deemba nɛ ŋ jaŋ daga pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba tuto: Hiburu tɩŋŋaa sɩ ŋaa yosuŋ

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ yɔɔ yoŋ-baal dɩ ʋ ŋaa Hiburu tɩɩna, ʋ maga dɩ yomo-la tɩma pɩ tɩɩna jɩsɩŋ balɩdʋ nɛ. Jɩ-pɛmɩŋ lɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ joŋ yomo-la ta. Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ yomo-la tiŋ kʋŋkala aŋ laa ʋ tɩtɩa.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ pɛ kɛŋ haala kɔ bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ yɔbʋ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ pɛ kɛŋ ʋ haala viiri, ka dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ haala kɛnɛ, ʋ dʋndʋŋa maga dɩ ʋ mʋ.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ yɔbʋ nɛ jaa haala pʋ dɩ ʋ kaa lʋl biiriŋ, dɩ yomo-la nɩɩ viiru, ʋ tɩɩna nɛ jaŋ tɩɩ haal-la arɩ biiriŋ. Yomo-la dʋndʋŋa nɛ jaŋ viiri.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ yomo-la nɛ sɩ, ‘Mɩ cho nɩɩ-la sɩ yɔɔmɛ nɛ, arɩ mɩ haala arɩ mɩ biiriŋ, mɩ bɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ jommi ta,’

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: ŋɩɩ-na nɩɩ-la sɩ yɔbʋ maga dɩ ʋ kɛnʋ kaa mʋ sarɩya diiree leriŋ. Ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ ʋ dɩgɩlɩŋ mɛrɛ boro lɛ, aŋ tɔ luri arɩ luro, ka dɩ ʋ ŋaa ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ a kaa mʋ wuu see ʋ sɩ sʋba.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kɛŋ ʋ tolo a yallɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa yomo, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba joŋ tolo-la ta arɩ ba sɩ yie joŋ yoŋ-baala ta ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ yɔbʋ nɛ faa chɛ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ tolo-la ŋaa ʋ haala aŋ bɩra bɩ tolo-la cho, ʋ maga dɩ tolo-la nyɩmma time laa ʋ tolo, bɛɛ wɩaa nɩɩ-la sɩ yɔbʋ nyɩsɛ tolo-la nɛ. Ʋ bɩ wombiiŋ kɛnɛ dɩ ʋ joŋu yalla pɩ nʋʋ sɩ bɩ Iziral tɩɩna ŋaa.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ joŋ tolo-la pɩ ʋ nanʋala dɩ ʋ ŋaa ʋ haal, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ kɛnʋ a nagɛ ʋ tolo nɛ.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ tɩtɩa ma nɛ jaa tolo aŋ bɩra jaa haal dɔŋ a pɛ, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ʋ keri ʋ ha-bumbuŋ-la sɩ ŋaa yomo kʋdiilee, ʋ gɛnnɩŋ arɩ ʋ bɔsɔ jʋʋnʋŋ ta.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ wɩaa deemba batori wuo ŋaa pɩpɩ haal-la, haal-la jaŋ wuo viiri. Dɩ ʋ nɩɩ viiru, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ kʋŋkala. Wɩɩ-la sɩ maga ba joŋo ŋaa nʋʋ lɛ dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ nʋʋ nɛ bɩ sɛnɛ aŋ kpʋ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna, ka dɩ Wɩa nɛ daga, leriŋ hɛ nɩmɛ ʋ sɩ jaŋ fá mʋ yuori.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ nʋʋ nɛ sɛnɛ aŋ kpʋ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna, dɩ tɩɩna nɛ paala fá mʋ yuori mɩ koru-la ma, ʋ maga dɩ ba lɛrʋ lɩɩ a kpʋʋ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala nɛ gaa nʋʋ yallɛ, koo dɩ ʋ ha hɛ tɩɩna teeŋ nɛ, dɩ ba kɛnʋ, ʋ maga ma kpʋʋ nɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala nɛ ŋmɩɛsa hɛ ʋ nyɩmma koo ʋ naaŋ lɛ, ʋ maga dɩ má kpʋʋ nɛ.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: dɩ nɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ bolimo nɛ bɩ sʋba, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ma ŋaa nɩɩ-la sɩ bolimu wɩɩkala. Ʋ wɩɩŋ nɛ dɩ ʋ tiŋ chɩŋ-la kala tɩɩna sɩ ŋmobo a beŋ ʋ tɩtɩa a duori.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ŋmoo ʋ yoŋ-baala koo yoŋ-haala arɩ daaŋ dɩ ʋ sʋʋ, ʋ maga dɩ má dɔgʋsʋ nɛ.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ yomo-la nɛ bɩ sʋba tapʋlɩɩ-la, koo tapʋlaa balɩa pɛgɛ, yomo-la tɩɩna bɩ chɩŋ kala kɛnɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ nɛ tɩɩʋ.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩaa balɩa nɛ yuo dɔŋɔ a mʋ ŋmoo hapuugo dɩ ʋ chei ta, ka ʋ bɩ chaasa bolimi, nɩɩ-la sɩ yɩʋ jaŋ tiŋ chɩŋ-la kala haal-la bala sɩ daga, dɩ sarɩya diire nɛ sɛyɛ.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Ama dɩ haal-la nɛ chaasa bolimi a sʋʋ, tɩɩna ma maga dɩ ma kpʋʋ nɛ.

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ŋmoo ʋ yoŋ-baal koo yoŋ-haal sɩɩŋ yɛrɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ joŋ yomo-la ta ʋ viiri nɛ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩɩ-la wɩaa.

english_verse: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nyɩlɩŋ ma nɛ ʋ ŋmoo churi, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ joŋu ta ʋ viiri nɛ a tɩŋ ʋ nyɩl-la wɩaa.

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: Dɩ nɛ-bele nɛ yɩ nʋʋ dɩ ʋ sʋʋ, má yagɛ nɛŋ-la kpʋ arɩ tabɩaa. Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ma chaŋ ʋ nammɩa. Má sɩ́ nɛŋ-la tɩɩna wɩɩkala ŋaa.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ nɛŋ-la nɛ vɛnɛɛ joŋ nɩaa dɩ ba bʋbʋl nɛŋ-la tɩɩna teeŋ, ka ʋ vɩa dɩ ʋ beŋ ʋ nyuŋ aŋ leŋ nɛŋ-la ha jujoŋ nɩaa, dɩ ʋ nɛ kpʋ nʋʋ, ʋ maga ma yagɛ nɛŋ-la arɩ ʋ tɩɩna kala kpʋ arɩ tabɩaa.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Dɩ chɩmɩŋ ma nɛ ba kere pɩ nɛŋ-la tɩɩna, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ nɛ aŋ laa ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Dɩ nɛŋ-la kpʋ hantolibie nɛ koo hambolibie nɛ, ʋ maga ma ŋaa ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa mɩ sɩ daga nɛ.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ lu bʋa koo dɩ buotuoŋ nɛ ʋ kaa suro ta, dɩ nɛŋ koo kakumo foro tuu a sʋʋ,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: nɩɩ-la sɩ lu bʋa-la koo a suri buotuo-la ta, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ nɛŋ-la koo kakumo-la chɩmɩŋ nɛ aŋ joŋ.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛŋ nɛ yɩ ʋ dɔŋɔ nɛŋ dɩ ʋ sʋʋ, ʋ maga dɩ ba yallɛ nɛ-wei-la a joŋ moribie-la a pɛ nɛ-sʋʋ-la lɛ a kaa kpaa a magɛ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Dɩ ba nɛ jɩma dɩ nɛŋ-la vɛnɛɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ nɛ, ka ʋ tɩɩna vɩa ʋ kaa tɔ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ kɛŋ nɛ-wei-la tiŋ nɛ-sʋʋ-la chɩmɩŋ aŋ joŋ nɛ-sʋʋ-la.

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ gaa nɛŋ koo piesu a yallɛ koo a kpʋ, dɩ ma kɛnʋ, nɛŋ-la chɩmɩŋ jaŋ ŋaa nɛsɩŋ banɔŋ. Dɩ piese ma nɛ, ʋ chɩmɩŋ jaŋ ŋaa piesee banɛsɛ.

english_verse: But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double. If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
translation_verse: Dɩ gaarɩ kɩalɩŋ nɛ ba na ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ dɩ ba ha weye, dɩ nɛŋ nɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ nɛsɩŋ balɩa, dɩ kakumo nɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ balɩa, dɩ piese ma nɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ balɩa.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ leŋe dɩ ʋ pʋsʋŋ mʋ dii nʋʋ baga kɩaa, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ keri ʋ baga dɩ-zɔmʋŋ nɛ a tiŋ nɩɩ-la kɩaa pʋsʋ-la sɩ die.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ nyɩgɛ nyiniŋ dɩ ʋ mʋ dii nʋʋ baga kɩaa, dɩ tɩɩna ta bil nɛ koo dɩ ba chɩna nɛ, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ nɛ.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ sɛyɛ a laa ʋ dɔŋɔ moribiee koo chʋgʋsʋŋ bil, dɩ ba gaa kɩalɩŋ, dɩ ba nɛ kɛŋ gaarʋ-la, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ kɩalɩŋ naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩa.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: A mʋ tɩgɛ kʋlɛlɛɛ nɩaa sɩ kaa lɛrɛ wɩaa: nɛsɩŋ, kakusuŋ, piesee arɩ gɛnnɩŋ koo kʋŋkala lɛ, nɩalɩŋ balɩa maga dɩ ba kɛŋ wɩɩ-la mʋ sarɩya diiree leriŋ nɛ dɩ ba bʋl wɩɩ-la. Nɩɩ-la sɩ laa cheeriŋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ kʋ-la naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩa nɛ a pɩ nɩɩ-la kɩaa sɩ sɩma.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kɛŋ nɛŋ koo piesu koo kakumo koo pʋŋ doho na-kala mʋ pɩ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna dɩ ʋ laa ta, dɩ ʋ nɛ sʋba koo dɩ ʋ nɛ pɩra koo dɩ ba gaa kiri nɛ, ka ʋ bɩ pɛ-naarʋ kɛnɛ,

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: ba maga ba kɔ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ laa kʋ-la ta ŋmɩɛsɛ a lɩɩsɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ arɩ ʋ bɩ kʋ-la wɩaa jɩŋ, dɩ nɩɩ-la ma sɩ tɩɩ kʋ-la sɛɩ, a sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ʋ tiŋ kʋ-la chɩmɩŋ.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ tɩɩna sɩ laa pʋsʋ-la ta nɛ jɩŋ ba wɩaa, ʋ jaŋ time pɩ pʋsʋŋ tɩɩna.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Dɩ baga kʋŋ ma nɛ kɛŋ pʋna-la dii, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ kɛŋ kʋkaanɩŋ kʋ dagɛ pʋna tɩɩna nɛ. Dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ tiŋ chɩŋ-kala.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ chɩŋ nʋʋ pʋna, dɩ ʋ bolimi koo dɩ ʋ sʋba nɛ, ka tɩɩna teeŋ ʋ sɩ chɩma tuo, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ.

english_verse: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ama dɩ pʋna-la nɛ jʋʋ wɩɩ, ka nɩɩ-la teeŋ ʋ sɩ chɩma hɛ nɩmɛ, ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ time laa nʋʋ pʋna a kaa mʋ dɩ ŋ tɩŋ aŋ kaa kʋ pa, dɩ ʋ dʋa wɩɩ, ŋ bɩra bɩ kʋŋ tiŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ folo tiŋ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɩaa sɩ jaŋ hɔŋ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa dɔŋɔ lɛ

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kɛŋ hatolo sɩ bɩ baal jɩŋ pɩŋ, ka nʋʋ bɩ haal-la sʋga, nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛnʋ pɩŋ jaŋ tiŋ tolo-la jaarɩŋ aŋ jaaʋ.

english_verse: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nyɩmma nɛ bɩ sɛyɛ dɩ tolo-la jaa baal-la sɩ kɛnʋ pɩŋ, nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛnʋ pɩŋ ha maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ ʋ jaarɩŋ nɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: Dɩ haal kala nɛ ŋaa chichiribu, má kpʋʋ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ kɛŋ pʋna pɩŋ, má kpʋʋ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ kpaarɛ vene aŋ vɩa mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA, má kpʋʋ.

english_verse: Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ma pɔ má sɩ́ nɩwogusuŋ kaa ŋmoo gbɛɛŋ koo a dɔgɩsɛba. Má jɩŋ arɩ ma ma fa ŋaa nʋhʋɔra nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
translation_verse: Ma pɔ má sɩ́ yo-haalaa arɩ biisinsiŋ kaa ŋmoo gbɛɛŋ.

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ kɛmba ŋmoo gbɛɛŋ dɩ ba yelle pɩmɛ, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA jaŋ nɩɩ ba yele a pɛ ba lɛ.

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: Mɩ baanɩŋ jaŋ sii dɩ mɩ leŋ dɩ ba yuo kpʋma, ka ma haalaa arɩ ma biiriŋ ma ŋaa yo-haalaa arɩ biisinsiŋ.

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ laa ŋ naambie gɛrɩŋ a tɩŋ ŋ chɩmɩŋ sɩ hɛ ʋ teeŋ wɩaa, joŋ tɩɩna gɛrɩŋ pʋ ka dɩ wɩa-na jʋʋ,

english_verse: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
translation_verse: bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ gɛrɩ-bɔsɔ kala nɛ ŋɩɩ. Bɛɛ nɛ ʋ jaŋ piliŋ tɩtaŋɩŋ? Dɩ tɩɩna nɛ yele pɩmɛ, mɩ jaŋ nɩɩ ʋ yele, mɩ ŋaa Wɩa sɩɩ fá nɩaa nenige nɛ.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: Má pɔ dɩ ma sɩ́ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ bʋl a mʋ tɩgɛ mɩ-na Wɩa lɛ a sɩ́ kalɩba hɛ ma kuoroo lɛ.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: Má ŋaa ma kʋdiilee arɩ ma tɩɩnɛnɛɛ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩmɛ. Má joŋ ma hambolibii bumbumba ma pɩmɛ.

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: Ma nɛsɩŋ arɩ ma piesee ma, má joŋ ba bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ a pɩmɛ. Dɩ ba nɛ lʋla, má leŋ dɩ ba hɛ ba naamba teeŋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ. Tapʋl-chori chɛɛŋ, má joŋo pɩmɛ.

english_verse: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_verse: Ma ŋaa mɩ nɩaa sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ nɛ, nʋʋkala pɔ ʋ sɩ́ nammɩa gɩrɩŋ kʋŋ sɩ die aŋ ka chaŋ, má joŋo pɩ vasɩŋ.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩaa nɛ yʋga a ŋɩŋaa wɩɩ sɩ bɩ zɔŋ, sɩ́ ba lɛ pɛ. Dɩ ma nɛ mʋ sarɩya dɩ-diiliŋ dɩ nɩ-daŋ bʋbʋl wɩɩ, ka ba kɩaa bɩ sɩŋ, sɩ́ wʋtɩtɩɩ joŋo faa a tɩŋ nɩ-daŋ-la wɩaa.

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: Sɩ́ nʋʋ kɩaa sɩ bɩ sɩŋ lɛ pɛ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa summu wɩaa sarɩya dɩ-diiliŋ.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ dʋndɔmɔ kakumo koo ʋ nɛŋ nɛ lɛlɛ, dɩ ŋ naʋ, kɛŋ a kaa mʋ pʋ.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ dʋndɔmɔ kakumo nɛ tele a tɩŋ ʋ chʋgʋsʋŋ sɩ yuŋŋie wɩaa, sɩ́ kiele bal, mʋ pɛ a kɛnʋ chʋʋlɛ.

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: Sɩ́ summo harɩŋ lɩɩ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ bɩ kʋŋ kɛnɛ wɩaa sarɩya dɩ-diiliŋ.

english_verse: Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
translation_verse: Má pɔ ma sɩ́ wɩaa nyɩɛ pɩ nɩaa. Má pɔ dɩ ma sɩ́ nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ wɩɩ cheye kpʋ. Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ chei wɩɩ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ leŋu pɛɩ.

english_verse: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ nɩwogusuŋ dɔgʋsʋ. Má jɩŋ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ naga nɛ dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa nʋhʋɔrʋ. Ma ma fa ŋaa nɩwogusuŋ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Chɛ-wiesii-la wɩaa

english_verse: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
translation_verse: Jɩsɩŋ balɩdʋ tʋɔŋ má jaŋ duu kɩaa ma bagɩsɩŋ lɛ a ŋɩŋaa.

english_verse: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
translation_verse: Ama jɩ-pɛɩ-la lɛ, má sɩ́ kʋŋkala duu ma bagɩsɩŋ lɛ. Dɩ kʋŋ nɛ wasɛ nɩmɛ ma, má leŋe pɩ summoo arɩ baga kɩaa. Má sɩ́ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ arɩ kʋŋkala ŋaa ma bagɩsɩŋ lɛ.
