translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ dantɩgɩsɩ-la jʋʋ bil lɛbɩ-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ, La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: The next day when Moses went into the tent, flowers and almonds were already growing on Aaron's stick.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, Mosis jʋʋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la sɩ hɛ, dɩ Arɔŋ dantɩga sɩ ŋaa Levi doho nɩaa kʋa tɔsɔ a fɩɩlɛ, a nɛŋ fʋfʋlaa.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis paa dantɩgɩsɩ-la kala La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ a kaa kʋ lɩɩ dagɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ba na wɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa. Nʋʋkala joŋ ʋ kʋa.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mɩɩra kɛŋ Arɔŋ dantɩga jʋʋ bil mɩ niiriŋ daga-la sɩpaaŋ dɩ ʋ ŋaa magɩl a chɩchagɩlɛ Iziral tɩmma-la sɩ bɩ mɩ niiŋ ka sɛɩ, dɩ ba bɩra sɩ́ wɩaa gʋrʋmʋ dɩ ŋɩɩ leŋ dɩ ba sʋʋ.”

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Mosis ŋaa ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa La TƖƖNA sɩ dagʋ.

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Ŋɩɩ-na la lɛlɛ nɛ, la kala jaŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Dɩ la nɛ mʋ kpagɛ La TƖƖNA dɩ-zɔŋ-la la jaŋ sʋʋ-na, ŋɩɩ-na la kʋŋ bɩra bɩ ka.”

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Leŋ dɩ ŋ naambiiriŋ Levi doho nɩaa kʋ pɛ ŋ dɩ ŋ hambolibiisiŋ lɛ, dɩ ma tɩtɩŋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ tɩŋ tɩntɩmɩɩ-la ma sɩ dagɛba dɩ ba tɩŋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ, ama ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba digi mɩ tɩntɩnnɩ kʋzɔmɔ-la sɩ hɛ mɩ dɩ-zɔmʋŋ lɛ koo koru-la. Dɩ ba nɛ dige, mɩ jaŋ kpʋ ma kala.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa dʋndʋŋa nɛ maga dɩ ba pɛ ma lɛ dɩ ma tɩtɩŋ lɛbɩ-la tɩntɩŋŋaa, nʋʋ dɔŋ kala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ kʋ kpagɛ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Ŋ dɩ ŋ hambolibiisiŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ maga dɩ ma tɩtɩŋ mɩ dɩ-zɔŋ-la tɩntɩŋŋaa arɩ koru-la nyuŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa, dɩ mɩ bɩra sɩ́ baanɩŋ na Iziral tɩŋŋaa nyuŋ.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Mɩ nɛ lɩɩsɛ ŋ naambiiriŋ Levi doho nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ a dii zile pɩŋ. Mɩ lɩɩsɛba nɛ dɩ ba ŋaa mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA nɩaa, a tɩtɩŋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ŋ dɩ ŋ hambolibiisiŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ maga dɩ ma ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa, a tɩtɩŋ Wɩɩsʋllɩ koru-la nyuŋ arɩ mɩ dɩ-zɔŋ-la sɩpaaŋ lee-la zɔmʋŋ sɩ bɩ magɩa kɛnɛ tɩntɩŋŋaa. Mɩ joŋ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa tɩntɩŋŋaa dii zile pɩma nɛ. Dɩ nɩwogo dɔŋ kala nɛ kʋ kpagɛ mɩ dɩ-zɔŋ-la, ʋ maga dɩ ma kpʋʋ.” Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa kpaalɩŋ

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ tɩɩ ba nammɩa arɩ ma sɩ tɩɩ vaa-la arɩ nadiiŋ hui-la ba sɩ kaa je a zaarɛ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Má diiba dɩ-zɔŋ, ba ŋaa kɩaa sɩ chaasa bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ nɛ. Baal na-kala jaŋ wuo diiba. Má jomba dɩ ba ŋaa kɩaa sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ tɩɩ kɩaa deemba ma: Kʋŋ na-kala Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ kaa kʋ je a zaara sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩmɛ. Mɩ jomba pɩ ŋ dɩ ŋ hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ŋ toloo nɛ, ma toruŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ bʋa na-kala lɛ. Ŋ dɩa nʋʋkala sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ jaŋ wuo diiba.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ ha tɩɩ kɩaa deemba ma sɩ chaasa zɔŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ yie kaa kʋ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩmɛ: olif nʋʋŋ, tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ arɩ mɩaa ba sɩ yie kaa kʋ ŋaa kʋdii falaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Ba tinteeŋ kʋdii fala-la kala ba sɩ yie kaa kʋ sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA ŋaa ma kɩaa nɛ. Ŋ dɩa nʋʋ na-kala sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ jaŋ wuo diiba.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Kʋŋ na-kala Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ maga dɩ ba joŋ ʋ kala pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA, ma nɛ jaŋ tɩɩʋ.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Nuhuobiinee arɩ pʋsʋŋ kala bii-bumbumba-la ba sɩ joŋo pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA, ma nɛ tɩɩba, ama má leŋ dɩ ba time laa hambolibii bumbumba arɩ pʋsʋ-la sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ bii-bumbumba sɩ ŋaa belliŋ.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Dɩ bii-bumbumba-la nɛ yi chɛnɛ, ba jaŋ time laa arɩ warɩpʋla banɔŋ arɩ ba sɩɩ tiŋ ŋɩɩ Wɩa dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba time laa nɛ-bele, piese koo bʋʋna, ba ŋaa kʋzɔmɔ nɛ mɩ teeŋ. Kpʋ ba-na a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a laa ba chalɩŋ mɩsɛ mɩ koru-la, aŋ kʋɔrɛ ba nʋʋŋ a nyɩgɛ. Ba sʋɔra sɩma nɛ a pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kʋzɔmɔ-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ yie kaa kʋ pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA, ba jaŋ ŋaa ŋ dɩ ŋ hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ŋ toloo kpaalɩŋ. Ʋ jaŋ ŋaa nii a pɩŋ mɩ dɩŋ arɩ ŋ doho nɩaa pɛgɛ a kaa mʋ wuu.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Arɔŋ, “Ŋ bɩ toruŋ kɛnɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tintee-la lɛ, ŋ bɩ kpaal ma kɛnɛ ba dʋa tʋɔŋ, mɩ nɛ ŋaa ŋ kpaalɩŋ arɩ ŋ dʋa Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mɩ joŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ yie kɛŋ kɩaa kpaa leree fii a joŋ kʋbala-la pɩmɛ, a pɩ Levi doho nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ nɛ. Ba ma time nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa dʋndʋŋa nɛ jaŋ tɩtɩŋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa, a bibeŋ ʋ nyuŋ. Dɩ wɩɩkala nɛ bɩ woruŋ vɛnɛ nɩmɛ, ba nɛ jaŋ laa cheeriŋ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ jaŋ pɩŋ a pɩ ba dɩ ba doho kala, a kaa mʋ wuu. Ba bɩ jaŋ laa kpaalɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Bʋla pɩ Levi doho nɩaa, dɩ ba nɛ laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ yie kɛŋ ba kɩaa kpaa leree fii a joŋ kʋbala-la pɩmɛ, mɩ sɩ joŋo pɩba ʋ ŋaa ba kpaalɩŋ, ba ma bɩra kaa kpaa leree fii a joŋ kʋbala a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩmɛ.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Ba Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ deeŋ jaŋ nagɛ paara sɩ kɛŋ ʋ mɩɩ-falaa arɩ ʋ tɩɩ-nɛŋ-falaa sɩnɩŋ kʋ sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩmɛ.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩ Levi doho nɩaa, dɩ ba nɛ kɛŋ lere-la sɩ chaasa zɔŋ kɔ, ʋ jaŋ nagɛ ba sɩ yie kɛŋ mɩɩ-falaa arɩ tɩɩ-nɛŋ-falaa sɩnɩŋ kʋ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ba dɩ ba dɩa nɩaa jaŋ wuo dii kɩalɩŋ lee na-kala. Ba sɩɩ tɩŋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa ŋɩɩ, ba time nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Dɩ ba nɛ kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ lere-la sɩ chaasa zɔŋ kʋ pɩmɛ, ba bɩ cheeri kala kɛnɛ. Ʋ ŋɩɩ bɩ disiŋ ma kɛnɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ sɩ chaasa zɔŋ lɛ. Ba bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla dɩ ma ŋaa nɛ ŋ-la: Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba kɛŋ nɛ-pa-fɩaŋ sɩ bɩ nyɔɔ kala kɛnɛ kɔ, kʋ-la ba ha sɩ bɩ kaa tɩŋ aŋ ka.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Ma joŋo pɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Elieza, dɩ ʋ kaa lɩɩ ma dɩhɔnʋŋ lɛ a leŋ dɩ nʋʋ kpʋʋ ʋ sɩɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Elieza jaŋ kɛŋ ʋ neniiŋ, a tagɛ nɛŋ-la chalɩŋ a mɩsɛ lɛbɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ sɩpaaŋ naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩpɛ.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Elieza jaŋ bibeŋ, ka dɩ ba nyɩgɛ nɛ-paha-la teniŋ, ʋ nammɩa, ʋ chalɩŋ arɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ kɩaa kala.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara jaŋ joŋ kuolu daaŋ arɩ kaku-dɩgɩlɩŋ arɩ ŋmɛŋ-fɩaŋ a yuo hɛ nyiŋ-la lɛ ba sɩ nyɩgɛ nɛ-paha-la.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ lɛ, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara jaŋ chɛsɛ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ a fo lɩɩŋ, aŋ-na mɩɩra jʋʋ ma dɩhɔnʋŋ. Ama ʋ ha jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la kala dɩ wɩa tuu jʋʋ.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Baal-la ma sɩ nyɩgɛ nɛ-paha-la jaŋ chɛsɛ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ a fo lɩɩŋ, ama ʋ ha jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la kala dɩ wɩa tuu jʋʋ.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Baala sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ nɛ jaŋ paa nɛ-paha-la tʋɔrʋŋ a hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ, a joŋo bil lee sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ mɩ teeŋ ma dɩhɔnʋŋ harɩŋ. Tʋɔrʋ-la nɛ ba jaŋ ŋaa a hɛ lɩɩŋ lɛ a kaa pɩɩsɛ ba wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ tɩta.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Baal-la ma sɩ paa tʋɔrʋ-la hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ, ʋ jaŋ chɛsɛ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ aŋ fo lɩɩŋ, arɩ ŋɩɩ kala ʋ ha jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la na-kala dɩ wɩa tuu jʋʋ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ jaŋ chɩŋ a pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ nʋhʋɔra-la kala sɩ hɛ ba tʋɔŋ a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ digi sʋʋŋ, tɩɩna jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Tɩɩna maga dɩ ʋ kɛŋ lɩɩ-la ba sɩ kaa pɩɩsɛ disiniŋ a chɛsɛ ʋ tɩtɩa tapʋl-tori arɩ tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ. Dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ʋ disiniŋ dɛrɛ nɛ. Ama dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ ʋ tɩtɩa pɩɩsa tapʋl-tori arɩ tapʋl-pɛɩ-la chɛɛŋ, ʋ disiŋ-la bɩ jaŋ dɛrɛ.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ digi sʋʋŋ aŋ bɩ ʋ disiniŋ pɩɩsa ta, tɩɩna ŋaa disiniŋ hɛ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dɩ-zɔŋ-la lɛ nɛ. Tɩɩna maga dɩ ba keru ta Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba ha bɩ lɩɩ-la ba sɩ kaa pɩɩsɛ disiniŋ tɩta mɩsa hɛ ʋ lɛ, ʋ disiniŋ ha bɩ dɛrɛ.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Wombii-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ a mʋ tɩgɛ nʋʋ sɩ sʋʋ lɛbɩŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ ŋ-la: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ hɛ lɛbɩŋ tʋɔŋ ka dɩ nʋʋ sʋʋ, tɩɩna jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ. Dɩ nʋʋ ma nɛ jʋʋ lɛbɩ-la, ʋ ma jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ba kpʋ dɩ-jalɩŋ koo dɩ ʋ paala sʋʋ ʋ Wɩa sʋʋŋ nɛ, dɩ nʋʋ mʋ digi, tɩɩna jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ. Koo dɩ nʋʋ nɛ digi nuhuobiine haŋgbeliŋ koo vaamɩŋ, tɩɩna jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Baal sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ mɩ teeŋ jaŋ joŋ kaku-dɩgɩlɩŋ, a yʋ lɩɩ-la a mɩsa hɛ lɛbɩ-la arɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ kɩaa arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ lɛ. Ʋ jaŋ bɩra ŋaa mɩsa hɛ nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ digi nuhuobiine haŋgbeliŋ koo vaamɩŋ koo nʋʋ ba sɩ kpʋa koo nʋʋ sɩ digi nʋʋ sɩ sʋʋ ʋ Wɩa sʋʋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Baal-la sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ mɩ teeŋ, jaŋ mɩsɛ lɩɩ-la hɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ lɛ tapʋl-tori arɩ tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ. Tapʋl-pɛɩ-la chɛɛŋ, ʋ jaŋ pɩɩsɛ ʋ disiniŋ ta. Nɩɩ-la disiniŋ ʋ sɩ pɩɩsa ta jaŋ chɛsɛ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ a fo lɩɩŋ, dɩ wɩa nɛ jʋa, ʋ disiniŋ dɛrɛ nɛ.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ nɛ bɩ ʋ disiniŋ pɩɩsa ta, ʋ maga dɩ ba keru ta Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ ŋaa disiniŋ hɛ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dɩ-zɔŋ-la lɛ nɛ a tɩŋ ba sɩ bɩ lɩɩ-la ba sɩ kaa pɩɩsɛ disiniŋ joŋo mɩsa hɛ ʋ lɛ, ʋ disiniŋ bɩ dɛrɛ.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Wɩɩŋ deeŋ jaŋ chɩŋ a pɩma a kaa mʋ wuu. Nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛŋ lɩɩ-la pɩɩsɛ nɩaa disiniŋ ta maga dɩ ʋ chɛsɛ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ. Dɩ nʋʋ ma nɛ digi lɩɩ-la, tɩɩna jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ dɩ wɩa tuu jʋʋ.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Kʋŋ na-kala nʋʋ sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ sɩ dige, kʋ-la kɛŋ disiniŋ nɛ. Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ digi kʋ-la, tɩɩna ma jaŋ kɛŋ disiniŋ dɩ wɩa tuu jʋʋ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Jɩna tʋɔŋ chɛŋ-bumbuŋ lɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala mʋ yi tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zɩŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba hɔŋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kadɛs lɛ. Nɩmɛ nɛ Mɩrɩam sʋʋ ba hugu.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Lɩɩŋ fa tuo lee-la dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nyʋa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kala sii a golli Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ a ŋɩŋaa goŋ ba nyuŋ.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba ŋaa goŋ Mosis nyuŋ a bʋl, “Dɩ la nɛ fa yaara sʋʋ, arɩ la naambiiri-la sɩ sʋʋ ŋɩɩ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ, ʋ nɛ kpɩa.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: La ŋaa la TƖƖNA nɩaa nɛ, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ kɛŋ la dɩ la pʋsʋŋ kʋ lɩɩ tintee-hɩlɩŋ deeŋ lɛ dɩ la sʋʋ?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ kɛnla kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a kɔ dɩ-kpuŋkpere deeŋ. Ʋ bɩ mɩaa koo tutogi-nambɩlaa kɛnɛ. Ʋ bɩ girep arɩ tɩɩnɛnɛ-la sɩ nagɛ kampoi nɛnɛɛ kɛnɛ. Lɩɩŋ ma paala tuo dɩ la nyʋa.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ leŋ nɩalɩŋ aŋ mʋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ boiŋ niiŋ a tuu tele chu. La TƖƖNA tʋla kʋ chaana hɛ ba lɛ.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Joŋ dantɩga-la, ka ŋ dɩ ŋ naambie Arɔŋ yɩrɛ nɩalɩŋ kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ. Chɩŋ ba sɩpaaŋ aŋ bʋl wɩaa bʋŋ-la teeŋ, dɩ lɩɩŋ kʋ lɩɩ ʋ lɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ kala nyʋa.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis joŋ dantɩga-la sɩ pɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ arɩ ʋ sɩ dagʋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Ʋ dɩ Arɔŋ yɩrɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ bʋŋ-la sɩpaaŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩba, “Má jegile nɩɩ, ma nɩaa deemba sɩ bɩ dagɩŋ ka nɩɩ. Maa chɛ dɩ la leŋ dɩ lɩɩŋ lɩɩ bʋŋ deeŋ lɛ pɩma, dɩ ma nyʋa nɛɛ?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ ʋ nɩsɩŋ je a ŋmoo bʋŋ-la naansɩɩŋ bʋlɩa arɩ ʋ dantɩga-la. Lɩɩŋ gbu lɩɩ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ kala nyʋa.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Ama La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ, “A tɩŋ ma sɩ bɩ mɩ laa dii woruŋ, a bɩ mɩ zile Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ, ma dee bɩ jaŋ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ tintee-la mɩ sɩ sɩ mɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩba.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba kala ŋaa Mɛrɩba lɛ nɛ, lee-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ gʋrɩmɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Nɩmɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA dagɛ ʋ doluŋ pɩba. Ba sɩ gʋrɩmɛ wɩaa nɛ tɩɩ ba hɛ lee-la yɩrɩŋ Mɛrɩba ŋɩɩ. Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa vɩa dɩ ba pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa wombiiŋ

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis tɩŋ nɩaa Kadɛs lɛ, dɩ ba kɛŋ tɩndaarɩŋ deeŋ mʋ pɩ Ɛdɔm tinteeŋ kuoro. Ʋ sɩ, “Ŋ naambiiriŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ tɩŋ tɩndaarɩŋ deeŋ aa pɩŋ. Ŋ jɩŋ hɛɛ-la kala sɩ jʋʋla nɛ.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: La naabalɩmaba mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ nɛ, la hɔŋ nɩmɛ jɩ-daŋ, Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa wʋrɩgɛ la dɩ la naabalɩmaba woruŋ.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ama la sɩ yele pɩ La TƖƖNA, ʋ nɩɩ la yele nɛ a leŋ ʋ tɩndaara kʋ kɛnla kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Lɛɛlɛ la kʋ hɔŋ taŋ-la ba sɩ yɩrɛ Kadɛs lɛ nɛ, ŋ tinteeŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: La saa sʋlʋŋ dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ la to ŋ tinteeŋ a bal. La jaŋ to womporuŋ a bal, la bɩ jaŋ gɛbɛ jʋʋ ma bagɩsɩŋ, la bɩ jaŋ nyʋa ma vilee lɩɩŋ ma.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa bʋl, “La bɩ jaŋ sɛɩ dɩ ma kʋ to la tinteeŋ bal. Dɩ ma nɛ vɩa aŋ to, la jaŋ sii a yuoma.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma bʋl, “Laa chɛ dɩ la to womporuŋ nɛ a bal, dɩ la kʋŋ koo dɩ la pʋna nɛ nyʋa ma lɩɩŋ, la jaŋ time pɩma. Wombiiŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ laa chɛ dɩ la to bal. La bɩ ma kʋŋkala ka chɛ.”

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa sɩ bɩ sɛyɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa to ba tinteeŋ bal ŋɩɩ, ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mɩɩrɛ. Arɔŋ sʋba

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sii Kadɛs lɛ a mʋ peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hɔɔ leriŋ.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ, “Arɔŋ jaŋ sʋʋ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ tintee-la mɩ sɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, bɛɛ wɩaa ma kala balɩa vɩa dɩ ma to ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ dagɛma nɛ Mɛrɩba lɛ.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Kɛŋ Arɔŋ arɩ ʋ nanʋala Elieza kaa jɩl peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hɔɔ nyuŋ,

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: a wuri Arɔŋ tɩntɩnnɩ gɛnnɩŋ a laalɛ ʋ nanʋala Elieza. Arɔŋ jaŋ sʋʋ daha peeliŋ deeŋ nyuŋ.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ dagʋ, a kɛŋ Arɔŋ arɩ ʋ nanʋala Elieza a jɩl peel-la nyuŋ, ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala bibeŋ.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis wuri Arɔŋ gɛnnɩ-la a joŋo laalɛ ʋ nanʋala Elieza, ka Arɔŋ sʋʋ peel-la nyuŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ nanʋala Elieza mɩɩra kʋ tuu.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ nɩa dɩ Arɔŋ sʋba, ba yel ʋ yoho tapʋlaa mara arɩ fii.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sii peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hɔɔ lɛ, a to wombii-la sɩɩ mʋ mʋga-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mʋgʋ-fɩaŋ dɩɩrɩŋ, dɩ ba golli Ɛdɔm tinteeŋ a mʋ. Ba sɩ mʋ magɛ ŋɩɩ, ba kenyiri kala dɛrɛ.

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: Ba ŋaa goŋ Wɩa arɩ Mosis nyuŋ, a bʋl, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma kɛnla lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ kɔ tintee-hɩlɩŋ deeŋ dɩ la sʋʋ? Kʋdiilii dɔŋ tuo daha, lɩɩŋ ma tuo, la mɩɩsɩŋ fɩɩ kʋdii-tɔɔŋ deeŋ nɛ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA leŋ dɩma kʋbalaba sɩ kɛŋ huoŋ woruŋ kʋ dɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ba nɩ-daŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩ ka kɔ Mosis teeŋ a bʋl, “La ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ la sɩ ŋaa goŋ ŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA nyuŋ. Sʋl La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ dɩma-la lɛl la tʋɔŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis sʋl La TƖƖNA a pɩba.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ libi dɩmɩŋ a joŋo mɛrɛ daaterige lɛ a joŋo pɛ. Dɩ dɩma-la kʋŋ nɛ dɩŋ nʋʋkala, dɩ ʋ wʋla beŋ kɔlɩɩŋ dɩŋ-la sɩ mɛrɛ daa-la lɛ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ libi dɩmɩŋ a joŋo mɛrɛ daaterige lɛ a joŋo pɛ. Dɩ dɩma-la kʋŋ nɛ dɩŋ nɩalɩŋ dɔŋɔ, ʋ yie wʋla beŋ kɔlɩɩŋ dɩŋ-la nɛ a duori. Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩɩ mʋ Mʋab

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɛŋ ŋɩɩ a mʋ hɔŋ lee-kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɔbɔf.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ba bɩra sii nɩmɛ ma, a mʋ hɔŋ fuo-kʋbala niiŋ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Anɔŋ. Ʋ ma hɛ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ nɛ. Fuo-la fa pɩŋ ŋɩɩ nɛ a mʋ jʋʋ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ. Anɔŋ fuo-la nɛ ŋaa Mʋab tɩŋŋaa arɩ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ bʋa.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ba bʋl wɩaa La TƖƖNA laalɩŋ teniŋ tʋɔŋ a mʋʋ tɩgɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Wahɛb sɩ hɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sufa arɩ fuonaasɩ-la arɩ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Anɔŋ wɩaa,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: arɩ fuonaa-luŋii-la sɩ pɩŋ ŋɩɩ a mʋ yi taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Aa, a mʋmʋ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ bʋa.

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bɩra sii Anɔŋ lɛ a mʋ vil-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛɛ. Vil-la leriŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ dɩ mɩ pɩba lɩɩŋ.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ a bʋl, “Viliŋ bul lɩɩŋ dɩ la yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ a dɛnnʋ,

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: vil-la kuori-biiriŋ sɩ kɛŋ ba kuori-dantɩgɩsɩŋ lu, arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa sɩ kɛŋ ba dantɩgɩsɩŋ lu.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba sii tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ a mʋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Matana.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Ba sii Bamɔf lɛ a mʋ fuonaa-la sɩ hɛ Mʋab lɛ, lee-la ŋ sɩ jaŋ chɩŋ peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Pɩsɩga bʋbʋɔŋ aŋ bibeŋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la. Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo dii Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Sɩhɔŋ arɩ Basaŋ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Ɔgɩ

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Sɩhɔŋ tabalɩŋ nɛ fa ŋaa Hɛsɩbɔŋ. Sɩhɔŋ nɛ fa yuo dii Mʋab tɩŋŋaa kuoru-bɩnɩŋ a laa ʋ tinteeŋ kala a mʋ yi Anɔŋ fuo-la.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa tɩŋ nɩaa dɩ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Sɩhɔŋ,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Leŋ dɩ la kʋ to ŋ tinteeŋ a bal. La bɩ jaŋ gɛbɛ jʋʋ ma bagɩsɩŋ kʋŋ, koo a nyʋa ma vilee kʋŋkala lɩɩŋ. La jaŋ to womporuŋ ŋɩɩ a mʋ lɩɩ ma tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Ama Sɩhɔŋ bɩ sɛyɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋ to ʋ tinteeŋ a bal. Ʋ kɛŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala ba lɩɩ dɩ ba yuo Iziral tɩŋŋaa tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ. Ba sɩ mʋ yi lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jahas, ba dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo laalɩŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo diiba a laa ba tinteeŋ, a chɩŋ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Anɔŋ lɛ a kaa mʋ yi fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jabɔk. Ama ba fa bɩ wuo mʋ jʋʋ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba-na gɩba fa dolie nɛ woruŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo dii Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa tabalaa kala, a pɛ Hɛsɩbɔŋ arɩ tabiisi-la kala sɩ gollu, a hɔŋ ba lɛ.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ gɔgʋ-dɩndɛnnɛɛ bʋl, “Má kɔ kuoro Sɩhɔŋ tabalɩŋ Hɛsɩbɔŋ, dɩ la wasa saaʋ.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Sɩhɔŋ laalɩyuoroo sii ʋ tabalɩŋ Hɛsɩbɔŋ lɛ a nagɛ nyiniŋ a mʋ dii Aa. Mʋab tinteeŋ tabalɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ, a dii fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Anɔŋ dundolluŋ kala.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Wɩɩŋ puuma, ma-na Mʋab tɩŋŋaa, ma nɩalɩŋ sɩ laa vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Chɛmɔs dii a kpʋkpaarʋ, ma dɛrɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ. Ma hambolibiisiŋ kala fá nɛ, aŋ ka ba kɛsɛ ma toloo a kaa mʋ pɩ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kuoro.

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa hɔŋ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Mosis tɩŋ baalaa ba mʋ lʋara beŋ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ jaŋ to a yuo dii tabal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jaza. Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ yuo dii taŋ-la arɩ tabiisi-la kala sɩ gollu, a kiri Amɔrɩ tɩmma-la kala fa sɩ hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩra lɩɩ nɩmɛ a joŋ wombiiŋ a chaasɛ Basaŋ tinteeŋ dɩɩrɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Basaŋ kuoro ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɔgɩ, ʋ dɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala kʋ lɩɩ dɩ ba chemba Ɛdɩrɛ lɛ a yuoba.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ŋ bɔyɛ joŋ, mɩ joŋ Basaŋ kuoro Ɔgɩ arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo arɩ ʋ tinteeŋ kala hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ joŋo ŋaa Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Sɩhɔŋ sɩ hɛ Hɛsɩbɔŋ lɛ, joŋ ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa ŋaa ba ma lɛ.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kpʋ kuoro Ɔgɩ arɩ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ʋ nɩaa kala, ba kʋbala ma bɩ ka, aŋ laa tintee-la kala a tɩɩ.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩra sii a mʋ hɔŋ Mʋab tinteeŋ dɩ-taalɩsɩ-la sɩ hɛ Jɔdaŋ fuo-la wɩɩjʋʋlʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a chaasɛ Jeriko.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa bʋla pɩ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ, “Nɩ-daŋ deeŋ jaŋ kɔ a dii la tinteeŋ kala a nagɛ nɛ-bele sɩ yie gbegisi yaŋ ŋɩɩ.” Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Zipo nanʋala Balak nɛ fa ŋaa Mʋab tɩŋŋaa kuoro.

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɩŋ nɩaa dɩ ba mʋ yɩrɛ Bioo nanʋala Balam. Balam fa hɛ ʋ jaŋ Pɛtɔ lɛ nɛ, a kpagɛ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Yufireti. Balak sɩ, “Nɩaa nɛ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a yʋgɛ woruŋ a kʋ hɔnɔ kpagɛmɛ.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Mɩ saa chɛ dɩ ŋ kɔ a kalɩba hɛ nɩaa deemba lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba dolie kɩɩmɛ nɛ. Ŋ bɩ pɔ dɩ ŋ nɛ kalɩba hɛ ba lɛ, mɩ jaŋ wuo yuo diiba, a kiriba dɩ ba lɩɩ mɩ tinteeŋ lɛ. Mɩ jɩma dɩ ŋ nɛ bʋl wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ pɩ nʋʋ, wɩalɩŋ yie sɛnɛ ŋaa nɛ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩra ŋmɩɛsa hɛ nʋʋ lɛ ma, ŋmɩaŋ-la yie dii tɩɩna nɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Balak joŋ moribiiŋ a pɩ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa arɩ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ dɩ ba kaa mʋ a pɩ Balam, dɩ ʋ laa a pɛ tabɩɩŋ pɩba. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɔ Balam teeŋ a bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala kuoro Balak sɩ bʋla a pʋ.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋla pɩba, “Má pɩŋ dɩ taŋ pʋl, mɩ chie jaŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pɩmɛ a pɩma.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ chʋa.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Wɩa kɔ Balam teeŋ tɩtaŋɩŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Kʋbɛɛba nɛ nɩaa deemba sɩ hɛ ŋ teeŋ?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋla pɩ Wɩa, “Zipo nanʋala Balak sɩ ŋaa Mʋab tɩŋŋaa kuoro nɛ tɩmba mɩ teeŋ, dɩ ba bʋla pɩmɛ arɩ

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: nɩaa nɛ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a yʋgɛ woruŋ a kʋ tɔ ʋ tinteeŋ kala. Ʋ saa chɛ dɩ mɩ kɔ a kalɩba hɛ ba lɛ, dɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ŋ bɩ pɔ, ʋ jaŋ wuo yuo diiba a kiriba dɩ ba lɩɩ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bʋla pɩ Balam, “Sɩ́ nɩalɩŋ harɩŋ to mʋ. Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ŋ ŋmɩɛsa hɛ nɩalɩŋ lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba ŋaa nɩa lɛ mɩ sɩ pɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, Balam sii a bʋla pɩ kuoro Balak tɩndaara-la, “Má mɩɩra mʋ ma tinteeŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA bɩ mɩ wombiiŋ pa dɩ mɩ to ma harɩŋ mʋ.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa mʋ Balak teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Balam vɩa dɩ ʋ to la harɩŋ kɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Balak bɩra wasa tɩŋ sɩpaalaaraa ba yʋga kɩɩ bumbuŋ nɩalɩŋ a kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ ma a kɩɩba.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Ba mʋ Balam teeŋ, a bʋla pʋ, “Ŋ-la nɛ Zipo nanʋala Balak bʋl: Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, hɛ doluŋ aŋ kɔ mɩ teeŋ, sɩ́ leŋe dɩ wɩɩkala kɛrɩŋ.

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ timiŋ a yʋgɛ, aŋ pɛ ŋaa wɩɩ-la ma kala ŋ sɩɩ chɛ. Ŋ-na kʋ kalɩba hɛ nɩaa deemba lɛ a pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋla pɩ Balak tɩndaara-la, “Dɩ Balak nɛ paala joŋ sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla-la kala sɩ hɛ ʋ kuori dɩa lɛ pɩmɛ ma, mɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo vɩa La TƖƖNA niiŋ aŋ ŋaa wɩɩkala pʋ.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Ma jaŋ wuo pɩŋ arɩ bumbuŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ pɩŋ ŋɩɩ, dɩ taŋ pʋl, dɩ mɩ na wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ jaŋ bʋla pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa kɔ Balam teeŋ tɩtaŋɩŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Nɩaa deemba bɩra sɩ kɔ dɩ ba yɩrɩŋ, sii to ba harɩŋ mʋ, ama ŋaa wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ dagɩŋ dʋndʋŋa. Sɩ́ wʋwogo kala ŋaa.” Balam arɩ ʋ kakumo

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, Balam sii a kpɩɛrɛ ʋ kakumo a to Mʋab tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩ-la harɩŋ.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Balam sɩɩ mʋ ŋɩɩ, Wɩa na baanɩŋ woruŋ ʋ nyuŋ, a leŋ ʋ-na La TƖƖNA tɩndaara lɩɩ kɛrʋ wombiiŋ lɛ. Balam fa jɩl kakumo nɛ, ʋ tɩntɩnnaa balɩa ma faa to ʋ harɩŋ.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Kakumo-la sɩ na La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la dɩ ʋ chɩŋ wombiiŋ lɛ a kori tokobiiŋ, ʋ gɛbɛ to gɩrɩŋ. Balam ŋmoo kakumo-la dɩ ʋ kʋ lɩɩ wombiiŋ.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la fa chɩŋ wombii-fʋgʋgʋ-bie lɛ nɛ girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ balɩa pɛgɛ, jebiiŋ hɛ sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ a hɛ sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ ma.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Kakumo-la sɩ na La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la ŋɩɩ, ʋ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa mʋ tɩɩgɛ jebii-la dɔŋɔ, a pɛ kɛŋ Balam naaŋ kaa tɩɩgɛ jee-la. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bɩra ŋmoo kakumo-la.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la bɩra mʋ chɩŋ wombii-la, lee sɩ faasa fʋgɛ, lee-la kakumo-la sɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo pɩɛga bal.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Kakumo-la bɩra sɩ na La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la ʋ tuu tel, Balam hɔŋ ʋ nyuŋ. Balam baanɩŋ sii, ʋ ŋmoo kakumo-la arɩ ʋ daaŋ.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA pɩ kakumo-la doluŋ ʋ wuo bʋl wɩaa. Ʋ pɩɛsɛ Balam, “Bɛɛ nɛ mɩ ŋaa cheyiŋ, ŋ ŋmoomi naansɩɩŋ butori kala?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋl, “Ŋ jommi arɩ mɩ ŋaa nɩyaarɩ nɛ. Dɩ mɩ nɛ fa kori tokobiiŋ, mɩ fa jaŋ kpʋŋ lɛɛlɛ.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kakumo-la pɩɛsɛ Balam, “Mɩ dee kakumo-la ŋ sɩ vɛnɛɛ jɩl? Mɩ ha ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ doho ŋ lɛɛ?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋl, “Aɩ.”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA leŋ Balam sɩaa suri ʋ na Wɩa tɩndaarʋ-la sɩ chɩŋ wombiiŋ lɛ a kori tokobiiŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tuu tele chu.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la pɩɛsɛ Balam, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ ŋmoo ŋ kakumo naansɩɩŋ butori-la? Mɩ kɔ dɩ mɩ kɛrɩŋ nɛ, mɩ bɩ cho dɩ ŋ mʋ lee-la.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Kakumo-la na mɩ nɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ʋ gɛbɛ naansɩɩŋ butori-la kala. Dɩ ʋ nɛ fa bɩ gɛbɛ, mɩ fa jaŋ kpʋŋ aŋ leŋu.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la, “Mɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ, mɩ bɩ jɩŋ arɩ ŋ kɛrɛ mɩ wombiiŋ nɛ a bɩ chɛ dɩ mɩ mʋ lee-la. Dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ bɩ tɔrɔ, mɩ jaŋ mɩɩrɛ.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la bɩra bʋla pɩ Balam, “Kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ dɩ ma mʋ, ama wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ bʋla pɩŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ maga dɩ ŋ bʋl.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam to nɩhɩasɩ-la harɩŋ ba mʋ.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Balak sɩ nɩa arɩ Balam ka kɔ, ʋ sii mʋ chemu taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Aa lɛ, Anɔŋ fuo-la leriŋ, Mʋab tɩŋŋaa arɩ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa bʋa nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balak pɩɛsɛ Balam, “Mɩ sɩ tɩma yɩrɩŋ, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ vɩa? Koo ŋ bɩɩna mɩ bɩŋ wuo tiŋ nɛ?”

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Balam sɩ, “Lɛɛlɛ mɩ kɔ nɛ, ama mɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo bʋl wɩɩkala, see wɩɩ-la Wɩa sɩ daga.”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam to Balak harɩŋ ba mʋ taŋ kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kɩrɩaf Hʋzɔf.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Nɩmɛ nɛ Balak kpʋ nɛsɩŋ arɩ piesee a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a chɔgɛ ba nammɩa a pɩ Balam arɩ nɩhɩasɩ-la sɩ hɛ ʋ teeŋ.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, Balak kɛŋ Balam ba jɩl lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bamɔf Baal. Nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ chɩŋ aŋ bee mʋ na Iziral tɩmma-la dɔnsʋŋ.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋla pɩ Balak, “Saa korunuŋ balɩpɛ a pɩmɛ, aŋ kɛŋ nɛ-belliŋ balɩpɛ arɩ pie-belliŋ balɩpɛ a kaa kɔ.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balak ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala Balam sɩ daga. Ba balɩa kpʋ nɛ-bele arɩ pie-bele koru na-kala lɛ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Balam bʋla pɩ Balak, “Chɩŋ ŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ sɛmɛ, ka dɩ mɩ sʋʋsɛ, kapo La TƖƖNA jaŋ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa a kʋ dagɛmɛ. Wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩ bʋla pɩmɛ, mɩ jaŋ kʋ bʋla pɩŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam sʋʋsa mʋ chɩŋ dundol-kpɩlɩɩ kʋbala nyuŋ.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Wɩa kɔ ʋ teeŋ, Balam bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ saa korunuŋ balɩpɛ nɛ a kpʋ nɛ-bele arɩ pie-bele koru na-kala lɛ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩalɩŋ Balam sɩ jaŋ mʋ bʋla pɩ Balak a pʋ.

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Balam mɩɩra mʋ dɩ Balak ha chɩŋ ʋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ, ʋ dɩ Mʋab nɩhɩasɩŋ.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋl wɩɩ-la Wɩa sɩ bʋla pʋ. Ʋ sɩ, “Mʋab tɩŋŋaa kuoro Balak nɛ yɩrɛmɛ mɩ lɩɩ Asiiria wɩɩpɔsʋŋ peele-la nyuŋ a kɔ dɩ mɩ kʋ kalɩba hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ.

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Ɛɛ nɛ saa mɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa a kalɩba hɛ nɩalɩŋ lɛ Wɩa sɩ bɩ kalɩba hɛ? Koo a bʋl wɩaa chei nɩalɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩ bɩ cheye?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: Mɩ chɩŋ bʋŋ nyuŋ nɛ aŋ na nɩalɩŋ, a bɩra chɩŋ dundolo ma nyuŋ aŋ bibemba. Ba ŋaa nɩaa sɩ chɩŋ ba dʋndʋŋ nɛ, ba bɩ tinteye-la dɔnsʋŋ naga.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa yʋga nɛ woruŋ a nagɛ hagɩlɩ-biee. Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo dɩɩsɛba? Leŋ dɩ mɩ sʋʋ a nagɛ tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa deemba sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ ŋɩɩ, dɩ mɩ dɩdɛrɩŋ ma nagɛ ba dɩdɛrɩŋ.”

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balak pɩɛsɛ Balam, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ wɩɩ nɛ ŋ ŋaa mɩ lɛ ŋ-la? Mɩ kɛnɩŋ kɔ dɩ ŋ kalɩba hɛ mɩ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ nɛ, ŋ vɩa aŋ mɩɩra sʋl Wɩa pɩba.”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋl, “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pɩmɛ, ʋ nɛ mɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ.” Balam sɩ bʋl wɩalɩŋ lɩa a tɩgɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Balak bɩra bʋla pɩ Balam, “Kɔ dɩ la mʋ sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ, ŋ jaŋ na Iziral tɩmma-la dɔnsʋŋ, ŋ bɩ jaŋ na ba kala. Chɩŋ nɩmɛ a kalɩba hɛ ba lɛ a pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ kɛnʋ mʋ Zofim pɔkɔŋ, ba jɩl peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Pɩsɩga nyuŋ. Nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ bɩra saa korunuŋ balɩpɛ a kpʋ nɛ-bele arɩ pie-bele koru na-kala nyuŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Balam bɩra bʋla pɩ Balak, “Chɩŋ ŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa sɛmɛ, ka dɩ mɩ mʋ cheŋ Wɩa.”

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA kɔ Balam teeŋ a bʋl wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ jaŋ mʋ bʋla pɩ Balak a pʋ.

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: Balam mɩɩraa mʋ dɩ Balak ha chɩŋ ʋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ sɛmɛ, ʋ dɩ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balak pɩɛsɛ Balam, “La TƖƖNA sɩ bɛɛ nɛ?”

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: Wɩa dagɛmɛ dɩ mɩ sʋlʋ dɩ ʋ pɛ ʋ nɩalɩŋ lɛ nɛ. Ʋ sɩ pɛ ba lɛ ŋɩɩ, mɩ saa bɩ jaŋ wuo kaa bɩrɩmɛ.

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Wʋbɔŋ koo hɛɛ-kala bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa. Ba Tɩɩna Wɩa chɩŋ ba harɩŋ nɛ. Ba yɩyɩrɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ a jʋjʋɔsɛ ʋ sɩ ŋaa ba kuoro.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Wɩa nɛ kɛmba kaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ba kɛŋ doluŋ a nagɛ baga nɛŋ nɛ.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Hɩl koo vʋgʋrʋ kala bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ. Nɩaa jaŋ naba a bʋl, ‘Na wɩalɩŋ Wɩa sɩ ŋaa pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa.’

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa nagɛ naachigiŋ nɛ. Dɩ ba nɛ kiri ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ, dɩ ba nɛ bɩ ba kpʋa, a chaŋ ba nammɩa a nyʋa ba chalɩŋ, ba bɩ wiesi.”

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balak bʋla pɩ Balam, “Ŋ folo bɩ kalɩba hɛ ba lɛ, saa sɩ́ bʋla wasɛba ma.”

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ bɩ bʋla pɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ sɩ mɩ ŋaa wɩɩ-la nɛ, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa?” Balam sɩ bʋl wɩalɩŋ tori a tɩgɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Balak bɩra bʋla pɩ Balam “Leŋ dɩ mɩ kɛnɩŋ mʋ sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ, kapo Wɩa tʋɔŋ jaŋ tɔrɛ dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ ŋ chɩŋ lee-la aŋ kalɩba hɛ ba lɛ pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ kɛŋ Balam ba jɩl peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Pio nyuŋ. Ba chɩŋ nɩmɛ aŋ bibeŋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balam bʋla pʋ, “Saa korunuŋ balɩpɛ a kɛŋ nɛ-belliŋ balɩpɛ arɩ pie-belliŋ balɩpɛ kɔ.”

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balak ŋaa ŋɩɩ Balam sɩ daga. Ba kpʋ nɛ-bele arɩ pie-bele a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, koru na-kala nyuŋ.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Balam sɩ kʋ jɩŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA ka chɛ dɩ ʋ bʋl wɩaa a wasɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ, ʋ bɩra bɩ mʋa dɩ ʋ chɛ na wɩɩkala arɩ ʋ fa sɩ yie mʋ chɛ ŋɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ kɛŋ ʋ sɩaa chaasɛ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la dɩɩrɩŋ,

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: a bee mʋ na Iziral tɩŋŋaa, dɩ ba hɔŋ doho doho. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa Dɩma kʋ tuu hɛ Balam lɛ.

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Ʋ bʋl wɩaa deemba Wɩa sɩ joŋo dagʋ: “Mɩ-na Bioo nanʋala Balam sɩ ŋaa nʋʋ, a nɩna wɩaa woruŋ nɩɩ bʋl wɩaa deemba.

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Mɩ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ Wɩa doluŋ kala Tɩɩna sɩ bʋla nɛ, a na wɩalɩŋ ma ʋ sɩ daga arɩ duosoo tʋɔŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ tuu tele chu, Wɩa suri mɩ sɩaa:

english_verse: “People of Israel, your camp is lovely.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩjʋʋlʋŋ zɔmɔ nɛ woruŋ,

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: a nagɛ fuonaa balaa sɩ jalla pɩpɛ, a nagɛ fuoŋ niiŋ gaarɩŋ, a nagɛ tɩɩ-pugu kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Alɔɩ, La TƖƖNA tɩtɩa sɩ chɔnsɔ, koo a nagɛ kuolu tɩɩsɩŋ sɩ chɩŋ fuoŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Duonuŋ jaŋ nɩɩ woruŋ a pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba duu ba kɩaa fɩɛlɩŋ lɛ. Ba kuoro jaŋ kɛŋ doluŋ a kɩɩ kuoru-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Agag. Ba tinteeŋ ma yɩrɩŋ jaŋ sisii.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Wɩa nɛ kɛmba lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ kɔ. Ba kɛŋ doluŋ a nagɛ baga nɛŋ nɛ. Ba jaŋ yuo dii ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ a bori ba tosuŋ, aŋ bori ba haŋgbelee ma muno muno.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa nagɛ naachigi-balaa nɛ. Dɩ ba nɛ pɩna, nʋʋkala tuo sɩ jaŋ wuo chɩsɛba. Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ sʋl Wɩɩ-sʋl zɔmʋŋ a pɩba, Wɩa jaŋ pɛ tɩɩna ma lɛ. Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kalɩba hɛ ba lɛ ma, Wɩa ma jaŋ kalɩba hɛ tɩɩna lɛ.”

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balak na baanɩŋ woruŋ Balam nyuŋ a kɛŋ ʋ nɩsɩŋ ŋmoo dɔŋɔ, aŋ bʋla pɩ Balam, “Mɩ yɩrɩŋ dɩ ŋ kʋ kalɩba hɛ mɩ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ nɛ, ŋ mɩɩra kʋ sʋl Wɩa pɩba naansɩɩŋ butori.

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Mɩ fa sɩ mɩ jaŋ timiŋ a yʋgɛ, ama La TƖƖNA bɩ sɛyɛ, sii viiri lɩma.”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: arɩ sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla nɛ paala su ŋ kuoru dɩa ŋ joŋo pɩmɛ ma, mɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo bʋl wʋzɔŋ koo wʋbɔŋ kala a lɩɩ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla harɩŋ.

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Mɩ-na mɩɩraa mʋ mɩ nɩaa teeŋ nɛ, ama mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa maachie sɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋ nɩaa lɛ.” Balam sɩ bʋl wɩalɩŋ nɛsɛ a tɩgɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ Wɩa sɩ joŋo dagʋ, ʋ bʋl nɛ ŋ-la: “Mɩ-na Bioo nanʋala Balam, sɩ ŋaa nʋʋ, a nɩna wɩaa woruŋ nɩɩ bʋl wɩaa deemba.

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: Mɩ na wɩɩ nɛ, ama lɛɛlɛ dee wɩɩ-la jaŋ ŋaa. Mɩ na arɩ kuoro jaŋ lɩɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ a chaanɛ a nagɛ chɛnwʋlʋŋ, a kori kuoru dantɩga. Ʋ jaŋ yuo dii Mʋab tɩŋŋaa arɩ Sɛf doho nɩaa kala.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa jaŋ kɛŋ doluŋ a yuo dii ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Kuoro jaŋ lɩɩ Jekɔb doho nɩalɩŋ tʋɔŋ a yuo dii nɩkaana-la sɩ hɛ ba tasɩŋ lɛ.” Balam sɩ to harɩŋ a bʋl wɩalɩŋ tɩgɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: Ama Asiiria tɩŋŋaa ha jaŋ yuo dii Keni tɩŋŋaa a chei ba tinteeŋ aŋ kɛsɛba viiri.”

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Lɩɩŋ daborusuŋ jaŋ lɩɩ Sapɩrɔs fuoŋ-niiŋ a kʋ yuo dii Asiiria tɩŋŋaa arɩ Ɛbɛ tɩŋŋaa, ama nɩalɩŋ sɩ kʋ yuo diiba ma kala jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Balam mɩɩra mʋ ʋ jaŋ, ka Balak ma viiri.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ hɔŋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩtɩm, ba baala-la suomo chɩchɛ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa toloo a kɛmba pɩpɩŋ.

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: Tolie-la yie kɛmba mʋ ba vʋɩyaa dɩ-kpaarɩŋ, ba pɛ didii ba vʋɩyaa kʋdiilee aŋ kpʋkpaarɛ ba vesi-la.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa pɛ a kpʋkpaarɛ ba vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal, a hɛ Pio lɛ. La TƖƖNA faasa na baanɩŋ ba nyuŋ.

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Kɛsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaara-la kala sɩ mʋ pɛ a kpʋkpaarɛ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal, a kpʋba wɩɩhɛyɛ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA baaŋ-la sɩ faasa sii jaŋ fɩɛlɛ dɩ mɩ leŋ nɩkaana-la.”

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ, “Má kpʋ baala-la kala sɩ hɛ ma doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ a mʋ pɛ kpʋkpaarɛ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal sɩ hɛ Pio lɛ.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa baal kʋbala kɛŋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa tolo a kʋʋ jʋʋ ʋ dɩa, Mosis arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sɩɩŋ lɛ. Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ baa yel lɛbɩ-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ boiŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Elieza nanʋala Finihas ma fa hɛ nɩmɛ. Ʋ fa ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Arɔŋ nihiŋ nɛ. Ʋ sɩ na wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ʋ lɩɩ nɩalɩŋ tʋɔŋ a joŋ timiŋ,

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: a to Iziral tɩɩna-la harɩŋ a jʋʋ ʋ lɛbɩŋ, a tɔbʋ arɩ tiŋ-la, ʋ luro lɩɩ kɛŋ haal-la luoruŋ lɛ. Ʋ sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, nyanyal-bɔŋ-la fa sɩ jʋʋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɛrɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: Ʋ dɩ ʋ doho nɩaa nɛ jaŋ ŋaa nɩalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ pɩpɩmɛ a kaa mʋ wuu, a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ bɩ sɛyɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɛnnɛ vene kala a pɛ mɩ lɛ, a laaba ta ba wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa baal-la fa sɩ kɛŋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa tolo jʋʋ dɩa ba kpʋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Zimiri. Ʋ fa ŋaa Salu nanʋala nɛ. Salu fa ŋaa Simioŋ doho nɩaa dɩa nɩhɩaŋ nɛ.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa tolo-la ma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Kozibi. Ʋ nyɩmma nɛ Zuu. Zuu fa ŋaa Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa doho dɔŋɔ sɩpaalaarʋ nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bɩra bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: bɛɛ wɩaa ba ŋaa wɩaa ma lɛ a nagɛ ma ŋaa dʋndɔmɔ nɛ. Ba nyɩsɛma Pio lɛ ma zil ba vene, a pɛ wʋbɔŋ-la ba dɩ-haala Kozibi Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaarʋ-la tolo sɩ ŋaa ma kpʋʋ bʋa-la lɛ nyanyal-bɔŋ-la sɩ jʋʋma.”

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Nyanyal-bɔŋ-la sɩ jʋʋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ŋɩɩ harɩŋ La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩ Mosis arɩ Elieza, Arɔŋ sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara nanʋala.

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ, “Má dɩɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩa dɩa, baal na-kala sɩ yi jɩsɩŋ mara koo a kɩɩ a jaŋ wuo mʋ laalɩŋ.”

english_verse: years and older, just as Moses and their ancestors had done when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Juda doho nɩaa gentisiŋ nɛ ŋ-la: Sela, ʋ nɛ kʋ ŋaa Sela tɩŋŋaa gentine. Pɛrɛs, ʋ nɛ kʋ ŋaa Pɛrɛs tɩŋŋaa gentine. Zɛra, ʋ nɛ kʋ ŋaa Zɛra tɩŋŋaa gentine.

english_verse: Israel was now camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. Moses and Eleazar told them
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Elieza bʋl wɩaa a pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa. Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ ba hɛ Mʋab tintee-taalɩsɩ-la sɩ kpagɛ Jɔdaŋ fuo-la, Jeriko cholo.

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Palu nanʋala nɛ fa Ɛlɩab.

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɛlɩab ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ fa Nɛmʋɛl, Dataŋ arɩ Abɩram. Dataŋ deeŋ arɩ Abɩram fa ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa nɛ. Ba nɛ pɛ Kora arɩ ʋ harɩ-tooro-la lɛ ba vɩa La TƖƖNA niiŋ, aŋ nyɛsɛ Mosis arɩ Arɔŋ nyuŋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tinteeŋ suri a paaba a pɛ Kora lɛ a liŋ. Kora harɩ-tooroo nɛ fa sʋba bʋa-la lɛ nyiniŋ sɩ joŋ baala-la zɔɔ-balɩa arɩ mahɩŋ balɩa arɩ fii dii. Ŋɩɩ ŋaa wɩɩ sɩ pɩna a chɩchagɩlɛ la Iziral tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Ama Kora doho nɩaa kala fa dee bɩ sʋba.

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Nɩaa deemba kʋŋkala fa tuo bʋa-la lɛ Mosis arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Arɔŋ sɩɩ dɩɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Sɩnaɩ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Arɔŋ ma lʋl Nadab, Abihu, Elieza arɩ Itama.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: “Nɩaa deemba ŋ sɩ dɩɩsa, kɛŋ tintee-la kpaa pɩba a magɛ doho kala sɩ magɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ tɔnsɔ dɛrɛ, nɩalɩŋ sɩ yʋga, ba jaŋ laa kʋbalɩŋ, nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ bɩ yʋgɛ jaŋ laa kʋbie.”

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa gentisi-la kʋbiisiŋ ma nɛ ha ŋ-la: Libini tɩŋŋaa gentine, Hɛbʋrɔŋ tɩŋŋaa gentine, Mali tɩŋŋaa gentine, Musi tɩŋŋaa gentine, Kora tɩŋŋaa gentine. Kohaf naabalɩma nɛ Amɩram.

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: Amɩram haala yɩrɩŋ nɛ Jokɛbɛd. Ʋ ŋaa Levi doho nʋʋ nɛ. Ba lʋlʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ. Jokɛbɛd nɛ lʋl Arɔŋ, Mosis arɩ ba dɩhaala Mɩrɩam a pɩ Amɩram.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ama Nadab arɩ Abihu nɛ fa sʋba ba sɩ nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ, ka ʋ bɩ ba ŋɩɩ daga.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Nɩaa deemba kala Mosis arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Elieza nɛ dɩɩsa, bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ dɩɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Mʋab tintee-taalɩsɩ-la lɛ, dɩ ba kpagɛ Jɔdaŋ fuo-la Jeriko cholo.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩmma-la arɩ ba jaŋ sʋʋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ. Ba kala sɛnɛ sʋʋ aŋ ka Jefuni nanʋala Kalɩb arɩ Nuŋ nanʋala Josua dʋndʋŋa.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: a mʋ lɛbɩ-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ yie kɔ Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ boiŋ niiŋ, a chɩŋ Mosis arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Elieza, arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sɩpaaŋ a bʋl,

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: “La nyɩmma bɩ hambolibie lʋla aŋ sʋʋ Sɩnaɩ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ, ama ʋ-na fa bɩ Kora arɩ ʋ harɩ-tooro-la sɩ vɩa La TƖƖNA niiŋ aŋ sii nyɛsɛ Mosis nyuŋ lɛ pɛ. Ʋ-na sʋʋ ʋ tɩtɩa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ sʋʋŋ nɛ.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Maa chɛ dɩ la nyɩmma yɩrɩŋ lɛl Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ nɛ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ bɩ hambolibie kɛnɛ wɩaa? La nyɩmma naambiiriŋ tʋɔŋ, dʋa-la fa sɩ jaŋ ŋaa ʋ kʋa, má joŋo pɩla.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis kɛŋ wɩɩ-la ba sɩ bʋla a mʋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ.

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ,

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: “Zelofihad toloo sɩ bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ nɛ. Ʋ maga dɩ ma pɩba dʋa ba nyɩmma naambiiriŋ dʋa tʋɔŋ nɛ. Dʋa-la fa sɩ jaŋ ŋaa ba nyɩmma kʋa, má joŋo pɩba.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ toloo ma kɛnɛ, má joŋo pɩ ʋ naambiiriŋ.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ naambiiriŋ ma kɛnɛ, má joŋo pɩ ʋ nyɩmma naambiiriŋ.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nyɩmma nɛ bɩ naambiiriŋ kɛnɛ, má joŋo pɩ ʋ dɩ nʋʋ sɩ pɛ chalɩŋ a kpagʋ. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ŋaa wombii nɛ a magɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tutou arɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ dagɛ Mosis ŋɩɩ.’ ” Josua nɛ jaŋ laa Mosis nyuŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bɩra bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Mʋ́ jɩl peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Abarɩm nyuŋ, a na tintee-la mɩ sɩ joŋo pɩpɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ naʋ, ŋ ma jaŋ sʋʋ a nagɛ ŋ naambie Arɔŋ sɩ sʋʋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ Ziŋ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ, Mɛrɩba lɩɩ-la sɩ hɛ Kadɛs lɛ, ma vɩa dɩ ma zilmi nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩpaaŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ.”

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: “La TƖƖNA Wɩa, ŋ nɩɩ pɩ nuhuobiiŋ kala mɩɩsɩŋ, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, lɩɩsɛ nʋʋ sɩ jaŋ wuo laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ,

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: a kɛmba mʋmʋ laalɩŋ. La Tɩɩna, ŋ nɩaa bɩ maga dɩ ba nagɛ piesee sɩ bɩ pie-daara kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis, “Lɩɩsɛ Nuŋ nanʋala Josua, a joŋ ŋ nɩsɩŋ daŋ ʋ lɛ. Mɩ Dɩma hɛ ʋ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Kɛnʋ mʋ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Elieza arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sɩpaaŋ, a leŋ dɩ ba jɩŋ arɩ ʋ nɛ laa ŋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: Chɔgɛ ŋ dol-la pʋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala tuto ʋ niiŋ.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Elieza jaŋ to Urim arɩ Tumim lɛ aa dagɛ wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩɩ chɛ a pɩpɩ Josua. Ŋ-la nɛ Josua jaŋ to a dagɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa wɩalɩŋ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ba ŋɩŋaa.”

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mosis ŋaa wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ dagʋ. Ʋ kɛŋ Josua a kaa lɩɩ ʋ chɩŋ Elieza arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sɩpaaŋ,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Pie-bel pɔrɔ-la balɩpɛ ma kʋŋkala lɛ, má pɛ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: Pie-bel-pɔrɔ-la ma kʋŋkala lɛ, ma jaŋ pɛ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a hɛ nʋʋŋ a ŋaa mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ. Kɩaa deemba kala nɛ ma jaŋ joŋo hɛ dɔŋɔ a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a nyɩga pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA. Ba sʋɔra sɩma nɛ a pɩmɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Mosis,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɩ ba kɛŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kʋdiilee kʋ nyɩga pɩmɛ bʋa-la lɛ sɩ maga. Ba sʋɔra sɩma nɛ a pɩmɛ.

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ jaŋ kaa kʋ ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩmɛ tapʋlɩɩ na-kala nɛ ŋ-la: Pie-pɔrɔɔ balɩa sɩ yi jɩna jɩna a bɩ nyɔɔ kala kɛnɛ.

english_verse: Along with each of them, one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: a pɛ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a hɛ Olif nʋʋŋ loŋ arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a ŋaa mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Kʋnyʋalaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ sɩ-yele loŋ arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ ma jaŋ joŋo pɛ pie-pɔrɔ-la kʋŋkala lɛ. Kʋnyʋalaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ maga dɩ ma joŋo bɩsa ta nɛ a pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA, Wɩa dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Chɛnɛ na-kala tapʋl bumbuŋ, má kɛŋ nɛ-bel pɔrɔɔ balɩa, pie-bele arɩ pie-bel pɔrɔɔ balɩpɛ sɩ yi jɩna jɩna, a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA. Ba kʋŋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ kɛŋ nyɔɔ.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Nɛ-bele na-kala lɛ, ma jaŋ pɛ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a hɛ nʋʋŋ a ŋaa mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ. Pie-bele-la ma lɛ, ma jaŋ pɛ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa a hɛ nʋʋŋ.

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: Chɛŋ-bumbuŋ tʋɔŋ tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɛsɛ chɛɛŋ nɛ maga ma gbieli mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA dɩɩsɩŋ kiele bal gbiele-la.

english_verse: The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Chɛŋ-bumbuŋ-la tʋɔŋ tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɔŋ chɛɛŋ, má suomi gbiele-la, a gbieli tapʋlaa balɩpɛ, aŋ didii boroboro sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ.

english_verse: On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Gbiele-la tapʋl-bumbuŋ, ma hilimi mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA yɩrɩŋ lɛ a sɩ́ tɩntɩmɩɩ kala tɩŋ.

english_verse: Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Má kɛŋ nɛ-bel-pɔrɔɔ balɩa arɩ pie-bel-pɔrɔɔ balɩpɛ sɩ yi jɩna jɩna, a kaa kʋ ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a nyɩga pɩ La TƖƖNA. Ba kʋŋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ kɛŋ nyɔɔ.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Nɛ-bel-pɔrɔ-la kʋŋkala lɛ, má kɛŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a hɛ nʋʋŋ a ŋaa mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ. Pie-bele-la ma lɛ, má pɛ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa a hɛ nʋʋŋ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Pie-bel-pɔrɔ-la ma kʋŋkala lɛ, má hɛ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me.
translation_verse: Má jaŋ ŋaa Wɩɩ-sʋlʋ kɩaa deemba a pɛ tapʋlɩɩ kala kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ ʋ kʋnyʋalaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa lɛ. Má nyɩga pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA tapʋlɩɩ na-kala, ŋɩɩ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ. Ba sʋɔra sɩma nɛ a pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: Then on the last day of the festival, you must once again rest from work and come together for worship. The Sacrifices during the Harvest Festival (Leviticus
translation_verse: Tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ, má kʋ hilimi La TƖƖNA yɩrɩŋ lɛ a sɩ tɩntɩmɩɩ kala tɩŋ. Kʋdii-falaa gbiele

english_verse: On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain.
translation_verse: Ma kʋdii falaa gbiele tapʋlʋŋ, tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ má yie kɛŋ ma kʋdii falaa kaa kʋ pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA ŋɩɩ. Tapʋlɩɩ-la má hilimi mɩ yɩrɩŋ lɛ aŋ sɩ́ tɩntɩmɩɩ kala tɩŋ.

english_verse: Offer two young bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Má kɛŋ nɛ-bel-pɔrɔɔ balɩa, pie-bele arɩ pie-bel-pɔrɔɔ balɩpɛ sɩ yi jɩna jɩna a kʋ ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a nyɩga pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA. Ba sʋɔra sɩma nɛ a pɩmɛ.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Nɛ-bele na-kala lɛ, má ŋaa mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a hɛ nʋʋŋ. Pie-bele-la ma lɛ, má hɛ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa.

english_verse: Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Má kɛŋ gbuŋgbogo a pɛ a ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ joŋo chɛnɩŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩɩsɛ ma disiniŋ ta.

english_verse: The animals must have nothing wrong with them and are to be sacrificed along with the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɩɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ deemba, má ŋaa ba kʋnyʋalaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ ma pɛ arɩ tapʋlɩɩ kala kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ ʋ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ. Pʋsʋ-la kala ma sɩ kaa ŋɩŋaa Wɩɩ-sʋlaa deemba kʋŋkala bɩ maga dɩ ʋ kɛŋ nyɔɔ.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, you must rest from your work and come together to celebrate at the sound of the trumpets.
translation_verse: Chɛŋ-pɛɩ tʋɔŋ tapʋl-bumbuŋ, má hilimi mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA yɩrɩŋ lɛ a sɩ́ tɩntɩmɩɩ kala tɩŋ. Tapʋlɩɩ-la ma maga dɩ ma ŋmʋʋ banyilliŋ.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Nɛ-bele-la lɛ, má ŋaa mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ a hɛ nʋʋŋ, aŋ ŋaa mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa ma a pɛ pie-bele-la ma lɛ.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: Pie-bel-pɔrɔ-la ma kʋŋkala lɛ, má hɛ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ kuokuo gbaŋa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: You must also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Má kɛŋ gbuŋgbogo ma a pɛ a ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ joŋo chɛnɩŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩɩsɛ ma disiniŋ ta.

english_verse: These sacrifices will be made in addition to the regular daily sacrifices and the sacrifices for the first day of the month. The smoke from these sacrifices will please me. The Sacrifices on the Great Day of Forgiveness (Leviticus
translation_verse: Má jaŋ ŋaa Wɩɩ-sʋlaa deemba a pɛ tapʋlɩɩ kala kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa lɛ, arɩ chɛnɛ na-kala kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa, a pɛ ba mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ ba kʋnyʋalaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa lɛ. Ba ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ kɩaa ma sɩ jaŋ nyɩga pɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA nɛ. Ba sʋɔra sɩma nɛ a pɩmɛ. Disiniŋ pɩɩsɩŋ tapʋlʋŋ
