english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Mosis hɩɩlɩ-baala fa ŋaa Keni tɩɩna nɛ. Ʋ doho nɩaa lɩɩ Jeriko, taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ abɛ tɩɩsɩŋ taŋ, a to Juda doho nɩaa harɩŋ, ba mʋ Juda doho nɩaa tintee-hɩlɩŋ sɩ hɛ Nɛgɛf lɛ, a kpagɛ Arad a hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Juda doho nɩaa ma pɛ ba naambiiriŋ Simioŋ doho nɩaa lɛ ba mʋ yuo Kɛnaŋ tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zɛfaf lɛ, a chei ʋ kala. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɛŋ lee-la yɩyɩrɛ Hɔma.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa chɩŋ Juda doho nɩaa harɩŋ nɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba yuo laa tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga. Ama ba fa bɩ wuo kiri nɩalɩŋ-na sɩ hɛ tintee-taalɩ-la lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa nɩalɩŋ fa kɛŋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba ba sɩ kɛŋ hɔɔnʋŋ ŋaa nɛ.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Mosis fa sɩ hɛ niiŋ pɩ Kalɩb, arɩ ʋ jaŋ joŋ Hɛbʋrɔŋ tinteeŋ a pʋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba joŋo pʋ. Ʋ kiri Anakɩ doho nɩaa nɩwaayiile-la nyɩŋ-nɩaa batori.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Ama Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa-na bɩ wuo kiri Jebus tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ. Arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala, Jebus tɩŋŋaa ha hɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ nɛ.

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: nɩalɩŋ mʋ na baal kʋbala dɩ ʋ lɩɩ taŋ-la tʋɔŋ kʋʋ lɩɩ. Ba bʋla pʋ, “Dagɛla ŋɩɩ la sɩ jaŋ to a jʋʋ taŋ deeŋ tʋɔŋ, ka dɩ la sɩ́ŋ wɩɩkala ŋaa.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la dagɛba, ba jʋʋ taŋ-la tʋɔŋ a kpʋ taŋ-la nɩaa, aŋ leŋ baal-la sɩ dagɛba wombiiŋ arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa kala.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la lɩɩ nɩmɛ a mʋ Hiti tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ, a saa taŋ nɩmɛ a hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Lus. Taŋ-la yɩrɩŋ nɛ ha ŋɩɩ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala.

english_verse: Canaanites lived in the towns of Beth-Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and all the villages nearby. The Canaanites were determined to stay, and the Manasseh tribe never did get rid of them. But later on, when the Israelites grew more powerful, they made slaves of the Canaanites.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ kʋ kɛŋ doluŋ, ba fʋgɛ Kɛnaŋ tɩmma-la hɛ, ba tɩtɩŋ yoŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa. Ama ba bɩ Kɛnaŋ tɩmma-la kala kire ba lɩɩ tintee-la lɛ.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Efirem doho nɩaa ma bɩ Kɛnaŋ tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Geza lɛ kire, ama ba lemba nɛ ba guoli ba tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Zebuluŋ doho nɩaa ma bɩ Kɛnaŋ tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Kɩtɩrɔŋ arɩ Nahalɔl lɛ kire, ba lemba nɛ ba guoli ba tʋɔŋ, ama ba fʋgɛba nɛ ba tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa pɩpɩba.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: Asa doho nɩaa sɩ bɩ ba kire ŋɩɩ, ba dɩ Kɛnaŋ tɩmma-la sɩ tɩɩ tintee-la kala hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Nafɩtalɩ doho nɩaa ma bɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ tasɩŋ deemba lɛ kire: Bɛf Sɛmɛs arɩ Bɛf Anaf. Ba leŋ Kɛnaŋ tɩmma-la fa sɩ tɩɩ tintee-la nɛ, ba dɩ ba kala hɔŋ. Ama ba fʋgɛba nɛ ba tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa a pɩpɩba.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kɛrɛ Daŋ doho nɩaa-na a hɛ tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ nɛ, a pɔ dɩ ba sɩ́ kʋ tuu tintee-taala-la leriŋ.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amɔrɩ tɩmma-la fa chaasa kɛŋ ba tʋɔŋ nɛ dɩ ba hɔŋ peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hɛrɩs lɛ, arɩ lere-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Aɩjalɔŋ arɩ Saalɩbɩm. Ama Efirem arɩ Manasɛ doho nɩaa doluŋ sɩ kʋ pʋŋa pɛ, ba fʋgɛ Amɔrɩ tɩmma-la ma hɛ ba tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa pɩpɩba.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ bʋa nɛ fa wombii-bie-la sɩ to peelee tʋɔŋ, baa yɩrɛ Nʋɔmʋŋ wombii-bie, a to ŋɩɩ mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɛla a kiele mʋ.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa tɩndaara lɩɩ Gɩlɩgal lɛ a mʋ Bokim a bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, “Mɩ kɛmma lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ, a kɛmma kaa mʋ tintee-la mɩ sɩ hɛ niiŋ arɩ mɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩ ma naabalɩmaba. Mɩ sɩ, ‘Mɩ bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ mɩ leŋe dɩ niiŋ deeŋ birigi.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Má ma bɩ maga dɩ ma leŋ ma dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ tinteeŋ deeŋ lɛ pɛ nii kala. Ʋ maga dɩ ma chei ba vʋɩyaa korunuŋ kala.’ Ama ma bɩ mɩ niiŋ lɛ to. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma ŋaa ŋɩɩ?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ mɩ bʋlaa pɩma, mɩ bɩ jaŋ kiri nɩalɩŋ ta ma sɩpaaŋ. Ba jaŋ nagɛ sɔsʋŋ ma yaraa lɛ, dɩ ba vesiŋ ma nagɛ bɛrɛ a kɩkɛsɛma.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba hɛ lee-la yɩrɩŋ Bokim . Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA nɩmɛ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɩa Wɩa niiŋ, ba yuo diiba

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ba joŋu hugi ʋ tɩtɩa tinteeŋ lɛ, Tɩmɩnaf Sɛra lɛ, a hɛ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ, peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gaas a hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Doho deeŋ nɩaa kala sɩ kʋ sʋʋ dɛrɛ, do-falɩɩ ma bɩra sii, a bɩ La TƖƖNA jɩŋ, a bɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma jɩŋ.

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Bʋa na-kala dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ mʋa dɩ ba yuo laalɩŋ, La TƖƖNA yie leŋ ba yuo diiba nɛ, arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ fa sɩ ŋmɩɛsa pɩba. Bʋa-la lɛ, ba chaasa hɛ hɛɛŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ woruŋ.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA lɩɩsɛ sɩpaalaaraa pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ba laaba ta laalɩyuoro-la sɩ yuo didiiba nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Ama Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɩa dɩ ba to sɩpaalaara-la niiŋ, aŋ ha joŋ ba tɩtɩa a hɛ vesiŋ lɛ a kpʋkpaarɛba. Doho deeŋ nɩaa-na fa bɩ ba nyɩmmaba naga, ba nyɩmmaba fa sɩɩ to La TƖƖNA niiŋ wɩaa ŋɩɩ. Ba-na guu vɩa ba kala nɛ.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Bʋa na-kala dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ lɩɩsɛ sɩpaalaara pɩba, ʋ yie chɩŋ sɩpaa-laarʋ-la harɩŋ nɛ, a lɩɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɩsɩŋ lɛ sɩpaa-laarʋ-la mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ. Bʋa na-kala dɩ ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ dɔgɩsɛba dɩ ba na hɛɛŋ a yele pʋ, ʋ yie fá ba nenige nɛ a laaba ta.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Ama dɩ sɩpaa-laarʋ-la nɛ sʋba, nɩalɩŋ yie bɩra vɩa La TƖƖNA nɛ aŋ mʋʋ to wombie-la sɩ bɔmɔ kɩɩ wombie-la ba nyɩmmaba fa sɩɩ to, a tuto vesiŋ a kpʋkpaarɛba. Ba vɩa dɩ ba joŋ ba wʋbɔmɔ-la arɩ ba nyu-duo-la a ta nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, La TƖƖNA chaasa na baanɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nyuŋ a bʋl, “A tɩŋ tinteeŋ deeŋ nɩaa sɩ chei nii-la mɩ sɩ hɛ mɩ dɩ ba naabalɩmaba pɛgɛ, a bɩ jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: tinteye-la Josua sɩ bɩ kire aŋ sʋʋ, mɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ kiriba ta ba sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ tinteye-la a magɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, a na dɩ ba jaŋ to mɩ wombiiŋ arɩ ba naabalɩmaba sɩ to ŋɩɩ koo ba bɩ jaŋ to.”

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa leŋe tinteye-la ka nɛ, ʋ bɩ ba-na joŋo hɛ Josua nɩsɩŋ lɛ ʋ kiriba ta bala.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Tinteye-la ʋ sɩ leŋe nɛ ŋ-la: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tinteeŋ sɩpaalaaraa banɔŋ, Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa kala, Sɩdɔŋ tɩŋŋaa arɩ Hivi tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ peelee leriŋ, a chɩŋ peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal Hɛmɔŋ a kaa mʋ Lebo Hamaf.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Ʋ lemba dɩ ʋ kɛmba magɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa a na ba jaŋ to niiri-la ʋ sɩ to Mosis lɛ a bile pɩ ba naabalɩmaba nɛɛ.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Ba faa jaa nɩaa deemba toloo nɛ, nɩalɩŋ ma jɩjaa ba toloo, ka ba pɛ kpʋkpaarɛ nɩalɩŋ vesiŋ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaara Ofiniel

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa wʋbɔŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, ba yʋ La TƖƖNA wɩaa aŋ tuto vesi-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal arɩ Asɩra.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA baanɩŋ sii Iziral tɩŋŋaa nyuŋ, ʋ jomba hɛ Aram Naharem tɩŋŋaa kuoru kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kusaŋ-Risatem nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa hɛ kuoro deeŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ jɩsɩŋ chori nɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yele pɩ La TƖƖNA dɩ ʋ pɛ ba lɛ. Ʋ lɩɩsɛ Kenas nanʋala Ofiniel ʋ laaba ta. Kenas fa ŋaa Kalɩb ŋaana nɛ.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩra ŋaa wʋbɔŋ kʋbala La TƖƖNA teeŋ. A tɩŋ wʋbɔŋ-la wɩaa, La TƖƖNA leŋ Mʋab kuoro Ɛgɩlɔŋ kɛŋ doluŋ a kɩɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛgɩlɔŋ yɩrɛ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa arɩ Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa ba kʋ pɛ ʋ lɛ ba yuo dii Iziral tɩŋŋaa a laa Jeriko, abɛ tɩɩsɩŋ taŋ-la.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Ehud sɩ kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ mʋ pʋ dɛrɛ, ʋ leŋ baala-la sɩ chʋŋ kɩalɩŋ mʋ mɩɩra kʋkɔ dɩa.

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Ehud kɛŋ nagʋa lɛrɛ tʋʋrɛ tokobii-la sɩ mɛrɛ ʋ nadiiŋ naapuiŋ, a tɔɔ kuoru-la luoruŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ mʋa harɩŋ, kuoru-la tɩntɩnnaa kɔ, dɩ lusuŋ nyuŋ dɩa-la borusuŋ yaga. Ba bʋl, “Ʋ naga ʋ jʋʋ sɩpaaŋ dɩa-la dɩ ʋ togili nɛ.”

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Ba gbɛrɛ a dieni a lɔl, ama ʋ ha sɩ bɩ dɩa-la borusuŋ kʋŋkala suro, ba joŋ boribiiŋ a suri. Ba suro dɩ ba nɩhɩaŋ tele pɩŋ tinteeŋ a sʋʋ.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ ba gbɛrɛ ŋɩɩ, ka Ehud fa viiri. Ʋ mʋ a kieli tɔmɔ-la leriŋ a fá mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɛɩra.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Ʋ bʋla pɩba, “Má to mɩ harɩŋ, La TƖƖNA joŋ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa sɩ ŋaa ma dʋndɔmɔ a hɛ ma nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba to ʋ harɩŋ tuu a laa lere-la kala Mʋab tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ jaŋ to a chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la, ba bɩ leŋe ba nɩbala ma chol.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo dii Mʋab tɩŋŋaa nɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ tintee-la fɩɛlɛ laalɩŋ lɛ jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ banɛsɛ. Iziral sɩpaalaara Samɩga

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Sɩpaalaarʋ-la ma sɩ kɔ Ehud harɩŋ nɛ Samɩga, Anaf nanʋala. Ʋ ma laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta nɛ. Ʋ kɛŋ nɛ-daarɩ-daaŋ a kpʋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa zɔɔ-balɩdʋ nɛ.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ehud sɩ sʋba harɩŋ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩra ŋaa wʋbɔŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ.

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA leŋ Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Jabɩŋ sɩ hɛ Hazɔ lɛ aŋ bibemba yuo dii Iziral nɩaa. Ʋ laalɩyuoroo nɩhɩaŋ ma nɛ fa ŋaa Sɩsɛra a hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Harɔsɛf Hagoyim lɛ.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Sɩsɛra bʋla pɩ Jaɛl, “Chɩŋ lɛbɩ-la boiŋ niiŋ, dɩ nʋʋkala kʋʋ bal a pɩɛsɩŋ, ‘Nʋʋ hɛ daha?’ Bʋl, ‘Aɩ.’ ”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Lapɩdɔf haala Debora sɩ ŋaa Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ nɛ fa ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaara bʋa-la lɛ.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: Debora fa yie hɔŋ ʋ tɩtɩa abɛ tɩa kʋbala bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ, Rama arɩ Bɛtɛl pɛgɛ, Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa yie kɛŋ ba kaalɛrɛba kɔ ʋ teeŋ nɩmɛ, ʋ jɩma pɩpɩba.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɩma yɩrɛ Abɩnʋam nanʋala Barak sɩ lɩɩ Kɛdɛs sɩ hɛ Nafɩtalɩ tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ kɔ ʋ bʋla pʋ, “La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ, ‘Mʋ tʋɔsɛ nɩaa bʋɩ fii Nafɩtalɩ arɩ Zebuluŋ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ a laa ba sɩpaaŋ dɩ ma mʋ peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tabɔ.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ nyɩsɛ Sɩsɛra sɩ ŋaa Jabɩŋ laalɩyuoroo kʋhɩaŋ arɩ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo dɩ ba kɔ Kɩsɔŋ fuoŋ, a jomba hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Debora bʋl, “Ʋ zɔmɔ, mɩ jaŋ mʋ. Ama ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ jaŋ yuo dii Sɩsɛra, yɩrɩ-la bɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋ kʋŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA nɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ joŋu a hɛ haala nɩsɩŋ lɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Debora sii ʋ dɩ Barak mʋ Kɛdɛs.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dɩ Hɛba, Keni tɩɩna kʋbala sɩ ŋaa Hobab doho nʋʋ, a ŋaa Mosis ma bajene, lɩɩsɛ ʋ tɩtɩa Keni tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ a mʋ hɛ ʋ lɛbɩŋ a hɔŋ tɩɩ-bal kʋbala bʋbʋɔŋ, Zaananim lɛ a kpagɛ Kɛdɛs.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Ba sɩ bʋla pɩ Sɩsɛra arɩ Abɩnʋam nanʋala Barak jɩla hɔŋ peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tabɔ lɛ nɛ,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Debora bʋla pɩ Barak, “Jɩnɩŋ La TƖƖNA joŋ Sɩsɛra a hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ, ŋɩɩ wɩaa mʋ! La TƖƖNA paala laa ŋ sɩpaaŋ a mʋ nɛ dɩ ʋ yuou pɩŋ.” Barak sii peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tabɔ nyuŋ a tuu, ʋ laalɩyuoroo bʋɩ fii ma to ʋ harɩŋ.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Barak sɩ mʋa a yuyuo laal-la, La TƖƖNA leŋ Sɩsɛra arɩ ʋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba-la vɩvɛŋ arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo wɩɩkala vʋgʋmɛ. Fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ ba kʋŋkala a tɩŋ Barak arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo wɩaa. Sɩsɛra fɩla tuu ʋ jaaba toruko lɛ, a fá.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Barak laalɩyuoroo kire to Sɩsɛra janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo harɩŋ a mʋ yi taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Harɔsɛf Hagoyim, a kpʋ Sɩsɛra laalɩyuoroo kala, kʋbala ma bɩ ka.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Sɩsɛra dʋndʋŋa nɛ wuo foro fá, a mʋ jʋʋ Keni tɩŋŋaa Hɛba haala Jaɛl lɛbɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa Hazɔ kuoro Jabɩŋ arɩ Hɛba dɩa nɩaa fa ŋaa sɩma nɛ.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Jaɛl lɩɩ cheŋ Sɩsɛra a bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ nɩhɩaŋ kʋ jʋʋ, sɩ́ fawʋllʋŋ fá.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ mʋ jʋʋ ʋ lɛbɩŋ. Ʋ kɛŋ gɛrɩŋ pilime tɔʋ.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Sɩsɛra bʋl, “Lɩɩ-nyʋasʋŋ kɛmmɛ nɛ, pɩmɛ lɩɩŋ mʋa dɩ mɩ nyʋa.” Jaɛl kɛŋ nɛ-yɩlɩŋ sɩ hɛ puruŋ tʋɔŋ niiŋ kaa puri a wɛnsɛ pʋ ʋ nyʋa, ka ʋ bɩra kɛŋ gɛrɩŋ pilime tɔʋ.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Dɩ lɔlʋŋ fa kɛŋ Sɩsɛra woruŋ ʋ faasa pɩŋ doŋ. Hɛba haala Jaɛl sii joŋ lɛbɩŋ daa-pɛ-bie arɩ hama a kaa lʋara mʋ ŋmoo hɛ Sɩsɛra nyuŋ lɛ a tuu kɛŋ tinteeŋ, ʋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Barak sɩ kiri Sɩsɛra libe kʋkɔ, Jaɛl lɩɩ mʋ chemu a bʋl, “Kɔ dɩ mɩ dagɩŋ baal-la ŋ sɩ gɔllɔ chɩchɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ to ʋ harɩŋ ba jʋʋ dɩ Sɩsɛra nɛ, ba joŋ lɛbɩŋ daa-pɛ-bie ŋmoo hɛ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ ʋ sʋʋ pɩŋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa doluŋ fa pʋŋa pɩpɛ nɛ ba yuo Jabɩŋ ŋɩɩ a mʋ kpʋʋ.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ Debora arɩ Abɩnʋam nanʋala Barak yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ deeŋ:

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: “Má dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA! Iziral sɩpaalaaraa kɔ nɛ a laa sɩpaaŋ, nɩalɩŋ ma sɛɩ a to ba harɩŋ.

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Kuoroo arɩ sɩpaalaaraa, má jegile nɩɩ. Mɩ jaŋ yɩɩ yɩɩlɩŋ a du kɩaa a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa.

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA, bʋa-la lɛ ŋ sɩ lɩɩ Sɛɛ peel-la leriŋ, lee-la Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa sɩ hɔnɔ, tinteeŋ fa zigile nɛ, duonuŋ lɔgɔ jaasɛ.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Peelee fa jigise nɛ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ, peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩnaɩ ma jigisi Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Anaf nanʋala Samɩga mɩɩsɩŋ bʋa lɛ arɩ Jaɛl ma mɩɩsɩŋ bʋa lɛ, wɛŋ-vɛnnɛɛ fa vɩa womporuŋ ta nɛ, aŋ vɩvɛŋ wɛŋ-biisiŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Tabiisiŋ nɩaa fa bɩra bɩ ba bagɩsɩŋ lɛ wuo tɩŋ, a kaa mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ mɩ-na Debora sɩ sii chɩna pɔ Iziral nɩaa a nagɛ ba naaŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ kʋʋ to vesiŋ, laalɩŋ kʋ jʋʋba nɛ. Iziral nɩaa bʋɩ mahɩŋ balɩa tʋɔŋ, hɔɔtaalɩ-la laalɩyuoroo sɩ kaa kɛrɛɛ laa bayuori hɛŋŋɛɛ koo timiŋ kʋbala ma fa tuo ba teeŋ.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Mɩɩ dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA, mɩ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ Iziral laalɩyuoroo sɩpaalaara-la nyuŋ arɩ laalɩyuoro-la sɩ sɛyɛ a kɛŋ ba tɩtɩa kʋ lɩɩ dɩ ba yuo laalɩŋ.

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Má nɩalɩŋ sɩ kpɩɛrɛ kaku-pʋllʋŋ a jɩla hɔŋ kaku-kpasɩnɩŋ nyuŋ, arɩ ma nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ vɛŋ naasɩŋ lɛ,

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: má jegile nɩɩ yɩɩla-la fuo-tuuroo sɩɩ yɩɩ vilee leree. La TƖƖNA tʋɔpʋl wʋŋaalɩa-la wɩaa nɛ ba bʋbʋl ŋɩɩ, a bɩra bʋl ʋ laalɩyuoro-la sɩ hɛ Iziral ma lɛ tʋɔpʋl wʋŋaalaa wɩaa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA nɩaa sii tuu taŋ-la boi-baalaa a bʋl,

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: ‘Sii, sii, Debora! Sii, sii ta yɩɩlɩŋ! Sii, Ahɩnʋam nanʋala Barak, yuo kɛsɛ la dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ.’

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩkaana-la mɩɩra kɔ ba sɩpaalaaraa teeŋ, La TƖƖNA nɩalɩŋ mɩɩra kɔ mɩ teeŋ nɛ arɩ nɩduoruŋ a ŋaa siri dɩ ba yuo.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Dɔnsʋŋ lɩɩ Efirem nɛ a kɔ, lee-la Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ hɔnɔ. Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa ma fa kɔ nɛ. Laalɩyuoroo sɩpaalaaraa ma fa lɩɩ Makɩɩ nɛ a kʋ tuu. Tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ ma lɩɩ Zebuluŋ kɔ.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Ɩsaka doho sɩpaalaaraa fa hɛ Debora arɩ Barak teeŋ nɛ, a to ʋ harɩŋ tuu fuonaaŋ. Ama Rubiŋ doho nɩaa-na fa ha bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ ba sɩ hɛ.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Rubiŋ doho nɩaa, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma ha hɛ ma pie-dɩɩsɩŋ leree? Maa chɛ dɩ ma nɩɩ ŋɩɩ pie-daaraa sɩ fʋʋla yɩyɩrɛ ba piesee nɛ koo? Rubiŋ doho nɩaa-na fa ha bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ ba sɩ hɛ.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gɩlɩad nɩaa hɔŋ Jɔdaŋ fuoŋ cholo wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nɛ. Daŋ doho nɩaa, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma-na ha hɛ lɩɩŋ daborusuŋ lɛ? Asa doho nɩaa ma hɔnɔ ta jɩa nɛ fuoŋ niiŋ, a hɛ lɩɩŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Ama Zebuluŋ arɩ Nafɩtalɩ nɩaa joŋ ba mɩɩsɩŋ a yɔɔ sʋʋŋ nɛ laalɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Taanak lɛ, Kɛnaŋ kuoroo kɔ nɛ, ba yuo laalɩŋ a kpagɛ Mɛgɩdɔ lɩɩ-la leriŋ. Ama ba bɩ wuo paa hɔɔ-pʋla koo kʋŋkala.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Chɛnwʋlaa faa vɛŋ wɩa-nyuŋ nɛ aŋ yuyuo Sɩsɛra.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Fuo-jɩna-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kɩsɔŋ, pɛllɛ paa Sɩsɛra nɩaa viiri nɛ. Mɩ jaŋ vɛŋ, a vɛŋ arɩ doluŋ.

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ janɩŋ fɩfɩl a yɩyagɛ tinteeŋ arɩ ba naasɩŋ.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaara bʋl, ‘Kalɩba hɛ Mɛrɔzɩ nɩaa lɛ, kalɩba hɛ ba lɛ woruŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa, ba bɩ kʋ pɛ La TƖƖNA lɛ dɩ ʋ yuo dii ʋ dʋndɔmɔ-la sɩ dolie.’

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Má zil Keni tɩŋŋaa Hɛba haala Jaɛl. Haala-la kala sɩɩ jʋʋ lɛŋŋɛɛ, ba tʋɔŋ má zilu a kɩɩ ba kala.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Sɩsɛra fa sʋl lɩɩŋ nɛ ʋ teeŋ, ʋ ŋaa nɛ-yɩlɩŋ pʋ, ʋ fa ŋaa nɛyɩl-dɩndɛrɩŋ nɛ a hɛ nɩbalaa gbaŋa lɛ a pʋ.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Ʋ joŋ lɛbɩŋ daa-pɛ-bie nɛ, aŋ kɛŋ nadiiŋ ma joŋ hama. Daa-pɛ-bie-la nɛ ʋ joŋo ŋmoo pɛ Sɩsɛra nyuŋ lɛ, ʋ nyu-kuŋkogulo yɛrɛ.

english_verse: Sisera sank to his knees and fell dead at her feet.
translation_verse: Sɩsɛra nyaga sii kpirimi, aŋ tele pɩŋ nɩmɛ, a sʋʋ Jaɛl naasɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: Sɩsɛra naaŋ to tokoro a nyilimi, a ŋmoo niiŋ a bʋl, ‘Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ʋ dieni ʋ bɩ kɔ? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ʋ didieni, ka la bɩ janɩŋ torukoba dɔmɔ ka nɩɩ?’

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Ʋ dɩ haala-la sɩ jɩŋ wɩaa kala bʋbʋl wʋbala,

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: ‘Kapo ba yuo dii kɩaa nɛ aa chɛ ba kaa kpaa dɔŋɔ, dɩ baal kala na hantolibie koo hantolibiisiŋ balɩa, dɩ Sɩsɛra ma na gɛrɩ-zɔmɔ-la ba sɩ yuo dii. Ka dɩ mɩ ma laa gɛrɩ-zɔmɔ-la kala ba sɩ sʋa.’

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA, a leŋ dɩ ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ kala sʋʋ a nagɛ Sɩsɛra, aŋ leŋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ choŋ chaanɛ a nagɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa hɔŋ tintee-la lɛ arɩ fɩɛlɩŋ jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ balɩa.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩra ŋaa wʋbɔŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, ʋ jomba hɛ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ jɩsɩŋ balɩpɛ.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: A tɩŋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ aa dɔgɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ba fá jɩl peelee nyuŋ a faa bʋ-bʋɔsʋŋ arɩ leree dɔnsʋŋ.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Bʋa na-kala lɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ duu kɩaa, Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa, Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa arɩ nɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ yie kʋ jʋʋ tintee-la nɛ a yuoba,

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Ba yie kiri ba pʋsʋŋ aŋ chʋŋ ba lɛŋŋɛɛ a kʋkɔ a nagɛ hɔbɩ-laalɩŋ sɩɩ kɔ. Ŋ bɩ ba dɩ ba bʋntaŋŋaba wuo dɩɩsɛ. Ba yie tɔ tintee-la kala nɛ a cheyu.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ ŋmoo niiŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA, a tɩŋ Midiaŋ tɩmma-la wɩaa,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: Mɩ bʋla pɩma nɛ, arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ma TƖƖNA Wɩa, má sɩ́ Amɔrɩ tɩmma-la tinteeŋ lɛ ma sɩ hɔnɔ vesiŋ to, ama ma bɩ jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ.’ ”

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA tɩndaara kʋ hɔŋ piine kʋbala bʋbʋɔŋ, a hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɔfɩra lɛ. Abieza tɩɩna kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jʋas nɛ fa tɩɩ tɩa-la. Nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ bie Gɩdɩɔŋ fa faa aa ŋmoo ʋ mɛmpɛ, lee-la ba sɩɩ chagɛ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ, dɩ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa sɩ́ ʋ na.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la sɩ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kʋ dagɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ, ʋ sɩ, “Laalɩyuori-babiibal, La TƖƖNA hɛ ŋ teeŋ nɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ pɩɛsɛ, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ hɛ la teeŋ, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ wɩaa deemba kala ŋaa la lɛ? Ka wʋkpuŋkperisi-la kala wɩaa, la nyɩmmaba sɩ bʋla pɩla, nɩɩ nɛ ba hɛ? Ba sɩ sɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa nɛ kɛnla kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ kɔ, ama lɛɛlɛ La TƖƖNA vɩala ta nɛ a jonla la hɛ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Dol-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ, kaa mʋ laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Mɩ-na nɩɩ tɩmɩŋ.”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA, “Ɛɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa a laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta? Manasɛ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ, mɩ nyɩŋ-nɩa nɛ bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ. Mɩ dɩa nɩaa ma tʋɔŋ, mɩ nɛ ba kʋbie.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ jaŋ chɩŋ ŋ harɩŋ, dɩ ŋ wuo kpʋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa kala hɛ dɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ ma bɩra bʋl, “Dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ tɔrɛ mɩ nyuŋ, pɩmɛ magɩlɩŋ sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ jɩŋ arɩ ŋ-na La TƖƖNA nɛ sɛnɛɛ bʋl wɩaa mɩ teeŋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, gbɛrɛ daha dɩ mɩ mʋ kɛŋ mɩ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa kʋ pɩŋ.” La TƖƖNA bʋl, “Mɩ jaŋ gbɛrɛ dɩ ŋ mʋ aŋ kɔ.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ mʋ dɩa a kɛŋ bʋ-bie kpʋ a bɩrɩmɛ a chɔ, a magɩsɛ munuŋ kuokuo gbaŋa sɩɩŋ bʋnɔŋ a wasɛ boroboro sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ, a joŋ nammɩa-la hɛ sime lɛ, aŋ joŋ ʋ yomuŋ ma hɛ pupoiŋ tʋɔŋ, a kaa kʋ lɩɩ pʋ, piine-la bʋbʋɔŋ.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Wɩa tɩndaarʋ-la bʋla pʋ, “Joŋ nammɩa-la arɩ boroboro-la sɩ bɩ sɩbʋrʋŋ kɛnɛ a daŋ bʋŋ deeŋ nyuŋ, aŋ joŋ yoŋ-la ma bɩsɛ wurisi.” Gɩdɩɔŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ daga.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la fa kori dantɩga nɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ʋ kɛŋ dantɩga-la niiŋ a digi nammɩa-la arɩ boroboro-la. Nyiniŋ lɩɩ bʋŋ-la lɛ a joŋ nammɩa-la arɩ boroboro-la kala dii. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa tɩndaarʋ-la ma nyɩɩgɛ.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ sɩ kʋ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA tɩndaara nɛ ʋ na ŋɩɩ, fawʋllʋŋ kɛnʋ ʋ bʋl, “La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna! Mɩ na ŋ tɩndaara arɩ mɩ sɩɩŋ.”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Ama La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Hɔŋ sɔm, sɩ́ leŋe dɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛnɩŋ. Ŋ bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ saa koruŋ nɩmɛ a pɩ La TƖƖNA, a hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ ‘La TƖƖNA nɩɩ pɩla fɩɛlɩŋ’. Koru-la ha hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɔfɩra lɛ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala. Abieza tɩŋŋaa nɛ tɩɩ lee-la.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋ-la tɩtɩa nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ, “Kɛŋ ŋ nyɩmma nɛsɩŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ-bele sɩ yi jɩsɩŋ balɩpɛ. Ŋmoo ŋ nyɩmma koru-la ʋ sɩ saa pɩ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal lo, a keri vene-la ma ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daa-la sɩ chɩna kpɛrɛ Baal lo,

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: aŋ saa koruŋ dɩ ʋ zɔŋ woruŋ dundolo deeŋ nyuŋ a pɩ mɩ-na ŋ TƖƖNA Wɩa. Kɛŋ Asɩra daa-la ŋ sɩ kere lo a hɛ nyiniŋ, a kpʋ nɛ-bele-la a sʋl kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ kɛŋ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa fii ba ŋaa ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pʋ. Ama a tɩŋ ʋ fa sɩɩ fá ʋ dɩa nɩaa arɩ taŋ-la nɩaa wɩaa, ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la tɩtaŋɩŋ nɛ, wɩɩhɛyɛ dee ʋ ŋaa.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla chʋchʋɔŋ, taŋ-la nɩaa sie dɩ ba giri vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal koru-la aŋ keri Asɩra daa-la ma sɩ chɩŋ ʋ sɛmɛ lo, aŋ ka ba kpʋ nɛ-bele a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ koru-falɩɩ-la nyuŋ.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Ba pɩɛsɛ dɔŋɔ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ?” Ba sɩ fɩɛlɛ sɩaa aŋ kpɛrɛ pɩɛsɛ, nʋʋ bʋla pɩba, “Jʋas nanʋala Gɩdɩɔŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ taŋ-la nɩaa bʋla pɩ Jʋas, “Kɛŋ ŋ nanʋala Gɩdɩɔŋ kaa kʋ lɩɩ, ʋ maga la kpʋʋ nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ giri Baal koruŋ nɛ aŋ keri Asɩra daa-la ma sɩ chɩŋ ʋ sɛmɛ lo.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Jʋas ma pɩɛsɛ nɩ-daŋ-la sɩ na baanɩŋ a gollu, “Maa chɛ dɩ ma laa Baal yuosuŋ a yuo nɛɛ? Ma chɩna ma laa pɛ ʋ lɛ nɛɛ? Nɩɩ-la kala sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ laa Baal yuosuŋ a yuo, ʋ maga dɩ ba kpʋʋ nɛ chʋchʋɔŋ! Dɩ Baal nɛ sɛnɛ ŋaa veŋ-tɩtɩɩ, ʋ koruŋ nɛ ba giri, ʋ maga ʋ nɛ laa ʋ tɩtɩa ta.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ ba mɩɩra kɛŋ Gɩdɩɔŋ a yɩyɩrɛ ‘Jerub-Baal’, aŋ bʋl, “Má leŋ dɩ Baal yuou, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ koruŋ nɛ ʋ giri.”

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa, Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ, ba chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la a ŋmoo buguŋ Jɛzɩrɛl fuonaaŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA Dɩma kʋ jʋʋ Gɩdɩɔŋ, ʋ ŋmʋʋ banyile a yɩrɛ Abieza tɩŋŋaa kala dɩ ba kʋ to ʋ harɩŋ,

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: aŋ tɩma yɩrɛ Manasɛ doho nɩaa, Asa, Zebuluŋ arɩ Nafɩtalɩ doho nɩaa kala, ba nyɩgɩlɛ a kʋ chemba.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: na pie-pʋnaa nɛ mɩ joŋo bil taha tʋɔŋ ŋ-la, dɩ taŋ nɛ pʋla dɩ nyalɩŋ nyal a kɛŋ pie-pʋna-la dʋndʋŋa ka dɩ tinteeŋ hɩl, mɩ jɩma ŋ sɛnɛ jaŋ to mɩ lɛ nɛ a laaba ta, arɩ ŋ sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ ŋaa. Gɩdɩɔŋ sii joŋ pie-pʋna-la, a chagɛ ba nyalɩŋ lɩɩŋ a su gbaŋa.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ bɩra bʋla pɩ Wɩa, “Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ŋ baanɩŋ sii mɩ nyuŋ. Leŋ dɩ mɩ bɩra magɩsɩŋ bala arɩ pie-pʋna-la. Bʋa deeŋ lɛ leŋ dɩ pie-pʋna-la hɩl, aŋ ka dɩ tinteeŋ kala tɔ arɩ nyalɩŋ.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋ-la ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ Wɩa ŋaa, pie-pʋna-la dʋndʋŋa nɛ hɩla, aŋ ka tinteeŋ kala tɔ nyalɩŋ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, Jerub-Baal arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala sii a mʋ ŋmoo buguŋ Harɔd lɩɩ-bulo leriŋ. Ka Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa ma hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa fuonaaŋ lɛ a kpagɛ Mɔrɛ dundolo-la.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ, “Ŋ laalɩyuoro-la yʋga nɛ arɩ mɩ sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma yuo dii Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa. Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa jaŋ bɩɩnɛ arɩ ba tɩtɩa nɛ yuo dii laal-la. Ba bɩ jaŋ joŋ yɩrɩŋ pɩmɛ.

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, heele bʋla pɩ laalɩyuoroo kala, ‘Nɩɩ-la kala fawʋllʋŋ sɩ kɛnɛ, ʋ jaŋ wuo chɩŋ Gɩlɩad peel-la lɛ a mɩɩra mʋ dɩa.’ ” Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩaa bʋɩ mara arɩ balɩa mɩɩrɛ, aŋ ka nɩaa bʋɩ fii.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Dɩ fawʋllʋŋ nɛ kɛnɩŋ arɩ ŋ sɩ jaŋ mʋ yuoba, kɛŋ ŋ tɩntɩnna ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Pʋra dɩ ma lʋara mʋ ba buguŋ,

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bɩra bʋla pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ, “Ŋ nɩalɩŋ ha yʋga nɛ. Kɛmba tuu lɩɩŋ leriŋ, mɩ jaŋ kɛmba pɔrɔ pɩŋ nɩmɛ. Dɩ mɩ nɛ sɩ, ‘Nɩa deeŋ jaŋ to ŋ harɩŋ mʋ,’ ʋ jaŋ mʋ, ama dɩ mɩ nɛ sɩ, ‘Nɩa deeŋ bɩ jaŋ to ŋ harɩŋ mʋ,’ ʋ bɩ jaŋ mʋ.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ kɛŋ laalɩyuoro-la kala ba tuu lɩɩ-la leriŋ. Nɩmɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ chu nyʋnyʋa lɩɩ-la a nagɛ vaha, a pɔrɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kpirime a kɛŋ nɩsɩŋ ŋaa nyʋnyʋa lɛ.”

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Nɩaa zɔɔ-batori nɛ fa kɛŋ nɩsaa a ŋaa lɩɩ-la nyʋnyʋa. Ka nɩkaanaa ma kala kpirimi a chu nyʋnyʋa.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ, “Nɩalɩŋ zɔɔ-batori sɩ kɛŋ nɩsaa ŋaa lɩɩ-la nyʋa, ŋ dɩ ba nɛ mɩ jaŋ kaa laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma yuo diiba. Leŋ dɩ nɩkaana-la kala mɩɩra mʋ ba dɩɩsɩŋ.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋɩŋ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ, “Má sii tuu yuo Midiaŋ tɩmma-la ba dɩhɔnʋŋ. Mɩ jaŋ jomba hɛ ma nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: a nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩɩ bʋl. Dɩ ŋ nɛ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ, ŋ nyuŋ jaŋ duori dɩ ŋ wuo yuoba.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ sii kɛŋ ʋ tɩntɩnna Pʋra ba mʋ ba dʋndɔmɔ-la dɩhɔnʋŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Dɩ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa, Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa arɩ nɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ kala sɩ lɩɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ hɔnɔ su fuonaa-la kala a nagɛ hɔbɔ sɩ su leriŋ. Ba bʋntaŋŋaba ma yʋgɛ woruŋ a nagɛ hagɩlɩ-bumbugulo sɩ pɩŋ mʋgʋ-balɩŋ niiŋ, ŋ bɩ ba wuo dɩɩsɛ.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ sɩ mʋ yi Midiaŋ laalɩyuoro-la buguŋ, ʋ nɩa dɩ ba dɔŋɔ bʋl ʋ sɩ duoso wɩaa a pɩpɩ ʋ nandɔŋɔ. Ʋ sɩ, “Mɩ duoso na boroboro gulumuŋ ba sɩ kɛŋ mɩaa ŋaa dɩ ʋ bilime kʋ jʋʋ la buguŋ arɩ doluŋ a yɩ lɛbɩŋ, ʋ tel a bɩrɩma chu.”

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Ʋ nandɔŋ-la bʋla pʋ, “Ŋ duoso-la mʋ tɩgɛ Jʋas nanʋala Gɩdɩɔŋ lɛ nɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoroo nɩhɩaŋ-la. Wɩa joŋ la Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa arɩ la laalɩyuoroo kala a hɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ sɩ nɩɩ duoso-la arɩ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ dagɛ ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ, ʋ dɛnnɛ Wɩa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ mɩɩra mʋ ba Iziral tɩŋŋaa buguŋ aŋ kpɩa, “Má sii la mʋ! La TƖƖNA joŋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoroo kala a hɛ la nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Dɩ mɩ dɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩɩ to mɩ harɩŋ nɛ ŋmʋʋ la banyilliŋ, ma nɩkaana-la sɩ golli ba dɩhɔnʋŋ chu, má ma ŋmʋʋ ma kɩaa, aŋ ŋaa goŋ a bʋl, ‘Má yuo laalɩŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA, má yuo laalɩŋ pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ.’ ”

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ zɔlɔ sɩɩ to ʋ harɩŋ mʋ yi Midiaŋ tɩmma-la buguŋ niiŋ tɩta-siesee nɛ, dɩ nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ kʋ laa nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔba lɛ, a pɔ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba ŋmʋʋ banyilliŋ aŋ joŋ ba tagɩsɩ-la ba sɩ koro a yaga yɛrɛ.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ laalɩyuori-kaana-la bʋbʋɔ-bugoo balɩa ma ŋmʋʋ banyilli-la ba sɩ koro ba nadiiŋ nɩsaa lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ joŋ tagɩsɩ-la ba ma sɩ koro yaga yɛrɛ, aŋ kori tʋʋ-diiri kapɩla-la arɩ nyiniŋ ba nagʋa nɩsaa lɛ, aŋ kala ŋaa goŋ a bʋl, “Má yuo laalɩŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA, má yuo laalɩŋ pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ.”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Ka ba kʋŋkala chɩŋ ʋ dɩchɩnɩŋ a golli Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa buguŋ a chu, Midiaŋ tɩmma-la kala fá, aŋ ŋmuŋmoo niiŋ.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ ŋmʋʋ banyilli-la kala zɔɔ-batori, La TƖƖNA leŋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoroo chaarɛ tokobiee a gʋra yuyuo dɔŋɔ ba buguŋ lɛ. Laalɩyuoro-la fá mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛf Sɩta a tʋʋlɛ Zɛrɛra fuonaaŋ a mʋ yi taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Abɛl Mehola sɩ kpagɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tabaf.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ, ba yɩrɛ Iziral laalɩyuoro-la kala sɩ lɩɩ Nafɩtalɩ, Asa arɩ Manasɛ doho doho, ba kʋ kire to Midiaŋ tɩmma-la harɩŋ.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Ka Gɩdɩɔŋ tɩŋ nɩaa ba mʋ laalɩyuoroo sɩ hɛ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ teeŋ a bʋl, “Má sii kʋ tuu a yuo Midiaŋ tɩmma-la, má pɔ Jɔdaŋ fuo-la arɩ fuonu-la kala a kɛŋ ŋɩɩ mʋ yi lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛf Bara dɩ Midiaŋ tɩmma-la sɩ chol.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Efirem laalɩyuoro-la kala ba fa sɩ yɩra kɔ, a chɩna pɔ fuonu-la kala a kaa mʋ yi Bɛf Bara.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Ba ha bɩra yuo kɛŋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa ma balɩa nɛ baa yɩrɛ, Ɔrɛb arɩ Zɛɛb. Ba kpʋ Ɔrɛb bʋŋ-la ba lɛɛlɛ sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɔrɛb lɛ nɛ, aŋ kpʋ Zɛɛb ma lee-la ba sɩɩ chagɛ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ ba lɛɛlɛ sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zɛɛb. Ba ha kire to Midiaŋ tɩmma-la harɩŋ nɛ, aŋ kɛŋ Ɔrɛb arɩ Zɛɛb nyusuŋ kaa kʋ pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ, dɩ ʋ fa hɛ Jɔdaŋ fuo-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ nɛ Efirem tɩŋŋaa pɩɛsɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ ŋaala ŋ-la? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ yuo Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa ŋ bɩ la yɩra?” Ba chaasa bʋl ʋ teeŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Ama Gɩdɩɔŋ bʋla pɩba, “Wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ ŋaa, nʋʋ jaŋ wuo kɛnʋ a magɩsɛ wɩalɩŋ ma sɩ ŋaa? Ma Efirem tɩŋŋaa sɩ ŋaa wʋbie-la nɛ paala kɩɩ wɩɩ-la mɩ nyɩŋ-nɩaa kala sɩ ŋaa.

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Wɩa paala leŋ ma kpʋ Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa Ɔrɛb arɩ Zɛɛb nɛ. Wʋbɛɛ nɛ mɩ ma ŋaa ʋ magɛ wɩɩ-la ma sɩ ŋaa?” Ʋ sɩ bʋl wɩɩŋ deeŋ, baaŋ-la ba fa sɩ na ʋ nyuŋ fɩɛlɛ.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: Dɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sʋkɔf kpagɛ nɩmɛ. Gɩdɩɔŋ mʋ a bʋla pɩ Sʋkɔf nɩaa, “Má pɩ mɩ laalɩyuoro-la kʋdiilee mʋa, ba lɔlɔ nɛ, ka mɩ haa kikiri Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna sɩ ŋaa Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa kuoroo.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Sʋkɔf tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ pɩɛsɛ, “Ŋ ha bɩ Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna kɛsɛ, bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ ŋ chɩchɛ dɩ la pɩ ŋ laalɩyuoroo kʋdiilee?”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ bʋl, “Ʋ maga, dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ leŋe mɩ yuo dii Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna, mɩ jaŋ mɩɩra kɔ ma lɛ, a vɩɩrɛma arɩ sɔ-fɩaŋ-mie arɩ lɔgɔdɩnlɔgɔ, dɩ ma yaraa kala bɩɛlɛ.”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ lɩɩ, a joŋo mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Pɛnɩɛl, a sʋl kʋdiilee ba ma teeŋ. Ba ma bʋl wɩɩ-la tɩtɩa Sʋkɔf nɩaa fa sɩ bʋla.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩ Pɛnɩɛl tɩmma-la ma, “Dɩ mɩ nɛ yuo diiba aŋ mɩɩra kɔ, mɩ jaŋ ŋmoo ma dɩɩ-leŋiŋ deeŋ lo.”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ mʋ Sʋkɔf nɩaa teeŋ a bʋl, “Má na Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna nɛ ŋ-la, nɩalɩŋ wɩaa ma fa sɩ sieri mɩ lɛ a bʋl, ‘Ŋ ha bɩ Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna kɛsɛ, bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ ŋ chɩchɛ dɩ la pɩ ŋ laalɩyuoro-la sɩ lɔlɔ kʋdiilee?’ ”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ to tintee-hɩlɩŋ niiŋ nɛ a mʋ jʋʋ ʋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ dɩhɔnʋŋ sɩ hɛ tasɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nɔba arɩ Jogbeha wɩɩpɔsʋŋ a yuo dɩ ba lɛ.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Midiaŋ kuorusu-la balɩa, Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna fá, ama ʋ kire kɛsɛba, aŋ yuo dii ba laalɩyuoroo kala.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ, Jʋas nanʋala sɩ mɩɩra lɩɩ laalɩŋ kʋkɔ, ʋ to wombii-bie-la sɩ hɛ peelee tʋɔŋ Hɛrɛs lɛ nɛ,

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ kɛŋ bapʋɔsɩ-bie kʋbala sɩ lɩɩ Sʋkɔf a pɩɛsʋ wɩaa. Ʋ ŋmʋnsɛ Sʋkɔf tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ mahɩŋ batori arɩ fii arɩ balɩpɛ yɩraa pʋ.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Aŋ kɛsɛ Sʋkɔf nɩhɩasɩ-la a dɔgɩsɛba woruŋ arɩ sɔ-fɩaŋ-mie arɩ lɔgɔdɩnlɔgɔ.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: Ʋ ha bɩra mʋ Pɛnɩɛl ma a ŋmoo ʋ dɩɩ-leŋii-la a lo, aŋ kpʋ baala-la sɩ hɛ taŋ-la lɛ.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ pɩɛsɛ Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna, “Nɩbɛɛ ba doho nɛ ma kpʋ Tabɔ lɛ?” Ba bʋl, “Ba nagɛ ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ naga nɛ, ba kʋŋkala nagɛ kuoru-bii nɛ.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ bʋl, “Ba kala ŋaa mɩ naambiiriŋ nɛ, mɩ naaŋ tɩtɩa bii-lʋlaa nɛ, La TƖƖNA sɩ weye yɩrɩŋ lɛ, dɩ ma nɛ fa bɩ ba kpʋa, mɩ ma bɩ jaŋ kpʋma.”

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ bʋla pɩ ʋ hambolibii-hɩaŋ Jɛta, “Sii kpʋba!” Ama Jɛta fa sɩ ŋaa hambie ŋɩɩ, ʋ bɩ bɔyɛ kɛnɛ arɩ ʋ sɩ jaŋ kpʋba.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna bʋl, “Ŋ tɩtɩa kʋ kpʋla. Baala sɩ yi ŋɩɩ, ʋ doluŋ ma yi ŋɩɩ nɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gɩdɩɔŋ sii a kpʋ Zɛba arɩ Zalɩmʋna, aŋ chaarɛ kpɩɛra-la fa sɩ hɛ ba bʋntaŋŋaba baŋŋaa lɛ. Gɩdɩɔŋ gɛrɩ-laala-daŋɩŋ

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Laalɩŋ sɩ dɛrɛ harɩŋ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa bʋla pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ, “Ŋ nɛ sɩ laala ta Midiaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ ŋɩɩ, ŋaa la kuoro, dɩ ŋ nɛ kʋ tuo, dɩ ŋ nanʋala ma bɩra ŋaa la kuoro, dɩ ʋ ma nɛ kʋ tuo, dɩ ŋ nihiŋ ma bɩra dii la kuoruŋ.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ bʋla pɩba, “Mɩ bɩ jaŋ ŋaa ma kuoro, mɩ nanʋala ma bɩ jaŋ dii ma kuoruŋ, La TƖƖNA nɛ jaŋ ŋaa ma kuoro.”

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ bɩra bʋla pɩba, “Wɩɩ-la kala mɩ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ma ŋaa pɩmɛ nɛ, kɩalɩŋ ma sɩ yuo laa laalɩŋ lɛ a kaa kpaa tʋɔŋ, má kʋŋkala tʋɔsɛ sɛlɩmɛ dɩgɩlɩŋ-kpɛnsɩŋ pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Ba bʋl, “La tʋɔŋ tɔrɔ nɛ, la jaŋ pɩŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ joŋ gɛrɩŋ jɛrɛ, ba kʋŋkala tʋɔsɛ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ yuo dii tʋɔŋ dɩgɩlɩŋ-kpɛnsɩŋ a joŋo lo hɛ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Haal-la ma ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa, aŋ leŋ ʋ hɔŋ Sɛkɛm lɛ, ʋ ma fa lʋl hambolibie nɛ a pʋ, ʋ hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Abɩmɛlɛk.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Jʋas nanʋala Gɩdɩɔŋ fa hɩɛsa nɛ woruŋ aŋ sʋʋ. Ba hugu ʋ nyɩmma Jʋas bʋa-la sɩ hɛ Ɔpɩra lɛ, Abieza tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Gɩdɩɔŋ sʋʋŋ harɩŋ lɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩra mɩɩra tuto vesi-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal nɛ, a joŋ Baal Bɛrɩf ʋ ŋaa ba vene ba kpʋkpaarɛ,

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: aŋ yʋ ba TƖƖNA Wɩa sɩ laaba ta ba dʋndɔmɔ-la kala sɩ golliba nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Ba bɩra bɩ Jeru-Baal dɩa nɩaa maa zil, arɩ ʋ sɩ ŋaa wʋzɔmɔ-la kala pɩba ma.

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Ʋ naaŋ dɩbaalaa sɩ bʋl wɩɩŋ deeŋ a pɩ Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa kala, ba kala sɛɩ dɩ ba to Abɩmɛlɛk harɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa, ba sɩ́, “Ʋ ŋaa la naambii nɛ.”

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Ʋ sii kɛmba ba mʋ ʋ nyɩmma dɩa Ɔpɩra lɛ, a kpʋ ʋ nyɩmma Gɩdɩɔŋ hambolibiisi-la mahɩŋ batori arɩ fii kala sɩ ŋaa ʋ naambiiriŋ, tabɩɩ-bala nyuŋ. Ba tʋɔŋ kʋbie ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jotam dʋndʋŋa nɛ wuo faa, ʋ bɩ ʋ na.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa arɩ Bɛf Milo nɩaa kala kʋ hilimi tɩɩ-bal kʋbala bʋbʋɔŋ sɩ chɩna kpagɛ jebii kʋbala sɩ hɛ Sɛkɛm lɛ, dɩ ba bil Abɩmɛlɛk kuoruŋ.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ bʋl wɩɩŋ deeŋ a pɩ Jotam, ʋ sii jɩl peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gɛrɩzɩm nyuŋ aŋ ŋaa goŋ a bʋl, “Sɛkɛm tɩmma, má jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ, dɩ Wɩa ma wuo jegile nɩɩ ma teeŋ.

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala nɛ tɩɩsɩŋ kala sii dɩ ba lɩɩsɛ ba kuoro. Ba bʋla pɩ Olif tɩa, ‘Ŋaa la kuoro.’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Olif tɩa-la ma bʋl, ‘Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ mɩ leŋ mɩ nʋʋ-la ba sɩ kaa zizil vesiŋ arɩ nuhuobiine kala ta aŋ kʋ bibeŋ tɩɩsɩŋ.’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Tɩɩsɩ-la bɩra bʋla pɩ tutogo ma, ‘Kʋ ŋaa la kuoro.’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Tutogo-la ma bɩra bʋl, ‘Ʋ bɩ maga mɩ leŋ mɩ nɛnɛ-la sɩ zɔmɔ aŋ sɩŋ ta aŋ kʋ bibeŋ tɩɩsɩŋ.’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩsɩ-la bɩra bʋla pɩ girep tɩa, ‘Kʋ ŋaa la kuoro.’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Girep tɩa-la ma bʋl, ‘Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ mɩ leŋ mɩ nɛŋ-sɩma-la sɩnɩŋ sɩ leŋe vesiŋ arɩ nuhuobiinee tʋɔŋ tʋtɔrɛ ta, aŋ kʋ bibeŋ tɩɩsɩŋ.’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Dɩdɛrɩŋ, tɩɩsɩ-la bʋla pɩ chɛɛŋ, ‘Kʋ ŋaa la kuoro.’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Chɛɛ-la bʋla pɩ tɩɩsɩ-la, ‘Dɩ ma nɛ sɛnɛɛ chɛ dɩ ma leŋ dɩ mɩ ŋaa ma kuoro, má kʋ jʋʋ mɩ fɩɛlɩŋ dɩ mɩ tɔ hɛ ma lɛ, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, nyiniŋ jaŋ lɩɩ mɩ lɛ a joŋ kuolu tɩɩsɩ-la kala sɩ hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ lɛ a dii.’

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Ama jɩnɩŋ ma sii chɩŋ mɩ nyɩmma dɩa nɩaa lɛ nɛ a kpʋ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ mahɩŋ batori arɩ fii tabɩɩ bala nyuŋ. Abɩmɛlɛk ŋaa mɩ nyɩmma yoŋ-haala bie nɛ. Ama a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa ma naambii wɩaa, ma leŋe ʋ dii Sɛkɛm kuoruŋ nɛ.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ fa to wʋtɩtɩɩ bʋa a ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga a pɩ Gɩdɩɔŋ arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa, ŋɩɩ-na a leŋ ma dɩ Abɩmɛlɛk pɛgɛ wɩaa vɩvɛŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ ma nɛ bɩ woruŋ ŋaa, Abɩmɛlɛk jaŋ nagɛ nyiniŋ a joŋ ma Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa arɩ Bɛf Milo nɩaa dii, dɩ ma Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa arɩ Bɛf Milo nɩaa ma nagɛ nyiniŋ a joŋ Abɩmɛlɛk dii.”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jotam fá, a mʋ hɛ taŋ kʋbala lɛ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa fawʋllʋŋ fa kɛnʋ nɛ a tɩŋ ʋ naambie Abɩmɛlɛk wɩaa.

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Abɩmɛlɛk sɩ beŋ Iziral nɩaa jɩsɩŋ batori,

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa hɛ nɩaa nɛ ba mʋ faa dundolluŋ nyuŋ dɩ ba kɛŋ Abɩmɛlɛk, dɩ nʋʋkala ma nɛ kʋ to lee-la a mʋmʋ, ba yie kɛŋ tɩɩna nɛ a laa ʋ kɩaa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ nʋʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la pɩ Abɩmɛlɛk.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala Ɛbɛd nanʋala Gaal sii a kɛŋ ʋ naambiiriŋ ba mʋ Sɛkɛm. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa laaʋ dii woruŋ.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Tɩɩ-nɛnɛ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ girep tɔrʋŋ sɩ yie, Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa kala lɩɩ mʋ ba tɩɩnɛnɛɛ bagɩsɩŋ, a tɔrɔ paa hɛ bʋɔsʋŋ lɛ a chagɛ ba lɩɩŋ a kaa ŋaa sɩnɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba jʋʋ ba vene dɩa a gbigbieli, a dii kɩaa aŋ nyʋnyʋa kɩaa, aŋ tʋtʋʋsɛ Abɩmɛlɛk.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Gaal Ɛbɛd nanʋala pɩɛsɛ, “Abɩmɛlɛk nɛ kʋbɛɛ, a magɛ la Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa tutou? Ʋ ŋaa Jeru-Baal nanʋala nɛ, Zebul ma nɩɩ tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ kuoruŋ lɛ. Má tɩma pɩpɩ ma naabalɩma Hamɔ doho nɩaa. Hamɔ nɛ ŋaa Sɛkɛm nyɩmma. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ la jaŋ tɩma pɩpɩ Abɩmɛlɛk?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Dɩ mɩ nɛ fa ŋaa Sɛkɛm nɩaa laalɩyuoru-hɩaŋ, mɩ fa jaŋ kiri Abɩmɛlɛk. Mɩ jaŋ bʋla pʋ, ‘Kɛŋ ŋ laalɩyuoroo kala hɛ dɔŋɔ a kɔ dɩ la yuo laalɩŋ.’ ”

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Zebul, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ taŋ-la sɩ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la Ɛbɛd nanʋala Gaal sɩ bʋla, ʋ faasa na baanɩŋ.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, tɩtaŋɩŋ ʋ maga dɩ ŋ kɛŋ ŋ laalɩyuoroo dɩ ma kʋ faa pɔkɔŋ nyuŋ nɛ a gbɛrɛ.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Dɩ taŋ nɛ pʋla chʋchʋɔŋ dɩ wɩɩ-muluŋ pɔsɔɔ lɩɩ, má sii guu mʋ a yuo taŋ-la. Dɩ Gaal arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo nɛ kʋ lɩɩ dɩ ba yuoma, má ŋaaba wɩɩ na-kala ma sɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩmɛlɛk kɛŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala kpaa leree banɛsɛ, ba sii tɩtaŋɩŋ a mʋ faa a kpagɛ Sɛkɛm dɩ ba yuoba.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Ɛbɛd nanʋala Gaal lɩɩ a chɩŋ ba taŋ boi-baal-la ba sɩ to jʋjʋʋ taŋ-la, dɩ Abɩmɛlɛk arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo sii lere-la ba sɩ faa a kʋʋ lɩɩ.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Gaal sɩ naba, ʋ bʋla pɩ Zebul, “Bee na, nɩaa nɛ lɩɩ peelee nyuŋ kʋʋ tuu!” Zebul bʋl, “Nɩaa dee, peelee daaliimee nɛ ŋ na ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Gaal bɩra bʋl: “Bee na, nɩaa nɛ lɩɩ peelee nyuŋ a kʋʋ tuu ŋɩɩ, ka dɔnsʋŋ ma lɩɩ vʋgʋraa tɩa-la leriŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a kʋkɔ.”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Zebul bɩra bʋla pʋ, “Nɩɩ nɛ ŋ wʋbala-la kala ŋ sɩ bʋla hɛ lɛɛlɛ? Ŋ sɩ, ‘Kʋbɛɛ nɛ Abɩmɛlɛk a magɛ dɩ la tutou?’ Nɩaa deemba lɛ dee ŋ sieri ŋɩɩ? Saa lɩɩ yuoba.”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gaal kɛsɛ Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ ba yuo Abɩmɛlɛk.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Abɩmɛlɛk kiru ʋ fá, ka ba bolimi nɩaa woruŋ laal-la lɛ. Ba kiriba ŋɩɩ nɛ halɩɩ a mʋ yi ba jaŋ boi-baalɩŋ.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Abɩmɛlɛk hɔŋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Aruma lɛ nɛ a kpagɛ Sɛkɛm, ka Zebul kiri Gaal arɩ ʋ naambiiriŋ kala ba lɩɩ Sɛkɛm lɛ.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla Sɛkɛm nɩaa kala ŋaa siri dɩ ba lɩɩ mʋ bagɩsɩŋ, nʋʋ dɔŋ kʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la pɩ Abɩmɛlɛk.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Ʋ sii kɛŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kpaa leree batori ba lɩɩ faa pɔkɔŋ nyuŋ a gbɛrɛ. Ba sɩ na nɩalɩŋ dɩ ba lɩɩ taŋ tʋɔŋ a kʋkɔ, ba sii lere-la ba sɩ faa dɩ ba yuoba.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abɩmɛlɛk arɩ laalɩyuoro-la dɔnsʋŋ guu fá mʋ pɔ ba taŋ boi-baalɩŋ. Laalɩyuoro-la bugoo balɩa-la ma guu mʋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ bagɩsɩŋ lɛ a kpʋba.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la kala Abɩmɛlɛk pɛsɛ taŋ-la lɛ ŋɩɩ nɛ halɩɩ a yuo laaʋ, a kpʋ nɩalɩŋ kala. Ʋ sɩ chei taŋ-la dɛrɛ, ʋ joŋ yɩsɩŋ mɩsɛ ʋ kala.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Sɩpaalaara-la sɩ hɛ Sɛkɛm dɩɩ-leŋii-la lɛ sɩ nɩɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ba sii fá jʋʋ ba vene Ɛl-Bɛrɩf dɩa sɩpaaŋ a faa.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Abɩmɛlɛk sɩ nɩa dɩ ba kala hilimi nɩmɛ,

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩaa kala sii jɩl peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zalɩmɔŋ. Abɩmɛlɛk joŋ saaŋ a mʋ keri tɩɩ-naakelee a paa baasɛ, aŋ bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ ma kala, “Má ŋaa lɩma, a ŋaa wɩɩ-la ma sɩ na dɩ mɩɩ ŋaa.”

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baala-la ma kala keri tɩɩ-naakelee a baasa tuto ʋ harɩŋ. Ba kaa mʋ faara tɔ dɩa-la tʋɔŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ jʋʋ faa, a joŋ nyiniŋ hɛ ʋ dii nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ. Nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ jʋʋ faa Sɛkɛm dɩɩ-leŋii-la tʋɔŋ, baalaa arɩ haalaa kala yi bʋɩ nɛ a kala sʋʋ.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ Abɩmɛlɛk bɩra mʋ golli Tɛbɛs chu a yuo diiu.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Taŋ-la tʋtʋɔbaanɩŋ, dɩɩ-leŋii kʋbala nɛ fa chɩŋ nɩmɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ taŋ-la baalaa arɩ haalaa kala jʋʋ faa ʋ tʋɔŋ. Ba kɛŋ boiŋ tɔ a hɛ ba tɩtɩa lɛ, aŋ kiele jɩla hɔŋ dɩa-la nyuŋ.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Abɩmɛlɛk arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo sɩ mʋa a wʋwalɩmɛ dɩ ba jʋʋ dɩɩ-leŋii-la, Abɩmɛlɛk tɩtɩa nɩnɛrɩgɛ dɩ ʋ nyɩgɛ dɩa-la borusuŋ.

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, haal kʋbala joŋ nɔŋ-biiŋ yuo ta ʋ lɩɩ dɩa-la nyuŋ kʋ tuu yagɛ Abɩmɛlɛk nyuŋ yɛrɛ.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩmɛlɛk guu yɩrɛ laalɩyuoru-la sɩɩ kori ʋ laalɩyuori kɩaa, a bʋla pʋ, “Lɩɩsɛ ŋ tokobiiŋ a kpʋmɛ, dɩ nɩaa sɩ́ bʋl arɩ haala nɛ kpʋmɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ laalɩyuoru-la lɩɩsɛ tokobiiŋ tɔɔ Abɩmɛlɛk ʋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ na dɩ Abɩmɛlɛk sʋba, ba mɩɩra mʋ dɩa.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Wɩa sɩ to ŋɩɩ a tiŋ nɩbɔŋ wɩalɩŋ Abɩmɛlɛk sɩ ŋaa ʋ nyɩmma dɩa lɛ, a kpʋ ʋ naambiiriŋ mahɩŋ batori arɩ fii-la chɩmɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Wɩa ha bɩra joŋ nɩbɔŋ wɩalɩŋ Sɛkɛm tɩŋŋaa ma sɩ ŋaa chɩmɩŋ a tiŋ ba lɛ nɛ. Gɩdɩɔŋ nanʋala Jotam ŋmɩaŋ-la sɛnɛ diiba nɛ.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Abɩmɛlɛk sʋʋŋ harɩŋ, Pʋa nanʋala Tola sɩ ŋaa Dodo nihiŋ ma nɛ bɩra laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta. Ʋ fa ŋaa Ɩsaka doho nʋʋ nɛ, aŋ hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Samɩɩ sɩ hɛ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Gɩlɩad tɩŋŋaa Jaa ma nɛ bɩra tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ. Ʋ ma laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ balɩa nɛ.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Jaa sɩ sʋba, ba hugu taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kamɔŋ lɛ nɛ. Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa dɔgɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: ʋ na baanɩŋ ba nyuŋ, a jomba hɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa arɩ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: So the same year that Jair died, Israel's army was crushed by these two nations. For
translation_verse: Jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ chori, ba dɔgɩsɛ Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ hɛ Jɔdaŋ fuo-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ Gɩlɩad tinteeŋ lɛ. Gɩlɩad fa ŋaa Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ nɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Gɩlɩad tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa bʋla pɩ dɔŋɔ, “Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ wuo laa sɩpaaŋ la yuo Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa, tɩɩna nɛ jaŋ ŋaa nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɔŋ Gɩlɩad lɛ nɩhɩaŋ.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa ma chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la dɩ ba yuo Juda, Bɛnjamɩŋ arɩ Efirem doho nɩaa, hɛɛŋ chaasa jʋʋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋmoo niiŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA, a bʋl, “La ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ ŋ teeŋ, la sɩ vɩa la Wɩa aŋ tuto vesi-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal.”

english_verse: The Lord answered: In the past when you came crying to me for help, I rescued you. At one time or another I've rescued you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines, the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites.
translation_verse: Sɩdɔŋ tɩŋŋaa, Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa arɩ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa sɩɩ dɔgɩsɛma, ma ŋmoo niiŋ pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ pɛ ma lɛ, mɩ bɩ ma laa ta ba nɩsɩŋ lɛɛ?
