english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Má mʋ ŋmoo niiŋ a pɩ vesi-la ma sɩɩ to. Má leŋ dɩ ba laama ta, dɩ wɩaa nɛ jʋʋma.”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma-la bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA, “La ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ. Wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩɩ chɛ, ŋaa la lɛ, ama lɛɛlɛ laa sʋlʋŋ laala ta.”

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba joŋ vesi-la sɩ hɛ ba teeŋ ta, aŋ tuto La TƖƖNA. Ʋ chaasa fá ba nenige. Ʋ bɩra bɩ leŋe ba na hɛɛŋ.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa sɩ yɩrɛ ba laalɩyuoroo kʋ ŋmoo buguŋ Gɩlɩad tinteeŋ lɛ, Iziral laalɩyuoroo ma kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ a ŋmoo buguŋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɩzɩpa lɛ.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ba bʋla pʋ, “Kʋ laa la sɩpaaŋ dɩ la mʋ yuo Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa.”

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta pɩɛsɛba, “Ma sɩ bɩ mɩ cho dee bɩ tɩɩ ma kirimi ta mɩ nyɩmma dɩa lɛɛ? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ wɩaa jʋʋma lɛɛlɛ ma chɩchɛ mɩ leriŋ?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Gɩlɩad nɩhɩasɩ-la bɩra bʋl, “La mɩɩra kɔ ŋ teeŋ nɛ lɛɛlɛ, dɩ ŋ kɔ la mʋ yuo Amɔŋ tɩmma-la, ka dɩ ŋ ŋaa la nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ Gɩlɩad tinteeŋ lɛ nɩhɩaŋ.”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jɛfɩta bɩra pɩɛsɛ, “Dɩ ma nɛ kɛmmɛ mɩɩra mʋ dɩ la yuo Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa, dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ jomba hɛ mɩ nɩsɩŋ lɛ, mɩ sɛnɛ jaŋ ŋaa ma tinteeŋ nɩhɩaŋ a bibemmaa?”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Gɩlɩad nɩhɩasɩ-la bʋl, “La TƖƖNA nɛ pɛ na wɩɩŋ deeŋ, wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ bʋla, la sɛnɛ jaŋ ŋaa.”

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta to Gɩlɩad nɩhɩasɩ-la harɩŋ ba mʋ, nɩalɩŋ leŋ ʋ ŋaa ba nɩhɩaŋ arɩ ba laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ. Wɩalɩŋ ʋ fa sɩ bʋla, ʋ bɩra wasa bʋl ba tɩtɩa La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɩzɩpa lɛ.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jɛfɩta tɩŋ tɩndaaraa ba mʋ pɩɛsɛ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa kuoro: “Bɛɛ kʋŋ yuosi nɛ hɛ la pɛgɛ, ŋ kʋ yuola?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Amɔŋ kuoro bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ Jɛfɩta sɩ tɩma, “Bʋa-la lɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ba laa mɩ tinteeŋ nɛ, a chɩŋ Anɔŋ fuo-la a kaa mʋ Jabɔk fuo-la, a kɛŋ ŋɩɩ kala a mʋ yi Jɔdaŋ fuo-la. Má joŋ tintee-la tɩa sɔm.”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta bɩra mɩɩra tɩŋ tɩndaaraa ba mʋ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa kuoro teeŋ

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: a bʋl, “Wɩɩ-la Jɛfɩta sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩ Mʋab tinteeŋ koo Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ laa.

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ba to tintee-hɩlɩŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ a mʋ to Mʋgʋ-fɩaŋ a mʋ Kadɛs.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tɩŋ tɩndaaraa ba mʋ sʋl Ɛdɔm kuoro a bʋl, ‘Pɩla wombiiŋ dɩ la to ŋ tinteeŋ a lɩɩ.’ Ama Ɛdɔm kuoro bɩ jegile nɩɩ. Ba bɩra tɩŋ tɩndaaraa ba mʋ Mʋab kuoro ma teeŋ, ʋ ma bɩra vɩa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa hɔŋ Kadɛs lɛ,

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: a bɩra sii to tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la tʋɔŋ a kpɛrɛ Ɛdɔm arɩ Mʋab tinteeŋ, a joŋ ŋɩɩ mʋ Mʋab tinteeŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ, a mʋ ŋmoo buguŋ Anɔŋ fuo-la sɛmɛ. Ba bɩ Mʋab tinteeŋ jʋa, bɛɛ wɩaa Anɔŋ fuo-la nɛ fa ŋaa ʋ bʋa.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tɩŋ tɩndaaraa ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa kuoro Sɩhɔŋ sɩ hɛ Hɛsɩbɔŋ lɛ aŋ bibemba, ‘Leŋ dɩ la to ŋ tinteeŋ tʋɔŋ a lɩɩ a mʋ la leriŋ.’

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Sɩhɔŋ ma fa bɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa laa dii arɩ ba sɩ jaŋ to ʋ tinteeŋ bal. Ʋ sii kɛŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala hɛ dɔŋɔ ba ŋmoo buguŋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jahas lɛ, a yuo Iziral tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa joŋ Sɩhɔŋ arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ, ba yuo diiba, aŋ laa Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa tintee-la kala lɛ ba sɩ hɔnɔ,

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: a chɩŋ Anɔŋ fuo-la a kaa mʋ Jabɔk fuo-la, a lɩɩ nɩmɛ a kaa mʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ a kɛŋ ŋɩɩ mʋ yi Jɔdaŋ fuo-la.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa, sɩ folo kiri Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa ta ʋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ, bɛɛ wombii nɛ ŋ kɛŋ dɩ ŋ laa tintee-la la teeŋ?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Ma vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kɛmɔs sɩ joŋ kʋ-la pɩma nɛ jaŋ ŋaa ma kʋa. Ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ la ma jaŋ tɩɩ kʋŋ na-kala La TƖƖNA Wɩa sɩ joŋo pɩla.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Ŋ kpɩa Mʋab kuoro Zipo nanʋala Balak nɛɛ? Ʋ ha kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo yuosuŋ koo a kɛmba yuo laalɩŋ ŋ naa?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Mɩ bɩ wɩɩkala ŋaa a cheyiŋ, ama ŋ-na nɩɩ ŋaamɛ wʋbɔŋ ŋ sɩ kɛmmɛ yuyuo laalɩŋ. La TƖƖNA nɛ ŋaa sarɩya diire, ʋ jaŋ laa wɩɩŋ deeŋ sɩ hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa pɛgɛ a jɩma pɩba jɩnɩŋ.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Ama Amɔŋ kuoro bɩ jegile nɩɩ tɩndaarɩ-la Jɛfɩta sɩ tɩma pʋ.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA Dɩma kʋ jʋʋ Jɛfɩta. Ʋ sii chol Gɩlɩad tinteeŋ arɩ Manasɛ tinteeŋ, a kiele mʋ Mɩzɩpa sɩ hɛ Gɩlɩad lɛ, a lɩɩ nɩmɛ a mʋ dɩ ʋ yuo Amɔŋ tɩmma-la.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ ta niiŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ: “Dɩ ŋ nɛ leŋe mɩ yuo dii Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa,

english_verse: and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
translation_verse: kʋŋ na-kala sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ lɩɩ mɩ dɩa lɛ a kʋ lɩɩ chemmi, ʋ jaŋ ŋaa ŋ-na La TƖƖNA kʋŋ, mɩ sɩ jaŋ kpʋ a kaa sʋl kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩŋ.”

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jɛfɩta mʋ dɩ ʋ yuo Amɔŋ tɩmma-la. La TƖƖNA jomba hɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta sɩ mɩɩra kʋkɔ ʋ jaŋ Mɩzɩpa, nʋʋ sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ kʋ lɩɩ chemu nɛ ŋaa ʋ tolo. Ʋ fa chɩgɩsɛ chɩnchɩga nɛ aŋ gʋgʋa a tɩŋ ʋ nyɩmma sɩ yuo laalɩŋ dii. Jɛfɩta bie kala nɛ fa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta sɩ naʋ, ʋ tʋɔŋ chei ʋ kɛŋ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ kɩɛsɛ aŋ ŋmoo niiŋ a bʋl, “Ou! Mɩ tolo! Ŋ kaa jʋʋ mɩ lɛ, mɩ tʋɔŋ faasa chei nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa mɩ ta niiŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo vɩa nii-la lɩɩsɩŋ.”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Tolo-la bʋl, “Mɩ nyɩmma, dɩ ŋ nɛ ta niiŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, kɛmmɛ ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ ta nii-la bʋl. La TƖƖNA folo leŋ ŋ yuo dii ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa nɛ.

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Ama mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ pɩmɛ: Pɩmɛ chɛnsɩŋ balɩa dɩ mɩ dɩ mɩ tanlɔsʋŋ gɔllɛ peelee nyuŋ a yel, a tɩŋ mɩ sɩ bɩ jaŋ jaa bala wɩaa.”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Ʋ nyɩmma bʋl, “Ŋ jaŋ wuo mʋ,” aŋ pʋ chɛnsɩ-la balɩa. Ʋ dɩ ʋ tanlɔsʋ-la gɔllɛ peelee nyuŋ a yel, a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ bɩ jaŋ jaa bala wɩaa.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Chɛnsɩ-la balɩa sɩ bala, ʋ mɩɩra kɔ ʋ nyɩmma teeŋ ʋ kɛnʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ ta nii-la a bʋl, dɩ ʋ ha ŋaa hapuŋ. A chɩŋ ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ wɩɩ-la ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa naaba wɩɩ.

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: Jɩna na-kala Iziral tɩŋŋaa hantolibiisiŋ yie lɩɩ gɔllɔ yel tapʋlaa banɛsɛ, a liliisi Gɩlɩad tɩŋŋaa Jɛfɩta tolo-la wɩaa.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala, Efirem doho nɩaa sii a yɩrɛ ba laalɩyuoroo hɛ dɔŋɔ, a chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la a mʋ lee kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Zafɔŋ a pɩɛsɛ Jɛfɩta, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ mʋ yuo Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa aŋ bɩ la yɩra dɩ la kʋ pɛ ŋ lɛ? La jaŋ nyɩgɛ ŋ dɩa dɩ ʋ dii a tɔ ŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta bʋl, “Mɩ dɩ mɩ nɩaa fa chaasa kɛŋ Amɔŋ tɩmma-la loo nɛ woruŋ. Mɩ yɩrɛma, ka ma bɩ kʋ laamɛ ta ba nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Mɩ sɩ na dɩ ma bɩ kɔ dɩ ma pɛ mɩ lɛ, mɩ joŋ mɩ mɩɩsɩŋ a yɔɔ sʋʋŋ, a chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la a yuo Amɔŋ tɩmma-la, La TƖƖNA leŋ mɩ yuo diiba. Bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ jɩnɩŋ ma kɔ dɩ ma yuomi?”

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ ka Jɛfɩta yɩrɛ Gɩlɩad laalɩyuoroo kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ ba mʋ yuo Efirem tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoroo. Gɩlɩad tɩmma-la chaasa kpʋ Efirem laalɩyuoroo woruŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa Efirem nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ, “Ma Gɩlɩad tɩŋŋaa ŋaa Efirem arɩ Manasɛ doho nɩaa nɛ, aŋ lɩɩ fá.”

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Gɩlɩad laalɩyuoroo laa lere-la kala Efirem nɩaa sɩ jaŋ wuo to chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la a mʋ ba tinteeŋ nɛ. Dɩ Efirem tɩmma-la nɩkaana-la kʋŋ nɛ kɔ a bʋl, “Má leŋ dɩ mɩ chol.” Gɩlɩad tɩmma-la yie pɩɛsʋ, “Ŋ ŋaa Efirem tɩɩna nɛɛ?” Dɩ ʋ nɛ sɩ, “Aɩ,”

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: ba yie bʋl, “Ʋ zɔmɔ, yɩrɛ ‘Sɩɩbɔlɛf’. Dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ woruŋ wuo yɩrɛ aŋ bʋl, ‘Sɩbɔlɛf’, ba yie kɛnʋ nɛ a kpʋ lere-la ba sɩ too chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la.” Bʋa-la lɛ ba kpʋ Efirem tɩmma-la bʋɩ mahɩŋ balɩa arɩ balɩa nɛ.

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta fa laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ jɩsɩŋ balɩdʋ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ sʋʋ, ba hugu ʋ jaŋ Mɩzɩpa sɩ hɛ Gɩlɩad tinteeŋ lɛ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa Ɩbɩzaŋ, Ɛlɔŋ arɩ Abɩdɔŋ

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Jɛfɩta sɩ sʋba harɩŋ, Ɩbɩzaŋ sɩ lɩɩ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm ma nɛ fa laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɩbɩzaŋ sʋʋ ba hugu Bɛtɩlɛhɛm lɛ.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Ɩbɩzaŋ ma sʋʋŋ harɩŋ, Zebuluŋ tɩŋŋaa Ɛlɔŋ ma nɛ bɩra laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ jɩsɩŋ fii.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛlɔŋ ma sʋʋ, ba hugu taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Aɩjalɔŋ sɩ hɛ Zebuluŋ tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hɩlɛl nanʋala Abɩdɔŋ ma sʋʋ, ba hugu Pɩratɔŋ sɩ hɛ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ. Nɩmɛ nɛ Amalɛk tɩŋŋaa fa hɛ.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa bɩra ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, ʋ jomba a hɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ balɩa.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ baal kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ baa yɩrɛ Manʋa, a lɩɩ taŋ kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Zora. Ʋ fa ŋaa Daŋ doho nʋʋ nɛ. Ʋ haala fa ŋaa hapɩrɩ nɛ a bɩ bii lʋla.

english_verse: but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said: You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
translation_verse: bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ jaŋ kɛŋ luoruŋ a lʋl hambolibie. Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba fʋŋ ʋ nyuŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ jaŋ joŋu hɛ Wɩa nɩsɩŋ lɛ a chɩŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ lʋlʋ, dɩ ʋ ŋaa nʋʋ sɩ tɔ nyukii. Ʋ nɛ jaŋ suomo laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ haal-la mʋ bʋla pɩ ʋ bala, “Wɩa nʋʋ kʋbala nɛ kɔ mɩ teeŋ. Ʋ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaarʋ nɛ, ʋ nagɩsɩŋ kɛŋ fawʋllʋŋ woruŋ. Mɩ bɩ ʋ pɩɛsa-na lee-la ʋ sɩ lɩa, ʋ ma bɩ ʋ yɩrɩŋ daga pɩmɛ.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Ama ʋ bʋla pɩmɛ, ‘Ŋ jaŋ kɛŋ luoruŋ a lʋl hambolibie. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa a chɩŋ lɛɛlɛ a kaa mʋ, pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ koo sɩ-yele kala nyʋa, a sɩ́ kʋŋ na-kala sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ Wɩa teeŋ ma dii, bɛɛ wɩaa a chɩŋ bile tapʋl-lʋlʋŋ a kaa mʋ ʋ sʋʋŋ, ʋ jaŋ hɛ Wɩa nɩsɩŋ lɛ a ŋaa nyukii tɩɩna.’ ”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Manʋa sʋl La TƖƖNA a bʋl, “Mɩ Tɩɩna, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, leŋ Wɩa nɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ tɩma ʋ kɔ la teeŋ bɩra kɔ a dagɛla ŋɩɩ la sɩ jaŋ dagɛ bile dɩ la nɛ lʋlʋ.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Wɩa nɩɩ Manʋa sʋla. Wɩa tɩndaarʋ-la bɩra mɩɩra kɔ haal-la teeŋ, dɩ ʋ lɩɩ hɔŋ ŋmaŋkaaŋ lɛ, ama ʋ bala na fa tuo nɩmɛ.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ haal-la guu sii fá mʋ bʋla pɩ ʋ bala, “Baal-la sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ a kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kʋ dagɛmɛ tapʋlɩɩ-la bɩra kɔ nɛ.”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Manʋa sii to ʋ haala harɩŋ mʋ. Ʋ sɩ mʋ Wɩa tɩndaarʋ-la teeŋ ʋ pɩɛsʋ, “Ŋ nɛ nɩɩ-la tapʋlɩɩ-la sɩ kʋ bʋl wɩaa mɩ haala teeŋ?” Ʋ bʋl, “Mɩ nɛ.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Manʋa bɩra pɩɛsʋ, “Dɩ wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ bʋla nɛ sɛnɛ kʋ ŋaa, wʋbɛɛ ba nɛ bile jaŋ tuto? Tɩntɩŋ bɛɛ nɛ ʋ jaŋ tɩtɩŋ?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la bʋl, “Ŋ haala maga dɩ ʋ to wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ bʋla pʋ.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ʋ dii girep nɛnɛɛ koo a nyʋa girep nɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ koo sɩ-yele kala, a sɩ́ kʋŋ na-kala sɩ kɛŋ disiniŋ Wɩa teeŋ dii. Ʋ maga dɩ ʋ to wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ dagʋ.”

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Manʋa bɩra bʋla pɩ La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la, “La jaŋ cho dɩ ŋ hɔnɔ dɩ la kɛŋ bʋ-pɔrʋŋ a kpʋ a ŋaa kʋdiilee pɩŋ.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la bʋl, “Dɩ mɩ nɛ hɔnɔ ma, mɩ bɩ jaŋ dii ma kʋŋkala. Ama dɩ ma nɩɩ chɛ, má kpʋ bʋʋŋ-la a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA.”

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Manʋa pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la, “Ŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ bɛɛ? Dɩ la wuo ziliŋ, dɩ wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ bʋla nɛ kʋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ.”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Ʋ pɩɛsɛ Manʋa, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ pɩɛsɛ mɩ yɩrɩŋ wɩaa? Mɩ yɩrɩŋ kɩɩ ŋ jɩmɩŋ nɛ.”

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Manʋa kɛŋ bʋ-pɔrʋŋ, a pɛ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ lɛ, a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ bʋŋ nyuŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA. Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA ŋaa wʋkpuŋkpere, ka Manʋa arɩ ʋ haala bibeŋ.

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: Nyiŋ-geliŋ sɩ lɩɩ koruŋ nyuŋ a jɩjɩl wɩa-nyuŋ, La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la to nyiŋ-gel-la lɛ a jɩl. Manʋa arɩ ʋ haala sɩ na wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ba tuu tel tinteeŋ a chu.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩndaarʋ-la bɩra sɩ bɩ ʋ tɩtɩa kaa dagɛ Manʋa arɩ ʋ haala ŋɩɩ, Manʋa jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA tɩndaara nɛ.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Manʋa bʋla pɩ ʋ haala, “La jaŋ sʋʋ, a tɩŋ la sɩ na Wɩa.”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Ama Manʋa haala bʋla pɩ ʋ bala, “Dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ faa chɛ dɩ ʋ kpʋla, ʋ fa bɩ jaŋ laa la kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ la mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, koo a dagɛla wɩaa deemba koo a bʋl wɩaa deemba a pɩla.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ lɛ Manʋa haala lʋl hambolibie, a hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Samɩsɩŋ. Ʋ waa, La TƖƖNA pɛ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA Dɩma suomo pʋpʋ doluŋ, dɩ ʋ fa hɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Daŋ buguŋ, tasɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zora arɩ Ɛsɩtɔl pɛgɛ.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala Samɩsɩŋ sii mʋ taŋ kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Tɩmɩna a na Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa tolo kʋbala nɩmɛ.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ mɩɩra kɔ, ʋ bʋla pɩ ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ, “Mɩ na Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa tolo nɛ Tɩmɩna lɛ, má jaaʋ pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ pɩɛsʋ, “hazɔŋ kala tuo la naambiiriŋ koo la nɩaa kala tʋɔŋ? Nɩaa deemba sɩ bɩ Wɩa ka to tʋɔŋ nɛ maga dɩ ŋ jaa ŋ haalaa?” Ama Samɩsɩŋ bʋla pɩ ʋ nyɩmma, “Jaa pɩmɛ, nɩɩ-la mɩ sɩɩŋ sɩ jʋa nɛ ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ arɩ ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ kala sii mʋ Tɩmɩna. Ba sɩ mʋ yi girep tɩɩsɩŋ baga kʋbala sɩ hɛ Tɩmɩna lɛ, naachigi-bie sii guu tʋɔra kʋkɔ Samɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA Dɩma kʋ jʋʋ Samɩsɩŋ a pʋ doluŋ ʋ kɛŋ naachigi-la pʋɔsɛ arɩ nɩsɩŋ, a nagɛ bʋ-bie. Ama ʋ bɩ wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa bʋla pɩ ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ Tɩmɩna, Samɩsɩŋ kɛŋ tolo-la bʋl wɩaa, ʋ chaasa chou woruŋ.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ, ʋ sɩ mɩɩra mʋ dɩ ʋ jaa haal-la, ʋ gɛbɛ jʋʋ dɩ ʋ na naachigi-la kʋsʋʋŋ. Ʋ mʋa dɩ tʋʋ-biee kʋ jʋʋ naachigi-sʋʋ-la a saa hɛ nʋʋŋ.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Ʋ kɛŋ nɩsɩŋ tuu a lɔgɛ tʋʋ-la a vɛŋ aŋ didii. Ʋ sɩ kɔ ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ teeŋ, ʋ lɔgɛ tʋʋ-la mʋa pɩba ba dii. Ama ʋ bɩ bʋla pɩ ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ arɩ naachigi-sʋʋŋ yaraa lɛ nɛ ʋ lɔgɛ tʋʋ-la.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ nyɩmma mʋ haal-la dɩa. Samɩsɩŋ leŋ ba ŋaa kʋdiilee ba didii aŋ gbigbieli, arɩ ŋɩɩ ba naabalɩma wombiiŋ sɩ daga dɩ bapʋɔsɛ biisiŋ to a jɩjaa haalaa.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sɩ na Samɩsɩŋ, ba leŋ bapʋɔsɛ biisiŋ mara arɩ fii mʋ kɛnʋ ba hɔŋ.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ bɩ wuo dagɛ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ, ma ma jaŋ pɩmɛ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ gɛnnɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ gɛrɩ-balaa mara arɩ fii.” Ba bʋl, “Magɛ ŋ namaga-la dɩ la nɩɩ.”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Samɩsɩŋ bʋl, “Kʋdiire niiŋ lɛ nɛ kʋdiilee lɩɩ, kʋduoŋ lɛ nɛ kʋsɩmɩŋ lɩɩ.” Tapʋlaa batori ba bɩ wuo dagɛ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Tapʋl nɛsɛ chɛɛŋ, bapʋɔsɛ biisi-la bʋla pɩ Samɩsɩŋ haala, “Nyɩsɛ ŋ bala dɩ ʋ dagɛ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ a pɩla, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, la jaŋ nyɩgɛ ŋ dɩ ŋ nyɩmma dɩa nɩaa kala dɩ ma sʋʋ. Ma yɩrɛla kaa kɔ daha dɩ ma laa la kɩaa nɛɛ?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ haala joŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kala a tele nyagɛ Samɩsɩŋ, aŋ yiyel, aŋ bʋl, “Ŋ bɛrɛmɛ nɛ! Ŋ bɩ chaasa chomi. Ŋ magɛ namaga a pɩ mɩ nɩaa nɛ, aŋ bɩ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ daga pɩmɛ.” Samɩsɩŋ bʋl, “Mɩ paala bɩ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ daga pɩ mɩ nyɩmma koo mɩ naaŋ, bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ mɩ jaŋ dagɛ ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ pɩ ŋ-na?”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Haal-la yel ŋɩɩ nɛ gbiele-la tapʋlaa balɩpɛ-la kala. Tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ dagɛ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ a pʋ, bɛɛ wɩaa haal-la vɛnɛɛ pɛsɛ ʋ lɛ nɛ. Ʋ sɩ daga pʋ ŋɩɩ, haal-la ma mʋ dagɛ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ a pɩ ʋ nɩaa.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Ka dɩ wɩɩ-muluŋ-na tuu jʋʋ tapʋl-pɛɩ-la chɛɛŋ, ba-pʋɔsa-la sii mʋ pɩɛsɛ Samɩsɩŋ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ sɩma a kɩɩ tʋʋŋ? Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ dolie a kɩɩ naachigiŋ?” Samɩsɩŋ bʋla pɩba, “Dɩ ma nɛ fa bɩ mɩ haala lɛ to, ma fa bɩ jaŋ wuo dagɛ mɩ namaga-la bʋbʋɔŋ.”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Samɩsɩŋ hɩɩlɩ-baala mɩɩra joŋ haal-la pɩ baal-la sɩ ŋaa Samɩsɩŋ nandɔŋɔ hajaarɩ gbiele-la lɛ.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: aŋ bʋla pɩ Samɩsɩŋ, “Mɩ-na bɩɩna ŋ chaasa bɛrɛ tolo-la nɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ joŋu pɩ ŋ nandɔŋɔ. Ama ʋ ŋaana hɛ nɩmɛ a zɔmɔ kɩɩʋ. Ŋ jaŋ wuo mɩɩra jaaʋ.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Samɩsɩŋ bʋl, “Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa lɛ ma, mɩ bɩ wɩɩ cheye.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: a chol nyiniŋ hɛ kapɩla-la lɛ aŋ kiri jollu-la ta ba jʋʋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa bagɩsɩŋ tʋɔŋ, lee-la mɛmpɛ sɩ bɩɩ chɩŋ a magɛ kʋmʋŋ. Ʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ nɛ a nyɩgɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa mɛmpɛ-la ba sɩ ta bil arɩ kɩalɩŋ kala sɩ chɩna ba dii. Ba girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ arɩ Olif tɩɩsɩŋ ma kala dii.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩmma-la pɩɛsɛ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ?” Ba bʋla pɩba, “Samɩsɩŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, a tɩŋ ʋ hɩɩlɩ-baala Tɩmɩna tɩɩna-la sɩ joŋ ʋ haala pɩ ʋ nandɔŋɔ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sii mʋ nyɩgɛ haal-la ʋ sʋʋ aŋ nyɩgɛ ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa kala.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Samɩsɩŋ bʋla pɩba, “Má sɩ folo ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ mɩ lɛ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ lemma da, mɩ jaŋ joŋ mɩ baanɩŋ a fɩɩsɛ ma lɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Ʋ chaasa yuoba, a kpʋba yʋgɛ woruŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ sii tuu taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛtam a hɛ ʋ bʋbʋa lɛ.

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa ma sii a mʋ ŋmoo buguŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, a jɛrɛ su lee-kala a kpagɛ taŋ kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lehi.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Juda tɩŋŋaa pɩɛsɛba, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma kɔ dɩ ma yuola?” Ba bʋl, “La kɔ dɩ la yuo kɛŋ Samɩsɩŋ nɛ, a ŋaaʋ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ ŋaa la lɛ.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ laalɩyuoroo bʋɩ batori sii Juda tinteeŋ lɛ a mʋ bʋbʋa-la sɩ hɛ Ɛtam lɛ a pɩɛsɛ Samɩsɩŋ, “Ŋ bɩ jɩŋ arɩ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɛ kɛŋ doluŋ la lɛɛ? Bɛɛ nɛ ŋ ŋaa la lɛ ŋ-la?” Samɩsɩŋ bʋl, “Wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ ŋaa mɩ lɛ nɛ mɩ ma joŋo ŋaa ba lɛ ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Laalɩyuoro-la bʋla pʋ, “La kɔ dɩ la vɔbʋŋ nɛ a kaa mʋ pɩ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa.” Samɩsɩŋ sɩ, “Má ŋmɩɛsa pɩmɛ arɩ ma tɩtɩa dee bɩ jaŋ kpʋmɛ.”

english_verse: Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ na kakumo talaŋa haŋgbeliŋ dɩ ʋ pɩna, ʋ joŋ a kpʋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩmma-la bʋɩ.

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ bʋl, “Kakumo talaŋa haŋgbeliŋ nɛ mɩ kaa kpʋ nɩaa bʋɩ. Kakumo talaŋa haŋgbeliŋ nɛ mɩ kaa kpʋba chʋɔrɛ.”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ dɛrɛ, ʋ joŋ haŋgbel-la a yuo ta. Ba kɛŋ lee-la a yɩyɩrɛ Rama Lehi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ lɩɩnyʋasʋŋ faasa kɛŋ Samɩsɩŋ, ʋ ŋmoo niiŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA, “Ŋ leŋe mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna yuo dii nɛ woruŋ. Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, sɩ́ leŋe dɩ lɩɩnyʋasʋŋ kpʋmɛ dɩ nɩaa deemba sɩ bɩŋ ka to kɛmmɛ.”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa suri lɩɩ-bulo Lehi lɛ. Lɩɩŋ bulo lɩɩ, Samɩsɩŋ nyʋa a bɩra kɛŋ doluŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɛŋ lɩɩ-bulo-la a yɩyɩrɛ Ɛŋ-Hakori, arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala ʋ ha hɛ Lehi lɛ.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Samɩsɩŋ laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ jɩsɩŋ mara nɛ, bʋa-la lɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nyuŋ.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gaza tɩŋŋaa nɩɩ arɩ Samɩsɩŋ hɛ ba taŋ tʋɔŋ. Ba sii mʋ ba taŋ boi-baalɩŋ lɛ a gbɛrʋ tɩtaŋ-la kala. Tɩtaŋ-la kala ba bɩ lee-kala mʋa. Ba sɩ, “Chie chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla la jaŋ kpʋʋ.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Wɩɩŋ deeŋ harɩŋ lɛ, Samɩsɩŋ na haal kʋbala sɩ hɛ Sɔrɛk fuonaaŋ lɛ, a chou woruŋ. Haal-la yɩrɩŋ nɛ Delaɩla.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kuoroo mʋ a bʋla pɩ haal-la, “Nyɩsɛ Samɩsɩŋ dɩ ʋ dagɩŋ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ ŋaa a faasa kɛŋ doluŋ arɩ ŋɩɩ la sɩ jaŋ wuo to a kɛnʋ vɔɔ a laa ʋ doluŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, la kʋŋkala jaŋ pɩŋ warɩpʋla bʋɩ arɩ zɔlɔ.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Delaɩla bʋla pɩ Samɩsɩŋ, “Dagɛmɛ ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ ŋaa a faasa kɛŋ doluŋ arɩ ŋɩɩ nʋʋ sɩ jaŋ to a kɛnɩŋ vɔɔ a laa ŋ doluŋ.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samɩsɩŋ bʋla pʋ, “Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kɛŋ teŋ-bii-laarɩŋ balɩpɛ a vɔɔmɛ, mɩ jaŋ pʋgʋmɛ a nagɛ nʋʋ dɔŋ kala.”

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Delaɩla bʋla pɩ Samɩsɩŋ, “Ŋ jommi mɩ ŋaa nɩyaarɩ nɛ, ŋ nyɩnyɩsɛmɛ. Lɛɛlɛ, dagɛmɛ ŋɩɩ nʋʋ sɩ jaŋ to a wuo vɔbʋŋ.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ bɩra bʋl, “Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kɛŋ ŋmɛŋ-falaa ba ha sɩ bɩ kaa vɔɔ kɩaa aŋ ka a chaasa vɔɔmɛ woruŋ, mɩ jaŋ pʋgʋmɛ a nagɛ nʋʋ dɔŋ kala.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Delaɩla kɛŋ ŋmɛŋ-falaa a vɔbʋ. Ka baalaa bɩra jʋʋ faa dɩa tʋɔŋ. Ʋ bɩra yɩrɛ, “Samɩsɩŋ, Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɩɩ kɔ ŋ lɛ.” Samɩsɩŋ bɩra kɛŋ ŋmɛŋ-falɩa-la ma sɩ vɔɔ ʋ nɩsaa kɛrɛ a nagɛ gɛrɩ-ŋmɛnɩŋ.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Delaɩla bʋla pɩ Samɩsɩŋ, “Ŋ ha jommi mɩ ŋaa nɩyaarɩ nɛ, ŋ nyɩnyɩsɛmɛ. Dagɛmɛ ŋɩɩ nʋʋ sɩ jaŋ wuo to a vɔbʋŋ.” Ʋ bʋl, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ kɛŋ mɩ nyu-pʋŋ gulimo-la balɩpɛ sɩ hɛ mɩ nyuŋ lɛ, a kaa hɛ kʋ-la ba sɩ kaa yuo gɛrɩpɛɛŋ lɛ, a yuo ʋ dɩ ʋ gɛrɩ-ŋmɛsɩ-la kala hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ a kaa mɩlɩmɛ dɩ ba jʋʋ dɔŋɔ lɛ, a kɛŋ pini chɛbɛ kɛŋ, mɩ jaŋ pʋgʋmɛ a nagɛ nʋʋ dɔŋ kala.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ pɩŋ doŋ, Delaɩla kɛŋ nyu-pʋna-la balɩpɛ sɩ hɛ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ, a yuo ba dɩ gɛrɩ-ŋmɛsɩ-la kala sɩ hɛ gɛrɩpɛ-yuori-daaŋ lɛ a hɛ dɔŋɔ,

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: a lɛrɛ hɛ ʋ jʋʋ dɔŋɔ lɛ, a kɛŋ pini chɛbɛ kɛŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ bɩra yɩrʋ, “Samɩsɩŋ, Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɩɩ kɔ ŋ lɛ.” Ʋ hirige sii doŋ lɛ, a kɛŋ ʋ nyu-pʋnaa lɛrɛ fuosi gɛrɩpɛ-yuori daa-la arɩ ŋmɛsɩ-la kala lɛ.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tolo-la pɩɛsʋ, “Ɛɛ nɛ ŋ jaŋ bʋl ŋ chomi nɛ, aŋ kɛŋ wɩaa fɩfaamɛ? Naansɩɩŋ butori nɛ ŋ-la, ŋ sɩ jommi mɩ ŋaa nɩyaarɩ ŋ nyɩsɛmɛ, aŋ ha bɩ ŋ dol-la bʋbʋɔŋ daga pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ pɛsɛ ʋ lɛ ŋɩɩ a bʋbʋl ʋ teeŋ tapʋlɩɩ kala, ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ paala mɩɩra fɩɩ.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ʋ walɩma ka aŋ bʋl wʋtɩtɩɩ a pɩ tolo-la. Ʋ sɩ, “Ba sɩ lʋlmɛ kala, nyu-fʋna ha bɩ mɩ nyuŋ lɛ dige, bɛɛ wɩaa ba joŋ mɩ hɛ Wɩa nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ mɩ ŋaa Nazarɩ tɩɩna, dɩ ba nɛ fʋŋ mɩ nyuŋ, mɩ doluŋ jaŋ lɩɩ dɩ mɩ pʋgʋmɛ a nagɛ nʋʋ dɔŋ kala.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Delaɩla sɩ na dɩ Samɩsɩŋ bʋl wʋtɩtɩɩ a pʋ, ʋ tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kuorusu-la, “Má bɩra mɩɩra kɔ, ʋ bʋl wʋtɩtɩɩ-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ kala pɩmɛ nɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kuorusu-la bɩra mɩɩra kɔ a kori warɩpʋla-la.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Delaɩla kɛŋ Samɩsɩŋ hɛ naasɩŋ nyuŋ ʋ pɩŋ doŋ, ʋ yɩrɛ nʋʋ dɔŋ ʋ kʋ fʋŋ nyu-pʋŋ-gulumo-la balɩpɛ sɩ hɛ Samɩsɩŋ nyuŋ lɛ a laa ʋ doluŋ, ka ʋ pʋgʋmɛ.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩmma-la kɛnʋ, a kɔrɩgɔ chaarɛ ʋ sɩaa aŋ kɛnʋ mʋ tɔ dɩa taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gaza lɛ, a kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ chɔrʋmɔɔ vɔbʋ aŋ leŋ ʋ nʋnɔŋ munuŋ dansarɩka-la lɛ.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Ama ba sɩ fʋŋ ʋ nyu-pʋna-la ŋɩɩ, ba bɩra suomo wʋwaa. Samɩsɩŋ sʋba

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala lɛ, Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kuorusu-la kʋ hilimi dɩ ba chaasa kpaarɛ ba vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Daagɔŋ aŋ pɛ gbieli. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bʋl, “La vene Daagɔŋ nɛ joŋ la dʋndɔmɔ Samɩsɩŋ a hɛ la nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!” The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god: Samson ruined our crops and killed our people. He was our enemy, but our god helped us capture him. They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof.
translation_verse: Ba tʋɔŋ sɩ faasa tɔrɛ, ba kpɩa goŋ, “Má kɛŋ Samɩsɩŋ a kʋ lɩɩ dɩ ʋ gbiele pɩla.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba yɩrɛ Samɩsɩŋ ʋ kʋ lɩɩ dansarɩka lɛ a gbiele pɩba. Nɩalɩŋ sɩ na Samɩsɩŋ, ba dɛnnɛ ba vene a bʋl, “La vene nɛ joŋ la dʋndɔmɔ Samɩsɩŋ a hɛ la nɩsɩŋ lɛ, nɩɩ-la sɩ chei la tinteeŋ aŋ kpʋ la nɩaa ma a yʋgɛ.” Ba fa leŋe Samɩsɩŋ chɩŋ jebiee pɛgɛ nɛ.

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ bʋla pɩ tɩntɩnnʋ-la sɩ kɛŋ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ, “Kɛmmɛ kaa mʋ dɩ mɩ laara na jebie-la sɩ chagɛ dɩa-la kɩɩ, mɩɩ chɛ mɩ yelliba nɛ.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ sʋl La TƖƖNA a bʋl, “Ou, mɩ TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ, liisi mɩ wɩaa. Wɩa, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, bɩra pɩmɛ doluŋ bala dɩ mɩ wuo ŋmoo Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa deemba bɩra, a tiŋ mɩ sɩaa chɩmɩŋ.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samɩsɩŋ laara mʋ yi jebie-la balɩa sɩ chɩŋ dɩa-la tʋtʋɔbaanɩŋ a chagɛ dɩa-la kɩɩ, a kɛŋ ʋ nadiiŋ kɛŋ dɔŋɔ, a kɛŋ ʋ nagʋa ma a kɛŋ dɔŋɔ,

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: aŋ bʋl, “Leŋ mɩ dɩ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa deemba kala sʋʋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ yigi jebie-la arɩ ʋ doluŋ kala. Dɩa-la tele tɔ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kuoroo arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ. Bʋa deeŋ lɛ Samɩsɩŋ sɩ sʋba, ʋ kpʋ nɩaa a kɩɩ bʋa-la lɛ ʋ fa sɩ weye.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ naambiiriŋ arɩ ʋ nyɩmma dɩa nɩaa kala sii mʋ Gaza a laa ʋ kʋsʋʋŋ kaa kɔ dɩa. Ba hugu ʋ nyɩmma Manʋa bʋa sɩ hɛ tasɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zora arɩ Ɛsɩtɔl pɛgɛ nɛ. Ʋ fa laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ jɩsɩŋ mara nɛ.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ bile bɩra joŋ warɩpʋla-la a pɩ ʋ naaŋ. Ʋ laa a lɩɩsɛ zɔɔ-balɩa a pɩ libire ʋ kɛŋ daaŋ saa tɔmʋŋ a kɛŋ hɔpʋla taara tɔ. Ba kaa jʋʋ bil Mɩka dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Mɩka fa kɛŋ lee nɛ a kpʋkpaarɛ vʋɩyaa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ yɛrɛ gɛrɩ-laala-daŋɩŋ, a mɛ tɔŋŋɔɔ a lɩɩsɛ ʋ bie dɔŋɔ ʋ kpʋkpaarɛ tɔmɔ-la.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Iziral tinteeŋ fa bɩ kuoro kɛnɛ. Nʋʋkala faa ŋaa wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ cho nɛ.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ lɩɩ nɩmɛ a gɔllɔ chɩchɛ leriŋ dɩ ʋ hɔŋ. Ʋ sɩɩ gɔllɛ ŋɩɩ, ʋ kɔ Mɩka dɩa sɩ hɛ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Mɩka pɩɛsʋ, “Nɩɩ nɛ ŋ lɩɩ?” Ʋ bʋl, “Mɩ ŋaa Levi doho nʋʋ nɛ a lɩɩ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm sɩ hɛ Juda lɛ. Leriŋ nɛ mɩ gɔllɔ chɩchɛ dɩ mɩ hɔŋ.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mɩka bʋla pʋ, “Hɔŋ mɩ teeŋ a ŋaa nɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ chɩchagɩlɛmɛ arɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ kpʋkpaarɛ mɩ tɔŋŋɔɔ. Jɩna kala mɩ jaŋ pɩŋ warɩpʋla fii, a pɩŋ gɛnnɩŋ arɩ kʋdiilee ma.”

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Mɩka laa Levi doho nɩɩ-la bil ʋ dɩa lɛ, a leŋ ʋ kpʋkpaarɛ ʋ tɔŋŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Mɩka bʋl, “Lɛɛlɛ mɩ jɩma La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ jaŋ tɔrɛ mɩ nyuŋ, a tɩŋ Levi doho nɩaa bapʋɔsɛ bie deeŋ sɩ ŋaa nɩɩ-la sɩɩ kpaarɛ mɩ tɔŋŋɔɔ.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Faafaa-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa bɩ kuoro kɛnɛ. Bʋa-la lɛ nɛ Daŋ doho nɩaa gɔllɔ chɩchɛ leriŋ ba sɩ jaŋ hɔŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba-na fa ha bɩ ba tinteeŋ kpaalɩŋ laa Iziral doho doho-la tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ tɩŋ laalɩyuori-babiibalaa banɔŋ ba lɩɩ tasɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zora arɩ Ɛsɩtɔl a mʋ dɩ ba lʋara beŋ tintee kʋbala a na lee-la ba sɩ jaŋ hɔŋ. Nɩaa deemba banɔŋ, nʋʋkala chɩŋ ʋ nyɩŋ-nɩaa nyuŋ nɛ. Ba bʋla pɩba, “Má mʋ a lʋara beŋ tintee-la a na.” Nɩalɩŋ lɩɩ mʋ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga, a mʋ jʋʋ Mɩka dɩa dɩ ba chʋa nɩmɛ.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Ba fa sɩ mʋʋ kpagɛ Mɩka dɩa, ba nɩɩ Levi doho nɩaa bapʋɔsɩ-bie-la yikoro. Ba mʋ ʋ teeŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ kɛnɩŋ kɔ daha? Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ ŋ ŋɩŋaa daha?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Ʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la Mɩka sɩ ŋaa pʋ a pɩba. Ʋ sɩ, “Ʋ ŋaa mɩ kpʋkpaarɛ ʋ tɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ, ka ʋ titimmi.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bʋla pʋ, “Laa sʋlʋŋ, pɩɛsɛ Wɩa a na la wombiiŋ deeŋ la sɩɩ vɛŋ jaŋ zɔŋ.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Tɔŋ-kpaarʋ-la bʋla pɩba, “Má mʋmʋ, wɩɩkala tuo, La TƖƖNA chɩŋ ma harɩŋ nɛ.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baala-la banɔŋ lɩɩ a mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Las, a na dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ hɔnʋŋ zɔmɔ, a nagɛ Sɩdɔŋ tɩŋŋaa sɩ hɔnɔ ta jɩa ŋɩɩ, wɩɩkala bɩ baa walɩmɛ. Ba tinteeŋ fa kɛŋ kɩaa nɛ woruŋ, ba bɩ kʋŋkala chɛɛ ka. Las tɩmma-la fa bɩ Sɩdɔŋ tɩŋŋaa kpaga, ba dɩ nɩa kala ma bɩ dɔŋɔ jɩŋ.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baala-la banɔŋ mɩɩra mʋ Zora arɩ Ɛsɩtɔl. Ba naambiiriŋ pɩɛsɛba, “Ɛɛ nɛ ma na wɩaa dɩ ba naga?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Dɩ la nɛ mʋ lee-la, ma jaŋ na ŋɩɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɔnɔ ta jɩa. Ba tintee-la jalɩa nɛ woruŋ, a kɛŋ kʋŋkala nuhuobiine sɩɩ chɛ. Wɩa joŋ tintee-la hɛ la nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Daŋ doho nɩaa laalɩyuoroo zɔɔ-balɩdʋ nyɩgɩlɛ a lɩɩ Zora arɩ Ɛsɩtɔl dɩ ba mʋ yuo laalɩŋ.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Ba sɩɩ mʋ, ba mʋ ŋmoo buguŋ a kpagɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kɩrɩaf Jɩarɩm sɩ hɛ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ba kɛŋ Kɩrɩaf Jɩarɩm wɩɩjʋʋlʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ aa yɩrɛ Daŋ Buguŋ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Nɩmɛ nɛ ba lɩɩ a mʋ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga a mʋ kpagɛ Mɩka dɩa.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ banɔŋ fa sɩ mʋ lʋara beŋ Las tintee-la bʋla pɩ ba naambiiri-la sɩ nyɩgɩla dɩ ba yuo laalɩŋ, “Dɩɩsɩŋ deemba dɔŋɔ lɛ, gɛrɩ-laala-daŋɩŋ hɛ nɩmɛ, arɩ tɔmʋŋ ba sɩ kɛŋ daaŋ saa a kɛŋ hɔpʋla taara tɔ a pɛ tɔŋŋɔɔ dɔnsʋŋ lɛ. Lɛɛlɛ ma jɩŋ ŋɩɩ ma sɩ jaŋ ŋaa.”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Ba bʋla pʋ, “Tɔrɛ ŋ niiŋ! Sɩ́ wɩɩkala bʋl. Kɔ a to la harɩŋ, a ŋaa nɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ chɩchagɩlɛla arɩ nɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ kpʋkpaarɛ la tɔŋŋɔɔ. Ʋ jaŋ ŋaa wʋzɔŋ, dɩ ŋ nɩɩ kpaarɛ Iziral doho dɔŋɔ tɔmʋŋ, a kɩɩ ŋ sɩ ŋaa nɩbala tɔŋ-kpaarʋ.”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɔŋ-kpaarʋ-la tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ. Ʋ joŋ gɛrɩ-laala-daŋɩɩ-la, arɩ tɔŋŋɔɔ dɔnsʋŋ a pɛ tɔŋ-la ba sɩ saa a kɛŋ hɔpʋla taara tɔ a to nɩalɩŋ harɩŋ.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ kɛsɛ ba hambiisiŋ, pʋsʋŋ arɩ kɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ kɛnɛ a hɛ sɩpaaŋ a lɩɩ mʋmʋ.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Ba sɩ lɩɩ mʋ dɩ-bolii mʋa, Mɩka yɩrɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ jʋʋ aa kpagʋ a bʋl wɩɩ-la pɩba. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba lɩɩ kiri ba libe, a mʋ puu Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Ba sɩ puuba, ba kpɩa ba lɛ. Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ mɩɩra pɩɛsɛ Mɩka, “Wʋbɛɛ nɛ kɔ, ŋ yɩrɛ ŋ nɩaa ma kɔ dɩ ma yuola?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Ʋ bʋl, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma pɩɛsɛmɛ ŋɩɩ? Ma paa mɩ tɔmɔ-la mɩ sɩ mɛ nɛ, a pɛ kɛŋ nɩɩ-la ma sɩɩ kpaarɛba viviiri. Mɩ bɩra bɩ kʋŋkala kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ bʋla pɩba, “Sɩ́ la kaa lɩlɛrɛ, dɩ ŋ nɛ leŋe la baanɩŋ sii, la jaŋ kpʋ ŋ dɩ ŋ dɩa nɩaa kala.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ viviiri. Mɩka ma sɩ na dɩ nɩalɩŋ kɛŋ doluŋ a kɩɩʋ, ʋ ma mɩɩra mʋ dɩa.

english_verse: The tribe of Dan took Micah's priest and the things Micah had made, and headed for Laish, which was located in a valley controlled by the town of Beth-Rehob. Laish was defenseless, because it had no walls and was too far from Sidon for the Sidonians to help defend it. The leaders of Laish had not even asked nearby towns to help them in case of an attack. The warriors from Dan made a surprise attack on Laish, killing everyone and burning it down. Then they rebuilt the town and settled there themselves.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala fa tuo dɩ ʋ laaba ta, bɛɛ wɩaa ba dɩ Sɩdɔŋ tɩŋŋaa fa bɩ dɔŋɔ kpaga, ka ba dɩ nɩa ma kala bɩ dɔŋɔ jɩŋ. Taŋ-la fa hɛ fuonaaŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ a kpagɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛf Rehob. Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ mɩɩra wasa saa taŋ-la a hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Daŋ doho nɩalɩŋ mɩɩra kɛŋ Las yɩyɩrɛ ba naabalɩma Daŋ tinteeŋ. Jekɔb nɛ fa lʋl Daŋ.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ bɩ kuoro kɛnɛ, Levi doho nʋʋ kʋbala fa hɛ gɩrɩŋ tʋɔŋ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ. Ʋ bil haal kʋbala sɩ lɩɩ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm sɩ hɛ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, aŋ ha bɩ jaa.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Ama haal-la fa na baanɩŋ ʋ bala nyuŋ, a leŋu aŋ mɩɩra mʋ ʋ nyɩmma dɩa Bɛtɩlɛhɛm lɛ. Ʋ sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ chɛnsɩŋ banɛsɛ,

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: ʋ bala mʋ dɩ ʋ sʋlʋ dɩ ʋ mɩɩra kɔ. Baal-la sɩɩ mʋ, ʋ pɛ kɛŋ ʋ tɩntɩnna arɩ kakusuŋ balɩa. Ba sɩ mʋa, haal-la kɛŋ baal-la jʋʋ ʋ nyɩmma dɩa. Ʋ nyɩmma sɩ na baal-la, ʋ cheme laaʋ arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Haal-la nyɩmma sʋlʋ dɩ ʋ hɔŋ ba teeŋ tapʋlaa baŋmɛnɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la hɛ ba teeŋ tapʋlaa batori a didii aŋ nyʋnyʋa.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Tapʋl nɛsɛ chɛɛŋ, ba sii chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, baal-la ŋaa siri dɩ ʋ viiri. Ama tolo-la nyɩmma bʋla pʋ, “Gbɛrɛ dii kɩaa a kɛŋ doluŋ aŋ-na mʋ.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba balɩa hɔnɔ dii kɩaa aŋ nyʋa. Ba sɩ dii kɩalɩŋ dɛrɛ, tolo-la nyɩmma bɩra bʋl, “Chʋa daha jɩnɩŋ bɩra dɩ la nɩɩ sɩma.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩɩ-la sii dɩ ʋ viiri, ama baal-la ha pɛsɛ a sʋsʋlʋ, ʋ sɛɩ a chʋa nɩmɛ bɩra.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Tapʋl-nɔŋ chɛɛŋ chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, baal-la bɩra ŋaa siri dɩ ʋ viiri. Tolo-la nyɩmma bɩra bʋl, “Gbɛrɛ dii kɩaa aŋ mʋ wɩɩhɛyɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba ŋaa kʋdiilee ba dii.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Baal-la arɩ ʋ haal-la ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la bɩra sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ba mʋ, tolo-la nyɩmma bɩra bʋl, “Má bee na, wɩa ka mʋa dɩ ʋ jʋʋ. Leriŋ jaŋ biri lɛɛlɛ kala. Má chʋa daha dɩ la nɩɩ sɩma, ka dɩ ma chie sii chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla a mʋ dɩa.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ama baal-la bɩra bɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ chʋa lee-la. Ʋ paa ʋ kakusuŋ gbagaa daŋ ʋ kakusuŋ nyuŋ, a kɛŋ ʋ haala arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnna ba to Jebus dɩɩrɩŋ a mʋmʋ .

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ kpagɛ Jebus, dɩ taŋ ka mʋa dɩ ʋ bire. Baal-la tɩntɩnnʋ-la bʋla pɩ ʋ nɩhɩaŋ, “Má leŋ dɩ la chʋa Jebus tɩŋŋaa taŋ deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ nɩhɩaŋ bʋl, “Aɩ, la bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ chʋa nɩaa sɩ bɩ Iziral tɩmma ŋaa taŋ lɛ. La jaŋ kiele mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gɩbɩa.”

english_verse: or maybe we can even reach Ramah before dark.”
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩra bʋl, “Má leŋ dɩ la nɛrɩgɛ mʋ Gɩbɩa koo Rama a chʋa ba dɔŋɔ lɛ.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba mʋmʋ, wɩɩ-muluŋ sɩɩŋ ka jʋʋ dɩ ba yi Gɩbɩa sɩ hɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Ba chɩŋ dɩ ba chʋa Gɩbɩa lɛ. Ba mʋ a hɔŋ lee-la taŋ-la nɩaa kala sɩɩ hilimu. Ama nʋʋkala bɩ ba kaa jʋʋ ʋ dɩa.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Sɩɩ-dɩsa-la ba sɩ hɔŋ ŋɩɩ, dɩ banɩhɩaŋ kʋbala lɩɩ baga a kʋ to ba teeŋ a bɩbal. Baal-la fa lɩɩ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga nɛ. Ama lɛɛlɛ ʋ hɛ Gɩbɩa lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Banɩhɩaŋ-la sɩ na Levi doho nɩɩ-la, ʋ jɩŋ arɩ wombii vɛnnʋ nɛ. Ʋ mʋ a pɩɛsɛ, “Nɩɩ nɛ ma lɩɩ, a mʋmʋ nɩɩ?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩɩ-la bʋl, “La mʋ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm sɩ hɛ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ aŋ mɩɩra mʋmʋ dɩa. Lɛɛlɛ laa mʋ tintee-la ba sɩɩ dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA nɛ. Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ la jaŋ mɩɩra mʋ dɩa. La taŋ hɛ gɩrɩŋ tʋɔŋ dɩ-luŋii nɛ, Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ. Nʋʋkala bɩ la kaa jʋʋ dɩ la chʋa ʋ dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: La kɛŋ la kakusuŋ kʋdiilee arɩ la tɩtɩa ma kʋdiilee arɩ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ nɛ. La bɩ kʋŋ dɔŋ kala ka chɛ see dɩpɩnɩŋ.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ banɩhɩaŋ-la bʋl, “Má kʋ jʋʋ mɩ dɩa. Mɩ jaŋ pɩma kʋŋkala ma sɩɩ chɛ. Má sɩ́ dɩ-jalɩŋ chʋa.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ kɛmba jʋʋ ʋ dɩa, a ŋaa kʋdiilee pɩ ba kakusuŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba sɔŋ ba naasɩŋ aŋ dii kɩaa aŋ nyʋa.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Ba fa sɩ hɛ dɩa-la lɛ a didii kɩaa arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ ŋɩɩ, taŋ-la nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ dɔnsʋŋ kɔ a golli dɩa-la lɛ ba sɩ hɛ, a ŋmuŋmoo dɩa-la boro, aŋ kpɩa banɩhɩaŋ-la sɩ tɩɩ dɩa-la lɛ a bʋl, “Kɛŋ baal-la sɩ kʋ jʋʋ ŋ dɩa kʋ lɩɩ dɩ la kɛnʋ pɩŋ.”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ banɩhɩaŋ-la lɩɩ bʋla pɩba, “Nandɔmba, má sɩ́ wʋbɔmʋŋ deeŋ sɩ kɛŋ hɩɩsɩŋ ŋaa, baal-la ŋaa mɩ nʋhʋɔrʋ nɛ.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Na baal-la haala ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa nɛ ŋ-la, arɩ mɩ tolo ha sɩ bɩ baal kala jɩŋ. Mɩ jaŋ kɛmba kʋ lɩɩ pɩma dɩ ma ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ma sɩɩ chɛ. Ama má sɩ́ wʋlɩɩla kala ŋaa baala deeŋ-na lɛ.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Ama baala-la bɩ chɛ dɩ ba jegile nɩɩ ʋ teeŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Levi doho nɩɩ-la kɛŋ ʋ haal-la ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa kʋ lɩɩ pɩba. Ba gurugu a pɩnʋ tɩtaŋ-la kala, sɩaa pʋʋraa kɔ ba joŋu ta.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla haal-la sii mʋ dɩa-la lɛ ʋ bala sɩ hɛ, a tele pɩŋ boiŋ niiŋ, leriŋ pʋlla nyɩɩsɛ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Ʋ bala-la sii chʋchʋɔŋ a suri boiŋ kʋ lɩɩ dɩ ʋ viiri, dɩ ʋ haala nɛ tele pɩŋ boiŋ niiŋ ŋɩɩ, ʋ nɩsaa kʋ tɩgɛ boiŋ nii-jʋʋlʋŋ tɩtɩa lɛ.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Baal-la bʋla pɩ ʋ haala, “Sii dɩ la viiri.” Ama haal-la bɩ wɩɩkala bʋla. Ʋ sʋba nɛ ŋɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ joŋu a sagɛ ʋ kakumo lɛ a kɛnʋ mʋ dɩa.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ mʋ yi dɩa, ʋ joŋ sɩa a kɛŋ ʋ haal-la ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa kʋsʋʋŋ keri nandaasɩŋ fii arɩ balɩa, a kpaa Iziral doho doho-la kala.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala sɩ na haal-la nammɩa, ʋ sɩ, “La ha bɩ wʋdoho deeŋ na Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ aŋ ka, a lɩɩ bʋa-la lɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a kaa kɔ jɩnɩŋ. Má leŋ la bɩɩna na wɩɩ-la sɩ maga dɩ la ŋaa.”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Levi doho nɩɩ-la haala ba sɩ kpʋa bʋl, “Mɩ dɩ mɩ haala mɩ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa nɛ mʋ Gɩbɩa sɩ hɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ tinteeŋ lɛ dɩ la chʋa nɩmɛ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Mɩ joŋu kaa keri muno muno a kpaa Iziral doho doho-la kala, bɛɛ wɩaa nɩalɩŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ arɩ hɩɩsɩ wɩɩ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala, má ma bʋl wɩɩ-la ma sɩ kɛnɛ a mʋ tɩgɛ wɩɩŋ deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ kala sii chɩŋ a bʋl, “La kʋŋkala bɩ jaŋ mɩɩra mʋ dɩa da.

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ a ŋaa nii-bala dɩ ba yuo taŋ-la.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tɩŋ nɩaa ba mʋ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa kala teeŋ a pɩɛsɛba, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ wʋbɔŋ nɛ ma ŋaa ŋɩɩ?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Má chaarɛ Gɩbɩa nɩbɔmɔ-la sɩ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ pɩla dɩ la kpʋba a lɩɩsɛ wʋbɔŋ-la ta Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ.” Ama Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ bɩ jegile nɩɩ wɩɩ-la ba Iziral tɩmma-la dɔnsʋŋ sɩ bʋla.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba lɩɩ ba tasɩŋ a kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ Gɩbɩa lɛ dɩ ba yuo ba Iziral tɩmma-la dɔnsʋŋ.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, Iziral tɩmma-la sii mʋ ŋmoo ba buguŋ a kpagɛ Gɩbɩa.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩmma-la lɩɩ a chɩŋ lee-la ba sɩ jaŋ yuo Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ Gɩbɩa lɛ.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ kʋ lɩɩ Gɩbɩa lɛ a kpʋ Iziral laalɩyuoroo bʋɩ mara arɩ balɩa tapʋlɩɩ-la.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Arɔŋ nihiŋ Finihas sɩ ŋaa Elieza nanʋala nɛ faa beŋ daga-la.) Ba pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA, “La bɩra mʋ a yuo Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa sɩ ŋaa la naambiiriŋ koo la sɩ́ mʋ?” La TƖƖNA bʋl, “Má mʋ, chie mɩ jaŋ jomba hɛ ma nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa leŋ ba laalɩyuoroo dɔnsʋŋ mʋ faa a golli Gɩbɩa.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba fá to tintee-hɩlɩŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a mʋmʋ, ama ba bɩ foro Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Iziral tɩmma-la sɩ faa a sii jʋʋ taŋ-la kʋ tɔba hɛ a kpʋba.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ laalɩyuoro-la sɩ kɛŋ tokobiee a yuyuo, ba nɩaa bʋɩ mara arɩ banɔŋ nɛ ba kpʋ. Ba kala fa ŋaa laalɩyuori babiibala nɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩmma-la mɩɩra mʋ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ tasɩŋ a kpʋ nʋʋkala sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ, arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ kala a chei ba kʋŋkala, aŋ nyɩgɛ tasɩ-la kala sɩ hɛ lee-la.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa ŋmɩɛsa nɛ Mɩzɩpa lɛ a bʋl, “La kʋŋkala bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nʋʋ jaa la tolo.”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ Bɛtɛl a hɔŋ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ, wɩa tuu jʋʋ, aŋ faasa yiyel.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: Ba yel a bʋl, “Ou, La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ ŋaa la lɛ? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ Iziral doho doho dɔŋɔ jaŋ lɛl jɩnɩŋ?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, ba sii saa Wɩɩ-sʋlla koruŋ a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ nii-magɛ dɔŋɔ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩmma-la pɩɛsɛ, “La tʋɔŋ nyɩŋ bɛɛ nɩaa nɛ bɩ kʋ hilimi La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ Mɩzɩpa lɛ?” Ba fa ŋmɩɛsa nɛ arɩ nʋʋkala nɛ vɩa dɩ ʋ kʋ hilimi La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ, ʋ maga dɩ ba kpʋʋ nɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ chei ba naambiiriŋ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ wɩaa ba bʋl, “Jɩnɩŋ Iziral doho doho dɔŋɔ lɛlɛ nɛ la tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Ɛɛ nɛ la jaŋ ŋaa a na haalaa pɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ sɩ ka, la sɩ ŋmɩɛsa La TƖƖNA yɩrɩŋ lɛ arɩ la bɩ jaŋ joŋ la toloo pɩba dɩ ba jaa?”

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ Jabɛs Gɩlɩad nɩalɩŋ tʋɔŋ, ba na hatoloo zɔɔ-banɛsɛ ha sɩ bɩ baal jɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɛsɛba a kaa mʋ ba buguŋ sɩ hɛ Sɩlɔ lɛ Kɛnaŋ tinteeŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ hilime tɩŋ tɩndaarɩŋ pɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ Rimoŋ bʋŋ-la leriŋ arɩ ba leŋ yuosuŋ, ka dɩ ba kɛŋ nii-bala.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ mɩɩra kɔ Iziral tɩmma-la dɔnsʋŋ teeŋ. Ba joŋ Jabɛs Gɩlɩad nɩaa tolie-la ba sɩ bɩ kpʋa a pɩba. Ama tolie-la fa bɩ nɩalɩŋ nyuŋ chese.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma-la tʋɔŋ chei a tɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩ leŋe Iziral doho doho-la dɔŋɔ fuoli.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba sɩpaalaaraa bʋl, “La kpʋ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa haalaa kala nɛ, nɩɩ nɛ la jaŋ to a na haalaa pɩ baala-la sɩ ka?”

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: La bɩ jaŋ wuo joŋ la toloo a pɩba dɩ ba jaa, bɛɛ wɩaa la ŋmɩɛsa nɛ arɩ nʋʋkala nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ŋmɩaŋ jaŋ diiŋ.”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bɩɩnɛ wɩɩ-la aŋ bʋl, “Jɩna na-kala la sɩ yie gbieli La TƖƖNA gbiele-la Sɩlɔ lɛ, ʋ kpaga nɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Ba bʋla pɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ, “Má mʋ faa girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ tʋɔŋ,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: aŋ bibeŋ, dɩ Sɩlɔ tɩŋŋaa tolie-la nɛ kʋ lɩɩ a gʋgʋa gbiele-la lɛ, má guu sii a fá a mʋ dɩ nʋʋkala kɛŋ haal-la ʋ sɩ cho a kaa mʋ ma tinteeŋ.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Dɩ tolie-la nyɩmmaba koo dɩ ba dɩ-baalaa nɛ ŋaa goŋ, la jaŋ bʋla pɩba, ‘Laa sʋlma, má leŋ dɩ ba kɛŋ ma tolie-la, bɛɛ wɩaa la bɩ wuo na haalaa a pɩ ba kala bʋa-la lɛ la sɩɩ yuo laalɩŋ Jabɛs lɛ. Ma bɩ jaŋ laa cheeri kala, bɛɛ wɩaa ma dee bɩ ma toloo joŋo pɩba.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ ba sɩ dagɛba. Bʋa-la lɛ tolie-la sɩ kʋ lɩɩ gʋgʋa, ba kʋŋkala sii a mʋ kɛŋ tolie-la dɔŋɔ, a kaa mʋ ŋaa ʋ haala. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba mɩɩra mʋ ba tinteeŋ a wasa saa ba tasɩŋ a hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ nɛ Iziral tɩmma-la kʋkaanaa ma kala mɩɩra mʋ ba doho doho arɩ ba nyɩŋ-nɩaa leriŋ.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa bɩ kuoro kɛnɛ, nʋʋkala faa ŋaa wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ cho nɛ.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Baal-la yɩrɩŋ nɛ Ɛlɩmɛlɛk, ʋ haala ma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Nawomi. Ʋ hambolibiisi-la ma yɩraa nɛ Malɔŋ arɩ Kilioŋ. Ba kala ŋaa Ɛfɩraf tɩŋŋaa nɛ a lɩɩ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm sɩ hɛ Juda tinteeŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba mʋ hɔŋ Mʋab tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛlɩmɛlɛk sʋʋ, aŋ ka Nawomi arɩ ʋ hambolibiisi-la balɩa.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Ʋ hambolibiisi-la jaa Mʋab tɩŋŋaa toloo. Tolie-la dɔŋɔ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Opa, dɔŋɔ ma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Ruf. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba hɛ nɩmɛ ŋɩɩ a mʋ yi jɩsɩŋ fii,

english_verse: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
translation_verse: Malɔŋ arɩ Kilioŋ ma sʋʋ, aŋ ka Nawomi dʋndʋŋa. Ʋ bɩ bala kɛnɛ, ʋ bɩ bii ma kɛnɛ.

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ dɩ ʋ bii-haalaa kala sii lee-la ba fa sɩ hɔnɔ, a lɩɩ joŋ wombiiŋ dɩ ba mɩɩra mʋ Juda tinteeŋ.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi bʋla pɩ ʋ bii-haala-la balɩa, “Má mɩɩra mʋ ma naamba teeŋ, La TƖƖNA jaŋ kɛmma woruŋ arɩ ma sɩ kɛmmɛ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ sʋba woruŋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA jaŋ pɛ ma lɛ dɩ ma na balaba a jaa, a hɔŋ arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa.” Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ, ʋ guoriba a taba dɩ ba viiri, ba faasa yel a bʋl,

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: “La jaŋ to ŋ harɩŋ a mʋ ŋ nɩaa teeŋ.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi bʋla pɩba, “Mɩ toloo, má mɩɩra mʋ ma jaŋ. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ maa chɛ dɩ ma to mɩ harɩŋ mʋ? Ma bɩɩna mɩ jaŋ bɩra wuo lʋl hambolibiisiŋ pɩma dɩ ma jaa?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Mɩ toloo, má mɩɩra mʋ ma jaŋ, mɩ hɩɛsa nɛ arɩ mɩ sɩ jaŋ bɩra jaa bala a lʋl biiriŋ. Dɩ mɩ nɛ paala jaa bala tɩtaŋɩŋ deeŋ a lʋl hambolibiisiŋ ma,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
