translation_verse: ma jaŋ wuo gbɛrɛ dɩ ba waa? Ma jaŋ tɩŋ ba wɩaa a sɩ́ balaba jaa? Mɩ toloo, aɩ, ŋɩɩ bɩ jaŋ ŋaa. Wɩɩ-la wɩɩmɛ a kɩkɩɩma, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA vɩamɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Nawomi sɩ bʋl wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ba bɩra yel, ŋɩɩ nɛ Opa-na guori ʋ bala naaŋ a taʋ aŋ mɩɩra mʋ dɩa, ka Ruf-na vɩa aŋ mɛrɛ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi bɩra bʋla pɩ Ruf, “Bee na, ŋ tol-dɔŋɔ mɩɩra nɛ a mʋ ʋ nɩaa arɩ ʋ vesiŋ teeŋ, ŋ ma mɩɩrɛ dɩ ma mʋ.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Ama Ruf ma sɩ, “Sɩ́ mɩ kiru ŋ harɩŋ. Lee-la kala ŋ sɩɩ mʋ, mɩ ma jaŋ mʋ, lee-la kala ŋ sɩ jaŋ hɛ, mɩ ma jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ. Ŋ nɩaa jaŋ ŋaa mɩ nɩaa, dɩ ŋ Wɩa ma ŋaa mɩ Wɩa.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Lee-la ŋ sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ, nɩmɛ nɛ mɩ ma jaŋ sʋʋ dɩ ba hugimi nɩmɛ. A leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA dɔgɩsɛmɛ dɩ mɩ nɛ mɩɩrɛ ŋ harɩŋ, see sʋʋŋ nɛ jaŋ kɛnla pɔrɛ.”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Nawomi sɩ na dɩ Ruf chaasa kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ dɩ ʋ to ʋ harɩŋ, ʋ leŋu ʋ bɩra bɩ ʋ kire.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba to dɔŋɔ a mʋ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm. Ba sɩ mʋ yi nɩmɛ, taŋ-la nɩaa hihirigi, haalaa ŋaa goŋ a pɩpɩɛsɛ, “Nawomi nɛ ŋ-la?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Nawomi bʋla pɩba, “Má bɩra sɩ́ mɩ Nawomi yɩrʋ, ma yɩyɩrɛmɛ Mara, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna leŋe mɩ na hɛɛŋ nɛ woruŋ.”

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Mɩɩ lɩɩ daha dɩ mɩ nɩsɩŋ kala suo nɛ, aŋ ka La TƖƖNA mɩɩra kɛmmɛ kɔ arɩ na-hɩllɩŋ. Bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ ma ha jaŋ yɩyɩrɛmɛ Nawomi? La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna joŋ wʋwalɩmaa a hɛ mɩ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Nawomi arɩ ʋ bii-haala Ruf lɩɩ Mʋab tinteeŋ a kɔ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm dɩ ba mɩɩ-bumbumba kʋmʋŋ yie yi.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩ diene dɩ Bʋas lɩɩ Bɛtɩlɛhɛm kɔ, a chʋɔlɛ tɩntɩnna-la aŋ bʋl, “La TƖƖNA Wɩa jaŋ hɛ ma teeŋ.” Ba ma bʋl, “La TƖƖNA jaŋ pɛ ŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas pɩɛsɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ, “Hantolibii bɛɛ nɛ ŋ-la?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ-la bʋl, “Mʋab tɩŋŋaa tolo-la sɩ to Nawomi harɩŋ kɔ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Ʋ sʋlmɛ nɛ dɩ mɩ leŋ dɩ ʋ to la harɩŋ a kukuuni kɩalɩŋ la sɩ gɛllɛ ta. Chʋchʋɔŋ kala nɛ ʋ kukuuni kɩaa, lɛɛlɛ nɛ ʋ hɔŋ la lɛbɩŋ lɛ dɩ ʋ wiesi mʋa.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas bʋla pɩ Ruf, “Mɩ tolo, jegile nɩɩ, sɩ nʋʋkala baga mʋ kuuni kɩaa, hɛ baga deeŋ lɛ, a kpagɛ haala-la sɩ tɩma pɩpɩmɛ.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Mʋ kuuni kɩaa lee-la baala-la sɩɩ tɩŋ, mɩ bʋla pɩba, dɩ ba sɩ́ ŋ walɩmʋ nɛ ka dɩ ŋ to haala-la harɩŋ dɩ ma kala tɩtɩŋ. Dɩ lɩɩnyʋasʋŋ nɛ kɛnɩŋ, mʋ nyʋa loŋ-la lɛ ba sɩɩ nyʋa.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Ruf sɩ nɩɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ʋ tuu kpirimi Bʋas sɩpaaŋ aŋ bʋl, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ wɩaa faasa chɩlɩŋ ŋ-la? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ kɛŋ zile mɩ ma nʋhʋɔra deeŋ teeŋ?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas bɩra bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa pɩ ŋ bala naaŋ nɛ, ŋ bala sʋʋŋ harɩŋ. Mɩ nɩɩ ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ leŋ ŋ nyɩmma arɩ ŋ naaŋ arɩ ŋ jaŋ aŋ kɔ dɩ ŋ hɛ nɩaa teeŋ ŋ ha sɩ bɩ jɩŋ.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA jaŋ timiŋ a tɩŋ wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa lɛ. A leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa teeŋ ŋ sɩ kɔ dɩ ʋ pɔŋ, faasa timiŋ yʋgɛ.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ruf bʋl, “Mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, ŋ zilmi kɩŋkɛŋ nɛ a leŋ mɩ yaraa faasa fɩɛlɛ, a tɩŋ ŋ sɩ fɩɛla bʋl wɩaa mɩ teeŋ. Mɩ paala bɩ mɩ tɩtɩa wuo kaa magɩsɛ ŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-haala-la kʋbala ma.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la sɩ yie dɩ ba dii kʋdiilee, Bʋas yɩrɛ Ruf, “Kʋ laa kʋdiilee a kaa yuu sɩ-nyalɩŋ a dii.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ kɔ ʋ dɩ tɩntɩnna-la hɔŋ, Bʋas joŋ mɩɩ-halaa pʋ, ʋ dii a vɔgɛ aŋ ka.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ sie dɩ ʋ bɩra kuuni kɩaa, Bʋas bʋla pɩ baala-la sɩɩ tɩŋ baga-la lɛ, “Má leŋ dɩ ʋ to a kukuuni pugulo-la ma tʋɔŋ, má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ hɩɩsɩŋ kɛnʋ.

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ruf kuuni kɩalɩŋ baga-la lɛ ŋɩɩ deeŋ deeŋ wɩa tuu jʋʋ. Ʋ sɩ ŋmoo mɩa-la ʋ sɩ kuuno, ʋ na kuokuo-gbansɩŋ banɔŋ nɛ.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Ʋ kaa mʋ dɩa a kaa dagɛ ʋ bala naaŋ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ kuuni kɩaa magɛ, aŋ pɛ joŋ kʋdii-kaana-la ʋ sɩ die aŋ ka pʋ.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi pɩɛsɛ Ruf, “Nɩɩ nɛ ŋ mʋ a kuuni kɩaa magɛ ŋ-la? Kʋbɛɛ baga lɛ nɛ ŋ mʋ kuuni? Wɩa jaŋ pɛ baal-la sɩ cho ŋ wɩaa a pɩŋ kɩaa magɛ ŋ-la.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ruf bʋla pɩ Nawomi arɩ nɩɩ-la baga lɛ ʋ sɩ mʋ kuuni kɩaa yɩrɩŋ nɛ Bʋas.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi bʋl, “La TƖƖNA nɩɩ beŋ nɩweyee arɩ nɩsʋʋnʋŋ kala, ʋ jaŋ pɛ Bʋas lɛ. Bʋas ŋaa mɩ bala naambii nɛ. Ʋ nɛ ŋaa nɩalɩŋ dɔŋɔ fa sɩ maga dɩ ʋ bibenla.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Ruf, Mʋab tɩŋŋaa tolo-la, bɩra bʋla pɩ Nawomi, “Ʋ sɩ́ dɩ mɩ pɛ tɩtɩŋ baga-la tɩntɩŋŋaa nɛ dɩ ba mʋ dɛrɛ.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi bʋl, “Mɩ tolo, ʋ jaŋ ŋaa wʋzɔŋ dɩ ŋ nɛ pɛ haala-la sɩ tɩmaa pʋ lɛ dɩ ma tɩtɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa dɩ ŋ nɛ mʋ nʋʋ dɔŋ baga, ba jaŋ wuo ŋaaŋ wʋbɔŋ.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ruf pɛ haala-la sɩ tɩmaa pɩ Bʋas lɛ a kuuni kɩaa ŋɩɩ deeŋ deeŋ ba mʋ kʋŋ mɛmpɛ-la arɩ mɩa-la dɛrɛ. Ka ba dɩ ʋ bala naaŋ ha jʋjʋʋ.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala Nawomi pɩɛsɛ ʋ bii-haala Ruf, “Mɩ tolo, ʋ bɩ jaŋ ŋaa wʋzɔŋ dɩ mɩ nɛ chɛ dɩhɔnʋŋ pɩŋ dɩ ŋ hɔŋ arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Ŋ jɩma Bʋas, nɩɩ-la tɩntɩnnɩ haalaa lɛ ŋ sɩ pɛ ma tɩtɩŋ, ŋaa mɩ bala naambii nɛ. Tɩtaŋɩŋ deeŋ ʋ jaŋ chɩchaarɛ ʋ mɩaa taha lɛ.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Fo lɩɩŋ, a tɩsɛ tʋlaalɩɩ a laalɛ gɛrɩ-zɔmʋŋ a mʋ taha-la. Ama sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ʋ jɩŋ arɩ ŋ hɛ nɩmɛ see dɩ ʋ dii kʋdiilee aŋ nyʋa kɩaa dɛrɛ.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ pɩna, jɩŋ lee-la ʋ sɩ pɩna dɩ ŋ mʋ a kɛŋ ʋ gɛrɩ-bɔsɔ suri ʋ naasɩŋ dɩɩrɩŋ aŋ pɩŋ nɩmɛ. Ʋ jaŋ dagɩŋ wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Ruf bʋl, “Mɩ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ bʋla.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ruf mʋ taha-la a ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ʋ bala naaŋ sɩ dagʋ.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Bʋas sɩ dii kʋdiilee a nyʋa kɩaa dɛrɛ ʋ yaraa kala fɩɛlɛ ŋɩɩ, ʋ mʋ yelli mɩɩ-bii-la a pɩŋ doŋ. Ruf lʋara mʋ kɛŋ ʋ gɛrɩ-bɔsɔ suri ʋ naasɩŋ dɩɩrɩŋ aŋ pɩŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas hirige sii tɩta-siesee a bɩrɩma na dɩ haal nɛ pɩŋ ʋ naasɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ pɩɛsɛ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ?” Ruf bʋl, “Mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna Ruf nɛ. Kɛŋ ŋ gɛrɩ-bɔsɔ tɔmɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ ŋaa mɩ bala nyɩmma naambii nɛ.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas bʋl, “La TƖƖNA jaŋ pɛ ŋ lɛ mɩ tolo, zile deeŋ ŋ sɩ ŋaa mɩ lɛ kɩɩ ŋ sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ. Ŋ fa jaŋ wuo kire to bapʋɔsaa harɩŋ, dɩ ba kɛŋ kʋŋ koo ba bɩ kʋŋ kɛnɛ, ama ŋ bɩ ŋɩɩ ŋaa.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ nɛ arɩ mɩ ŋaa ŋ bala nyɩmma naambii nɛ, ama la naambie dɔŋɔ hɛ nɩmɛ a kpagɛ ŋ jaanɩŋ a kɩɩmɛ.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Pɩŋ daha dɩ taŋ pʋl, dɩ la naambile nɛ jaŋ laaŋ ʋ zɔmɔ, dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩŋ laa, La TƖƖNA doluŋ lɛ mɩ-na jaŋ beniŋ, ŋ-na pɩŋ daha dɩ taŋ pʋl.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ruf pɩŋ Bʋas naasɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ taŋ pʋl, aŋ laa sɩpaaŋ sii dɩ nʋʋkala bɩ jɩŋ. Bʋas bʋla pɩ Ruf, “Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ nʋʋkala jɩŋ arɩ haal dɩa pɩŋ taha deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Bʋas bɩra bʋl, “Kɛŋ gɛrɩ-la sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ ŋ sɩ laala kaa jɛrɛ.” Ʋ sɩ kaa jɛrɛ, Bʋas ŋaa mɩa-la gbansɩŋ fii hɛ pʋ, a kaa chʋŋʋ, ʋ mʋ dɩa.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Aŋ bɩra bʋl, “Ʋ sɩ́ ʋ bɩ maga dɩ mɩ kɛŋ na-hɩllɩŋ kɔ dɩa aŋ ŋaa mɩaa gbansɩŋ fii a pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ tolo, gbɛrɛ a na wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa. Bʋas bɩ jaŋ hɔŋ see dɩ ʋ na wɩɩ-la dɩdɛrɩŋ jɩnɩŋ.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas mʋ hɔŋ ba taŋ-la boiŋ niiŋ, lee-la ba sɩɩ hilimu, dɩ Ɛlɩmɛlɛk naambile wɩaa Bʋas sɩ bʋla kʋʋ bal. Bʋas yɩrʋ, “Nandɔŋ, kʋ hɔŋ daha.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ mʋ a hɔŋ.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Bʋas yɩrɛ taŋ-la nɩhɩasɩŋ fii ba kʋ pɛ ba lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋl, “Ma ma hɔŋ daha.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba hɔŋ.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ kʋ hɔnɔ dɛrɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas bʋla pɩ ʋ naambile sɩ maga dɩ ʋ dii Ɛlɩmɛlɛk dʋa, “Nawomi sɩ lɩɩ Mʋab tinteeŋ kɔ, ka chɛ dɩ ʋ yallɛ la naambie Ɛlɩmɛlɛk ŋmaŋkaaŋ nɛ.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Mɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ jɩŋ wɩɩŋ deeŋ lɛ nɛ, dɩ ŋ nɩɩ chɛ ŋmaŋkaa-la, laa yɔɔ nɩhɩasɩŋ deemba kala sɩ hɔŋ daha sɩpaaŋ dɩ ba na. Dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩra bɩ chɛ ma, leŋ dɩ mɩ jɩŋ. Bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ nɛ maga ŋ yɔɔ ŋmaŋkaaŋ deeŋ, a lɩɩ ŋ harɩŋ mɩ ma nɛ tɩga.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la bʋl, “Mɩ jaŋ yɔɔ.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Bʋas sɩ, “Ŋ wasa nɛ, ta jɩŋ, dɩ ŋ nɛ yɔɔ ŋmaŋkaa-la Nawomi teeŋ, ŋɩɩ daga arɩ ŋ nɛ tɩɩ Ruf ma, Mʋab tɩŋŋaa tolo-la bala sɩ sʋba, dɩ ŋmaŋkaa-la hɛ nɩsʋʋ-la dɩa nɩaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la bʋl, “Dɩ ŋɩɩ-na nɛ mɩ bɩ jaŋ yɔɔ ŋmaŋkaa-la, bɛɛ wɩaa, ŋɩɩ daga dɩ mɩ nɛ sʋba, mɩ biiriŋ bɩ ŋmaŋkaa-la wuo tɩɩ. Laa yɔɔ, mɩ-na bɩ jaŋ wuo.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la bʋla pɩ Bʋas, “Ŋ tɩtɩa laa ŋmaŋkaa-la yɔɔ,” aŋ chaarɛ ʋ nɛntɛŋŋɛɛ pɩ Bʋas.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas bʋla pɩ nɩhɩasɩ-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala fa sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ, “Jɩnɩŋ ma kala pɛ na nɛ arɩ mɩ nɛ yɔɔ Ɛlɩmɛlɛk arɩ ʋ biiriŋ Kilioŋ arɩ Malɔŋ dʋa kala Nawomi teeŋ.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: A lɩɩ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ, Ruf, Mʋab tɩŋŋaa tolo-la Malɔŋ fa sɩ jaa, ma lɛɛlɛ ŋaa mɩ haala nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ jaŋ leŋ dɩ nɩsʋʋ-la yɩrɩŋ sɩ́ lɛl ʋ nɩaa tʋɔŋ, dɩ ʋ dʋa ma hɛ ba nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Jɩnɩŋ ma ŋaa pɛ-naara nɛ wɩɩŋ deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩhɩasɩ-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hilimi taŋ-la boi-baalɩŋ niiŋ bʋl, “Oo, la pɛ na nɛ, La TƖƖNA jaŋ pɛ ŋ haal-la lɛ dɩ ʋ nagɛ Rakɛl arɩ Liya sɩ lʋl biiriŋ yʋgɛ ŋɩɩ a pɩ Jekɔb doho nɩaa. Wɩa jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ Ɛfɩraf doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ a ŋaa nɩbal Bɛtɩlɛhɛm lɛ.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA jaŋ leŋ dɩ biiri-la tol-bie deeŋ sɩ jaŋ lʋla pɩŋ nagɛ Pɛrɛs, bile Tama sɩ lʋla pɩ Juda.”

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bʋas jaa Ruf ba pɛ bɔsɔ, La TƖƖNA pɛ Ruf lɛ ʋ kɛŋ luoruŋ a lʋl hambolibie.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ haalaa bʋla pɩ Nawomi, “Dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA, jɩnɩŋ ʋ pɩŋ nihiŋ nɛ dɩ ʋ beniŋ. Wɩa jaŋ leŋ dɩ bie deeŋ kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Ŋ bii-haala choŋ nɛ, ʋ paala kɩɩ hambolibiisiŋ balɩpɛ. Lɛɛlɛ ʋ lʋl nihiŋ sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ wɩaa bɩra zɔmɔ pɩŋ nɛ ŋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, dɩ ŋ nɛ kʋ hɩɛsɛ ma ʋ jaŋ bibeniŋ.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nawomi joŋ bile hɛ ʋ naasɩŋ lɛ, a bibeŋ ʋ nyuŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Haala-la sɩ hɛ lee-la hɛ bile yɩrɩŋ Ɔbɛd, aŋ bʋla pɩ nʋʋkala arɩ ba lʋl hambolibie nɛ a pɩ Nawomi. Ɔbɛd nɛ sii lʋl Jesi, Jesi ma lʋl Devit.

english_verse: Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
translation_verse: Ɔbɛd ma nɛ lʋl Jesi. Jesi ma nɛ lʋl Devit.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Baal kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ, ʋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Ɛlɩkaana. Ʋ ŋaa Zuf nyɩŋ-nɩaa dɔŋɔ nɛ, a lɩɩ Rama sɩ hɛ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ. Ʋ nyɩmma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Jeroham. Jeroham ma nyɩmma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Elihu. Elihu ma nyɩmma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Tohu. Tohu ma nyɩmma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Zuf. Zuf fa ŋaa Efirem tɩɩna nɛ.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Ɛlɩkaana fa kɛŋ haalaa balɩa nɛ, dɔŋɔ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Hana, dɔŋɔ ma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Penina. Penina lʋl biiriŋ, ka Hana bɩ bii lʋla.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Jɩna na-kala, Ɛlɩkaana yie lɩɩ ʋ jaŋ Rama a mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩlɔ dɩ ʋ zil La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna aŋ pɛ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ. Sɩlɔ lɛ baal kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ baa yɩrɛ Eli. Ʋ fa ŋaa La TƖƖNA Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaarʋ nɛ. Ʋ fa kɛŋ hambolibiisiŋ balɩa nɛ, baa yɩrɛ Hofini arɩ Finihas, ba ma fa ŋaa La TƖƖNA Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɛ.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Bʋa na-kala lɛ dɩ Ɛlɩkaana nɛ kʋ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, ʋ yie kpaa nammɩa-la a pɩ ʋ haala Penina arɩ ʋ biiriŋ kala nɛ.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Ama kpaal-la ʋ sɩ yie joŋo pɩ Penina, ʋ bʋlɩa nɛ ʋ yie joŋo pɩ Hana, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ fa chou nɛ woruŋ, aŋ ka La TƖƖNA kɛŋ ʋ lʋla tɔ.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA sɩ kɛŋ Hana lʋla tɔ ŋɩɩ wɩaa, ʋ ha-dɔŋɔ Penina yie ŋaa wɩaa a sisii ʋ baanɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Ʋ vɛnɛɛ ŋaaʋ ŋɩɩ nɛ jɩna na-kala. Dɩ Hana nɛ mʋ La TƖƖNA dɩa, ʋ ha-dɔŋ-la yie dii ʋ baanɩŋ lɛ, ʋ yel a vɩa kʋdiilee.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Ʋ bala Ɛlɩkaana yie pɩɛsɛ, “Hana, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ yiyel? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ vɩa kʋdiilee? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ chei? Ŋ bɩ bene arɩ mɩ kɩɩ hambolibiisiŋ fii ŋ teeŋ?”

english_verse: When the sacrifice had been offered, and they had eaten the meal, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli was sitting in his chair near the door to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala ba sɩ dii kʋdiilee dɛrɛ La TƖƖNA dɩa lɛ Sɩlɔ lɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ Hana sii chɩŋ, dɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Eli ma hɔŋ kpasa nyuŋ, La TƖƖNA dɩa boiŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: Hannah was heartbroken and was crying as she prayed,
translation_verse: Hana tʋɔŋ kala fa cheye nɛ, ʋ chaasa yiyel aŋ chʋchʋɔlɛ Wɩa.

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ ta niiŋ a bʋl, “La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna, mɩ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ nɛ, na mɩ wɩɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ hɛɛŋ ŋɩɩ. Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, pɩmɛ hambolibie. Dɩ ŋ nɛ pɩmɛ hambolibie, ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ mɩ jaŋ joŋu a hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Nyu-fʋna kala bɩ jaŋ lɔgɛ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Hana fa kɛŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ nɛ a chʋchʋɔlɛ Wɩa, aŋ ka ʋ niipinee ta jijigisi, ŋ bɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩɩ bʋl ka nɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Eli-na fa bɩɩnɛ ʋ bugo nɛ.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩ Hana, “Ɛɛ nɛ ŋ chɛ dɩ ŋ bugo diene magɛ? Leŋ dɩ sɩŋ-la lɩɩ ŋ sɩaa lɛ.”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Sɩ́ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna joŋo arɩ mɩ ŋaa hatɔɔ nɛ, ba lɩma kɛmmɛ nɛ. Mɩ tʋɔŋ nɛ cheye kɩŋkɛŋ mɩ sʋsʋl Wɩa ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Eli bʋl, “Ŋ jaŋ mʋ dɩa arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa, a leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa pɩŋ kʋ-la kala ŋ sɩ sʋlaa chɛ ʋ teeŋ.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Hana bʋl, “A leŋ dɩ ŋ zile yʋgɛ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna teeŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ mʋ, a dii kɩaa, ʋ tʋɔ-chee-la dɛrɛ.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla Ɛlɩkaana arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa sii chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla a zil La TƖƖNA, aŋ mɩɩra mʋ ba jaŋ Rama. Ɛlɩkaana arɩ ʋ haala Hana pɛ bɔsɔ, La TƖƖNA laa ʋ sʋla.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hana kɛŋ luoruŋ, a lʋl hambolibie, a hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Samʋɛl, aŋ bʋl, “Mɩ sʋl La TƖƖNA nɛ ʋ joŋu pɩmɛ.” Hana joŋ Samʋɛl hɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Harɩŋ, Ɛlɩkaana arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa kala bɩra sii mʋ Sɩlɔ dɩ ba kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, arɩ ba sɩ vɛnɛɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ jɩna na-kala, aŋ pɛ lɩɩsɛ nii-la ʋ sɩ ta.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Ama Hana-na bɩ mʋa. Ʋ bʋla pɩ ʋ bala, “Dɩ bile nɛ waa dɩ mɩ kɛrʋ yɩlɩŋ lɛ, ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ mɩ jaŋ kɛnʋ kaa mʋ pɩ La TƖƖNA, dɩ ʋ hɛ nɩmɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Ʋ bala bʋla pʋ, “Ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ bɩɩna dɩ ʋ zɔmɔ pɩŋ. Hɛ daha a kaa mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ ŋ sɩ jaŋ kɛrʋ yɩlɩŋ lɛ, a leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA ŋaa dɩ nii-la ŋ sɩ hɛ chɩŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hana hɛ dɩa lɛ, a dɩɛsɛ bile ŋɩɩ a mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩ kɛrʋ yɩlɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Hana bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, mɩ nɛ tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala kʋ chɩŋ ŋ sɛmɛ aa sʋl La TƖƖNA ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Bie deeŋ nɛ mɩ fa sʋlaa chɛ. La TƖƖNA ŋaa wɩɩ-la mɩ fa sɩ sʋla chɩchɛ pɩmɛ nɛ,

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: ŋɩɩ wɩaa mɩ joŋu hɩhɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ, La TƖƖNA nɛ jaŋ tɩɩʋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA lee-la.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hana chʋɔlɛ Wɩa a bʋl, “La TƖƖNA leŋe mɩ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ nɛ woruŋ. Ʋ nɛ leŋe mɩ kɛŋ doluŋ, aa mɔŋ mɩ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ. Mɩ tʋɔŋ tɔrɔ nɛ woruŋ ʋ sɩ laamɛ ta.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala tuo a bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ, see La TƖƖNA dʋndʋŋa, nʋʋkala tuo a magʋ. Nʋʋkala tuo a jaŋ wuo pɔla a magɛ la Wɩa.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ babiibal wɩaa bʋbʋl koo a bibigisi ma tɩtɩa lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA Wɩa nɛ jɩŋ wɩɩkala, a jaŋ dii nʋʋkala sarɩya.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Laalɩyuori babiibalaa tosuŋ boro nɛ, aŋ ka nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ mɩɩra kɛŋ doluŋ.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ dii vʋvɔgɛ mɩɩra pɛrɛ pachɩŋŋaa nɛ didii, ama losuŋ fa sɩ kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ mɩɩra dii vʋvɔgɛ nɛ. Haal-la sɩ bɩ bii lʋla, mɩɩra lʋl biiriŋ balɩpɛ nɛ. Ka haal-la fa sɩ kɛŋ biiriŋ yʋgɛ bɩra bɩ bii kɛnɛ.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA nɛ leŋe nɩaa sʋsʋʋ. Ʋ nɩɩ pɩ nɩaa mɩɩsɩŋ ma. Ʋ nɛ yie leŋ nɩaa sʋʋ a mʋ lɛlɛɛ-jaŋ, aŋ bɩra chɩsɛba ba kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA nɛ yie leŋ nɩa ŋaa summu koo a ŋaa kɩaa tɩɩna. Ʋ nɛ yie kɛŋ nɩa muuri koo a ŋaa ʋ ŋaa nɩbal.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Ʋ nɛ yie chʋʋlɛ summoo kʋŋkɔlʋŋ lɛ, aŋ kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ ta ba sii tʋɔrʋŋ nyuŋ, a leŋ ba guoli kuori-biiriŋ tʋɔŋ, a leŋ ba hɔŋ lee sɩ kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ. La TƖƖNA nɛ ŋaa tinteeŋ gentine kala, a leŋ dʋnɩa chɩŋ ʋ nyuŋ a ŋaa ʋ kʋŋ.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ pɔ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tou arɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ. Ama nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ-na jaŋ lɛl birimiŋ tʋɔŋ. Nuhuobiine bɩ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa doluŋ a ŋaa wɩɩkala.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA jaŋ chei nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ vɩaʋ. Ʋ jaŋ na baanɩŋ, a kpɩa ba lɛ a nagɛ duonuŋ. La TƖƖNA jaŋ dii dʋnɩa nɩaa kala sarɩya. Ʋ jaŋ joŋ doluŋ a pɩ kuoru-la ʋ sɩ lɩɩsa, dɩ ʋ kɛŋ doluŋ kʋŋkala nyuŋ.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛlɩkaana mɩɩra mʋ ʋ jaŋ Rama, ka Samʋɛl pɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Eli lɛ a tɩma pɩpɩ La TƖƖNA. Eli hambolibiisiŋ

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Ba bɩ wombie-la Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa sɩ maga dɩ ba to a laa kɩaa nɩaa teeŋ ka to. Ba wɩɩŋ nɛ, dɩ nʋʋ nɛ kpʋ pʋna a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a joŋ nammɩa-la chɔ, ba kʋŋkala yie tɩŋ ʋ tɩntɩnna, ʋ joŋ nammɩɩ-lɩɩsɩrɩ laha sɩ kɛŋ kerikee batori a kori.

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ laha-la a mʋ tʋʋ pupoiŋ koo kʋŋ na-kala ba sɩ kaa chɔ nammɩa-la tʋɔŋ. Kʋ-la na-kala ʋ sɩ lɩɩsa, ba nɛ tɩɩʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba yie joŋo ŋaa Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ yie kɔ Sɩlɔ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ ma dʋndʋŋa dee, ka dɩ ba-na paala lɩɩsɛ pʋna nʋʋŋ a nyɩgɛ, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara tɩntɩnna jaŋ mʋ bʋl nɩɩ-la sɩɩ sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ lɛ, “Chɔgɛ nammɩa pɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara dɩ ʋ wasɛ. Ʋ bɩ nammɩɩ chɔɔlʋŋ ka chɛ, see kʋhuoŋ.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩɩ-la nɛ bʋla pʋ, “Leŋ dɩ mɩ laa sɩpaaŋ a nyɩgɛ nʋʋ-la aŋ ka ŋ-na chɔgɛ magɛ ŋɩɩ kala ŋ sɩɩ chɛ,” tɩntɩnnʋ-la yie bʋl, “Aɩ, chɔgɔ pɩmɛ lɛɛlɛ, ŋɩɩ dee, mɩ jaŋ chɔgɛ arɩ doluŋ.”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Wɩɩŋ deeŋ Eli hambolibiisi-la sɩɩ ŋaa chaasa ŋaa wʋbɔŋ-bal nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba kɛŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kaa kʋ pɩ La TƖƖNA aa ŋmoo gbɛɛŋ nɛ.

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Ama Samʋɛl-na fa hɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ nɛ a tɩma pʋpʋ bʋa na-kala. Ʋ fa ŋaa bii-bie nɛ a laalɛ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ gɛrɩ-laala-daŋɩŋ.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Jɩna na-kala ʋ naaŋ yie yɛrɛ gɛrɩ-duduo-bie nɛ a kaa kʋ pʋ, dɩ ʋ dɩ ʋ bala nɛ kɔ dɩ ba kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa ba jɩna Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Eli yie sʋl Wɩa pɩ Ɛlɩkaana arɩ ʋ haala a bʋl, “La TƖƖNA jaŋ pɛ ŋ dɩ ŋ haala deeŋ lɛ dɩ ma lʋl biiriŋ, dɩ ba chɩŋ bie deeŋ nyuŋ, bie deeŋ ʋ sɩ sʋl Wɩa ʋ joŋo pʋ ʋ ma bɩra joŋu hɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ.” Dɩ ʋ nɛ sʋl Wɩa pɩba dɛrɛ, ba yie mɩɩra mʋ dɩa.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA pɛ Hana lɛ, ʋ bɩra lʋl hambolibiisiŋ batori arɩ hantolibiisiŋ ma balɩa. Ama Samʋɛl-na hɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ nɛ a mʋ waa.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Mɩ biiri, má sɩ́ ŋɩɩ ŋaa, wɩɩŋ deeŋ La TƖƖNA nɩaa sɩ gɔllɔ bʋlaa bal ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ ʋ dɔŋɔ lɛ, Wɩa jaŋ wuo jʋʋ ma balɩa pɛgɛ a kɛmma hɛ dɔŋɔ, ama dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ŋaa wɩaa chei La TƖƖNA teeŋ, kʋbɛɛ ma nɛ saa bɩra jaŋ jʋʋ ma pɛgɛ a kɛmma hɛ dɔŋɔ?” Ama ʋ hambolibiisi-la bɩ jegile nɩɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ kpʋrɩsɛ ba dɩgɩlaa, bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA paala kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ dɩ ʋ kpʋba.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Ka Samʋɛl ha wʋwaa, La TƖƖNA arɩ nuhuobiinee kala tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ ʋ nyuŋ. Ba bʋl wɩalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa Eli dɩa nɩaa lɛ

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala lɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla kɔ Eli teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Mɩ fa chaasa kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa kʋ dagɛ ŋ nyɩmma dɩa nɩaa nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ ŋaa Ijipiti kuoro yosi.

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ: Mɩ fa bʋla pɩ ŋ dɩa nɩaa arɩ ŋ nyɩŋ-nɩaa, dɩ ba nɛ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa bʋa na-kala, ama lɛɛlɛ mɩ bʋla arɩ ŋɩɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ chɩŋ. Nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ zilmi, mɩ ma jaŋ zilba, aŋ bɛrɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ mɩ kaa tɩtɩŋ.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala jaŋ yi dɩ mɩ kpʋ ŋ dɩa bapʋɔsaa arɩ ŋ nyɩŋ-nɩaa bapʋɔsaa kala. Ŋ doho nʋʋkala bɩ jaŋ hɩɛsɛ aŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Ŋ jaŋ na hɛɛŋ woruŋ, ka dɩ mɩ ŋaa wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ a pɩpɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa. Ŋ dɩa nɩaa tʋɔŋ, nʋʋkala bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ ʋ hɩɛsa aŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Dɩ mɩ nɛ paala bɩ nʋʋ kpʋa ŋ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ ma, ka dɩ ʋ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaarʋ, ʋ jaŋ yel a nyʋlɩmɛ dɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ faasa chei woruŋ. Ŋ doho nɩaa kala jaŋ sʋʋ nɩduo-sʋʋŋ.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Ŋ hambolibiisi-la balɩa, Hofini arɩ Finihas kala jaŋ sʋʋ chɛ bala. Ŋɩɩ jaŋ ŋaa magɩl arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ bʋla sɛnɛ jaŋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩba.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ lɩɩsɛ nɩtɛŋɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaarʋ, a ŋɩŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩɩ chɛ. Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ʋ dɩa chɩŋ woruŋ, ʋ jaŋ tɩma pɩpɩ kuoru-la mɩ sɩ lɩɩsa bʋa na-kala.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ka ŋ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ, ʋ jaŋ kʋ kpirimi mɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara sɩpaaŋ, a sʋlʋ a chɩchɛ moribiee arɩ kʋdiilee mʋa. Ʋ jaŋ sʋlʋ a bʋl: Leŋ dɩ mɩ pɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa lɛ a tɩtɩŋ a ma wuo na kʋdiilee mʋa a didii.’ ”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dɩ Wɩa chaanɩŋ ba sɩ nyɩga bil Wɩa dɩa tʋɔŋ ma ha bɩ dɩsa, ka Samʋɛl ma pɩŋ nɩmɛ. Lee-la nɛ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la ma chɩŋ.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA yɩrɛ Samʋɛl. Ʋ sɩ, “Namɛ,”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: aŋ sii fá mʋ Eli teeŋ a bʋl, “Ŋ sɩ yɩrɛmɛ, mɩ kɔ nɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Eli bʋl, “Mɩ bɩŋ yɩra, mɩɩra mʋ pɩŋ.” Samʋɛl mɩɩra mʋ pɩŋ.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bɩra yɩrʋ, “Samʋɛl!” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ hirige sii a bɩra mʋ Eli teeŋ a bʋl, “Ŋ sɩ yɩrɛmɛ, na mɩ nɛ ŋ-la.” Eli sɩ, “Mɩ bii, aɩ, mɩ bɩŋ yɩra, mɩɩra mʋ pɩŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Samʋɛl fa bɩ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ. La TƖƖNA fa ha bɩ ʋ wɩaa kaa dagʋ aŋ ka.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bɩra yɩrɛ Samʋɛl torimuŋ lɛ, ʋ sii fá mʋ Eli teeŋ a bʋl, “Ŋ sɩ yɩrɛmɛ, namɛ nɛ ŋ-la.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Eli tʋɔbɩɩnaa kɔ, ʋ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA nɩɩ yɩrɛ bile.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Eli bʋla pɩ Samʋɛl, “Mɩɩra mʋ pɩŋ, dɩ nʋʋ nɛ bɩra yɩrɩŋ, bʋl: La TƖƖNA, bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ, ŋ tɩntɩnna ka jegili nɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl mɩɩra mʋ pɩŋ ʋ dɩpɩnɩŋ.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bɩra kɔ a yɩrʋ arɩ ʋ sɩ vɛnɛɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, “Samʋɛl! Samʋɛl!” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl bʋl, “Bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ, mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna ka jegili nɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Bee na, mɩɩ chɛ mɩ ŋaa wɩɩ nɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la, ʋ jaŋ hirigi.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Mɩ fa bʋla pʋ arɩ mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ ʋ dɩa nɩaa a kaa mʋ wuu, a tɩŋ wʋbɔŋ-la ʋ biiriŋ sɩ ŋaa, ʋ jɩŋ aŋ bɩ ba kire.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa mɩ ŋmɩɛsa pɩ Eli dɩa nɩaa, arɩ wʋbɔŋ-la ba sɩ ŋaa, kʋŋkala tuo ba sɩ jaŋ wuo kaa kpʋ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a pɩɩsɛ ba wʋbɔŋ-la ta.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl pɩŋ taŋ pʋl, ʋ sii kɛŋ La TƖƖNA dɩa boiŋ niiree a suri. Ka fawʋllʋŋ fa kɛnʋ arɩ ʋ sɩ jaŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ na arɩ duosoo tʋɔŋ a pɩ Eli.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Eli yɩrʋ a bʋl, “Mɩ nanʋala Samʋɛl.” Ʋ sɩ, “Namɛ.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Eli pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩŋ?” Pɔ ŋ sɩ́ wɩɩ-la joŋo faamɛ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ bʋla pɩŋ bʋla pɩmɛ, Wɩa jaŋ dɔgʋsʋŋ kɩŋkɛŋ.

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala a pʋ, ʋ bɩ ba kʋŋkala joŋo faaʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Eli bʋl, “Ʋ nɛ La TƖƖNA, wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩ bene dɩ ʋ zɔmɔ pʋ, ʋ́ ŋaa.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samʋɛl sɩɩ waa ŋɩɩ, La TƖƖNA chɩŋ ʋ harɩŋ nɛ woruŋ a leŋ wɩalɩŋ kala Samʋɛl sɩ bʋla sɛnɛ kʋ ŋaa.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala, a chɩŋ Daŋ tinteeŋ lɛ a kaa mʋ yi taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛɛsɩba, nʋʋkala jɩma arɩ Samʋɛl sɛnɛ ŋaa La TƖƖNA wʋlaabʋllʋ nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa vɛnɛ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa kʋʋ dagɛ Samʋɛl nɛ Sɩlɔ lɛ a bʋl wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ jaŋ dagɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa pʋ.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala fa jegile nɩnɩɩ Samʋɛl teeŋ nɛ. Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala Iziral tɩŋŋaa sii a mʋ dɩ ba yuo Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa. Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ ŋmoo ba buguŋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛbɛnɩza, ka Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa ma hɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Afɛk.

english_verse: The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩmma-la yuyuo Iziral tɩŋŋaa. Laal-la sɩ chaasa kʋ lɩŋ, ba yuo dii Iziral tɩŋŋaa, a kpʋ ba baalaa bʋɩ banɛsɛ laal-baga-la lɛ.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba tɩŋ nɩaa ba mʋ Sɩlɔ, a joŋ La TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna niiriŋ daga-la kaa kɔ. Daga-la nyuŋ kɛŋ kɩaa sɩ kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ nɛ a nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa balɩa, La TƖƖNA hɔŋ ba pɛgɛ. Eli hambolibiisiŋ balɩa, Hofini arɩ Finihas ma to Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la harɩŋ a mʋ ba buguŋ.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Iziral laalɩyuori-kaana-la sɩ mɩɩra mʋ ba buguŋ, Iziral nɩhɩasɩŋ pɩɛsɛ dɔŋɔ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ La TƖƖNA leŋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa yuo diila jɩnɩŋ? Má leŋ la mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɩlɔ a joŋ La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la kɔ dɩ ʋ hɛ la teeŋ, a laala ta la dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ kɛŋ La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la kɔ ba buguŋ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa faasa ŋaa goŋ tinteeŋ zigili.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sɩ nɩɩ goŋ-la, ba pɩɛsɛ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ goŋ nɩɩ ŋaa Hiburu tɩmma-la buguŋ lɛ ŋɩɩ?” Ba sɩ kʋ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga nɛ ba kaa kɔ ba buguŋ,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩmma-la, ba bʋl, “Vene nɛ kɔ ba buguŋ. Wʋdoho deeŋ ha bɩ ŋaa aŋ ka.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Wɩɩŋ jʋʋla, kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ laala ta veŋ-duoruŋ deemba nɩsɩŋ lɛ? Vesi-la nɛ fa joŋ wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ a ŋaa Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa lɛ ŋɩɩ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩmma, má nyɩrɛ bɔyɛ, a yuo arɩ baalɩŋ, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee ma jaŋ bɩrɩmɛ Hiburu tɩmma-la yosi arɩ ba fa sɩ ŋaa ma yosi ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Ba yuo a laa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la, aŋ kpʋ Eli biiri-la ma balɩa, Hofini arɩ Finihas. Eli sʋba

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa nɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa laalɩyuoru kʋbala lɩɩ fá laal-baga lɛ, a kɛŋ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ kɩɛsɛ aŋ ŋaa hagɩla bʋgɛ ʋ nyuŋ aa dagɛ tʋɔ-cheeŋ, a fá mʋ Sɩlɔ.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Ʋ mʋa dɩ Eli hɔŋ wombiiŋ niiŋ a bibeŋ leriŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ bɔyɛ faa joŋ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la wɩaa nɛ. Baal-la sɩ jʋʋ taŋ-la, a bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala sɩ ŋaa a pɩba, jaŋ nɩaa kala ŋmoo niiŋ.

english_verse: “I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.” “Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
translation_verse: Ʋ bʋla pɩ Eli, “Laal-baga nɛ mɩ lɩɩ ŋɩɩ, jɩnɩŋ nɛ mɩ fá lɩɩ nɩmɛ kɔ.” Eli pɩɛsʋ, “Mɩ bii, wʋbɛɛ nɛ ŋaa nɩmɛ?”

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Baal-la sɩ kɛŋ duoso kɔ bɩra bʋl, “Iziral tɩŋŋaa fá nɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ. Ba chaasa kpʋ la laalɩyuoro nɛ woruŋ. Ba kpʋ ŋ nanʋa-baala-la balɩa ma nɛ, Hofini arɩ Finihas, aŋ laa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la ma.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Baal-la sɩ yɩrɛ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la yɩrɩŋ, Eli sɩ hɔŋ kpasa-la nyuŋ boi-baalɩŋ lɛ, ʋ wulle tel hambayala. Ʋ sɩ tele ŋɩɩ, ʋ baŋŋaa bori ʋ sʋʋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ fa hɩɛsa nɛ aŋ yuŋ woruŋ. Ʋ fa laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaaŋ jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ balɩa nɛ.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dɩ Eli nanʋala Finihas haala kɛŋ luoruŋ, ʋ lʋlʋŋ yi. Ʋ sɩ nɩa dɩ ba yuo laa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la, ʋ bala nyɩmma arɩ ʋ bala ma kala sʋʋ, ʋ luoruŋ guu wʋwɩɩ dɩ ʋ lʋl, ama ʋ luo-wɩɩla-la jʋʋ ʋ lɛ nɛ woruŋ, ʋ chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ sʋʋ, haala-la sɩ kɛnʋ ʋ lʋl bʋla pʋ, “Sɩ́ fawʋllʋŋ fá, hambolibie nɛ ŋ lʋl.” Ama ʋ bɩ wɩɩkala bʋla, ʋ bɩ ba teeŋ jegile.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sɩ yuo laa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la ŋɩɩ, ba joŋu a lɩɩ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛbɛnɩza, a kaa mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩdɔd.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ kaa mʋ ŋɩɩ, ba kaa jʋʋ bil ba vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Dagɔŋ dɩa lɛ, ʋ chɩna kpagʋ.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, Asɩdɔd tɩŋŋaa sie dɩ Dagɔŋ-la tele chu tinteeŋ, La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la sɩpaaŋ. Ba kaa chʋʋla kɩɩ ʋ dɩchɩnɩŋ.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ bɩra pʋla chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, ba sie dɩ Dagɔŋ-la tele chu tinteeŋ, La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la sɩpaaŋ. Bʋa deeŋ-na lɛ, dɩ ʋ nyuŋ yɛrɛ, ʋ nɩsaa ma bori a pɩŋ boiŋ niiŋ, ka ʋ yaraa dʋndʋŋa pɩŋ lee-la.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala nɩalɩŋ sɩ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ pɩpɩ ba vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Dagɔŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩɩ tou nɛ jʋʋ Dagɔŋ-la dɩa Asɩdɔd lɛ, ba bɩ boiŋ niiŋ lee-la-na ka nʋɔsɛ.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa dɔgɩsɛ Asɩdɔd tɩŋŋaa arɩ lere-la kala sɩ gollu nɛ woruŋ. Ʋ fa leŋe ba na hɛɛŋ nɛ woruŋ, a ŋmɛrɛ mɔpʋllʋŋ.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Asɩdɔd tɩŋŋaa sɩ na wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋaa ba lɛ, ba bʋl, “Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la bɩ maga dɩ ʋ hɛ la teeŋ daha, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋʋ dɔgɩsɛ la dɩ la vene Dagɔŋ kala nɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba yɩrɛ kuorusu-la kala sɩɩ beŋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tinteeŋ a kʋ hilimi a pɩɛsɛba, “Ɛɛ nɛ la jaŋ joŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la ŋaa?” Ba bʋl, “Má joŋ a kaa mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gaf.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba joŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la a kaa mʋ Gaf.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Ba sɩ kɛnʋ mʋ lee-la ma, La TƖƖNA bɩra dɔgɩsɛ taŋ-la ma nɩaa, a leŋ fawʋllʋŋ chaasa jʋʋba ba chichel. Ʋ leŋ mɔpʋllʋŋ ŋmɛrɛ taŋ-la nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ hambiisiŋ kala lɛ.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba sii joŋ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la a kaa mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛkʋrɔŋ. Ba sɩ kaa mʋ dɩ ba jʋʋ, Ɛkʋrɔŋ tɩŋŋaa ŋmoo niiŋ a bʋl, “Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la nɛ ba kaa kɔ la jaŋ dɩ ʋ kpʋ la dɩ la nɩaa kala.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Ɛkʋrɔŋ tɩmma-la yɩrɛ kuorusu-la kala sɩ hɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tinteeŋ lɛ, a kʋ hilimi a bʋl, “Má joŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la a kaa mɩɩra mʋ bil ʋ dɩ-biliŋ, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, ʋ jaŋ kpʋ la dɩ la nɩaa kala dɛrɛ,” bɛɛ wɩaa Wɩa fa dɔgɩsɛba nɛ woruŋ, nɩaa sʋʋ ba jaŋ lɛ, fawʋllʋŋ kɛmba.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ bɩ sʋba ŋmɛrɛ mɔpʋllʋŋ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ taŋ-la nɩaa ŋmoo niiŋ pɩ ba vesiŋ dɩ ba pɛ ba lɛ.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la fa sɩ hɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tinteeŋ lɛ a mʋ yi chɛnsɩŋ balɩpɛ,

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sii yɩrɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ kpaarɛ ba vʋɩyaa arɩ vʋgʋraa kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ a pɩɛsɛba, “Ɛɛ nɛ la jaŋ ŋaa La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la? Má dagɛla ŋɩɩ la sɩ jaŋ to a kɛnʋ mʋ bil ʋ dɩ-biliŋ.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Ba bʋl, “Dɩ ma nɩɩ chɛ ma kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la mɩɩra mʋ, ma bɩ maga ma kɛnʋ mʋ arɩ na-hɩllɩŋ. Ʋ maga dɩ ma chɛ cheeriŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa pɛ nɛ a kaa mʋ pʋ. Dɩ ma nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ma jaŋ na dɩ ma duoro, aŋ pɛ bɩra jɩŋ wɩɩ-la ma sɩ tɩɩ ʋ dʋdɔgɩsɛma.”

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Ʋ maga dɩ ma mɛ kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ mɔpʋllʋŋ, a bɩra mɛ kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ taatɩaa. Kɩaa deemba nɛ jʋʋ chichei ma tinteeŋ. Má kɛmba kaa mʋ zil Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa. Kapo ʋ jaŋ leŋ ma dɩ ma vesiŋ arɩ ma tinteeŋ kala dɔgʋsʋŋ.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma kɛŋ tʋɔ-doluŋ arɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa a nagɛ ba kuoro fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ? Bʋa-la lɛ Wɩa sɩ dɔgɩsɛba ba na hɛɛŋ woruŋ, ba bɩrɩmɛ ba tʋɔbɩɩnaa nɛ a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa viiri.

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ, má ŋaa nɛsɩŋ toruko-falɩŋ, a kɛsɛ nɛsɩŋ balɩa sɩ kɛŋ biiriŋ aŋ ha bɩ toruko lɛrɛ aŋ ka. Má kɛsɛba a joŋ toruko-la hɛba, aŋ kɛrɛ ba biiriŋ mʋ tɔ nɛ-dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Má joŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la daŋ toruko-la nyuŋ, a joŋ sɛlɩmɛ kɩalɩŋ sɩ ŋaa ma cheeriŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa, ma sɩ kaa mʋmʋ ma pʋ, a hɛ dagɩ-bie lɛ a joŋo bil Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la sɛmɛ. Má kaa lɩɩ ta dɩ ʋ mʋ ʋ tɩtɩa lɛ.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Ama, má chɩŋ a bibeŋ, dɩ ʋ nɛ to lee-la ʋ sɩ lɩɩ kɔ, a mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛf Sɛmɛs dɩɩrɩŋ, ŋɩɩ daga arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ joŋ nyanyal-bɔmɔ-la hɛ la lɛ. Ama dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ nɩmɛ to, la jaŋ bɩra jɩŋ arɩ ʋ dee bɩ nyanyal-bɔmɔ-la joŋo hɛ la lɛ, ba ma ta paala jʋʋla nɛ.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ ba sɩ daga, a kɛsɛ nɛsɩ-la a joŋ toruko hɛba, aŋ kɛrɛ ba biiriŋ tɔ nɛ-dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Ba joŋ La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la arɩ dagɩ-bie-la tʋɔŋ sɛlɩmɛ taatɩa-la arɩ mɔpʋllʋ-la sɩ hɛ kala daŋ toruko-la nyuŋ.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɛsɩ-la joŋ wombiiŋ ŋɩɩ tegi tegi a tʋʋlɛ Bɛf Sɛmɛs dɩɩrɩŋ mʋmʋ aŋ yiyel. Ba bɩ nadiiŋ koo nagʋa gɛbɛ. Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kuorusu-la to ba harɩŋ ŋɩɩ halɩɩ a mʋ yi Bɛf Sɛmɛs tinteeŋ bʋa.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Bɛf Sɛmɛs tɩŋŋaa ka kʋŋ mɛmpɛ fuonaaŋ lɛ. Ba sɩ bee na Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la, ba tʋɔŋ kala tɔrɛ.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kuorusu-la banɔŋ chɩna na wɩaa deemba kala nɛ, aŋ mɩɩra mʋ Ɛkʋrɔŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Kɩalɩŋ banɔŋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ mɛ ba nagɛ mɔpʋllʋŋ ba kaa mʋ sʋl cheeriŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA, ba kʋŋkala chɩŋ taŋ nyuŋ nɛ. Tasɩ-la nɛ ŋ-la: Asɩdɔd, Gaza, Asɩkɛlɔŋ, Gaf arɩ Ɛkʋrɔŋ.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Ba sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ mɛ kɩalɩŋ banɔŋ ma ba nagɛ taatɩaa, ba ma kʋŋkala chɩŋ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa tasɩ-la kuorusu-la banɔŋ sɩɩ beŋ nyuŋ nɛ, tabala-la ba sɩ saa kɛrɛ golli arɩ tabiisi-la ba sɩ bɩ kɛrɛ saa golli. Bʋ-bal-la sɩ hɛ Bɛf Sɛmɛs tɩŋŋaa baal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Josua baga lɛ, ba joŋ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la daŋ ʋ nyuŋ. Ʋ ha hɛ nɩmɛ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala, a ŋaa magɩl aa dagɛ wɩɩ-la fa sɩ ŋaa.

english_verse: Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed
translation_verse: Ama Wɩa kpʋ Bɛf Sɛmɛs tɩŋŋaa mahɩŋ batori arɩ fii nɛ, a tɩŋ ba sɩ nyilimi daga-la tʋɔŋ. Nɩaa yel woruŋ, a tɩŋ nɩ-daŋ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ kpʋa ba jaŋ lɛ wɩaa.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Bɛf Sɛmɛs tɩŋŋaa pɩɛsɛ dɔŋɔ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ jaŋ wuo chɩŋ La TƖƖNA Wɩa deeŋ sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ sɩpaaŋ? Kʋbɛɛba teeŋ nɛ Wɩa niiriŋ daga deeŋ jaŋ mʋ lɛɛlɛ?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ tɩŋ ba bʋla pɩ Kɩrɩaf Jɩarɩm nɩaa, “Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kɛŋ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la mɩɩra kɔ nɛ. Má kʋ tuu joŋ a kaa mʋ ma leriŋ.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Kɩrɩaf Jɩarɩm tɩmma-la kʋ joŋ La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la. Ba sɩ joŋo, ba kaa mʋ bil nɩɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Abɩnadab dɩa lɛ, dundolo nyuŋ, aŋ joŋ ʋ nanʋala Elieza hɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ, dɩ ʋ nɛ bibeŋ La TƖƖNA niiriŋ daga-la nyuŋ. Samʋɛl yuo dii Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa Mɩzɩpa lɛ

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl fa bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala, “Dɩ ma nɩɩ chɛ dɩ ma joŋ ma tʋɔŋ kala a pɩ La TƖƖNA, ŋɩɩ-na má vɩa nɩwogusuŋ vesiŋ arɩ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩtɔrɛf, aŋ joŋ ma tɩtɩa kala a pɩ La TƖƖNA a tuto ʋ dʋndʋŋa. Dɩ ma nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ʋ jaŋ laama ta Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɩa vesi-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal arɩ Asɩtɔrɛf, aŋ joŋ ba tɩtɩa kala pɩ La TƖƖNA a tuto ʋ dʋndʋŋa.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl bɩra bʋl, “Má leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala kʋ hilimi lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɩzɩpa, dɩ mɩ sʋl La TƖƖNA pɩma.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ba sɩ kʋ hilimi Mɩzɩpa lɛ, ba ŋaa lɩɩŋ a ta La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ a sʋlʋ, aŋ vɔɔ niiŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la kala a bʋl, “La ŋaa wʋbɔŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA lɛ.” Samʋɛl nɛ fa ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaara Mɩzɩpa lɛ.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa sɩ nɩa dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa hilimi Mɩzɩpa lɛ nɛ, ba kuorusu-la banɔŋ sii a kɛsɛ ba laalɩyuoroo mʋmʋ dɩ ba yuoba. Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ nɩɩ ba wɩaa, fawʋllʋŋ kɛmba.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Ba bʋla pɩ Samʋɛl, “Ŋ sɩ bunso pɩpɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa dɩ ʋ pɛ la lɛ ŋɩɩ, sɩ́ leŋ. Sʋlʋ dɩ ʋ laala ta Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Samʋɛl fa sɩɩ sʋl kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlɩɩ-la ŋɩɩ, Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa kʋ kpagɛ dɩ ba yuo Iziral tɩŋŋaa. Ama tapʋlɩɩ-la, La TƖƖNA leŋ taŋ faasa kpɩa Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa lɛ, ba wɩɩkala vʋgʋmɛ, ba fá aŋ ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩmma-la lɩɩ Mɩzɩpa lɛ a kire to Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa harɩŋ a kpʋba wombiiŋ lɛ ŋɩɩ halɩɩ a mʋ kpagɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛf Kaa.

english_verse: The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them. For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ yuo dii Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa ŋɩɩ, ba bɩra bɩ ba tinteeŋ jʋa. Samʋɛl mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ, La TƖƖNA chaasa chɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa harɩŋ nɛ woruŋ, ba wuo Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Tabala-la kala sɩ hɛ Ɛkʋrɔŋ arɩ Gaf pɛgɛ, Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ yuo laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa teeŋ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa mɩɩra laa ba kala nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ nii-magɛ dɔŋɔ lɛɛlɛ hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa pɛgɛ.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl ha ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaara ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Jɩna na-kala, ʋ yie sii gɔllɛ Bɛtɛl, Gɩlɩgal arɩ Mɩzɩpa kala nɛ a laa ba wɩaa bʋla wasɛ pɩba.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ ʋ nɛ tɩŋ ʋ tɩntɩŋŋaa dɛrɛ, ʋ ha yie mɩɩra kɔ ʋ dɩa nɛ Rama lɛ. Ʋ yie kɔ nɩmɛ a laa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma wɩaa a bʋla wasɛ pɩba. Rama lɛ, ʋ saa Wɩɩsʋllɩ koruŋ nɛ a pɩ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Ʋ bii-bumbuŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Jowɛl, bii-lɩa ma yɩrɩŋ nɛ Abija. Ba kala fa hɛ Bɛɛsɩba lɛ nɛ a ŋaa ba sɩpaalaaraa.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Ama ʋ biiriŋ deemba wʋŋaalaa fa bɩ ba nyɩmma wombiee lɛ to. Ba mɩɩra chɩl kɩaa wɩaa nɛ, aa gʋrɛ nɩaa, a lɩlaa kpalaa a bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ ka bʋl.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ kala sii hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ a mʋ Samʋɛl teeŋ Rama lɛ,

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: a bʋla pʋ, “Ŋ hɩɛsa nɛ, ka ŋ biiriŋ wʋŋaalaa bɩ ŋ wombiee lɛ ka to, ŋɩɩ wɩaa lɩɩsɛ kuoro pɩla dɩ ʋ laa la sɩpaaŋ arɩ tinteye-la dɔnsʋŋ kala sɩ kɛŋ kuoroo ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ sɩ, “Lɩɩsɛ kuoro pɩla dɩ ʋ laa la sɩpaaŋ,” ŋɩɩ leŋ Samʋɛl tʋɔŋ chei, ʋ sʋl La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Jegile nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ kala nɩalɩŋ sɩ bʋlaa pɩŋ. Ŋ dee ba vɩa, mɩ-na sɩ ŋaa ba kuoro nɛ ba vɩa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: A chɩŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la lɛ mɩ sɩ kɛmba lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a kaa kɔ jɩnɩŋ, ba vɩamɛ nɛ aŋ tuto vesiŋ, ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ ba joŋo ŋɩŋaa ŋ ma lɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Ŋ-na jegile nɩɩ ba teeŋ, ama kpʋrɩsɛ ba dɩgɩlaa woruŋ, a leŋ dɩ ba jɩŋ wɩalɩŋ kala kuoru-la sɩ jaŋ joŋo ŋaa ba lɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla pʋ a pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ pɩɛsʋ a chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ lɩɩsɛ kuoro pɩba.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ, “Wɩalɩŋ kuoru-la sɩ jaŋ bibemma sɩ jaŋ joŋo ŋaa ma lɛ nɛ ŋ-la: Ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma hambolibiisiŋ ŋaa ʋ laalɩyuoroo, dɔnsʋŋ jaŋ kɛŋ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba tɩtɩŋ, dɩ dɔnsʋŋ ma jɩjɩl ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ, ka dɩ ʋ lɩɩsɛ dɔnsʋŋ ma dɩ ba laa ʋ tɩtɩa janɩŋ torukoba sɩpaaŋ a fɩfá.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma toloo nɛ ŋɩŋaa ʋ tʋlaalɩɩba, ʋ kʋdiilee, aŋ pɛ wʋwasɛ ʋ boroboro ma.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ ma bagɩsɩ-la sɩ sɩma arɩ ma girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ arɩ ma Olif tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ kala sɩ zɔmɔ laa ma teeŋ, a joŋo pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma kɛŋ ma mɩaa arɩ ma girep nɛnɛɛ kpaa leree fii, dɩ ʋ laa kpaalɩŋ dɔŋɔ a pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa dɔnsʋŋ.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Ma tɩntɩnnɩ-baalaa arɩ haalaa arɩ ma nɛsɩŋ arɩ kakusu-la sɩ zɔmɔ, ʋ jaŋ laa ba kala dɩ ba tɩmaa pʋ.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ laa ma piesee arɩ bʋʋnaa fii na-kala tʋɔŋ kʋbala, ka dɩ ma tɩtɩa ŋaa ʋ yosi.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Dɩ tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ yie, ma jaŋ yele chɩchɛ dɩ La TƖƖNA laama ta kuoru-la ma sɩɩ chɛ nɩsɩŋ lɛ, ka dɩ ʋ fʋʋla yagɛma.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: Laa chɛ kuoro nɛ dɩ ʋ bibenla a laa la sɩpaaŋ a kɛnla mʋ dɩ la yuyuo laalɩŋ, dɩ la ma nagɛ tinteye-la dɔnsʋŋ.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samʋɛl sɩ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ kala nɩalɩŋ sɩ bʋla, ʋ bɩra mʋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala a pɩ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋl, “Jegile nɩɩ ba teeŋ a lɩɩsɛ kuoro pɩba.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl bʋla pɩ Iziral baala-la kala, “Má kʋŋkala mɩɩra mʋ ŋ jaŋ.”

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa baal kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ, ʋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Kɩs. Ʋ fa kɛŋ kɩaa nɛ woruŋ, nɩaa zizilu. Ʋ nyɩmma nɛ Abɩɛl, Abɩɛl ma nyɩmma nɛ Zɛrɔ, Zɛrɔ ma nyɩmma nɛ Bɛkɔraf, Bɛkɔraf ma nyɩmma nɛ Afɩa.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Kɩs fa kɛŋ nanʋa-baal nɛ baa yɩrɛ Sɔɔl, a ŋaa bapʋɔsɛ zɔŋ woruŋ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala tʋɔŋ ʋ dɔŋ fa tuo. Ʋ nɛ duomo a kɩɩ ba kala ma.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nyɩmma Kɩs fa kɛŋ kakusuŋ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ kakusu-la lɩɩ lɛl. Kɩs bʋla pɩ ʋ nanʋala Sɔɔl, “Kɛŋ tɩntɩnna-la dɔŋɔ dɩ ma lɩɩ chɛ kakusu-la.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la lɩɩ to Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga ŋɩɩ a mʋ to lere-la sɩ golli taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Salɩsa, aŋ bɩ ba na. Ba joŋ ŋɩɩ mʋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Saalɩm, ama kakusu-la tuo nɩmɛ ma. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bɩra joŋ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa tinteeŋ ma kala a baara cheŋ, aŋ bɩ ba na.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ yi tintee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zuf, Sɔɔl bʋla pɩ ʋ dɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la sɩɩ vɛŋ, “Kɔ dɩ la mɩɩra mʋ dɩa, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee mɩ nyɩmma jaŋ leŋ kakusu-la wɩaa bɩɩnɩŋ, la wɩaa nɛ jaŋ mɩɩra chɩlʋ.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Ama ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la bʋl, “Bee na, Wɩa tɩntɩnnʋ nɛ hɛ taŋ deeŋ lɛ, nɩaa zizilu woruŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa dɩ ʋ nɛ bʋl wɩɩkala, wɩɩ-la sɛnɛ yie kʋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ nɛ. Leŋ dɩ la mʋ ʋ teeŋ. Kapo ʋ jaŋ dagɛla wombii-la la sɩ jaŋ to.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl pɩɛsɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la, “Dɩ la nɛ mʋa, bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ la jaŋ joŋo pɩ baal-la? Kʋdiile-la fa sɩ hɛ la lʋagaba lɛ kala dɛrɛ nɛ. La bɩ kʋŋ kɛnɛ la sɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩ Wɩa tɩntɩnnʋ-la. Koo la kɛŋ kʋŋ nɛ?”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩntɩnnʋ-la bɩra bʋla pɩ Sɔɔl, “Na, mɩ kori warɩpʋla mʋa nɛ, mɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩ Wɩa tɩntɩnnʋ-la, ka dɩ ʋ dagɛla wombii-la la sɩ jaŋ to a na kakusu-la.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl bɩra bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la, “Wʋzɔŋ nɛ, kɔ la mʋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba mʋmʋ taŋ-la lɛ Wɩa tɩntɩnnʋ-la sɩ hɛ.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ jɩl dundolo, ka dɩ ba-na jʋʋ taŋ-la, ba cheŋ hatolibiisi kʋbalaba dɩ ba kʋʋ lɩɩ dɩ ba ŋaa lɩɩŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba pɩɛsɛba, “Wɩa sɩɩ-naarʋ-la hɛ nɩmɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Ba bʋl, “Ʋ hɛ nɩmɛ. Ʋ hɛ ma sɩpaaŋ. Má ŋaa lɩma, ma jaŋ puu. Jɩnɩŋ nɛ ʋ kɔ la jaŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa nɩaa ka chɛ dɩ ba kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ nɛ dundolo-la nyuŋ ba sɩɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ jʋʋ taŋ-la, ma jaŋ naʋ, ka dɩ ʋ na jɩl dundolo-la nyuŋ ba sɩɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ dɩ ba dii kɩaa. Dɩ ʋ nɛ bɩ mʋa, nɩaa bɩ jaŋ suomo dii kɩaa, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ maga dɩ ʋ sʋl Wɩa hɛ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ lɛ nɛ, ka dɩ nɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ yɩra-na dii. Dɩ ma nɛ jɩla lɛɛlɛ, ma jaŋ naʋ bʋa deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ jʋjʋʋ taŋ-la, dɩ Samʋɛl nɛ joŋ wombiiŋ a tʋʋlɛba kʋkɔ ŋɩɩ, a jɩjɩl dundolo-la nyuŋ ba sɩɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ jaŋ pʋl ka dɩ Sɔɔl-na kɔ, La TƖƖNA laa sɩpaaŋ bʋl ŋ-la nɛ a pɩ Samʋɛl:

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Chie bʋa deeŋ lɛ, mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ baal kʋbala lɩɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ a kɔ. Dɩ ʋ nɛ kɔ, joŋ Wɩɩsʋllɩ nʋʋŋ tɩsʋ, dɩ ʋ ŋaa mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaara. Ʋ nɛ jaŋ laa mɩ nɩaa ta Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Mɩ na hɛɛ-la mɩ nɩaa sɩɩ na nɛ, a nɩɩ ba nii-ŋmobo ma.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Samʋɛl sɩɩŋ sɩ na Sɔɔl, La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Baala deeŋ wɩaa nɛ mɩ bʋla pɩŋ ŋɩɩ, ʋ nɛ jaŋ bibeŋ mɩ nɩaa.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Sɔɔl mʋ yi Samʋɛl dɩ ʋ hɛ taŋ-la boi-baalɩŋ niiŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, dagɛmɛ Wɩa sɩɩ-naarʋ-la dɩa.”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Samʋɛl bʋl, “Mɩ-na nɛ Wɩa sɩɩ-naarʋ-la, laa mɩ sɩpaaŋ dɩ la jɩl dundolo-la nyuŋ ba sɩɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ. Jɩnɩŋ mɩ dɩŋ nɛ jaŋ dii kɩaa, dɩ taŋ nɛ pʋla, mɩ jaŋ bʋl ŋ tʋɔŋ wɩaa kala pɩŋ ka dɩ ŋ-na mʋ.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Kakusu-la sɩ lɛlɛ tapʋlaa batori sɩ bala, sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ba wɩaa walɩmɩŋ, ba naba nɛ. Ŋ dɩ ŋ nyɩmma dɩa nɩaa lɛ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔbɩɩnaa kala daŋ dɩ ma ŋaa ba sɩpaalaaraa.”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Sɔɔl bʋl, “Mɩ ŋaa Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nʋʋ nɛ, ʋ nɛ saa muuro Iziral doho doho-la kala tʋɔŋ. Mɩ nyɩŋ-nɩaa ma nɛ muuro Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa nyɩŋ-nɩaa kala tʋɔŋ. Bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ ŋ bʋl wɩɩŋ deeŋ pɩpɩmɛ?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Kʋdii-ŋaarʋ-la joŋ vaa-la kaa kʋ bil Sɔɔl sɩpaaŋ. Samʋɛl bʋl, “Na kʋ-la mɩ sɩ joŋo bil ma lɛ nɛ ŋ-la, má chaŋ. Mɩ paala chaasa joŋu bil ma lɛ nɛ, dɩ ma kʋ dii gbiele deeŋ lɛ, bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩɩ yɩrɛ nʋhʋɔraa.” Tapʋlɩɩ-la Sɔɔl arɩ Samʋɛl nɛ dii kɩaa.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Ba sɩ lɩɩ dundolo-la nyuŋ ba sɩɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a kʋ tuu jaŋ tʋɔŋ, Samʋɛl bil bɔsɔ ʋ lusuŋ nyuŋ a pɩ Sɔɔl ʋ pɩŋ.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Ba sɩ sii chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla, Samʋɛl yɩrɛ Sɔɔl lusu-la nyuŋ a bʋl, “Kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ dɩ mɩ kɛnɩŋ lɩɩ hɛ wombiiŋ lɛ.” Sɔɔl sɩ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ, ʋ dɩ Samʋɛl kala to dɔŋɔ a lɩɩ dɩ-jalɩŋ.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ lɩlɩɩ taŋ-la niiŋ, Samʋɛl bʋla pɩ Sɔɔl, “Bʋla pɩ ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la dɩ ʋ laa la sɩpaaŋ mʋmʋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ vɩvɛŋ, ka ʋ bɩra bʋl, “Gbɛrɛ mʋa daha, dɩ mɩ bʋl wɩɩ-la Wɩa sɩ bʋla a tɩgɛ ŋ lɛ pɩŋ.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
