english_verse: Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?” Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Ma bɩ liise ŋɩɩ ba sɩ kpʋ Jerub-Bɛsɛf nanʋala Abɩmɛlɛk? Haala nɛ joŋ nɔŋ-biiŋ to kɛrɛ a yagʋ kpʋ Tɛbɛs lɛ. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma faasa mʋ kpagɛ taŋ-la kɛrɛ?’ Dɩ ʋ nɛ pɩɛsɩŋ wɩaa deemba, bʋla pʋ, ‘Ŋ tɩntɩnna Yuria, Hiti tɩɩna-la ma sʋba nɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩndaarʋ-la mʋ Devit teeŋ a bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala Jʋab sɩ bʋla a pʋ.

english_verse: He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate.
translation_verse: Tɩndaarʋ-la bɩra bʋla pɩ Devit, “La dʋndɔmɔ-la fa wuola nɛ, a kirila a jɩl pɔkɔŋ nyuŋ, la ma bɩra kiriba ŋɩɩ a kaa mʋ hɛ ba jaŋ boiŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ dʋndɔmɔ-la to kɛrɛ a yuo ŋ tɩntɩnnaa arɩ to-hɛŋŋɛɛ a kpʋ ŋ laalɩyuoroo dɔnsʋŋ. Ŋ tɩntɩnna Yuria Hiti tɩɩna-la ma sʋba nɛ.”

english_verse: David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
translation_verse: Devit bʋla pɩ tɩndaarʋ-la, “Bʋla pɩ Jʋab dɩ ʋ sɩ́ leŋe dɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ chei wɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa lɛ, ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo jɩŋ nɩɩ-la ba sɩ jaŋ kpʋ laalɩŋ lɛ. Bʋla pʋ ʋ hɛ doluŋ a yuo taŋ-la, a cheyu. Bʋl ŋ-la pɩ Jʋab dɩ ʋ nyuŋ nyaasɛ.”

english_verse: When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
translation_verse: Yuria haala Bɛfɩsɛba sɩ nɩa dɩ ʋ bala sʋba, ʋ yel ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son. The Lord's Message for David The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ yel ʋ bala lɛ a dɛrɛ, kuoro Devit tɩŋ ba mʋ kɛnʋ kɔ ʋ dɩa, ʋ ŋaa ʋ haal a lʋl hambolibie a pʋ. Ama La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ fa bɩ wɩɩ-la Devit sɩ ŋaa lɛ tɔrɔ.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Kɩaa tɩɩna-la fa kɛŋ piesee arɩ nɛsɩŋ nɛ woruŋ.

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala, nʋhʋɔrʋ sii kɔ kɩaa tɩɩna-la teeŋ. Kɩaa tɩɩna-la vɩa dɩ ʋ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa piesee koo nɛsɩ-la dɔŋɔ kpʋ a ŋaa kʋdiilee a pɩ nʋhʋɔrʋ-la sɩ kɔ ʋ teeŋ, aŋ mɩɩra sii kɛŋ summu-la pie-kee-bie-la a kpʋ a ŋaa kʋdiilee pɩ nʋhʋɔrʋ-la.”

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Devit sɩ nɩɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ʋ baanɩŋ chaasa sii kɩaa tɩɩna-la nyuŋ. Ʋ bʋla pɩ Netaŋ, “Mɩ ŋmɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ weye, baal-la sɩ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ maga ʋ sʋʋ nɛ!

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tiŋ pie-kee-bie-la chɩmɩŋ naasɩŋ bʋnɛsɛ nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ bɩ summu-la nenige fá aŋ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ.”

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Netaŋ bʋla pɩ Devit, “Ŋ nɛ ŋaa baal-la sɩ ŋaa wɩɩ-la. Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Mɩ nɛ lɩɩsɩŋ ŋ ŋaa kuoro Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ a laaŋ ta Sɔɔl nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: Mɩ joŋ ŋ nɩhɩaŋ dɩa arɩ ʋ haalaa kala a hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ. Mɩ joŋ Iziral arɩ Juda tinteeŋ ma kala a pɩŋ nɛ. Dɩ kɩaa deemba kala nɛ fa bɩ yʋgɛ, mɩ fa ha jaŋ pɩŋ kɩaa a kɩɩ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ vɩa mɩ-na ŋ Tɩɩna niiŋ aŋ ŋaa wʋbɔmʋŋ deeŋ? Ŋ leŋe Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa kpʋ Yuria nɛ laalɩŋ lɛ, ka ŋ laa ʋ haala jaa.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa ŋ dɩ ŋ doho nɩaa bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ ma wiese laalɩŋ lɛ, a tɩŋ ŋ sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ, aŋ laa Yuria, Hiti tɩɩna-la haala a jaa.’

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Mɩ jaŋ ŋaa dɩ ŋ tɩtɩa dɩa nʋʋ leŋ dɩ wʋlɔrʋŋ jʋʋŋ woruŋ. Ŋ sɩɩŋ lɛ, mɩ jaŋ joŋ ŋ haalaa a pɩ nʋʋ dɔŋ. Ʋ jaŋ kɛmba pɩŋ pʋlʋmʋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Ŋ-na lʋara nɛ a ŋaa wʋbɔmʋŋ deeŋ, ama mɩ-na jaŋ leŋ dɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ ŋaa pʋlʋmʋŋ lɛ, dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala na.’ ”

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Ama a tɩŋ ŋ sɩ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ŋ leŋe La TƖƖNA dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ tʋʋsɛ ʋ joŋŋoo nɛ. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, bile haal-la sɩ lʋla pɩŋ jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Netaŋ sɩ mɩɩra mʋ dɩa, La TƖƖNA leŋ bile Yuria haal-la sɩ lʋla pɩ Devit wʋwɩɩlɛ.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Devit sʋl Wɩa dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ bile duori. Ʋ yie vɩa kʋdiilee aŋ jʋʋ pɩŋ ʋ dɩa tinteeŋ tɩtaŋ na-kala.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Ʋ dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ yie kʋ chɩŋ ʋ sɛmɛ a nɩnɛrɩgɛ dɩ ʋ sii tintee-la lɛ, ʋ vɩa, aŋ pɔ ʋ bɩ sie ba didii kɩaa.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Bile sɩ wɩɩla ʋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ chɛɛŋ, ʋ sʋʋ. Fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ Devit tɩntɩnnaa arɩ ba sɩ jaŋ bʋl bile sʋʋŋ wɩaa pʋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba sɩ, “Bile fa sɩ paala hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, la bʋl wɩaa a pɩ Devit nɛ, ka ʋ bɩ la teeŋ jegile. Ɛɛ nɛ saa la jaŋ wuo ŋaa a bʋl bile sʋʋŋ wɩaa a pʋ? Dɩ la nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ʋ jaŋ wuo ŋaa ʋ tɩtɩa wʋbɔŋ.”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Devit sɩ na dɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa munso bʋbʋl wɩaa dɔŋɔ ba teeŋ, ʋ jɩŋ arɩ bile sʋba nɛ. Ʋ pɩɛsɛ, “Bile sʋba nɛɛ?” Ba bʋl, “Oo, ʋ sʋba nɛ.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Ʋ tɩntɩnnaa pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ wɩɩ nɛ ŋ ŋaa ŋ-la? Bile fa sɩ weye, ŋ vɩa kʋdiilee nɛ aŋ yiyel, ama bile sɩ sʋba, ŋ sie nɛ a dii kɩaa.”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Devit bʋl, “Bile fa sɩ weye, mɩ vɩa kʋdiilee nɛ aŋ yiyel, bɛɛ wɩaa mɩ fa bɩɩna La TƖƖNA jaŋ fá mɩ nenige a leŋ dɩ bile kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Ama ʋ sʋba nɛ lɛɛlɛ, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ jaŋ vɩa kʋdiilee? Mɩ bɩra jaŋ wuo ŋaa dɩ ʋ sii? Mɩ-na nɛ tapʋlɩɩ dɔŋɔ jaŋ mʋ ʋ teeŋ, ama ʋ-na bɩra bɩ jaŋ kɔ mɩ teeŋ.”

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit nyagɛ ʋ haala Bɛfɩsɛba bɔyɛ. Ba pɛ bɔsɔ ʋ kɛŋ luoruŋ. Ʋ lʋl hambolibie, ba hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Solomoŋ. La TƖƖNA fa cho bile nɛ woruŋ.

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: A tɩŋ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ cho bile wɩaa, ʋ tɩŋ ʋ wʋlaabʋlla Netaŋ dɩ ʋ hɛ bile yɩrɩŋ Jɛdɩdɩa.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Jʋab ha hɛ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ a yuyuo tabal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Raba, a yuo dii ʋ dɩ-duoŋ.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: Jʋab tɩŋ nɩaa ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Devit, “Mɩ yuo laa Raba lɩɩŋ leriŋ kala nɛ.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Yɩrɛ laalɩyuoro-la kʋkaanaa hɛ dɔŋɔ, a kʋ golli tabal-la chu a yuo diiu dɩ ʋ ŋaa ŋ kʋŋ. Dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, ka mɩ yuo diiu, nɩaa jaŋ bʋl mɩ nɛ yuo diiu.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit yɩrɛ laalɩyuori-kaana-la kala hɛ dɔŋɔ a mʋ yuo dii Raba.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: aŋ kɛsɛ nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ kʋ lɩɩ a fʋgɛba hɛ ba tɩtɩŋ. Ba kɛŋ sɔɔba, pɩŋgaasɩba arɩ piri-saasɩŋ a kaa tɩtɩŋ, aŋ fʋgɛba hɛ ba ŋɩŋaa tiebiee ma. Ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ Devit ŋaa Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa tasɩ-la dɔnsʋŋ ma kala lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala mɩɩra mʋ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Devit nanʋala Abɩsalɔm fa kɛŋ dɩ-haal kʋbala nɛ baa yɩrɛ Tama. Ʋ fa zɔmɔ nɛ woruŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Amɩnɔŋ ma sɩ ŋaa Devit nanʋala chou a hɩhɩɛnʋ.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Amɩnɔŋ fa sɩ cho ʋ dɩ-haala Tama ŋɩɩ, aŋ bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa dɩ ʋ jʋʋ ʋ nɩsɩŋ, aŋ bɩra bɩ jaŋ wuo bʋla pʋ ma arɩ ʋ chou nɛ a hɩhɩɛnʋ, ʋ tɩŋ ŋɩɩ wɩaa wʋwɩɩlɛ. Tolo-la fa ha bɩ baal kala jɩŋ.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Dɩ Amɩnɔŋ fa kɛŋ nandɔŋ kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Jonadab. Ʋ ŋaa kuoro Devit naambie Sɩmɩa nanʋala nɛ. Jonadab sɩɩŋ fa waga nɛ woruŋ.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Ʋ pɩɛsɛ Amɩnɔŋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ ŋaa kuoro bie, ka tapʋlɩɩ kala ŋ yie kɛŋ sɩaa chei? Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɩɩ walɩmɩŋ?” Amɩnɔŋ bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ cho mɩ naambie Abɩsalɔm dɩ-haala Tama nɛ.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Jonadab bʋla pʋ, “Jʋʋ pɩŋ a fugoo wɩɩlɛ. Dɩ ŋ nyɩmma nɛ kɔ dɩ ʋ naŋ, bʋla pʋ, ‘Mɩɩ chɛ mɩ dɩ-haala Tama nɛ kʋ ŋaa kʋdiilee pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ dii. Mɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ ŋɩŋaa kʋdiile-la ka dɩ mɩ bibeŋ nɛ, dɩ ʋ nɛ dɛrɛ, ʋ tɩtɩa ŋaa pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ dii.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Amɩnɔŋ jʋʋ pɩŋ a fugo wʋwɩɩlɛ. Kuoro sɩ kɔ dɩ ʋ naʋ, Amɩnɔŋ bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ nyɩmma, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, leŋ dɩ mɩ dɩ-haala Tama kɔ dɩ mɩ bibeŋ ka dɩ ʋ chaasa ŋaa kʋdii-zɔŋ a pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ dii.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Devit tɩŋ ba mʋ ʋ dɩa a bʋla pɩ Tama: “Mʋ ŋ dɩ-baala Amɩnɔŋ dɩa a ŋaa kʋdiilee pʋ.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Tama mʋ ʋ dɩ-baala Amɩnɔŋ dɩa, dɩ ʋ pɩna. Ʋ ŋaa munuŋ buu, a ŋmʋrɛ, a wasɛ boroboro ʋ sɩɩŋ lɛ,

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: a joŋ boroboro-la a hɛ gbaŋa lɛ a kaa mʋ pʋ. Ʋ vɩa dɩ ʋ dii, aŋ bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ dɩa-la tʋɔŋ, “Má kala lɩɩ daha.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kala lɩɩ.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ lɩa, Amɩnɔŋ bʋla pɩ Tama, “Kɛŋ kʋdiile-la kʋ jʋʋ mɩ dɩpɩnɩŋ a ŋaa pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ dii.” Tama joŋ kɩalɩŋ jʋʋ ʋ dɩ-baala Amɩnɔŋ dɩpɩnɩŋ a pʋ.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ kaa jʋʋ pʋ dɩ ʋ dii ŋɩɩ, ʋ guu kɛnʋ aŋ bʋl, “Kɔ la pɩŋ, mɩ dɩ-haala.”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Tama bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ dɩ-baala, sɩ́ ŋɩɩ ŋaa. Sɩ́ mɩ fʋgʋ. Wʋdoho deeŋ bɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ! Sɩ́ wʋbɔmʋŋ deeŋ ŋaa.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ mɩ lɛ, nɩɩ nɛ mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ hɩɩsɩ-la to mʋ? Ka ŋ-na tɩtɩa? Ŋ jaŋ nagɛ nɩpɛɩ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ. Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, bʋl wɩɩ-la pɩ kuoro, ʋ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ jaaŋ.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Ama Amɩnɔŋ bɩ jegile nɩɩ wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ bʋla. Ʋ sɩ kɛŋ doluŋ a kɩɩ tolo-la ŋɩɩ, ʋ gurigu.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Amɩnɔŋ sɩ gurigu dɛrɛ, ʋ tʋɔŋ mɩɩra lɩɩ tolo-la a kɩɩ ʋ fa sɩ chou ŋɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Amɩnɔŋ bʋla pʋ, “Sii lɩɩ daha.”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Tolo-la bʋla pʋ, “Aɩ, sɩ́ mɩ kire ta, dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ŋɩɩ nɛ paala ŋaa wʋbɔmʋŋ a kɩɩ wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ ŋaa mɩ lɛ.” Ama Amɩnɔŋ bɩ jegile nɩɩ ʋ teeŋ,

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: aŋ yɩrɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ tɩma pʋpʋ tapʋlɩɩ kala, ʋ kʋ jʋʋ ʋ bʋl, “Kiri haala deeŋ ta dɩ ʋ lɩɩ daha, aŋ kɛŋ boro tɔ a kaa yagɛ.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Ʋ tɩntɩnnʋ-la kiru ta ʋ lɩɩ, aŋ kɛŋ boro tɔ a kaa yagɛ. Dɩ Tama fa laalɛ gɛrɩ-duduoŋ ba sɩ chaasa kpɩɛrɛ. Gɛrɩ-dosunu-la kuoro toloo ha sɩ bɩ balaba jaa fa sɩɩ laalɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Tama ŋaa tʋɔrʋŋ a bʋgɛ ʋ nyuŋ, aŋ kɛŋ gɛrɩ-la ʋ fa sɩ laala a kɩɛsɛ, aŋ paa nɩsaa chʋŋ nyuŋ lɛ aŋ faasa yele viviiri.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Ʋ dɩ-baala Abɩsalɔm sɩ naʋ, ʋ pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ kɛnɩŋ? Ŋ dɩ-baala Amɩnɔŋ kɛnɩŋ pɩŋ ba? Mɩ dɩ-haala, sɩ wɩɩ-la joŋo hɛ ŋ tʋɔŋ lɛ, Amɩnɔŋ ŋaa ŋ naambii nɛ. Sɩ́ wɩɩ-la bʋla pɩ nʋʋkala.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Tama mʋ hɛ ʋ dɩ-baala Abɩsalɔm dɩa lɛ, a chaasa ŋaa tʋɔ-chee tɩɩna, a jʋjʋʋ ʋ dʋndʋŋa.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm faa ŋaa wɩaa Amɩnɔŋ teeŋ a nagɛ ʋ dɩ Amɩnɔŋ bɩ wɩɩkala kɛnɛ, ama aŋ bɛrʋ woruŋ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ gurigi ʋ dɩ-haala Tama. Abɩsalɔm kpʋ Amɩnɔŋ

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Jɩsɩŋ balɩa sɩ bala, nɩalɩŋ fa sɩɩ kɛ Abɩsalɔm piesee pʋnaa hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal Hazɔ lɛ a kpagɛ Efirem tinteeŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm yɩrɛ kuoro biiriŋ kala dɩ ba kɔ lee-la.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm mʋ kuoro teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ kɛ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna piesee pʋnaa kɔ nɛ. Kuoro, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ ŋ dɩ ŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ jaŋ wuo kʋ pɛ la lɛɛ?”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋl, “Aɩ mɩ bii, la kala bɩ jaŋ wuo kɔ, la jaŋ ŋaa chʋga a pɩŋ. Abɩsalɔm vɩa aŋ pɛsɛ, ka ʋ ha vɩa dɩ ʋ mʋ, ama aŋ sʋl Wɩa pʋ.”

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm bʋl, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩ jaŋ wuo kɔ, leŋ dɩ mɩ naambie Amɩnɔŋ kɔ.” Kuoro pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ cho dɩ ʋ kɔ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Ama Abɩsalɔm ha pɛsɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro leŋ Amɩnɔŋ arɩ ʋ hambolibii-kaanaa kala mʋ.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm fa bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa, “Má jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ: Dɩ Amɩnɔŋ nɛ faasa nyʋa sɩnɩŋ a bugi, dɩ mɩ nɛ bʋla pɩma, arɩ ma ŋmobu lo, má kpʋʋ. Má sɩ́ fawʋllʋŋ fá. Mɩ-na nɛ pɩma wombiiŋ. Má kɛŋ bɔɩ-duoŋ.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm tɩntɩnnaa ŋaa wɩɩ-la Abɩsalɔm sɩ sɩ ba ŋaa Amɩnɔŋ lɛ a kpʋʋ. Kuoro bii-kaanaa sii a jɩl ba kakusuŋ a fá viiri.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Ba fa ha hɛ wombiiŋ lɛ nɛ a mʋmʋ Jerusalɛm, ka duoso mʋ yi kuoro Devit: “Abɩsalɔm kpʋ kuoro biiriŋ kala nɛ, kʋbala ma bɩ ka.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Kuoro sii a kɛŋ ʋ gɛrɩŋ a kɩɛsɛ a dɩdagɛ tʋɔ-cheeŋ, aŋ pɩŋ tinteeŋ. Ʋ tɩntɩnnaa ma kala sii chɩŋ a kɛŋ ba gɛnnɩŋ kɩɛsɛ.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Ama Devit naambie Sɩmɩa nanʋala Jonadab bʋl, “Mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, ŋ biiriŋ kala dee ba kpʋ, Amɩnɔŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ sʋba. Wɩɩŋ deeŋ fa hɛ Abɩsalɔm tʋɔŋ lɛ nɛ faafaa kala, a chɩŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la Amɩnɔŋ sɩ gurigi ʋ dɩ-haala Tama.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Kuoro mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, sɩ́ leŋe dɩ wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ nɩa arɩ ŋ biiriŋ sʋba walɩmɩŋ. Amɩnɔŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ sʋba.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Abɩsalɔm fá lɛl. Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ pɔ leriŋ beŋ a na nɩ-daŋ dɩ ba to dundolo sɛmɛ a kʋʋ tuu wombii-la sɩɩ mʋ Horonem. Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ pɔ leriŋ mʋ bʋla pɩ kuoro, “Mɩ na nɩaa dɩ ba joŋ wombii-la sɩɩ mʋ Horonem a lɩɩ dundolo sɛmɛ a kʋkɔ.”

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Jonadab bʋla pɩ kuoro, “Bee na, ŋ biiriŋ nɩɩ kɔ, arɩ ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ bʋla pɩŋ.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Ʋ yie bʋla dɩdɛrɛ dɩ kuoro biiriŋ kʋ jʋʋ a ŋmuŋmoo niiŋ. Kuoro arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa ma yiyel, ba chaasa yel woruŋ.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Devit tʋɔŋ sɩ fɩɛla Amɩnɔŋ wɩaa, ʋ bɩra cho dɩ ʋ na Abɩsalɔm ma.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Zeruya nanʋala Jʋab jɩma dɩ Devit tʋɔbɩɩnaa kala hɛ Abɩsalɔm lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Tɛkʋa tɩŋŋaa haal-la mʋ kuoro teeŋ a tuu kpirimi ʋ sɩpaaŋ a zilu, aŋ bʋl, “Kuoro, pɛ mɩ lɛ.”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Kuoro pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɩɩ walɩmɩŋ?” Haal-la bʋl, “Mɩ bala sʋba nɛ ka mɩ ŋaa yo-haal.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna fa kɛŋ hambolibiisiŋ balɩa nɛ. Ba sii a yuyuo dɔŋɔ baga lɛ, nʋʋkala tuo dɩ ʋ kɛmba kɛrɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ dɔŋɔ ŋmoo dɔŋɔ a kpʋ.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ nyɩŋ-nɩaa kala sii a hosi mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna nyuŋ a bʋl, ‘Joŋ ŋ bile sɩ kpʋ ʋ naambie a pɩla dɩ la ma kpʋʋ, a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ kpʋ ʋ naambie wɩaa. Baa chɛ dɩ ba kpʋʋ nɛ aŋ laa la tinteeŋ.’ Ma sɩɩ-bala sɩ ka, ʋ nɛ baa chɛ dɩ ba togi, dɩ mɩ bala yɩrɩŋ lɛl dʋnɩa lɛ.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋla pɩ haal-la, “Mʋ dɩa, mɩ jaŋ wasɛ wɩɩ-la pɩŋ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ haal-la bʋla pʋ, “Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa, dɩ cheeriŋ nɛ hɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ, ʋ jaŋ ŋaa mɩ dɩa nɩaa wɩɩ. Ŋ dɩ ŋ dɩa nɩaa-na bɩ cheeriŋ kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋla pʋ, “Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ bʋl wɩɩ ŋ teeŋ, kɛnʋ kɔ mɩ teeŋ, tɩɩna bɩra bɩ jaŋ walɩmɩŋ.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Haal-la bʋl, “Kuoro, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, ŋmɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA ŋ Wɩa dɩ ʋ pɔ dɩ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ chɛ ʋ kpʋ mɩ bie a tɩŋ mɩ nanʋa-baal-la sɩ sʋba wɩaa, sɩ́ wombiiŋ na a ŋaa ŋɩɩ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit bʋl, “Mɩ ŋmɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ weye, ŋ nanʋala nyu-pʋŋ bala ma bɩ jaŋ churo tel.”

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ haal-la bʋl, “Jaaŋ jaaŋ, leŋ dɩ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna bɩra bʋl wɩɩ ŋ teeŋ.” Kuoro sɩ, “Bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Haal-la bɩra bʋl, “Bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ ŋ bɩɩnɛ wɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ zɔŋ a mʋ tɩgɛ Wɩa nɩaa lɛ? Wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ bʋla, ŋ tɩtɩa nɛ ŋ kɛŋ, ŋ sɩ bɩ leŋe ŋ bile ŋ sɩ kire ta mɩɩra kɔ.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: La kala jaŋ sʋʋ, la nagɛ lɩɩŋ sɩ bɩsa ta tinteeŋ nɛ, nʋʋkala bɩ jaŋ wuo paa. Ama Wɩa bɩ laa kpʋ, ʋ yie chɛ wombiiŋ nɛ a kɛsɛ la nɩalɩŋ sɩ lɛlɛ a kaa kʋ kpagɛ ʋ tɩtɩa.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ kaa kɔ dɩ mɩ bʋla pɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ, bɛɛ wɩaa nɩalɩŋ ŋaa fawʋllʋŋ kɛmmɛ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna bɩɩnɛ mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ, ‘Dɩ mɩ nɛ kʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la a pɩ ŋ-na kuoro, ŋ bɩ pɔ ŋ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna sɩɩ chɛ.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Ŋ bɩ pɔ ŋ-na kuoro jaŋ sɛɩ, a laa mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna ta baal-la nɩsɩŋ lɛ, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ walɩmɛ dɩ ʋ kpʋ mɩ dɩ mɩ nanʋala, a lɩɩsɛla ta tintee-la Wɩa sɩ joŋo pɩ la lɛ.’

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, mɩ bʋl mɩ tʋɔŋ lɛ arɩ ŋ wʋbʋlaa jaŋ wuo laamɛ ta dɩ mɩ wiesi, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ-na kuoro nagɛ Wɩa-tɩndaara nɛ, a jɩŋ wʋzɔmʋŋ arɩ wʋbɔmʋŋ bʋa. A leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA ŋ Wɩa chɩŋ ŋ harɩŋ.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bʋla pɩ haal-la, “Mɩɩ chɛ mɩ pɩɛsɩŋ wɩɩ nɛ, pʋpɔ ŋ sɩ́ wɩɩ-la bʋbʋɔŋ joŋo faamɛ.” Haal-la bʋl, “Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, pɩɛsɛmɛ wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Kuoro pɩɛsʋ, “Jʋab nɩsɩŋ hɛ wɩaa deemba lɛ nɛɛ?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ haal-la bʋl, “Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, ŋ sɩ hɛ ŋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ wɩaa, nʋʋkala bɩ jaŋ wuo joŋ wɩɩ a faaŋ. Wʋtɩtɩɩ, ŋ tɩntɩnna Jʋab nɛ dagɛmɛ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ jaŋ ŋaa arɩ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ jaŋ bʋl.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Ŋ tɩntɩnna Jʋab ŋaa ŋɩɩ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ ŋ tʋɔbɩɩnaa nɛ a bɩrɩmɛ a mʋ tɩgɛ wɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋaa lɛ. Mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, ŋ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a nagɛ Wɩa-tɩndaara nɛ, ŋ jɩŋ wɩɩkala sɩɩ ŋaa tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ kuoro yɩrɛ Jʋab a bʋla pʋ, “Wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ chɛ mɩ ŋaa, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa. Mʋ chɛ kɛŋ Abɩsalɔm kɔ.”

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Jʋab tuu kpirime kɛŋ sɩaa chu tinteeŋ a zilu, aŋ bʋl, “Wɩa jaŋ pɛ ŋ lɛ. Jɩnɩŋ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna jɩma arɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ mɩ nyuŋ nɛ, ŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna sɩɩ chɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab sii a mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gesu, a kɛŋ Abɩsalɔm mɩɩra kɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Ama kuoro bʋla pɩ Jʋab, “Leŋ dɩ ʋ mʋ ʋ dɩa, mɩ bɩ chɛ mɩ naʋ mɩ sɩpaaŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm mʋ ʋ dɩa, ʋ bɩ kuoro sɩpaaŋ kɔ.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Jɩna jɩna nɛ ʋ kaa kɩkɛ ʋ nyuŋ. Dɩ ʋ nyu-pʋnaa nɛ faasa waa dɩ ba kɛ, ba yuŋuŋ yie ŋaa kilo balɩa nɛ, dɩ ba nɛ kɛŋ sanɩa-la ba sɩ kaa mɩmagɩsɛ kɩaa kuoro dɩa lɛ a magɩsɛ.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm fa lʋl hambolibiisiŋ batori nɛ arɩ tolo kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Tama. Tolo-la fa zɔmɔ nɛ woruŋ.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm fa hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ jɩsɩŋ balɩa nɛ, ʋ bɩ wuo kɔ kuoro sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm tɩŋ ba yɩrɛ Jʋab dɩ ʋ kɛnʋ a mʋ kuoro teeŋ. Jʋab vɩa. Ʋ bɩra tɩŋ ba yɩrʋ lɩamɩŋ lɛ, ʋ bɩra vɩa.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa, “Jʋab baga kpagɛ mɩ baga nɛ, ʋ mɩaa hɛ nɩmɛ. Má mʋ nyɩgɛ ʋ baga-la.” Abɩsalɔm tɩntɩnna-la mʋ a joŋ nyiniŋ a hɛ baga-la lɛ.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab sii a mʋ Abɩsalɔm dɩa a pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ tɩntɩnnaa mʋ nyɩgɛ mɩ baga?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm bʋla pɩ Jʋab, “Mɩ tɩma ba yɩrɩŋ nɛ ŋ vɩa. Mɩ faa chɛ dɩ ŋ mʋ kuoro teeŋ a pɩɛsʋ, ‘Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ lɩɩ Gesu a kɔ daha? Ʋ fa jaŋ kpɩa a pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ nɛ ha hɛ nɩmɛ. Lɛɛlɛ mɩ cho dɩ mɩ mʋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ nɛ, dɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa wɩɩ a chei, leŋ dɩ ʋ kpʋmɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab mʋ kuoro teeŋ, a bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala Abɩsalɔm sɩ bʋla a pʋ. Ʋ yɩrɛ Abɩsalɔm, ʋ kɔ a tuu kpirime yi tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro guoru.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala lɛ, Abɩsalɔm chɛ janɩŋ arɩ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba arɩ baalaa mahɩŋ balɩa arɩ fii dɩ ba laa ʋ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Ʋ fa yie sii chʋchʋɔ-fɩɛla a lɩɩ chɩŋ wombii-la sɛmɛ lee-la ba sɩ to a mʋmʋ ba jaŋ boi-baalɩŋ. Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ kɛŋ wɩɩ a kʋkɔ kuoro teeŋ dɩ ʋ wasɛ pʋ, Abɩsalɔm yie yɩrɛ tɩɩna ʋ kɔ ʋ teeŋ ʋ pɩɛsʋ, “Tabɛɛ nɛ ŋ lɩɩ?” Dɩ nɩɩ-la nɛ sɩ ʋ lɩɩ Iziral doho doho-la dɔŋɔ nɛ,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm yie bʋl, “Ŋ kɩaa sɩma, ama nʋʋ tuo a chɩŋ kuoro naasɩŋ lɛ dɩ ʋ jegile nɩɩ ŋ wɩɩŋ.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ kʋ kpagɛ Abɩsalɔm a chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ tuu kpirimi ʋ sɩpaaŋ a chʋɔlʋ, ʋ yie guu lɩɩsɛ nɩsɩŋ nɛ, a kɛŋ tɩɩna a guoru.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Mɛlɛ deeŋ nɛ Abɩsalɔm kɛŋ Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ kɛŋ ba wɩaa kʋkɔ kuoro teeŋ dɩ ʋ wasa pɩba lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ ŋaa nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ cho ʋ wɩaa.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Jɩsɩŋ banɛsɛ sɩ bala, Abɩsalɔm bʋla pɩ kuoro, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, leŋ dɩ mɩ mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hɛbʋrɔŋ a lɩɩsɛ nii-la mɩ sɩ ta La TƖƖNA teeŋ.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna fa sɩ hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gesu sɩ hɛ Siiria tinteeŋ lɛ, mɩ fa ta niiŋ nɛ a bʋl, ‘Dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ kɛmmɛ mɩɩra mʋ Jerusalɛm, mɩ jaŋ zilu Hɛbʋrɔŋ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bʋla pʋ, “Ŋ jaŋ mʋ woruŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ sii mʋ Hɛbʋrɔŋ.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩndaara kɔ Devit teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala mɩɩra cho Abɩsalɔm nɛ a tutou.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la kala sɩ hɛ ʋ teeŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ, “Má leŋ dɩ la fá, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee la bɩ jaŋ fori Abɩsalɔm nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ʋ maga dɩ la ŋaa lɩma nɛ, dɩ ʋ sɩ́ la kʋ puu a yuo diila a kpʋ la dɩ la taŋ-la nɩaa kala.”

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala kʋ kielu bal a pɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔʋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Giti tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoro-la zɔɔ-balɩdʋ-la ma sɩ to ʋ harɩŋ a lɩɩ Gaf, ba ma kʋ bal.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Kuoro pɩɛsɛ Giti tɩɩna kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Ɩtaɩ sɩ ŋaa Giti tɩmma-la laalɩyuoro sɩpaalaara, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ tuto la harɩŋ? Mɩɩra mʋ kuoru-falɩŋ Abɩsalɔm teeŋ. Ŋ ŋaa nɩwogo nɛ, a lɩɩ Gaf tinteeŋ.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Ŋ sɩ kɔ daha, ʋ bɩ diene. Bɛɛ nɛ saa tɩɩ mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ tuto mɩ harɩŋ jɩnɩŋ, mɩ paala bɩ jɩŋ lee-la mɩ sɩɩ mʋ. Mɩɩrɛ a kɛŋ ŋ laalɩyuoroo dɩ ma viiri. A leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA dagɛma ʋ chonuŋ arɩ ʋ wʋtɩtɩɩ.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Ɩtaɩ ma bʋla pɩ kuoro, “La TƖƖNA arɩ ŋ-na kuoro sɩ weye wɩaa, lee-la kala ŋ sɩɩ mʋ, nɩmɛ nɛ mɩ ma ŋ tɩntɩnna jaŋ mʋ, dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa mɩɩsɩŋ lee koo sʋʋŋ lee.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Devit bʋla pɩ Ɩtaɩ, “Vɛnɛ kʋ mʋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɩtaɩ, Giti tɩɩna-la arɩ baala-la arɩ ba dɩa nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ ʋ teeŋ mʋ.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ fa faasa ŋmoo niiŋ nɛ bʋa-la lɛ, Devit arɩ ʋ nɩaa sɩɩ lɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro mʋ chol Kɩdɩrɔŋ fuonaa-la, ba kala tʋʋlɛ tintee-hɩlɩŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a mʋmʋ.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Zadɔk arɩ Abɩata Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa fa hɛ nɩmɛ. Levi doho nɩaa ma hɛ nɩmɛ a chʋŋ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba chʋgɛ daga-la bil, Abɩata kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩ La TƖƖNA ŋɩɩ deeŋ deeŋ nɩalɩŋ kala lɩɩ taŋ-la lɛ dɛrɛ.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit bʋla pɩ Zadɔk, “Má joŋ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la a mɩɩra jʋʋ bil Jerusalɛm lɛ. Dɩ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ tɔrɛ mɩ nyuŋ, tapʋlɩɩ dɔŋ ʋ jaŋ kɛmmɛ mɩɩra kɔ, dɩ mɩ na daga-la arɩ ʋ dɩchɩnɩŋ.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ ʋ nɛ sɩ, ‘Mɩ tʋɔŋ bɩ ŋ nyuŋ tɔrɔ,’ ŋɩɩ-na, mɩ chɩna gbɛrɛ nɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaamɛ wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩ na dɩ ʋ zɔmɔ a pʋ.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Kuoro bɩra pɩɛsɛ Zadɔk, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara, “Na ŋ ŋaa Wɩa sɩɩ-naarʋ nɛ? Kɛŋ ŋ nanʋala Ahɩmaas, dɩ Abɩata ma kɛŋ ʋ nanʋala Jonataŋ dɩ ma mɩɩra mʋ taŋ tʋɔŋ sɔm.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ gbɛrɛma fuo-la lɛ ŋ sɩ yie chol aŋ mʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ a kaa mʋ bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩ jaŋ nɩɩ wɩɩ ma teeŋ.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Zadɔk arɩ Abɩata joŋ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la a mɩɩra mʋ Jerusalɛm a hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Ka Devit kiele jɩl peel-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Olif peeliŋ, aŋ yiyel, aŋ joŋ kʋa tɔ ʋ nyuŋ a vɩvɛŋ naabirimee a dɩdagɛ tʋɔ-cheeŋ. Nɩalɩŋ ma kala sɩɩ to ʋ harɩŋ paa kɩaa tɔ ba nyusuŋ aŋ ma yele tuto.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Nʋʋ bʋla pɩ Devit, “Ahitofɛl ma lɩɩ ŋ harɩŋ nɛ, a chɩŋ Abɩsalɔm harɩŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit chʋɔlɛ Wɩa, “La TƖƖNA, leŋ dɩ wɩalɩŋ Ahitofɛl sɩ jaŋ dagɛ kuoro ŋaa wʋpɛɩba.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Devit sɩ jɩla yi Olif peel-la nyu-gbaŋa, lee-la ba fa sɩɩ chʋɔlɛ Wɩa, dɩ Aakɩ tɩɩna kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Husai fa hɛ nɩmɛ dɩ ʋ chemu. Ʋ gɛnnɩŋ kala kɩɛsɛ, ʋ nyuŋ ma kala ŋaa kʋŋkɔlʋŋ.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Devit bʋla pʋ, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ to mɩ harɩŋ, ŋ jaŋ ŋaa chʋga a pɩmɛ.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ ŋ nɛ mɩɩra mʋ taŋ tʋɔŋ a bʋla pɩ Abɩsalɔm, ‘Kuoro, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ, bumbuŋ kala mɩ ŋaa ŋ nyɩmma tɩntɩnnʋ nɛ, ama lɛɛlɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ.’ Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ŋ jaŋ wuo pɛ mɩ lɛ dɩ la kɛŋ wɩalɩŋ kala Ahitofɛl sɩ bɩɩna dɩ ʋ ŋaa a pugo ta.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa, Zadɔk arɩ Abɩata ma jaŋ hɛ ŋ teeŋ. Ŋ jaŋ wuo bʋl wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ nɩa kuoro dɩa lɛ a pɩba.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Ba hambolibiisi-la balɩa, Ahɩmaas arɩ Jonataŋ ma jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ. Tɩmba dɩ ba kʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ nɩa a pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Devit nandɔŋɔ Husai yie kʋʋ jʋʋ Jerusalɛm dɩ Abɩsalɔm ma kʋʋ jʋʋ tabal-la tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Kuoro Devit sɩ kieli Olif peel-la nyu-gbaŋa a mʋ sɩpaaŋ mʋa, dɩ Mɛfɩbɔsɛf tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ziba nɛ ŋɩɩ, a kʋ chemu. Ʋ fa kɛŋ kakusuŋ nɛ a daŋŋɛ dɔŋɔ ba chʋŋ boroboroba zɔɔ-balɩa, tɩɩnɛŋ hɩlaa kɩŋkɛsɩmɛɛ zɔlɔ, tutogi-nambɩlaa kɩŋkɛsɩmɛɛ zɔlɔ arɩ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ puruŋ sɩɩ.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Kuoro pɩɛsɛ Ziba, “Bɛɛ nɛ ŋ kɛŋ kɩaa deemba kala kɔ dɩ ŋ ŋaa?” Ziba bʋl, “Kakusu-la ŋaa ŋ dɩa nɩaa kɩaa nɛ dɩ ba jɩjɩl, boroboroba-la arɩ tɩɩnɛnɛ-la ŋaa ŋ nɩaa kʋdiilee nɛ dɩ ba didii, tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩŋ-la ma nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ lɔlɔ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ jaŋ nyʋa a bɩra kɛŋ doluŋ.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Kuoro Devit bɩra pɩɛsɛ, “Nɩɩ nɛ ŋ nɩhɩaŋ Sɔɔl nihiŋ Mɛfɩbɔsɛf hɛ?” Ziba bʋl, “Ʋ nɛ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ bɩɩna Iziral tɩŋŋaa jaŋ joŋ ʋ naabalɩma kuoruŋ a pʋ.”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bɩra bʋla pɩ Ziba, “Mɛfɩbɔsɛf fa sɩ tɩɩ kɩalɩŋ kala, lɛɛlɛ ba ŋaa ŋ kɩaa nɛ.” Ziba bʋl, “Kuoro mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, mɩ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ nɛ, a leŋ dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ mɩ nyuŋ bʋa na-kala.” Sɩmɛɩ bʋl wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ hɛ Devit lɛ

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Kuoro Devit sɩ mʋ yi taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bahurim, baal kʋbala sɩ ŋaa Sɔɔl nyɩŋ-nɩaa dɔŋɔ kʋ lɩɩ a suomo bʋl wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ hɩhɛ ʋ lɛ. Baal-la yɩrɩŋ nɛ Sɩmɛɩ a ŋaa Gɛra nanʋala.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Ʋ paa tabɩaa a yɩyagɛ Devit arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ kala. Devit laalɩyuoroo arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔʋ kala fa hɛ Devit nadiiŋ arɩ ʋ nagʋa kala nɛ, ka baal-la ŋɩŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Sɩmɛɩ tʋʋsʋ aŋ bʋl “Mʋ lɩɩ, mʋ lɩɩ, ŋ ŋaa nɩkpʋʋrʋ nɛ, a ŋaa nɩbɔŋ.

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA joŋ nɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ kpʋa Sɔɔl dɩa lɛ chɩmɩŋ nɛ a tiŋ ŋ lɛ. Ʋ kuoruŋ nɛ ŋ gaa dii ŋɩɩ. La TƖƖNA laa kuorii-la nɛ ŋ teeŋ a joŋo pɩ ŋ nanʋala Abɩsalɔm. Ŋ ŋaa nɩkpʋʋrʋ nɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ wɩaa deemba kala jʋʋŋ.”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Zeruya nanʋala Abɩsaɩ pɩɛsɛ kuoro, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ va-sʋʋŋ deeŋ tʋtʋʋsɛ kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ? Leŋ dɩ mɩ mʋ keri ʋ nyuŋ.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Ama kuoro Devit sɩ, “Ŋ wɩɩ tuo wɩɩŋ deeŋ lɛ, dɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ sɩ Sɩmɛɩ tʋʋsɛmɛ, kʋbɛɛ nɛ kaŋ dɩ ŋ bʋl ʋ sɩ́ ŋɩɩ ŋaa?”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit bɩra bʋla pɩ Abɩsaɩ arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ kala, “Mɩ tɩtɩa bii-lʋlʋŋ nɩɩ walɩmɛ dɩ ʋ kpʋmɛ. Bɛɛ nɛ jaŋ tɩɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩa deeŋ-na bɩ jaŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ kpʋmɛ? Má leŋu dɩ ʋ tʋʋsɛmɛ ŋɩɩ kala ʋ sɩɩ chɛ. La TƖƖNA nɛ sɩ ʋ tʋʋsɛmɛ.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Kapo La TƖƖNA jaŋ bɩra wuo na wɩalɩŋ sɩ jʋʋmɛ jɩnɩŋ arɩ ŋɩɩ ba sɩɩ tʋʋsɛmɛ, a fá mɩ nenige a joŋ wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ a timmi.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Devit arɩ ʋ nɩaa joŋ wombiiŋ a vɩvɛŋ, aŋ ka Sɩmɛɩ ma kpɛrɛ to dundolo sɛmɛ a chaasʋ, a tʋtʋʋsʋ a bʋl wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ hɩhɛ ʋ lɛ, aŋ paa tabɩaa arɩ hagɩla a yuyuou.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Kuoro arɩ ʋ nɩaa kala sɩ kʋ yi Jɔdaŋ fuo-la, dɩ ba chaasa lɔl, ba hɔŋ nɩmɛ a wiesi. Wɩalɩŋ Husai arɩ Ahitofɛl sɩ dagɛ Abɩsalɔm

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ, dɩ Abɩsalɔm, Ahitofɛl arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala kɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Husai, Aakɩ tɩɩna-la, Devit nandɔŋɔ, sii mʋ Abɩsalɔm teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “A leŋ dɩ kuoro mɩɩsɩŋ duomi.”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm pɩɛsɛ Husai, “Ŋ-la nɛ ŋ dagɛ arɩ ŋ cho ŋ nandɔŋɔ nɛɛ? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ bɩ ŋ nandɔŋɔ harɩŋ to mʋ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Husai bʋla pʋ, “Aɩ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ mʋ. Ŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA arɩ Iziral nɩaa lɩɩsɛ ŋ dii kuoruŋ. Ŋ harɩŋ nɛ mɩ jaŋ to a tɩma pɩpɩŋ.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Kʋbɛɛ nɛ maga dɩ mɩ tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa pa? Mɩ nɩhɩaŋ nanʋala dee? Ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ tɩŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa a pɩ ŋ nyɩmma Devit, ŋɩɩ nɛ maga dɩ mɩ tɩŋ a pɩ ŋ ma.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm mɩɩra pɩɛsɛ Ahitofɛl, “Dagɛla wɩɩ-la sɩ maga dɩ la ŋaa. Wʋbɛɛ nɛ maga dɩ la ŋaa?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ahitofɛl bʋl, “Kɛŋ ŋ nyɩmma haala-la ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa a leŋ ba pʋpɔ ʋ kuoru dɩa pɩŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, Iziral nɩaa kala jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ ŋ dɩ ŋ nyɩmma ŋaa dʋndɔmɔ nɛ. Nɩalɩŋ kala sɩɩ toŋ jaŋ chaasa chɩŋ ŋ harɩŋ.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba hɛ lɛbɩŋ kuoru-dɩa lusuŋ nyuŋ a pɩ Abɩsalɔm. Iziral nɩaa kala bibeŋ, ka ʋ kɛŋ ʋ nyɩmma haala-la ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa pɩŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ, wɩalɩŋ Ahitofɛl fa sɩ dagɛ Abɩsalɔm fa nagɛ nɩa sɩ nɩɩ wɩaa Wɩa teeŋ nɛ. Devit arɩ Abɩsalɔm kala fa bɩɩna wɩalɩŋ lɩɩ Wɩa teeŋ nɛ.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: dɩ la kala mʋ yuo Devit lee-la kala la sɩ jaŋ naʋ. La jaŋ tuu ʋ lɛ a nagɛ nyalɩŋ sɩ yie kʋ tuu tinteeŋ ŋɩɩ. Dɩ la nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩaa kʋŋkala bɩ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ yuou bʋa-la lɛ lɔlʋŋ sɩ jʋʋ-ʋ, ʋ nandaasɩŋ kala yʋɔrɛ. Mɩ jaŋ guu mʋ dɩ ʋ lɛ, dɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛnʋ, dɩ ʋ nɩaa kala fá viiri. Ka dɩ mɩ kpʋ ʋ dʋndʋŋa,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: aŋ kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ kala a mɩɩra kʋ pɩŋ, a nagɛ ba sɩ kpɩɛrɛ ha-falɩŋ a kaa mʋ pɩ ʋ bala. Kuoro dʋndʋŋa mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ ŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ŋ lɩɩsɛ, ka dɩ nɩkaanaa kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm arɩ Iziral doho doho-la sɩpaalaaraa kala na dɩ wɩalɩŋ Ahitofɛl sɩ daga ŋaa wʋzɔmɔ.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm bʋl, “Má yɩrɛ Husai, Aakɩ tɩɩna-la dɩ ʋ kɔ, dɩ la nɩɩ wɩɩ-la ʋ ma sɩ jaŋ bʋl.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Husai sɩ kɔ, Abɩsalɔm bʋl wɩɩ-la Ahitofɛl sɩ dagɛba, aŋ pɩɛsʋ, “La ŋaa koo la leŋ? Dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, ŋ ma bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ.”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Husai bʋla pɩ Abɩsalɔm, “Bʋa deeŋ-na lɛ, wɩɩ-la Ahitofɛl sɩ dagɛma bɩ zɔŋ.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Ŋ jɩma woruŋ ŋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ nɩaa chaasa ŋaa laalɩyuoro nɛ. Lɛɛlɛ ŋ-la ba yaraa kala hoso nɛ a nagɛ lʋgʋmʋŋ bie ba sɩ kpʋa ʋ yaraa hosi. Ŋɩɩ ma dʋndʋŋa dee, ŋ nyɩmma ŋaa laalɩyuori-bɩnɩɩ nɛ, a bɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo tʋɔŋ ka guoli tɩtaŋɩŋ.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Magɛ ŋ-la ʋ paala jʋʋ faa bʋ-bʋa lɛ koo lee dɔŋ. Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ nɩa dɩ Devit kpʋ ma laalɩyuoroo dɔnsʋŋ, nɩaa jaŋ bɩɩnɛ laalɩyuoro-la kala sɩɩ to Abɩsalɔm harɩŋ nɛ ba kpʋ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Ŋ laalɩyuoro-la ma kala sɩ paala ŋaa baalaa, a kɛŋ bɔɩ-duoŋ a nagɛ naachigiŋ, fawʋllʋŋ jaŋ jʋʋba dɩ ba nandaasɩŋ yʋɔrɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa nʋʋkala sɩ hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ jɩma dɩ ŋ nyɩmma ŋaa laalɩyuori-babiibal nɛ, ʋ nɩaa ma kala ŋaa bɔɩ-duo tɩmma.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na sɩ jaŋ bʋl nɛ: Leŋ dɩ la yɩrɛ laalɩyuoro-la kala sɩ hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, a chɩŋ Daŋ sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ, a kaa mʋ Bɛɛsɩba ma sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ, dɩ ba kala kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ, dɩ ŋ laalɩyuoroo yʋgɛ a nagɛ hagɩlɩ-bumbugulo sɩ pɩŋ fuoŋ niiŋ, dɩ ŋ-na tɩtɩa Abɩsalɔm laa ba sɩpaaŋ a kɛmba mʋ laalɩŋ,

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ leŋe aŋ fá jʋʋ taŋ-la ba sɩ saa kɛrɛ a golli, la nɩaa kala jaŋ kɛŋ ŋmɛsɩŋ a kʋ vɔɔ taŋ-la jebiee a lɛrɛ lo, a lɛrʋ tuu fuonaaŋ. La bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ tabɩɩ-bie ma ka nɩmɛ.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm arɩ Iziral nɩaa kala bʋl, “Wɩɩ-la Husai, Aakɩ tɩɩna-la sɩ bʋla nɛ kpɩa wɩɩ-la Ahitofɛl sɩ bʋla.” La TƖƖNA faa chɛ dɩ ba sɩ́ wʋzɔŋ-la Ahitofɛl sɩ bʋla to nɛ, ka dɩ ʋ joŋ wʋlɔrʋŋ a ŋaa Abɩsalɔm lɛ.

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Husai mʋ bʋla pɩ Zadɔk arɩ Abɩata, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa, “Ahitofɛl dagɛ Abɩsalɔm arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa dɩ ba ŋaa ŋ-la arɩ ŋ-la nɛ, ama mɩ ma dagɛba dɩ ba ŋaa ŋ-la arɩ ŋ-la nɛ.”

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩra bʋl, “Ŋaa lɩma a leŋ dɩ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Devit, dɩ ʋ sɩ́ fuonaa-la ŋ sɩ yie kieli aŋ jʋʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ chʋa. Má bʋla pʋ dɩ ʋ chol fuo-la, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, ba jaŋ kpʋ ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩaa kala.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Abɩata nanʋala Jonataŋ arɩ Zadɔk bie Ahɩmaas fa hɛ Ɛŋ-Rɔgɛl lɩɩ-bulo-la leriŋ nɛ, Jerusalɛm niiŋ aa gbɛrɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa dɩ ba nɛ naba dɩ baa jʋʋ taŋ-la, ʋ bɩ jaŋ zɔŋ a pɩba. Tɩntɩnnɩ hantolibie kʋbala nɛ fa yie mʋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala sɩ ŋaa a pɩba, ba ma kaa mʋ bʋla pɩ kuoro Devit.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Ama bapʋɔsɩ-bie kʋbala naba, a mʋ bʋla pɩ Abɩsalɔm. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jonataŋ arɩ Ahɩmaas sii lɩma lɩma a mʋ faa baal kʋbala sɩ hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bahurim dɩa lɛ. Dɩ baal-la fa kɛŋ viliŋ ʋ kaala tʋɔŋ, ba tuu faa ʋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ʋ haala joŋ kʋa a tɔ vil-la niiŋ a joŋ mɩaa a yieni, dɩ nʋʋkala sɩ́ wuo jɩŋ.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abɩsalɔm nɩaa kɔ haal-la teeŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Nɩɩ nɛ Ahɩmaas arɩ Jonataŋ hɛ?” Haal-la bʋla pɩba, “Ba chol fuoŋ cholo nɛ.” Nɩalɩŋ gɔllɔ chɛba, a bɩ ba na aŋ mɩɩra mʋ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩ chɛba ka aŋ mɩɩra viiri, Ahɩmaas arɩ Jonataŋ kʋ lɩɩ vil-la tʋɔŋ, a mʋ bʋla pɩ kuoro Devit. Ba sɩ, “Sii lɩma a chol fuo-la.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bʋl wɩalɩŋ Ahitofɛl sɩ bʋla a tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ a pʋ.

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Devit arɩ ʋ nɩaa kala sii a chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la. Taŋ ka pʋl dɩ ba kala cholo dɛrɛ, ba kʋŋkala bɩ ka.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ahitofɛl sɩ na dɩ Abɩsalɔm arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa bɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ daga to, ʋ sii kpɩɛrɛ ʋ kakumo a mɩɩra mʋ ʋ jaŋ Gilo. Ʋ sɩ mʋa, ʋ dagɛ ʋ dɩa nɩaa arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ jaŋ ŋaa, aŋ lieŋi ʋ tɩtɩa, a sʋʋ. Ba joŋu hugi ʋ nyɩmma bʋa lɛ.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Devit sii a mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mahanem, ka Abɩsalɔm arɩ Iziral nɩalɩŋ kala chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ, dɩ Abɩsalɔm lɩɩsɛ Amasa nɛ ʋ laa Jʋab nyuŋ a ŋaa ʋ laalɩyuoroo nɩhɩaŋ. Amasa nyɩmma yɩrɩŋ nɛ fa Jɛta, a ŋaa Iziral tɩɩna, a jaa Abɩgɛl sɩ ŋaa Nahas tolo, aŋ ŋaa Zeruya ma naambii. Zeruya nɛ fa ŋaa Jʋab naaŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala fa ŋmoo buguŋ Gɩlɩad tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Devit sɩ kɔ Mahanem, Nahas nanʋala Sobi sɩ lɩɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Raba a hɛ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ lɛ, arɩ Amɩɛl nanʋala Makɩɩ ma sɩ lɩɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lo Dɛba, arɩ Baazɩlaɩ, Gɩlɩad tɩɩna-la ma sɩ lɩɩ Rɔgɛlɩm,

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: tʋʋŋ arɩ nɛyɩl-dɩndɛrɩŋ, piesee arɩ nɛyɩl-nʋʋŋ, a kaa kʋ pɩba dɩ ba dii, bɛɛ wɩaa ba sɩ, “Losuŋ kɛŋ nɩalɩŋ nɛ, lɩɩnyʋasʋŋ ma kɛmba, lɔlʋŋ ma jʋʋba tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Ʋ kɛŋ laalɩyuoro-la kala kpaa leree batori nɛ. Jʋab laa dɔnsʋŋ sɩpaaŋ, Jʋab naambie Abɩsaɩ, Zeruya nanʋala ma laa dɔnsʋŋ sɩpaaŋ, ka Ɩtaɩ, Giti tɩɩna-la ma laa dɔnsʋŋ sɩpaaŋ. Kuoro Devit fa bʋla pɩba, “Mɩ tɩtɩa jaŋ to ma harɩŋ a mʋ laal-la.”

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ laalɩyuoro-la bʋl, “Ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ŋ mʋ, dɩ la dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ kirila dɩ la fá, ba sɩpaaŋ jaŋ tuo la-na lɛ. Dɩ ba nɛ kpʋ la kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ ma, ʋ bɩ jaŋ ŋaaba wɩɩkala. Ama ŋ kɩɩ la nɩaa bʋɩ fii nɛ. Ʋ jaŋ kpɩa dɩ ŋ nɛ hɛ dɩa lɛ, dɩ la nɛ kɛŋ wɩɩ, dɩ ŋ pɛ la lɛ.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Laalɩyuoro-la dɔŋɔ sɩ na ŋɩɩ, ʋ bʋla pɩ Jʋab, “Mɩ na Abɩsalɔm dɩ ʋ sagɛ piine kʋbala nyuŋ, a lilieŋi.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Laalɩŋ pusi lee-la kala. Nɩalɩŋ duu-la sɩ leŋe ba sʋʋ tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ kɩɩ nɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kpʋa laalɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dɩ Abɩsalɔm mʋ cheŋ Devit laalɩyuoroo. Ʋ fa jɩl kakumo nɛ. Kakumo-la kɛnʋ jʋʋ piiŋ-lugu kʋbala bʋbʋɔŋ. Tɩa-la naakelee kɛŋ Abɩsalɔm nyu-pʋnaa lɛ a soru kakumo-la nyuŋ ʋ lilieŋi, ka kakumo-la kiele mʋmʋ.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Jʋab bʋla pɩ baal-la sɩ bʋl wɩɩ-la pʋ, “Bɛɛba! Ŋ naʋ nɛɛ? Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ bɩ ʋ ŋmoo lo tinteeŋ lee-la? Mɩ fa jaŋ pɩŋ warɩpʋla fii arɩ laalɩyuoroo ŋmɛnɩŋ.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Wɩɩkala nɛ kuoro nɩnɩɩ, dɩ mɩ fa vɩa ʋ niiŋ aŋ kpʋ Abɩsalɔm, ŋ fa bɩ jaŋ chɩŋ mɩ harɩŋ.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Jʋab bʋl, “Mɩ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ chɩna kɛmmɛ didieni.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ joŋ tiŋŋee batori a yagɛ hɛ Abɩsalɔm bɔyɛ lɛ, dɩ Abɩsalɔm ha weye, a sagɛ piine-la nyuŋ.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab laalɩyuoro-la fii sɩ kori ʋ laalɩyuori kɩaa kʋ golli Abɩsalɔm chu a kpʋʋ.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab ŋmʋʋ banyile a giri ʋ laalɩyuoroo dɩ ba bɩra sɩ́ Iziral laalɩyuoroo kiru.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Ba joŋ Abɩsalɔm kʋsʋʋŋ a yuo hɛ buotuo-luŋii lɛ duu-la tʋɔŋ, a paa tabɩaa yʋgɛ a daŋ ʋ lɛ, ba sii chʋɔrɛ. Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala fá a mʋ ba dɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Abɩsalɔm fa sɩ hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, ʋ kɛŋ tabɩaa nɛ a saa kɛrɛ ʋ chɩŋ kuoro fuonaaŋ lɛ ba sɩ jaŋ kaa liliisi ʋ wɩaa. Ʋ sɩ, “Mɩ bɩ bii kala kɛnɛ sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ yɩrɩŋ sɩ́ dɩsʋ.” Ʋ joŋ ʋ tɩtɩa yɩrɩŋ a hɛ pɩ jebii-la. Arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala ba haa yɩrɛ jebii-la Abɩsalɔm jebiiŋ nɛ. Devit yel Abɩsalɔm lɛ

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Zadɔk nanʋala Ahɩmaas bʋla pɩ Jʋab, “Leŋ dɩ mɩ fá mʋ hɛ duoso pɩ kuoro Devit, arɩ La TƖƖNA laaʋ ta nɛ ʋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Jʋab bʋla pʋ, “Jɩnɩŋ, ŋ dee nɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ kɛŋ duoso-la mʋ. Tapʋlɩɩ dɔŋ nɛ ŋ jaŋ kɛŋ duoso-la mʋ, ama jɩnɩŋ-na dee, bɛɛ wɩaa kuoro nanʋala sʋba nɛ.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab bʋla pɩ Kus tɩɩna kʋbala, “Mʋ a bʋl wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ na a pɩ kuoro.” Baal-la tuu kpirimi Jʋab sɩpaaŋ a zilu, aŋ sii fá mʋ.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Zadɔk nanʋala Ahɩmaas bɩra bʋla pɩ Jʋab, “Ʋ cho dɩ ʋ nagɛ ŋɩɩ kala, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, leŋ dɩ mɩ ma ha to mʋ.” Ama Jʋab bɩra pɩɛsɛ, “Mɩ bii, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ cho dɩ ŋ mʋa? Ŋ bɩ wɩɩkala kɛnɛ ŋ sɩ jaŋ mʋ bʋl a laa siilee.”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ahɩmaas ha bʋl, “Ʋ cho dɩ ʋ nagɛ ŋɩɩ kala, mɩ ha cho mɩ mʋa nɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab bʋl, “Saa fá mʋ ba.” Ahɩmaas lɩɩ a joŋ wombii-la sɩ to Jɔdaŋ fuonaaŋ, a fá mʋ kieli Kus tɩɩna-la.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Devit hɔŋ ba jaŋ boiŋ niiree balɩa-la pɛgɛ, kʋ-la sɩ hɛ tʋɔŋ arɩ kʋ-la sɩ hɛ jeeŋ harɩŋ. Nɩɩ-la sɩɩ pɔ ba taŋ-la sii jɩl boiŋ niiŋ jee-la lusuŋ nyuŋ. Ʋ sɩ bene, ʋ na baal kʋbala dɩ ʋ dʋndʋŋa fá a kʋkɔ.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Baal-la sɩɩ pɔ ba taŋ yɩrɛ kuoro a bʋl wɩɩ-la pʋ. Kuoro bʋl, “Dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa ʋ dʋndʋŋa, ŋɩɩ-na wʋzɔmɔ nɛ ʋ kaa kʋkɔ.” Ka baal-la kʋʋ kpagɛ.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ pɔ ba taŋ bɩra na baal dɔŋ ma, dɩ ʋ fá kʋkɔ. Ʋ yɩrɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ pɔ boi-baalɩŋ a bʋl, “Bee na, baal dɔŋ ma dʋndʋŋ nɛ bɩra fá a kʋkɔ.” Kuoro bɩra bʋl, “Ŋ bɩ pɔ wʋzɔmɔ nɛ ʋ ma kaa kɔ.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Baal-la sɩɩ pɔ ba taŋ bʋl, “Mɩ-na teeŋ bumbuŋ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ fá nagɛ Zadɔk nanʋala Ahɩmaas nɛ.” Kuoro bʋl, “Ʋ wɩaa zɔmɔ. Wʋzɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ ʋ jaŋ kaa kɔ.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ahɩmaas yɩrɛ kuoro a bʋl, “La die nɛ! La die nɛ!” Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ tuu kpirimi kuoro Devit sɩpaaŋ a zilu aŋ bʋl, “Dɛnnɛ ŋ TƖƖNA Wɩa! Ʋ nɛ leŋe ŋ yuo dii ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Kuoro pɩɛsʋ, “Ka bapʋɔsɩ-bie-la, Abɩsalɔm, wɩɩkala bɩ ʋ ŋaa?” Ahɩmaas bʋl, “Mɩ fa na leriŋ chaasa vʋgʋmɛ nɛ bʋa-la lɛ Jʋab sɩɩ tɩŋ ʋ tɩntɩnna arɩ mɩ-na, ama mɩ bɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la kala sɩ tɩɩ.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋl, “Gɛbɛ chɩŋ daha a gbɛrɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ gɛbɛ chɩŋ.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Kus tɩɩna-la ma kɔ a bʋl, “Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, nɩɩ wʋzɔŋ-la mɩ sɩ kaa kɔ. La TƖƖNA laaŋ ta nɛ jɩnɩŋ ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ kala nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bɩra pɩɛsʋ ma, “Ka Abɩsalɔm, wɩɩkala bɩ ʋ ŋaa?” Kus tɩɩna-la bʋl, “Mɩ fa jaŋ cho dɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ ŋaa ŋ-na kuoro mɩ nɩhɩaŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ vɩaŋ aŋ yuyuoŋ, dɩ ba dɩdɛrɩŋ kala nagɛ bapʋɔsɩ-bie-la.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Kuoro kala chichel. Ʋ sii jɩla jʋʋ dɩa-la sɩ hɛ boiŋ niiŋ lusuŋ nyuŋ a yel. Ʋ sɩɩ jʋʋ ŋɩɩ, ʋ bʋl: “Mɩ bii Abɩsalɔm! Mɩ bii, mɩ bii Abɩsalɔm! Mɩ nɛ fa maga dɩ mɩ sʋʋ aŋ kaŋ. Mɩ bii Abɩsalɔm, mɩ bii.”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Nʋʋ dɔŋ mʋ bʋla pɩ Jʋab, “Kuoro ka yel nɛ a tɩŋ Abɩsalɔm sɩ sʋba wɩaa.”

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Tʋɔtɔrʋ-la laalɩyuoro-la kala sɩ kɛnɛ tapʋlɩɩ-la mɩɩra bɩrɩmɛ yele, bɛɛ wɩaa ba nɩa arɩ kuoro tʋɔŋ cheye nɛ, ʋ yiyel ʋ bie wɩaa.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Laalɩyuoro-la lʋara jʋʋ taŋ tʋɔŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la, a nagɛ nɩaa ba sɩ kire ba fá laalɩŋ lɛ hɩɩsɩŋ kɛmba.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Kuoro fa paa nɩsaa nɛ a tɔ ʋ sɩaa, aŋ faasa yiyel, “Mɩ bii Abɩsalɔm! Abɩsalɔm, mɩ bii, mɩ bii!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jʋab mʋ kuoro dɩa a bʋla pʋ, “Jɩnɩŋ ŋ joŋ hɩɩsɩŋ hɛ nɩaa kala lɛ nɛ, nɩalɩŋ sɩ laa ŋ mɩɩsɩŋ, ŋ hambolibiisiŋ, toloo arɩ ŋ haala-la ŋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa.

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Ŋ cho nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɛrɩŋ nɛ, aŋ bɛrɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ choŋ. Jɩnɩŋ ŋ leŋe la chaasa jɩŋ arɩ ŋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ arɩ ba nɩaa kala bɩ kɩaa ŋaa ŋ teeŋ. Mɩ bɩra na jɩnɩŋ arɩ ŋ fa cho dɩ Abɩsalɔm nɛ wei, ka dɩ la kala sʋʋ.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Sii lɛɛlɛ a lɩɩ bʋl wɩaa pɩ ŋ laalɩyuoroo dɩ ba nyuŋ nyaasɛ, dɩ ŋɩɩ dee, mɩ ŋmɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA, nɩbala ma bɩ jaŋ chɩna gbɛrɩŋ chie chʋchʋɔŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ jaŋ lɔrɔ pɩŋ a kɩɩ wʋlɔrʋnʋ-la kala sɩ ŋaa ŋ lɛ, a chɩŋ ŋ hambiiriŋ kala lɛ a kaa kɔ bʋa deeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro sii a lɩɩ hɔŋ jaŋ boiŋ niiŋ. Ba bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ, “Kuoro nɛ hɔŋ jaŋ boiŋ niiŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kala kɔ ʋ sɩpaaŋ. Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala fa fá mʋ ba dɩɩsɩŋ. Devit mɩɩra mʋ Jerusalɛm

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Kuoro Devit nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ Iziral tɩmma-la sɩɩ bʋl, a tɩŋ tɩndaarɩŋ deeŋ a pɩ Zadɔk arɩ Abɩata, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa: “Má pɩɛsɛ Juda nɩaa sɩpaalaaraa na, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ba chɩchɛ dɩ ba nɛ to harɩŋ a kɛŋ kuoro kɔ ʋ dɩa?”

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩra bʋl, “Má ŋaa mɩ naambiiriŋ nɛ, mɩ chalɩŋ nɛ ka ma. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma chɩchɛ dɩ ma nɛ to harɩŋ a kɛŋ mɩ-na kuoro kɔ?”

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Aŋ bɩra pɩɛsɛ Amasa ma, “Mɩ chalɩŋ dee bɩŋ kaa? A lɩɩ bʋa deeŋ lɛ a kaa mʋ, dɩ mɩ nɛ bɩ leŋe dɩ ŋ ŋaa mɩ laalɩyuoroo nɩhɩaŋ, a laa Jʋab nyuŋ, a leŋ dɩ Wɩa dɔgɩsɛmɛ kɩŋkɛŋ.”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Kuoro Devit sɩ bʋl wɩɩ-la leŋ Juda nɩaa kala tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ ʋ nyuŋ. Ba tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pʋ, “Ŋ dɩ ŋ nɩaa kala, má mɩɩra kɔ.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Gɛra nanʋala Sɩmɛɩ, Bɛnjamɩŋ tɩŋŋaa baal-la sɩ lɩɩ Bahurim, sii lɩma lɩma, ʋ dɩ Juda tɩmma-la kʋ tuu dɩ ba cheŋ kuoro Devit.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: bɛɛ wɩaa mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna jɩma arɩ mɩ ŋaa wɩaa cheyiŋ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ jɩnɩŋ Iziral doho doho-la kala sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa tʋɔŋ, mɩ nɛ laa sɩpaaŋ kɔ daha dɩ mɩ na ŋ-na kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Ba chol fuo-la, lee-la sɩ bɩ luŋ dɩ ba kɛŋ kuoro dɩa nɩaa chol, aŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩɩ chɛ. Gɛra bie Sɩmɛɩ sɩ chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la, ʋ tuu kpirime yi tinteeŋ kuoro sɩpaaŋ,

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: aŋ bʋla pʋ, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, sɩ́ cheeriŋ joŋo pɩmɛ. Sɩ́ ŋɩɩ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna fa sɩ tʋʋsʋŋ bʋa-la lɛ ŋ sɩɩ lɩɩ Jerusalɛm lɛ liisu. Kuoro, paala sɩ́ wɩɩ-la joŋo hɛ ŋ tʋɔŋ lɛ,

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Devit bʋl, “Ma-na Zeruya biiriŋ, ma wɩɩ tuo wɩɩŋ deeŋ lɛ. Sɩ́ wɩaa lɔgɔ hɛ mɩ lɛ. Jɩnɩŋ ʋ maga dɩ la kpʋ nʋʋ nɛ Iziral lɛɛ? Ŋ bɩɩna mɩ bɩ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ bɩra ŋaa Iziral kuoro jɩnɩŋ?”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Kuoro hɛ niiŋ pɩ Sɩmɛɩ, a bʋl, “Ŋ bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Ʋ bʋl, “Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, ŋ jɩma mɩ ŋaa gbɛrɩgʋ nɛ. Mɩ bʋla pɩ mɩ tɩntɩnna Ziba nɛ, dɩ ʋ kpɩɛrɛ mɩ kakumo pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ jɩla to ŋ harɩŋ. Ʋ nyɩsɛmɛ ta aŋ mʋ,

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: a nyɩɛ wɩaa a tɩgɛ mɩ lɛ a pɩŋ. Kuoro mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, ŋ kɛŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ a nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaara nɛ. Wɩɩ-la kala sɩ tɔrɛ ŋ tʋɔŋ, ŋaa.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, mɩ nyɩmma dɩa nɩaa kala paala magɛ dɩ ŋ fa kpʋla nɛ. Ama ŋ wuo pɩmɛ wombiiŋ nɛ, mɩ didii kɩaa ŋ dɩa lɛ. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa wombii bɛɛ nɛ mɩ kɛŋ dɩ mɩ ma bɩra pɩɛsa chɩchɛ wɩɩ ŋ-na kuoro teeŋ?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋla pʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ bʋl wɩaa a nɩna hɛɛŋ? Ŋ dɩ Ziba kɛŋ Sɔɔl dʋa kpaa dɔŋɔ.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Mɛfɩbɔsɛf bɩra bʋla pɩ kuoro, “Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, ŋ sɩ folo kɔ dɩa arɩ yarɩfɩɛlaa, leŋ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ dʋa-la kala.”

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Gɩlɩad tɩɩna-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bazɩlaɩ ma sii a lɩɩ Rɔgɛlɩm a kɔ dɩ ʋ kɛŋ Devit chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la, a hɛʋ wɛnɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋla pʋ, “Chol fuo-la dɩ la mʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ. Mɩ jaŋ bibeniŋ.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Bazɩlaɩ pɩɛsɛ kuoro, “Jɩsɩŋ baŋmɛɛ nɛ mɩ bɩra jaŋ hɛ dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛ, a magɛ mɩ dɩ mɩ kuoro mʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna jaŋ to ŋ harɩŋ dɩ la chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la, a vɛnɛ mʋ mʋa. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ kuoro jaŋ dii zile kɩŋkɛŋ mɩ lɛ ŋ-la?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Leŋ dɩ mɩ mɩɩra mʋ dɩa, a sʋʋ mɩ jaŋ lɛ, dɩ ba hugimi kpagɛ mɩ nyɩmma arɩ mɩ naaŋ vaamɩŋ. Ama, na ŋ tɩntɩnna Kɩmɩham nɛ ŋ-la. Kuoro, mɩ nɩhɩaŋ, leŋ dɩ ʋ ma to ŋ harɩŋ a chol fuo-la. Ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ŋ sɩ bene dɩ ʋ zɔmɔ a pʋ.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋl, “Kɩmɩham jaŋ to mɩ harɩŋ chol, wɩɩ-la kala sɩ tɔrɛ ŋ tʋɔŋ, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa pʋ. Kʋŋ na-kala ŋ ma tɩtɩa sɩɩ chɛ mɩ teeŋ, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa pɩŋ.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ laalɩyuoro-la kala chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la, kuoro ma chol. Kuoro arɩ Bazɩlaɩ guori dɔŋɔ. Kuoro sʋl Wɩa pʋ. Ka Bazɩlaɩ mɩɩra mʋ dɩa.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Kuoro sɩ chol fuo-la a mʋ Gɩlɩgal, Kɩmɩham ma chol a to ʋ harɩŋ. Juda laalɩyuoroo kala arɩ Iziral laalɩyuoroo kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ fa kɔ dɩ ba kɛŋ kuoro chol a hɛʋ wɛnɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩ diene ka Iziral laalɩyuoroo kala sii kɔ kuoro Devit teeŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ la naambiiriŋ, Juda laalɩyuoroo kʋ lʋara kɛŋ ŋ-na kuoro arɩ ŋ dɩa nɩaa arɩ ŋ nɩaa kala a chol Jɔdaŋ fuo-la?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Juda laalɩyuoro-la kala bʋla pɩ Iziral laalɩyuoroo, “La dɩ kuoru-la ŋaa naambiiri nɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ la ŋaa ŋɩɩ. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma na baanɩŋ? Kuoro kʋdiilii nɛ la laa dii? La laa kʋŋ nɛ ʋ teeŋ?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Iziral laalɩyuoro-la ma bʋla pɩ Juda laalɩyuoroo, “La tɩɩ Devit a kɩɩma naansɩɩŋ fii, dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa ma kʋŋ ma, bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma bee gʋʋnɛla? La dee bɩ sɩpaaŋ laa bʋl arɩ ma leŋ la kɛŋ la kuoro mɩɩra kɔɔ?” Ama Juda tɩmma-la ha faasa hosi a kɩɩ Iziral tɩmma-la.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
