translation_verse: Solomoŋ bɩra leŋ ba kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ a ŋaa La Tɩɩna dɩɩ-bal-la kɩaa deemba: Wɩɩsʋllɩ koruŋ, teebʋl-la nyuŋ ba sɩ yie joŋ boroboro daŋ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ,

english_verse: ten lampstands that went in front of the most holy place; flower designs; lamps and tongs;
translation_verse: arɩ chaaŋ daasɩŋ. Banɔŋ hɛ nadiiŋ, banɔŋ ma hɛ nagʋa, a chɩŋ Wɩa dɩa-la lee-la sɩ chaasa zɔŋ sɩpaaŋ. Tɩɩ-fɩɩlaa, chaanaa arɩ chɛŋŋɛɛ,

english_verse: cups, lamp snuffers, and small sprinkling bowls; dishes for incense; fire pans; and the hinges for the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
translation_verse: gbansɩŋ, kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kaa kikeri chaaŋ ŋmɛnɩŋ, kʋmɩsɩrɩ gbansɩŋ, kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ hɛnsɩŋ arɩ nyiniŋ hɛntɛrɛɛ, Wɩa dɩa-la lee-la zɔmʋŋ sɩ bɩ magɩa kɛnɛ borusuŋ wenjeba, arɩ Wɩa dɩa-la dɩɩ-balɩŋ borusuŋ.

english_verse: After the Lord's temple was finished, Solomon put into its storage rooms everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord, including the gold and the silver.
translation_verse: Solomoŋ sɩ tɩŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la tɩntɩŋŋaa kala dɛrɛ, ʋ paa kɩalɩŋ kala ʋ nyɩmma Devit fa sɩ joŋo pɩ La TƖƖNA a kaa jʋʋ bil La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ, ba dʋa dɩ-biliŋ. Kɩalɩŋ nɛ sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla arɩ kɩaa dɔnsʋŋ.

english_verse: Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
translation_verse: Ka kuoro Solomoŋ arɩ Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ laa daga-la sɩpaaŋ, a kpʋ piesee arɩ nɛsɩŋ a yʋgɛ woruŋ, nʋʋ sɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo dɩɩsɛ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: The poles were so long that they could be seen from right outside the most holy place, but not from anywhere else. And they stayed there from then on.
translation_verse: Daasɩŋ deemba fa duomo nɛ woruŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ jʋʋ Wɩa dɩ-zɔŋ-la lee-la zɔmʋŋ sɩ bɩ magɩa kɛnɛ tʋɔŋ a chɩŋ, ŋ jaŋ wuo naba, ama dɩ ŋ nɛ hɛ ʋ harɩŋ, ŋ bɩ jaŋ wuo naba. Daasɩ-la ha hɛ nɩmɛ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala.

english_verse: The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kʋŋkala fa tuo Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la tʋɔŋ a pɛ tabɩɩ-taala-la balɩa Mosis sɩ joŋo hɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ Sɩnaɩ peel-la lɛ, bʋa-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ hɛ niiŋ ʋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa pɛgɛ, ba sɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ harɩŋ.

english_verse: Now I have built a glorious temple where you can live forever.” Solomon Speaks to the People (
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ mɩ saa ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ a pɩŋ, lee ŋ sɩ jaŋ hɛ a kaa mʋ wuu.”

english_verse: Solomon turned toward the people standing there. Then he blessed them
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa hilime chɩŋ lee-la nɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Solomoŋ bɩrɩma chaasɛba, a sʋl Wɩa pɩba.

english_verse: and said: Praise the Lord God of Israel! Long ago he brought his people out of Egypt. He did not choose a city from any tribe in Israel where his temple would be built, but he kept his promise to make my father David the king of Israel.
translation_verse: ‘A chɩŋ bʋa-la mɩ sɩ kɛŋ mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, mɩ bɩ tabal kala lɩɩsa Iziral doho doho-la tʋɔŋ dɩ ba saa mɩ dɩɩ-balɩŋ dɩ ba zizilmi nɩmɛ, ama Devit nɛ mɩ lɩɩsɛ dɩ ʋ bibeŋ mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa.’

english_verse: So when David wanted to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel,
translation_verse: Mɩ nyɩmma Devit fa kɛŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ nɛ dɩ ʋ saa Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ nɛ dɩ ba chʋchʋɔlɛ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa nɩmɛ.

english_verse: the Lord said, “It's good that you want to build a temple where I can be worshiped.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ mɩ nyɩmma Devit, ‘Ʋ ŋaa wʋzɔŋ nɛ ŋ sɩ kɛŋ ŋ tʋɔŋ dɩ ŋ saa mɩ dɩɩ-balɩŋ pɩmɛ dɩ ba zizilmi nɩmɛ.

english_verse: But you're not the one to do it. Your son will build a temple to honor me.”
translation_verse: Ama ŋ dee nɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ saa mɩ dɩɩ-balɩŋ pɩmɛ. Ama ŋ tɩtɩa bii-lʋlʋŋ nɛ jaŋ saa mɩ dɩɩ-balɩŋ dɩ ba chʋchʋɔlɛmɛ nɩmɛ.’

english_verse: The Lord has done what he promised. I am the king of Israel like my father, and I've built a temple for the Lord our God.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA kɛŋ nii-la ʋ fa sɩ hɛ kaa tɩŋ nɛ. Mɩ laa mɩ nyɩmma Devit nyuŋ a dii kuoruŋ nɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ, a saa Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ ma dɩ ba chʋchʋɔlɛ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa nɩmɛ.

english_verse: I've also made a place in the temple for the sacred chest. And in that chest are the two flat stones on which is written the solemn agreement the Lord made with our ancestors when he led them out of Egypt. Solomon Prays at the Temple (
translation_verse: Mɩ bɩra wuo chɛ leriŋ nɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ dɩ Wɩa niiriŋ daga-la chɩŋ nɩmɛ. Ʋ tʋɔŋ nɛ tabɩɩ-taalɩ-la balɩa lɛ ba sɩ ŋmʋnsɛ niiri-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bile ʋ dɩ la nyɩmmaba pɛgɛ bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩ kɛmba kaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ hɛ.” Solomoŋ sʋl Wɩa hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ

english_verse: Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple,
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋhʋɔra-la ma sɩ bɩ ŋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋŋ ŋaa nɛ nɩɩ ŋ yɩrɩ-balɩŋ wɩaa, ŋ doluŋ wɩaa arɩ wʋduoru-la ŋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa a lɩɩ tinteye-la sɩ bolie a kɔ dɩ ʋ dɛnnɩŋ, a joŋ ʋ sɩaa chaasɛ ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ a sʋlʋŋ,

english_verse: and prayed: Lord God of Israel, no other god in heaven or on earth is like you! You never forget the agreement you made with your people, and you are loyal to anyone who faithfully obeys your teachings.
translation_verse: aŋ chʋɔlɛ Wɩa a bʋl: “Ou, La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa, kʋŋkala tuo wɩa-nyuŋ koo tinteeŋ lɛ a magɩŋ. Ŋ sɩ cho ŋ nɩaa a hɛ nii-la ŋ dɩ ba pɛgɛ, ŋ bɩ ʋ wɩaa yʋa. Ŋ yie chɩŋ ŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ ba tʋɔŋ kala a tuto wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ daga harɩŋ nɛ.

english_verse: My father David was your servant, and today you have kept every promise you made to him.
translation_verse: Ŋ kɛŋ nii-la ŋ sɩ hɛ pɩ mɩ nyɩmma Devit sɩ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ a tɩŋ nɛ. Jɩnɩŋ ŋ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ hɛ niiŋ pʋ arɩ ŋ jaŋ ŋaa nɛ.

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you promised my father that someone from his family would always be king of Israel, if they do their best to obey you, just as he did.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa, ŋ hɛ niiŋ a pɩ mɩ nyɩmma Devit sɩ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ nɛ a bʋl, ‘Nʋʋ jaŋ lɩɩ ŋ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ bʋa na-kala a dii Iziral kuoruŋ, dɩ ba nɛ fɩɛlɛ ba sɩaa a to mɩ niiŋ arɩ ŋ-na Devit sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.’

english_verse: There's not enough room in all of heaven for you, Lord God. How could you possibly live on earth in this temple I have built?
translation_verse: Ama Wɩa, ŋ sɛnɛ jaŋ hɛ dʋnɩa deeŋ lɛɛ? Wɩa-nyuŋ arɩ wɩa-nyuŋ balegi balegi ma paala bɩ jalɩa magɛ ŋ jʋʋnʋŋ. Ɛɛ nɛ saa ŋ jaŋ wuo jʋʋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ mɩ sɩ saa tinteeŋ lɛ?

english_verse: This is the temple where you have chosen to be worshiped. Please watch over it day and night and listen when I turn toward it and pray.
translation_verse: Ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ nɛ ŋaa lee-la ŋ sɩ sɩ ŋ jaŋ lɩɩsɛ dɩ ba dɩdɛnnɩŋ nɩmɛ. Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, bibeŋ ʋ nyuŋ wɩɩhɛyɛ arɩ tɩtaŋɩŋ kala. Dɩ mɩ-na ŋ tɩntɩnna nɛ joŋ mɩ sɩaa chaasʋ aŋ sʋlʋŋ, jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ.

english_verse: I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So whenever any of us look toward this temple and pray, answer from your home in heaven and forgive our sins.
translation_verse: Mɩ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ nɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa ŋ nɩaa. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, bʋa na-kala dɩ la kʋŋ nɛ joŋ sɩaa a chaasɛ ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ a sʋlʋŋ, ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ, jegile nɩɩ a laa la sʋla a joŋ la wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ chɛla.

english_verse: Suppose someone accuses a person of a crime, and the accused has to stand in front of the altar in your temple and say, “I swear I am innocent!”
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ ŋaa wɩɩ a chei ʋ dɔŋɔ, a magɛ dɩ tɩɩna kʋ jʋʋ chɩŋ ŋ koruŋ sɩpaaŋ ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ lɛ a ŋmɩɛsɛ arɩ ʋ bɩ wɩɩ jɩŋ,

english_verse: Listen from heaven and decide who is right. Then punish the guilty person and let the innocent one go free.
translation_verse: ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ, jegile nɩɩ a laa wɩɩ-la jɩŋ. Dɔgɩsɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ laa cheeriŋ, aŋ joŋ nɩɩ-la sɩ bɩ wɩɩ cheye ta.

english_verse: Suppose your people Israel sin against you, and then an enemy defeats them. If they come to this temple and beg for forgiveness,
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ a cheyiŋ dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ yuo diiba, dɩ ba nɛ mɩɩra kɔ ŋ teeŋ a sʋsʋlʋŋ ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ lɛ arɩ ba cheye nɛ,

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven. Forgive them and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
translation_verse: ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ, jegile nɩɩ ba sʋla a joŋo chɛba aŋ mɩɩra kɛmba kɔ tintee-la ŋ sɩ joŋo pɩ ba naabalɩmaba.

english_verse: Suppose your people sin against you, and you punish them by holding back the rain. If they turn toward this temple and pray in your name and stop sinning,
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɩaa nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ cheyiŋ dɩ ŋ dɔgɩsɛba a pɔ dɩ duonuŋ sɩ́ nɩɩ, dɩ ba nɛ joŋ ba sɩaa chaasɛ ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ a yɩrɛ ŋ yɩrɩŋ a sʋlʋŋ arɩ ba cheye nɛ aŋ leŋ wʋbɔmɔ-la,

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And please send rain on the land you gave them to be theirs forever.
translation_verse: ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ, jegile nɩɩ a joŋo chɛba. Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnaa nɛ, ŋɩɩ wɩaa dagɛba dɩ ba ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ, aŋ leŋ dɩ duonuŋ bɩra nɩɩ tintee-la lɛ ŋ sɩ joŋo pɩba ʋ ŋaa ba kʋŋ.

english_verse: Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Dɩ losuŋ nɛ jʋʋ tinteeŋ a tɩŋ kʋduuloo sɩ cheye wɩaa koo hɔbɔ sɩ die koo dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ kʋ gollo chu ba tasɩ-la dɔŋɔ koo nyanyal bɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ jʋa, koo wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ koo nyanyalaa nɛ jʋʋ kpʋkpʋ nɩaa,

english_verse: Listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple.
translation_verse: dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋŋ tʋɔŋ chei a tɩŋ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ ŋaa, dɩ ʋ kɛŋ ʋ nɩsaa je a chaasɛ ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ a sʋlʋŋ,

english_verse: You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to the way they live and what is in their hearts.
translation_verse: ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ, jegile nɩɩ a joŋ ʋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ chɛʋ aŋ pɛ ʋ lɛ. Ŋ jɩŋ nʋʋkala tʋɔbɩɩnaa arɩ ʋ mɛlɛ sɩ nagɛ ŋɩɩ nɛ. Ŋaa ŋɩɩ sɩ maga dɩ ŋ ŋaa nʋʋkala lɛ.

english_verse: Then your people will worship and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ nɩaa jaŋ fɩfáŋ a tuto ŋ wombiee, bʋa-la kala ba sɩ hɛ tintee-la ŋ sɩ joŋo pɩ la naabalɩmaba ʋ ŋaa ba kʋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just like your people Israel, and they will know that I have built this temple to honor you.
translation_verse: ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ, jegile nɩɩ nʋhʋɔrʋ-la sʋla a ŋaa wɩɩ-la kala ʋ sɩɩ chɛ pʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ dʋnɩa nɩaa kala jaŋ jɩmɩŋ a fɩfáŋ arɩ ŋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, aŋ bɩra jɩŋ arɩ mɩ saa ŋ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ a pɩŋ nɛ dɩ ba chʋchʋɔlʋŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Our Lord, sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA, dɩ ŋ nɛ kʋ hɛ ŋ nɩaa dɩ ba mʋ laalɩŋ a yuo ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ, dɩ ba joŋ ba sɩaa chaasɛ tabalɩŋ deeŋ ŋ sɩ lɩɩsa arɩ ŋ dɩɩ-bal-la mɩ sɩ saa dɩ ba chʋchʋɔlʋŋ nɩmɛ a sʋlʋŋ,

english_verse: Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
translation_verse: ŋ hɛ ŋ jaŋ lɛ nɛ, jegile nɩɩ ba sʋla a leŋ dɩ ba yuo dii ba dʋndɔmɔ-la.

english_verse: Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala tuo ʋ bɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ka ŋaa. Ama dɩ ŋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɛ kʋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ, dɩ ŋ baanɩŋ sii ba nyuŋ a leŋ ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ yuo diiba a kɛsɛba kaa mʋ ba tinteeŋ, dɩ lee-la kpaga koo ʋ bolie,

english_verse: Forgive your people no matter how much they have sinned against you. Make the enemies who defeated them be kind to them.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɩaa nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ a cheyiŋ magɛ ŋɩɩ ma kala, joŋo chɛba. Ŋaa dɩ ba dʋndɔmɔ-la sɩ yuo diiba fá ba nenige.

english_verse: Remember, they are the people you chose and rescued from Egypt that was like a blazing fire to them.
translation_verse: Ba ŋaa ŋ nɩaa nɛ. Ba nɛ ŋ laata Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ, lee-la ba fa sɩ hɛ a nɩna hɛɛŋ sɩ nagɛ nyiŋgeliŋ sɩɩ dii.

english_verse: I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So listen when any of us pray and cry out for your help.
translation_verse: Mɩ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ nɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa ŋ nɩaa. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa dɩ la kʋŋkala nɛ sʋlʋŋ a yele pɩŋ a chɩchɛ dɩ ŋ pɛ la lɛ, jegile nɩɩ.

english_verse: When you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, you told your servant Moses to say to them, “From all people on earth, the Lord God has chosen you to be his very own.” Solomon Blesses the People
translation_verse: Ŋ sɩ kɛŋ la naabalɩmaba lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ŋ-na La TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ bʋla pɩ ŋ tɩntɩnna Mosis dɩ ʋ bʋla pɩba arɩ ba nɛ ŋaa nɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ lɩɩsa dʋnɩa nɩaa kala tʋɔŋ dɩ ba ŋaa ŋ nɩaa.”

english_verse: When Solomon finished his prayer at the altar, he was kneeling with his arms lifted toward heaven. He stood up,
translation_verse: Solomoŋ sɩ kpirimi La TƖƖNA koru-la sɩpaaŋ aŋ kɛŋ ʋ nɩsaa je wɩa-nyuŋ a chʋɔlɛ Wɩa dɛrɛ, ʋ sii chɩŋ,

english_verse: Praise the Lord! He has kept his promise and given us peace. Every good thing he promised to his servant Moses has happened.
translation_verse: “Má dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA, ʋ kɛŋ nii-la ʋ sɩ hɛ tɩŋ nɛ a leŋ la hɔŋ arɩ fɩɛlɩŋ. Wʋzɔmɔ-la kala ʋ sɩ bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnna Mosis arɩ ʋ jaŋ ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ʋ ŋaa.

english_verse: The Lord our God was with our ancestors to help them, and I pray that he will be with us and never abandon us.
translation_verse: A leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa hɛ la teeŋ arɩ ʋ fa sɩ hɛ la naabalɩmaba teeŋ ŋɩɩ. Mɩɩ sʋlʋ dɩ ʋ hɛ la ma teeŋ a sɩ́ la vɩa ta.

english_verse: May the Lord help us obey him and follow all the laws and teachings he gave our ancestors.
translation_verse: A leŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA kɛŋ la tʋɔŋ bɩrɩmɛ dɩ la wuo to niiri-la ʋ sɩ bile arɩ ʋ wombiee arɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ dagɛ la naabalɩmaba.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord our God will remember my prayer day and night. May he help everyone in Israel each day, in whatever way we need it.
translation_verse: Mɩɩ sʋl La TƖƖNA Wɩa dɩ ʋ liliisi mɩ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ deeŋ wɩɩhɛyɛ arɩ tɩtaŋɩŋ kala. A leŋ dɩ ʋ pɛ ʋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ ba kuoro lɛ dɩ ba na wɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩɩ chɛ tapʋlɩɩ kala.

english_verse: Then every nation will know that the Lord is the only true God.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ jaŋ leŋ dɩ tinteeŋ nɩaa kala jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA Wɩa dʋndʋŋa nɛ Wɩa, kʋŋ dɔŋ kala bɩra tuo a pɛ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Obey the Lord our God and follow his commands with all your heart, just as you are doing today. Solomon Dedicates the Temple (
translation_verse: Má kɛŋ ma tʋɔŋ kala a to La TƖƖNA Wɩa. Má to ʋ wombiee arɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ daga arɩ ŋɩɩ ma sɩɩ ŋaa jɩnɩŋ.” Solomoŋ joŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ hɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ

english_verse: On that day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and made it acceptable for worship. He offered the sacrifices there because the bronze altar in front of the temple was too small.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa nɛ Solomoŋ joŋ kaala-la sɩ hɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la sɩpaaŋ tʋtʋɔbaanɩŋ a hɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ, aŋ ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, a nyɩgɛ nii-magɛ dɔŋɔ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pʋsʋ-la nʋʋŋ leree. Ʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ bɛɛ wɩaa ba sɩ kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ koru-la sɩ hɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la sɩpaaŋ muuro kɩŋkɛŋ nɛ arɩ ba sɩ jaŋ joŋ Wɩɩ-sʋla kɩalɩŋ kala daŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ.

english_verse: Solomon and the huge crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters at the temple for seven days. There were people from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north.
translation_verse: Solomoŋ arɩ Iziral nɩ-daŋ-la kala chaasa gbieli lɛŋŋɛɛ gbiele-la nɛ. Nɩalɩŋ chaasa yʋgɛ nɛ woruŋ a lɩɩ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lebo Hamaf sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa a kaa mʋ Ijipiti fuonaa luŋii-la sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ kala a kɔ. Ba gbieli gbiele-la tapʋlaa balɩpɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA Wɩa sɩpaaŋ, aŋ bɩra gbieli tapʋlaa balɩpɛ pɛ. Tapʋlɩa-la kala ŋaa fii arɩ banɛsɛ.

english_verse: Then on the eighth day, he sent everyone home. They said goodbye and left, very happy, because of all the good things the Lord had done for his servant David and his people Israel.
translation_verse: Taŋ sɩ pʋla, kuoro Solomoŋ ta nɩalɩŋ kala ba mʋ dɩɩsɩŋ. Ba kala lɔllʋ aŋ mʋ dɩɩsɩŋ arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ a tɩŋ wʋzɔmɔ-la kala La TƖƖNA sɩ ŋaa pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnna Devit arɩ ʋ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: I will no longer let my people Israel live in this land I gave them. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped. Then people everywhere will think this nation is only a joke and will make fun of it.
translation_verse: ŋɩɩ-na, mɩ jaŋ kiri ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa ta tintee-la mɩ sɩ joŋo pɩma lɛ, aŋ vɩa mɩ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ mɩ sɩ lɩɩsa ʋ ŋaa mɩ kʋŋ dɩ ba dɩdɛnnɛmɛ nɩmɛ ta. Dɩ ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋaa, ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala jaŋ mɩɩra ŋaa nɩtɔɔnɩ dɩ nɩaa kala mʋmɔmma.

english_verse: Solomon did not force the Israelites to do his work. They were his soldiers, officials, leaders, commanders, chariot captains, and chariot drivers. But he did make slaves of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were living in Israel. These were the descendants of those foreigners the Israelites could not destroy, and they remained Israel's slaves.
translation_verse: Ama Solomoŋ fa bɩ leŋe Iziral tɩɩna kala ŋaa yomo. Ba nɛ fa ŋaa ʋ laalɩyuoroo, arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ, arɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ ʋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ torukoba-la vɩvɛŋ.

english_verse: The Lord said: I heard your prayer and what you asked me to do. This temple you have built is where I will be worshiped forever. It belongs to me, and I will never stop watching over it.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pʋ, “Mɩ nɩɩ ŋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ nɛ. Mɩ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ ŋ sɩ saa dɩ ba dɩdɛnnɛmɛ nɩmɛ, ŋaa mɩ kʋa nɛ, mɩ sɩaa arɩ mɩ tʋɔŋ kala jaŋ hɛ ʋ lɛ bʋa na-kala.

english_verse: You must obey me, as your father David did, and be honest and fair. Obey my laws and teachings,
translation_verse: Ŋ-na Solomoŋ, dɩ ŋ nɛ tomi arɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ, arɩ ŋɩɩ ŋ nyɩmma Devit fa sɩ tomi, a ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ daga, a to mɩ niiriŋ arɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile,

english_verse: But if you or any of your descendants disobey my commands or start worshiping foreign gods,
translation_verse: Ama dɩ ŋ-na, koo dɩ ŋ doho nɩaa kʋŋ nɛ vɩamɛ a bɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ daga arɩ mɩ niiriŋ ka to, aŋ mɩɩra mʋ tuto vesiŋ a kpʋkpaarɛba,

english_verse: Then they will answer, “We know why the Lord did this. The people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.” Other Things Solomon Did (
translation_verse: Nɩaa jaŋ bʋla pɩba, ‘Ba vɩa dɩ ba to ba TƖƖNA, ba nyɩmmaba Wɩa sɩ kɛmba kaa kʋ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ, aŋ mɩɩra tuto vesiŋ a kpʋkpaarɛba, ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ ʋ joŋ wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ deemba kala ŋaa ba lɛ.’ ” Solomoŋ tɩntɩŋŋaa dɔnsʋŋ

english_verse: Baalath, and Tamar in the desert of Judah.
translation_verse: arɩ Baalaf, arɩ Tama ma sɩ hɛ Juda tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ,

english_verse: When Hiram went to see the towns, he did not like them.
translation_verse: Ama Hɩram fa sɩ sii lɩɩ Taaya a mʋ na tasɩ-la Solomoŋ sɩ joŋo pʋ, ʋ tʋɔŋ fa bɩ ba nyuŋ tɔrɔ.

english_verse: He said, “Solomon, my friend, are these the kind of towns you want to give me?” So Hiram called the region Cabul because he thought it was worthless.
translation_verse: Ʋ pɩɛsɛ, “Bɛɛ kɩaa tasɩŋ nɛ ŋ-la ŋ joŋo pɩmɛ, mɩ naambii?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ hɛ tasɩ-la yɩrɩŋ Kabʋl. Tasɩ-la yɩrɩŋ nɛ ha ŋɩɩ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala.

english_verse: After Solomon's workers had finished the temple and the palace, he ordered them to fill in the land on the east side of Jerusalem, to build a wall around the city, and to rebuild the towns of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
translation_verse: Kuoro Solomoŋ sɩ fʋgɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa hɛ ba saa La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la arɩ ʋ kuoru dɩa dɛrɛ, ʋ leŋ ba chʋŋ hagɩla a dɩŋ Jerusalɛm wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ, aŋ saa kɛrɛ a golli taŋ-la, a wasa saa tasɩŋ deemba ma: Hazɔ, Mɛgɩdɔ arɩ Gɛza.

english_verse: Earlier, the king of Egypt had captured the town of Gezer; he burned it to the ground and killed the Canaanite people living there. Then he gave it to his daughter as a wedding present when she married Solomon.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro fa yuo dii Gɛza nɛ, a joŋ nyiniŋ hɛ ʋ dii. Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa nɛ fa hɔŋ nɩmɛ. Ʋ kpʋ ba kala aŋ joŋ taŋ-la dii zile pɩ ʋ tolo-la sɩ jaa Solomoŋ.

english_verse: So Solomon had the town rebuilt. Solomon ordered his workers to rebuild Lower Beth-Horon,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Solomoŋ wasa saa Gɛza. Ʋ fa wasa saa Bɛf Horoŋ sɛmɛ-la ma sɩ hɛ bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ,

english_verse: They also built towns where he could keep his supplies and his chariots and horses. Solomon ordered them to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere in his kingdom.
translation_verse: a pɛ tasɩ-la kala lɛ ʋ sɩ saa ʋ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩ-bilee arɩ tabala-la lɛ ʋ janɩŋ arɩ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba sɩɩ chɩŋ. Ʋ saa dɩa na-kala ʋ sɩ cho nɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ arɩ Lɛbanɔŋ tinteeŋ lɛ arɩ lere-la kala ʋ sɩɩ beŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the older part of Jerusalem to her new palace. Then Solomon had the land on the east side of Jerusalem filled in.
translation_verse: Solomoŋ haala Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro tolo-la sɩ lɩɩ Devit tabal-la lɛ a kɔ kuoru dɩa-la Solomoŋ sɩ saa pʋ, Solomoŋ bɩra leŋ ba chʋŋ hagɩla a dɩŋ tabal-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ.

english_verse: Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built. Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Jɩna tʋɔŋ, naansɩɩŋ butori nɛ Solomoŋ yie kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ nii-magɛ dɔŋɔ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ koru-la ʋ sɩ saa nyuŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA. Ʋ lɛɛlɛ saa Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la dɛrɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Kuoro Solomoŋ fa bɩra kpaasɛ lɩɩŋ daborusuŋ ma nɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛzɩɔŋ Geba lɛ, a kpagɛ Ɛlaf sɩ hɛ Ɛdɔm tinteeŋ, Mʋgʋ-fɩaŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: King Hiram let some of his experienced sailors go to the country of Ophir with Solomon's own sailors, and they brought back about
translation_verse: Ba duoro mʋ tintee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ofi a kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ yuŋuŋ sɩ yi kilo bʋɩ fii arɩ banɛsɛ a kaa mɩɩra kʋ pɩ kuoro Solomoŋ.

english_verse: He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
translation_verse: Solomoŋ ma chaarɛ wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ pɩɛsa sɩaa. Wɩalɩŋ kʋŋkala fa bɩ wʋhaa ŋaa Solomoŋ teeŋ.

english_verse: The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: kʋdiile-la ʋ sɩɩ dii, dɩɩsɩ-la ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ sɩɩ jʋʋ, arɩ gɛnnɩ-la ʋ tɩntɩnnaa sɩɩ laalʋ, nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ kori ʋ nyʋnyʋalʋsʋŋ, arɩ kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlɩɩ-la Solomoŋ sɩ sʋla La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ, ʋ sɩaa biri.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Ʋ bʋla pɩ kuoro Solomoŋ, “Mɩ sɩ hɛ mɩ tinteeŋ lɛ aŋ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa arɩ wʋjɩmɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ, sɛnɛ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ nɛ.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told.
translation_verse: Ama mɩ fa bɩ laa dii, see mɩ tɩtɩa sɩɩŋ sɩ na ŋ-la. Mɩ paala bɩ ŋ wɩaa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ ma nɩa. Ŋ wʋjɩmɩŋ arɩ ŋ dʋa yʋga kɩɩ ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ nɩa nɛ.

english_verse: Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: Ŋ nɩaa ŋaa nyu-sɩŋ tɩmma nɛ. Ŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ ŋ sɩpaaŋ bʋa na-kala ŋaa tʋɔtɔrɛ tɩmma nɛ, ba sɩ jaŋ nɩnɩɩ ŋ wʋjɩmɩɩ-la.

english_verse: The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, many jewels, and more spices than anyone had ever brought into Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ haal-la sɩ ŋaa Sɩɩba kuoro joŋ sɛlɩmɛ yuŋuŋ sɩ kɩɩ kilo bʋɩ banɛsɛ a pɩ Solomoŋ, arɩ tegisiŋ sʋɔra sɩ sɩma a yʋgɛ woruŋ arɩ tabɩɩ-tʋlaa. Nʋʋkala ha bɩ tegisi-la doho kaa kʋ pɩ kuoro Solomoŋ a magɛ kɩalɩŋ Sɩɩba kuoro sɩ joŋo pʋ.

english_verse: He was the richest and wisest king in the world.
translation_verse: Kuoro Solomoŋ nɛ fa kɛŋ kɩaa arɩ wʋjɩmɩŋ a kɩɩ kuoru kala sɩ hɛ tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The merchants and traders, as well as the kings of Arabia and rulers from Israel, also gave him gold.
translation_verse: Lampoo-la bayalaa sɩ yie tiŋ arɩ Arebia kuoroo kala sɩ yie tiŋ kɩalɩŋ arɩ Iziral tinteeŋ nɩhɩasɩŋ sɩ yie joŋ kɩalɩŋ pʋ na bɩ pɛ.

english_verse: His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro leŋ ba kɛŋ batu-nyɩlɩŋ ŋaa kuoru kpasɩ-bal, aŋ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ sɩ chaasa zɔŋ taara tɔ.

english_verse: The back of the throne was rounded at the top, and it had armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on both sides of the throne, and there was a statue of a lion at both ends of each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
translation_verse: Lusuŋ-chol sɩa-la balɩdʋ lɛ, kɩaa sɩ nagɛ naachigee fii arɩ balɩa chɩŋ ba sɛsɩŋ. Lusuŋ-chol sɩɩ kala niipiniŋ lɛ, balɩa hɛ nɩmɛ, dɔŋɔ chɩŋ nadiiŋ, dɔŋɔ ma chɩŋ nagʋa. Ba ha bɩ kuoru kpasa deeŋ doho ŋaa tintee dɔŋ kala lɛ.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Kuoro fa kɛŋ lɩɩŋ daborusuŋ ma nɛ. Ba dɩ Hiram lɩɩŋ daborusuŋ yie duori lɩɩŋ a mʋmʋ bayalɩŋ. Jɩsɩŋ batori na-kala ba yie mɩɩra kɔ bala nɛ, a chʋŋ sɛlɩmɛ, hɔpʋla, batu-nyɩlaa, ŋmaŋŋaa arɩ fɔsʋŋ.

english_verse: People from every nation wanted to hear the wisdom God had given him.
translation_verse: Dʋnɩa nɩaa kala fa cho dɩ ba kʋ jegile nɩɩ Solomoŋ wʋjɩmɩɩ-la Wɩa sɩ joŋo pʋ nɛ.

english_verse: Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
translation_verse: Jɩna kala, nʋʋ na-kala sɩ kɔ dɩ ʋ na Solomoŋ yie kɛŋ kɩaa nɛ kʋ dii zile pʋ: hɔpʋla kɩaa, sɛlɩmɛ kɩaa, gɛnnɩŋ, laalɩyuori kɩaa arɩ tegisiŋ, janɩŋ arɩ kakusuŋ.

english_verse: While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Solomoŋ sɩ dii kuoruŋ, hɔpʋla fa pʋrɩga nɛ woruŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ a nagɛ tabɩaa, kuolu daasɩŋ ma pʋrɩgɛ woruŋ a nagɛ tutogusuŋ sɩ hɛ Juda tinteeŋ dundollu-la sɩ hɛ peelee bʋbʋɔŋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Ʋ mɩɩra kpʋkpaarɛ Sɩdɔŋ tɩŋŋaa veŋ-haal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩtɔrɛf arɩ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa veŋ-bɔŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɔlɛk nɛ.

english_verse: Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Solomoŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, ʋ bɩ La TƖƖNA to arɩ ʋ tʋɔŋ kala arɩ ʋ nyɩmma Devit fa sɩ to ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Jerusalɛm wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dundolo kʋbala nyuŋ, Solomoŋ ŋaa wʋkɩsɩɩ a saa vʋɩyaa dɩ-kpaarɩŋ, a kpʋkpaarɛ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Chɛmɔs arɩ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa veŋ-bɔŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɔlɛk.

english_verse: In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa nɛ ʋ ŋaa a pɩ ʋ ha-nʋhʋɔra-la ma ʋ sɩ jaa, ba kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a kpʋkpaarɛ ba vesiŋ a nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ pɩpɩba.

english_verse: and he said to Solomon: You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Solomoŋ, “Ŋ mɛlɛ sɩ folo nagɛ ŋ-la, ŋ bɩ nii-la mɩ sɩ bile arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ dagɩŋ to, mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ ŋ kuoruŋ laa a joŋo pɩ ŋ tɩntɩnnaa dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him.
translation_verse: Ama, a tɩŋ ŋ nyɩmma Devit wɩaa, mɩ bɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ dɩ ŋ ha hɛ ŋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ŋ nanʋala nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la.

english_verse: When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city. Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Mɩ bɩ jaŋ laa kuorii-la kala ʋ teeŋ, ama mɩ jaŋ leŋ doho bala pʋ dɩ ʋ bibeŋ, a tɩŋ mɩ tɩntɩnna Devit arɩ Jerusalɛm mɩ sɩ lɩɩsa wɩaa.” Solomoŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ

english_verse: Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA leŋ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa kuoru bii kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Hadad bɩrɩmɛ Solomoŋ dʋndɔŋ a chɩŋ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Some time earlier, when David conquered the nation of Edom, Joab his army commander went there to bury those who had died in battle. Joab and his soldiers stayed in Edom six months, and during that time they killed every man and boy who lived there.
translation_verse: Jʋab arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa laalɩyuoroo kala fa hɔŋ Ɛdɔm lɛ chɛnsɩŋ balɩdʋ nɛ a kpʋ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa baalaa kala, nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ hambiisiŋ kala.

english_verse: Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
translation_verse: Tapɛnɛs ŋaaŋ-la arɩ Hadad lʋl hambolibie a hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Genubaf. Tapɛnɛs kɛŋ bile mʋ kuoro dɩa a dɩɛsʋ. Genubaf arɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro biiriŋ kala fa hɛ dɩ-bala nɛ.

english_verse: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
translation_verse: Hadad fa sɩ hɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ nɩɩ arɩ Devit sʋba, ʋ laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ Jʋab ma sʋʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hadad bʋla pɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro, “Leŋ dɩ mɩ mɩɩra mʋ mɩ tinteeŋ.”

english_verse: “Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?” “No, I just want to go home.” Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ ŋ chɛ ka daha a chɩchɛ dɩ ŋ mɩɩra mʋ ŋ tinteeŋ?” Hadad bʋl, “Kʋŋkala dee, ama leŋ dɩ mɩ mʋ.”

english_verse: Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon: Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Wɩa bɩra leŋ Ɛlɩada nanʋala Rɛzɔŋ ŋaa Solomoŋ dʋndɔŋ. Rɛzɔŋ fa lɩɩ fá nɛ ʋ nɩhɩaŋ Hadadɛza sɩ ŋaa Zɔba kuoro teeŋ.

english_verse: Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon.
translation_verse: Nɛbat nanʋala Jerobuam ma bɩra vɩa kuoro Solomoŋ niiŋ. Ʋ fa ŋaa Solomoŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ dɔŋɔ nɛ, a ŋaa Efirem tɩɩna a lɩɩ Zɛrɛda. Ʋ naaŋ yɩrɩŋ nɛ Zɛrʋa, ʋ fa ŋaa yo-haal nɛ.

english_verse: Here is how it happened: While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls,
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la sɩ tɩɩ ʋ vɩa kuoro niiŋ nɛ ŋ-la: Solomoŋ fa leŋe ba chʋŋ hagɩla nɛ a dɩŋ buotuonuŋ Jerusalɛm wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ aŋ wasa sɩsaa kɛrɛ-la sɩ golli taŋ-la.

english_verse: Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Jerobuam fa ŋaa bapʋɔsɩɩ a chaasa tɩtɩŋ woruŋ. Solomoŋ sɩ na dɩ ʋ faasa tɩtɩŋ ŋɩɩ, ʋ leŋ ʋ nɛ ŋaa Manasɛ arɩ Efirem doho nɩalɩŋ ba sɩ fʋga hɛ ba tɩtɩŋ tɩntɩmɩa-la nɩhɩaŋ.

english_verse: But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
translation_verse: Ama a tɩŋ mɩ tɩntɩnna Devit arɩ Jerusalɛm wɩaa, taŋ-la mɩ sɩ lɩɩsa Iziral doho doho kala tʋɔŋ, ʋ jaŋ bibeŋ doho bala.

english_verse: “Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa Solomoŋ arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa vɩamɛ nɛ aŋ kpʋkpaarɛ Sɩdɔŋ tɩŋŋaa vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩtɔrɛf, arɩ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa vene Chɛmɔs, arɩ Amɔŋ tɩŋŋaa vene Mɔlɛk. Solomoŋ bɩ mɩ wombiee to, a bɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩɩ chɛ ŋaa arɩ ʋ nyɩmma Devit sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: “Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies.
translation_verse: Ama mɩ bɩ jaŋ kɛŋ kuorii-la kala laa Solomoŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Mɩ leŋe ʋ dii kuoruŋ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ nɛ, a tɩŋ mɩ tɩntɩnna Devit mɩ sɩ lɩɩsa ʋ to mɩ wombiee arɩ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ daga wɩaa.

english_verse: Then I will give you ten tribes to rule,
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ laa kuorii-la ʋ nanʋala nɩsɩŋ lɛ a joŋ doho doho fii-la pɩŋ dɩ ŋ bibeŋ.

english_verse: but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ joŋ doho bala pɩ ʋ nanʋala dɩ ʋ bibeŋ, dɩ mɩ tɩntɩnna Devit doho nɩaa ha wuo didii kuoruŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ, taŋ-la mɩ sɩ lɩɩsa dɩ ba dɩdɛnnɛmɛ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: “You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want.
translation_verse: Ama ŋ-na, ŋ jaŋ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, a bibeŋ lere-la kala ŋ sɩ cho.

english_verse: I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ dagɩŋ, a to mɩ wombiee a ŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ mɩ sɩpaaŋ a kɛŋ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ daga a kaa tɩtɩŋ arɩ mɩ tɩntɩnna Devit fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, mɩ jaŋ hɛ ŋ teeŋ bʋa na-kala. Mɩ jaŋ leŋ ŋ dɩ ŋ doho nɩaa didii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ bʋa na-kala, arɩ mɩ sɩ leŋe Devit doho nɩaa didii kuoruŋ ŋɩɩ. Iziral tinteeŋ kala jaŋ hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Solomoŋ sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, arɩ wʋjɩmɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ kɛnɛ kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ ʋ wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi Jerusalɛm lɛ, Devit tabal-la, ka ʋ nanʋala Rihobuam dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_verse: His younger advisors said: Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bapʋɔsɩa-la bʋl, “Bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋmɛŋ ŋ teeŋ arɩ ŋ nenii-bie nɛ paala barɩma kɩɩ ŋ nyɩmma tɩŋa.

english_verse: But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba tɩma yɩrɛ Jerobuam, ʋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala to dɔŋɔ a mʋ Rihobuam leriŋ a bʋla pʋ:

english_verse: “Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Rihobuam bʋla pɩba, “Má mʋ aŋ mɩɩra kɔ tapʋl tori chɛɛŋ.” Nɩalɩŋ mɩɩra viiri.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Rihobuam pɩɛsɛ nɩhɩasɩ-la fa sɩ tɩma pɩ ʋ nyɩmma Solomoŋ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ bʋa lɛ, “Wʋbɛɛ nɛ ma jaŋ dagɛmɛ dɩ mɩ bʋla pɩ nɩaa deemba?”

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Nɩhɩasɩ-la sɩ, “Dɩ ŋ nɩɩ chɛ dɩ nɩaa deemba toŋ a tɩma pɩpɩŋ, kɛŋ zile ba teeŋ a ŋaa wɩɩ-la ba sɩɩ chɛ pɩba jɩnɩŋ.”

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Rihobuam vɩa wɩɩ-la nɩhɩasɩ-la sɩ dagʋ, aŋ mɩɩra mʋ pɩɛsɛ bapʋɔsɩa-la sɩ ŋaa ʋ wielee aŋ lɛɛlɛ tɩma pʋpʋ.

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: Ʋ pɩɛsɛba, “Wʋbɛɛ nɛ ma ma kɛŋ dɩ ma bʋl? Wʋbɛɛ nɛ la jaŋ bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ sɩ mɩ lɩɩsɛba tɩntɩŋ-duoru-la lɛ mɩ nyɩmma sɩ jomba hɛ?”

english_verse: Three days later, Jeroboam and the others came back.
translation_verse: Tapʋlaa batori harɩŋ, Jerobuam arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala mɩɩra kɔ Rihobuam teeŋ, arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ bʋla.

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors.
translation_verse: Rihobuam vɩa wɩɩ-la nɩhɩasɩ-la sɩ dagʋ, aŋ bʋl wɩaa kpɩa nɩalɩŋ lɛ arɩ baanɩŋ,

english_verse: He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: aŋ to wɩɩ-la ʋ bapʋɔsɩa-la sɩ dagʋ a bʋl, “Mɩ nyɩmma leŋe ma tɩŋ tɩntɩŋ-duoruŋ nɛ, ama mɩ-na jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma wasa tɩŋ tɩntɩŋ-duoruŋ a kɩɩ ŋɩɩ. Mɩ nyɩmma vɩɩrɛma arɩ kpaasa nɛ, ama mɩ-na jaŋ joŋ hɔɔnʋŋ a hɛ kpaasɩ-bie-la niiriŋ lɛ a kaa vɩɩrɛma.”

english_verse: When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family. Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam (
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ nɩa arɩ Jerobuam mɩɩra kɔ nɛ, ba tɩma yɩrʋ ʋ kɔ ba hilimi a bilu kuoruŋ ʋ bibeŋ Iziral tinteeŋ. Juda doho nɩaa dʋndʋŋa nɛ fa haa to Devit doho nɩaa.

english_verse: After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and take control of the whole country. So he called together
translation_verse: Rihobuam sɩ mɩɩra kɔ Jerusalɛm, ʋ yɩrɛ Juda arɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa laalɩyuoroo bʋɩ zɔlɔ arɩ mahɩŋ banɛsɛ hɛ dɔŋɔ, dɩ ba mʋ yuo Iziral tɩmma-la dɔnsʋŋ a laa kuorii-la pɩ Solomoŋ nanʋala Rihobuam.

english_verse: Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Ama Wɩa fa bʋla pɩ Sɛmaaya sɩ ŋaa Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ,

english_verse: to give Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin this warning:
translation_verse: “Bʋla pɩ Solomoŋ nanʋala Rihobuam sɩ ŋaa Juda kuoro a pɛ Juda arɩ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩaa arɩ nɩkaana-la kala lɛ,

english_verse: “Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home. Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
translation_verse: arɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ: ‘Ma pʋpɔ má sɩ́ ma naambiiriŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo. Má mʋ ma dɩɩsɩŋ, mɩ nɛ leŋe wɩɩŋ deeŋ ŋaa.’ ” Ba sɛɩ La TƖƖNA niiŋ a mɩɩra mʋ dɩa. Ba kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ libi nɛ-biisiŋ balɩa bil Bɛtɛl arɩ Daŋ tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jerobuam saa kɛrɛ a golli taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɛkɛm sɩ hɛ Efirem tintee-la peelee sɩ yʋga lɛ a hɔŋ nɩmɛ. Ʋ bɩra lɩɩ nɩmɛ a mʋ saa kɛrɛ a golli taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Pɛnɩɛl ma.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩaa deemba nɛ mʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, ba jaŋ mɩɩra kʋ to ba nɩhɩaŋ Rihobuam sɩ ŋaa Juda kuoro. Ba jaŋ kpʋmɛ aŋ tutou.”

english_verse: Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jerobuam pɩɛsɛ nɩaa ba dagʋ wɩaa. Ʋ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ libi kɩaa balɩa sɩ nagɛ nɛ-bel-biisiŋ, aŋ bʋla pɩ ʋ nɩaa, “Ma jaŋ walɩmɛ ma tɩtɩa, ma sɩ jaŋ mʋ Jerusalɛm a dɩdɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA. Iziral tɩmma, má na vesi-la sɩ laama ta Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a kɛmma kaa kʋ lɩɩ nɛ ŋ-la.”

english_verse: Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan.
translation_verse: Ʋ joŋ dɔŋɔ a bil taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛtɛl lɛ aŋ joŋ dɔŋɔ ma a bil Daŋ tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma-la yie mʋ Bɛtɛl arɩ Daŋ a kpʋkpaarɛ vesi-la, ʋ ŋɩɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ.

english_verse: Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Jerobuam ha bɩra saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa nɛ a lɩɩsɛ nɩaa sɩ bɩ Levi doho nɩaa ŋaa ba kpʋkpaarɛ vesi-la.

english_verse: He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_verse: Chɛŋ chori tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɔŋ-la ʋ sɩ lɩɩsa pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ, ʋ ma tɩtɩa yie mʋ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ nɛ koru-la ʋ sɩ saa Bɛtɛl lɛ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ a gbieli gbiele-la.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted: The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
translation_verse: Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la ŋmoo niiŋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla a tɩgɛ koru-la lɛ: “Koruŋ, wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Ba jaŋ lʋl hambolibie Devit doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ a hɛ ʋ yɩrɩŋ Josaaya. Ʋ jaŋ kpʋ nɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ lɩɩsa ba kpʋkpaarɩŋ a ŋɩŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ ŋ nyuŋ, aŋ nyɩgɛ nuhuobiine haŋgbelee ŋ nyuŋ.’ ”

english_verse: You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la bɩra bʋl: “Koruŋ deeŋ jaŋ yɛrɛ, dɩ tʋɔrʋ-la sɩ hɛ ʋ lɛ bɩsa jaasɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ La TƖƖNA nɛ to mɩ lɛ a bʋl wɩaa deemba.”

english_verse: The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
translation_verse: Koru-la ma yɛrɛ, ʋ tʋɔrʋŋ bɩsa jaasɛ arɩ ŋɩɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ bʋla La TƖƖNA yɩrɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: “Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged. The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bʋla pɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, sʋl ŋ Tɩɩna Wɩa pɩmɛ dɩ ʋ leŋ dɩ mɩ nɩsɩ-la fɩɛlɛ.” Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sʋl La TƖƖNA pʋ, ʋ leŋ kuoro nɩsɩŋ fɩɛlɛ a nagɛ ŋɩɩ ʋ fa sɩ naga.

english_verse: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Kuoro Jerobuam bɩra bʋla pɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la, “Kɔ dɩ la mʋ mɩ dɩa a dii kɩaa, ka dɩ mɩ joŋ kʋŋ a dii zile ŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: “No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either.
translation_verse: Ama Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la bʋla pɩ kuoro, “Dɩ ŋ nɛ jaŋ paala joŋ kɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ ma pɩmɛ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ to ŋ harɩŋ mʋ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ dii kʋŋ koo a nyʋa kʋŋ daha,

english_verse: The Lord said I can't eat or drink anything and that I can't go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: bɛɛ wɩaa La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩmɛ nɛ: ‘Ŋ bɩ maga dɩ ŋ dii kʋŋ koo a nyʋa lɩɩŋ koo a bɩra to wombii-la ŋ sɩ to kɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then he started home down a different road. An Old Prophet from Bethel
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ mɩɩra joŋ wombii dɔŋ, aŋ vɩa wombii-la ʋ sɩ to kɔ Bɛtɛl.

english_verse: At that time an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons told him what the prophet from Judah had said and done.
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ, dɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-hɩaŋ kʋbala hɛ Bɛtɛl lɛ. Ʋ hambolibiisiŋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ ŋaa tapʋlɩɩ-la a pʋ. Ba bɩra bʋla pɩ ba nyɩmma wɩalɩŋ kala baal-la sɩ bʋla pɩ kuoru-la.

english_verse: “Show me which way he went,” the old prophet said, and his sons pointed out the road.
translation_verse: Ba nyɩmma pɩɛsɛba, “Wombii bɛɛ nɛ ʋ to viiri?” Ʋ hambolibiisi-la dagʋ wombii-la Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ lɩɩ Juda sɩ joŋo viiri.

english_verse: “Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩ ʋ hambolibiisi-la, “Má kpɩɛrɛ kakumo pɩmɛ.” Ba sɩ kpɩɛrɛ kakumo-la pʋ, ʋ jɩl a

english_verse: and rode off to look for the prophet from Judah. The old prophet found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the prophet from Judah?” “Yes, I am.”
translation_verse: kiri Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la harɩŋ. Ʋ mʋ naʋ dɩ ʋ hɔŋ piiŋ tɩa kʋbala sɩ kɛŋ fɩɛlɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ. Ʋ pɩɛsʋ, “Ŋ nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ lɩɩ Juda kɔɔ?” Baal-la bʋl, “Mɩ nɛ.”

english_verse: “Come home with me,” the old prophet said, “and have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-hɩaŋ-la bʋla pʋ, “Kɔ dɩ la mʋ mɩ dɩa dɩ ŋ dii kɩaa.”

english_verse: “I can't go back with you,” the prophet replied, “and I can't eat or drink anything with you.
translation_verse: Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ, “Mɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo mɩɩra to ŋ harɩŋ mʋ. Mɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo dii kʋŋ koo a nyʋa kʋŋ daha.

english_verse: The Lord warned me not to eat or drink or to go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩmɛ nɛ arɩ ʋ bɩ maga dɩ mɩ dii kʋŋ koo a nyʋa kʋŋ koo a bɩra to wombii-la mɩ sɩ to kɔ.”

english_verse: The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. One of the Lord's angels told me to take you to my house and give you something to eat and drink.” The prophet from Judah did not know that the old prophet was lying,
translation_verse: Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-hɩaŋ-la sɩ, “Mɩ ma ŋaa Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ nɛ. Wɩa tɩndaara bʋla pɩmɛ nɛ arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ, ‘Kɛnʋ mɩɩra mʋ ŋ dɩa dɩ ʋ dii kɩaa aŋ nyʋa lɩɩŋ.’ ” Ama baal-la faa nyɩɛ nɛ.

english_verse: so he went home with him and ate and drank.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la mɩɩra to ʋ harɩŋ ba mʋ ʋ dɩa, ʋ dii kɩaa aŋ nyʋa lɩɩŋ ma.

english_verse: During the meal the Lord gave the old prophet
translation_verse: Ba sɩ hɔnɔ didii kɩaa ŋɩɩ, La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa a pɩ ʋ wʋlaabʋllʋ-hɩaŋ-la sɩ kɛnʋ mɩɩra kɔ.

english_verse: a message for the prophet from Judah: Listen to the Lord's message. You have disobeyed the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋmoo niiŋ a bʋla pɩ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ lɩɩ Juda kɔ, “La TƖƖNA sɩ ŋ vɩa ʋ niiŋ nɛ a bɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ dagɩŋ to.

english_verse: He told you not to eat or drink anything here, but you came home and ate with me. And so, when you die, your body won't be buried in your family tomb.
translation_verse: Ʋ fa sɩ ŋ sɩ́ kɩaa dii nɛ daha, ka ŋ vɩa aŋ mɩɩra to mɩ harɩŋ kʋ dii kɩaa a nyʋa lɩɩŋ daha. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa ba bɩ jaŋ hugi ŋ kʋsʋʋŋ ŋ nyɩmmaba dɩ-huguŋ.”

english_verse: After the meal the old prophet got a donkey ready,
translation_verse: Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ dii kɩalɩŋ aŋ nyʋa lɩɩŋ dɛrɛ, Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-hɩaŋ-la sɩ kɛnʋ mɩɩra kɔ, sii kpɩɛrɛ kakumo pʋ.

english_verse: and the prophet from Judah left. Along the way, a lion attacked and killed him, and the donkey and the lion stood there beside his dead body.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ jɩl kakumo-la a mʋmʋ, naachigiŋ kʋ chemu a kpʋʋ. Ʋ kʋsʋʋŋ pɩŋ wombiiŋ lɛ, ka kakumo-la arɩ naachigi-la chɩŋ ʋ sɛmɛ.

english_verse: Some people walked by and saw the body with the lion standing there. They ran into Bethel, telling everyone what they had seen.
translation_verse: Nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ sɩ to lee-la bɩbal, ba na ʋ kʋsʋʋŋ dɩ ʋ pɩna, ka naachigi-la ma chɩŋ ʋ sɛmɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba mʋ Bɛtɛl lee-la Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-hɩaŋ-la sɩ hɛ a bʋl wɩɩ-la ba sɩ na a pɩ nɩaa.

english_verse: When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
translation_verse: Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-hɩaŋ-la sɩ kɛŋ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la wombiiŋ lɛ mɩɩra kɔ sɩ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la, ʋ bʋl, “Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la sɩ lɩɩ Juda vɩa La TƖƖNA niiŋ nɛ. La TƖƖNA nɛ joŋu hɛ naachigiŋ lɛ ʋ kpʋʋ. La TƖƖNA fa kpʋrɩsɛ ʋ dɩgɩlaa nɛ ka ʋ bɩ nɩa.”

english_verse: The old prophet told his sons to saddle his donkey, and when it was ready,
translation_verse: Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ hɩaŋ-la bʋla pɩ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ, “Má kpɩɛrɛ kakumo pɩmɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kpɩɛra pʋ.

english_verse: he left. He found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and lion standing there. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Ʋ jɩla mʋ na ʋ kʋsʋʋŋ dɩ ʋ pɩŋ wombiiŋ lɛ, ka kakumo arɩ naachigiŋ chɩŋ ʋ sɛmɛ. Naachigi-la bɩ ʋ chaŋa, ʋ bɩ kakumo-la ma kpʋa.

english_verse: The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ hɩaŋ-la joŋ baal-la kʋsʋʋŋ, a daŋ ʋ kakumo nyuŋ, a kɛnʋ mɩɩra kɔ Bɛtɛl a yel ʋ yoho aŋ joŋo hugi.

english_verse: He buried the body in his own family tomb and cried for the prophet.
translation_verse: Ʋ joŋu hugi ʋ tɩtɩa bʋa lɛ, aŋ yel a bʋl, “Mɩ naambii ba.”

english_verse: He said to his sons, “When I die, bury my body next to this prophet.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ hugu dɛrɛ, ʋ bʋla pɩ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ, “Dɩ mɩ nɛ sʋba, má hugimi bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩ hugi Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la, dɩ la pɛ bʋa bala.

english_verse: I'm sure that everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the shrines in Samaria will happen.”
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ to ʋ lɛ a bʋl a tɩgɛ koru-la sɩ hɛ Bɛtɛl arɩ veŋ-kpaarɛ lere-la kala sɩ hɛ Samarɩa tasɩ-la lɛ, sɛnɛ jaŋ kʋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ.”

english_verse: But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one.
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba harɩŋ lɛ, Jerobuam ha bɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ leŋe, aŋ ha lɩɩsɛ nʋʋ na-kala yee ba kpʋkpaarɛ vesi-la ʋ sɩ saa. Nʋʋkala sɩ cho dɩ ʋ ŋaa veŋ-kpaarʋ, ʋ yie kɛnʋ hɛ nɛ.

english_verse: This sinful thing led to the downfall of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ deemba nɛ Jerobuam ŋaa, ʋ kuoruŋ arɩ ʋ doho nɩaa kala yagɩsɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: About the same time, Abijah son of Jeroboam got sick.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la tɩtɩa lɛ dɩ Jerobuam nanʋala Abija ka wɩɩlʋ.

english_verse: She got ready and left for Ahijah's house in Shiloh. Ahijah was now old and blind,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jerobuam haala ŋaa wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ bʋla, a sii mʋ Ahija dɩa Sɩlɔ lɛ. Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Ahija hɩɛsa, ʋ sɩaa bɩra bɩ na.

english_verse: But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said: Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you.
translation_verse: Ahija sɩ nɩɩ haal-la naasɩŋ dɔmɔ boiŋ niiŋ, ʋ bʋl, “Jerobuam haala, kʋ jʋʋ. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ kɛŋ ŋ tɩtɩa bɩrɩmɛ arɩ ŋ ŋaa nʋʋ dɔŋ nɛ? Wʋbɔŋ nɛ mɩ kɛŋ dɩ mɩ bʋla pɩŋ.

english_verse: Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Mʋ a bʋla pɩ Jerobuam arɩ wɩɩŋ deeŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa bʋl, ‘Mɩ nɛ lɩɩsɩŋ mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ a leŋ ŋ ŋaa ba sɩpaalaara.

english_verse: I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
translation_verse: Mɩ nɛ kɛŋ kuorii-la laa Devit doho nɩaa teeŋ a joŋo pɩŋ. Ama ŋ vɩa nɛ dɩ ŋ nagɛ mɩ tɩntɩnna Devit. Devit fa to wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ daga nɛ, a kɛŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ kala a to mɩ niiŋ a ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩ zɔmɔ dʋndʋŋ mɩ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: “You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
translation_verse: Ŋ nɛ paala ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ a kɩɩ nɩalɩŋ kala fa sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ dii kuoruŋ aŋ ka pɩŋ. Ŋ vɩamɛ nɛ, aŋ mɛ vesiŋ a pɩ ŋ tɩtɩa, a kɛŋ hɔɔŋ ma libi tɔŋŋɔɔ a kpʋkpaarɛ, a joŋ harɩŋ yɩamɛ, a ŋaa mɩ baanɩŋ sii.

english_verse: “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash.
translation_verse: A tɩŋ ŋ-la wɩaa, mɩ jaŋ chei Jerobuam doho nɩaa kala. Mɩ jaŋ kpʋ ʋ doho nʋʋkala sɩ ŋaa baal, nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ hambiisiŋ kala, yosuŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ yosuŋ ŋaa. Mɩ jaŋ dɛrɛ Jerobuam dɩa kala arɩ ba sɩ yie nyɩgɛ nɛ-bɩnɩŋ ʋ kala dii ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala jaŋ yel ʋ yoho aŋ joŋu hugi. Ʋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ ŋaa Jerobuam nʋʋ ba sɩ jaŋ hugi, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ dʋndʋŋa nyuŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ.

english_verse: The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tɩtɩa jaŋ lɩɩsɛ ʋ kuoro dɩ ʋ bibeŋ Iziral. Ʋ nɛ jaŋ chei Jerobuam doho nɩaa kala. Tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ jɩnɩŋ, ʋ nɛ bʋa deeŋ.

english_verse: The people of Israel have made the Lord angry by setting up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah. So the Lord will punish them until they shake like grass in a stream. He will take them out of the land he gave to their ancestors, then scatter them as far away as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ba jaŋ nagɛ yaŋ sɩ sagɛ lɩɩŋ nyuŋ a bibiegi. Ʋ jaŋ lɩɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tintee-zɔmʋŋ deeŋ ʋ sɩ joŋo pɩ ba naabalɩmaba lɛ, a kɛmba pɩsɛ a mʋ kieli Yufireti fuo-la, bɛɛ wɩaa ba ŋaa vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daasɩŋ nɛ, a tutou a ŋaa La TƖƖNA baanɩŋ sii.

english_verse: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jerobuam haala sii a mɩɩra mʋ ʋ jaŋ Tɩɩza. Ʋ sɩ yie joŋ ʋ naaŋ a nʋɔsɛ ʋ dɩa boiŋ niiŋ dɩdɛrɛ, ʋ nanʋal-la sʋʋ.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
translation_verse: Ba joŋu hugi, ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala yel ʋ yoho, arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ to ʋ tɩntɩnna Ahija, ʋ wʋlaabʋllʋ-la lɛ a bʋl ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Jerobuam sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, arɩ laala-la ʋ sɩ yuo, ba ŋmʋnsɛ ba kala nɛ a hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Ba ma fa saa veŋ kpaarɛ leree nɛ, a bil tabɩa, a pɛ Asɩra daasɩŋ dundolluŋ nyuŋ arɩ tɩɩ-lugunuŋ bʋbʋɔŋ a kpʋkpaarɛ.

english_verse: Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Baalaa arɩ haalaa fa hɛ tintee-la lɛ a ŋɩŋaa wʋlɩɩlɩŋ lee-la ba sɩɩ kpaarɛ ba vesiŋ. Ba faa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ La TƖƖNA sɩɩ kɩsʋ nɛ, wɩalɩŋ nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ hɛ lee-la a ŋɩŋaa La TƖƖNA kiriba ta.

english_verse: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Rihobuam sɩ dii kuoruŋ, ʋ jɩ-nɔŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro Sɩsak kʋ yuo Jerusalɛm,

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Rihobuam leŋ ba kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ libi hɔɔtaalɩ-la laalɩyuoroo sɩ kaa kɛrɛɛ laa bayuori hɛŋŋɛɛ, a hɛ sɛlɩmɛ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ paa nyuŋ lɛ. Ʋ joŋ kɩalɩŋ hɛ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la sɩɩ pɔ kuoru dɩa boiŋ niiŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
translation_verse: Bʋa na-kala dɩ kuoro nɩɩ mʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la, nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔ lee-la yie paa hɔɔtaalɩ-la laalɩyuoroo sɩ kaa kɛrɛɛ laa bayuori hɛŋŋɛɛ a to ʋ harɩŋ nɛ. Dɩ ba nɛ ŋaa wɩaa dɛrɛ, ba bɩra mɩɩra kaa jʋʋ bil nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔ leriŋ dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Rihobuam sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: He and Jeroboam were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Laalɩŋ fa hɛ Rihobuam arɩ Jerobuam pɛgɛ nɛ bʋa na-kala.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Rihobuam sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi Devit tabal-la lɛ ʋ nyɩmmaba tʋɔŋ. Ʋ naaŋ nɛ fa Naama, ʋ fa ŋaa Amɔŋ tɩɩna nɛ. Rihobuam sɩ sʋba, ʋ nanʋala Abija nɛ laa ʋ nyuŋ a dii kuoruŋ.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Asa nahɩma Maaka nɛ fa paala ŋaa haalaa kuoro ʋ kaa laa, a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ pɛ veŋ-haal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daaŋ a kpʋkpaarɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asa keri daa-la lo a kaa mʋ Kɩdɩrɔŋ fuonaaŋ a nyɩgɛ.

english_verse: Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Nɛbat nanʋala Jerobuam sɩ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩ-fii arɩ chori lɛ nɛ Abija ma dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Asa ŋaa ba bʋla pɩ Juda nɩaa kala ba paa tabɩa-la arɩ daasɩ-la Baasa fa sɩ kaa sɩsaa dɩ ʋ golli Rama. Ba nɛ kuoro Asa kaa saa golli taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Geba sɩ hɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ tinteeŋ arɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɩzɩpa.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Wʋbɔmɔ-la kala ʋ nyɩmma fa sɩ ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ʋ ma ŋaa. Ʋ fa bɩ chaasa joŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ kala a pɩ ʋ TƖƖNA Wɩa, arɩ ʋ naabalɩma Devit fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: Devit fa ŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ nɛ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ, ʋ fa bɩ ʋ niiŋ wɩaa vɩa ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ, see wʋbɔŋ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa Yuria lɛ, Hiti tɩɩna-la.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Abija sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Abija sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi Devit tabal-la lɛ, ka ʋ nanʋala Asa dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ. Juda kuoro Asa

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ paa hɔpʋla arɩ sɛlɩmɛ-la arɩ tɩntɩnnɩ kɩalɩŋ ʋ dɩ ʋ nyɩmma fa sɩ joŋo pɩ La TƖƖNA a kaa kʋ jʋʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Laalɩŋ fa hɛ Asa arɩ Iziral kuoro Baasa pɛgɛ nɛ ba kuoruŋ bʋa kala lɛ.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Jerobuam sɩ dii kuoruŋ Iziral lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara lɛ nɛ Asa ma dii kuoruŋ Juda lɛ.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Ʋ fa kiri baala-la arɩ haala-la kala sɩɩ ŋaa wʋlɩɩlɩŋ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa ta nɛ ba lɩɩ tintee-la lɛ, aŋ giri tɔmɔ-la kala ʋ naabalɩmaba fa sɩ mɛ.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Asa fa bɩ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa kala cheye, ama ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ ʋ chaasa to La TƖƖNA nɛ.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala lɛ Iziral kuoro Baasa sii mʋ yuo Juda nɩaa, a chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ saa kɛrɛ golli taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Rama, dɩ nʋʋkala sɩ́ Juda kuoro Asa leriŋ lɩɩ mʋ lee koo a kʋ jʋʋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asa sii paa warɩpʋla arɩ sɛlɩmɛ-la kala sɩ ka La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-balɩŋ arɩ ʋ kuoru dɩa lɛ, a joŋo tɩŋ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ dɩ ba kaa mʋ pɩ Siiria tinteeŋ kuoro Bɛŋ-Hadad sɩ hɛ Damasɩkʋs lɛ, Tabɩrɩmɔŋ nanʋala, a ŋaa Hɛzɩyɔŋ ma nihiŋ, aŋ bʋla pʋ,

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: “Leŋ dɩ mɩ dɩŋ pɛ niiŋ a ŋaa kʋbala, arɩ la nyɩmmaba fa sɩ pɛ niiŋ ŋɩɩ. Mɩ joŋ warɩpʋla arɩ sɛlɩmɛ pa nɛ dɩ ba kaa kʋ dii zile pɩŋ. Leŋ ŋ dɩ Iziral kuoro Baasa pɛgɛ chei dɩ ʋ dɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo lɩɩ mɩ tinteeŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Bɛŋ-Hadad sɛɩ wɩɩ-la kuoro Asa sɩ bʋla a leŋ ʋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ arɩ ba nɩaa mʋ yuo Iziral tasɩŋ. Ba yuo dii Ɩjɔŋ, Daŋ, Abɛl Bɛf Maaka arɩ Kɩnɛrɛf tinteeŋ a pɛ Nafɩtalɩ tinteeŋ kala lɛ.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Baasa sɩ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la, ʋ leŋ Rama saanɩŋ ta aŋ mɩɩra mʋ Tɩɩza.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Asa fa sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa a laa yɩrɩŋ, arɩ tasɩ-la ʋ sɩ saa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ. Ʋ fa sɩ kʋ hɩɛsɛ, naasɩŋ nyanyalaa kɛnʋ.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Asa sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda lɛ, ʋ jɩ-lɩa lɛ nɛ Jerobuam nanʋala Nadab ma dii kuoruŋ Iziral lɛ, a bemba jɩsɩŋ balɩa.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Nadab ma fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, arɩ ʋ nyɩmma sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ dii kuoruŋ, ʋ guu kpʋ Jerobuam dɩa nɩaa kala. Ʋ bɩ leŋe Jerobuam dɩa nɩaa kʋŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ. Ʋ kpʋ ba kala nɛ arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ to ʋ tɩntɩnna Ahija, Sɩlɔ tɩɩna-la lɛ a bʋl ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Wɩɩŋ deeŋ ŋaa a tɩŋ Jerobuam sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la wɩaa nɛ, a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa ba tɩtɩa, ŋɩɩ leŋ La TƖƖNA baanɩŋ sii.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Nadab sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, arɩ wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ ŋaa nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Laalɩŋ fa hɛ Asa arɩ Iziral kuoro Baasa pɛgɛ nɛ ba kuoruŋ bʋa kala lɛ. Baasa dii Iziral kuoruŋ

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Asa sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda lɛ, ʋ jɩ-tori lɛ nɛ Ahija nanʋala Baasa dii Iziral kuoruŋ, a hɔŋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tɩɩza lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ banɛsɛ.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ʋ ma fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, arɩ ʋ nyɩmma Jerobuam sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩ Hanani nanʋala Jehu a tɩgɛ Baasa lɛ a bʋl:

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: “Ŋ fa bɩ nʋʋkala ŋaa, ka mɩ lɩɩsɩŋ, a leŋ ŋ ŋaa mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaara. Ama ŋ to Jerobuam naabʋɔsʋŋ nɛ a leŋ mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ a leŋ mɩ baanɩŋ sii a tɩŋ ba wʋcheelie-la wɩaa.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa mɩ kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ dɩ mɩ chei Baasa arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa, a nagɛ mɩ sɩ chei Jerobuam dɩa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Baasa naambiiri-la sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ jaŋ lɛ, vasɩŋ nɛ jaŋ dii ba kʋsʋʋnʋŋ, ka dɩ zaaraa ma dii nɩalɩŋ sɩ jaŋ sʋʋ gɩrɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA to Hanani nanʋala Jehu, ʋ wʋlaabʋllʋ-la lɛ nɛ a bʋl wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ a tɩgɛ Baasa arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa lɛ, a tɩŋ wʋbɔmɔ-la kala ʋ sɩ ŋaa La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ a leŋ ʋ baanɩŋ sii. Ʋ ma wʋŋaalaa fa nagɛ Jerobuam nɛ, a paala bɔmɔ kɩɩba ʋ sɩ kpʋ Jerobuam dɩa nɩaa kala. Ɛla dii Iziral kuoruŋ

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Asa sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ balɩdʋ lɛ nɛ Baasa nanʋala Ɛla dii kuoruŋ Iziral lɛ, a hɔŋ Tɩɩza lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ balɩa.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Omiri fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ kɩŋkɛŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ a kɩɩ kuorusu-la kala sɩ laa ʋ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ dɔŋɔ fa hɛ nɩmɛ baa yɩrɛ Zimiri. Ʋ nɛ faa beŋ kuoro laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ. Ʋ chɩchɛ wombiiŋ dɩ ʋ kpʋ kuoro. Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Ɛla hɛ Tɩɩza lɛ, a bubugi Aaza dɩa lɛ, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ kuoro dɩa Tɩɩza lɛ.

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Zimiri kʋ jʋʋ a kpʋ Ɛla, aŋ laa ʋ nyuŋ dii kuoruŋ. Bʋa-la lɛ dɩ Asa sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ balɩpɛ lɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Zimiri sɩ dii kuoruŋ dɛrɛ, ʋ kpʋ Baasa dɩa nɩaa kala. Ʋ bɩ ba baal kala leŋe, a pɛ Baasa nandɔnsʋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Zimiri kpʋ Baasa dɩa nɩaa kala, arɩ La TƖƖNA sɩ to ʋ wʋlaabʋlla Jehu lɛ a bʋl ŋɩɩ tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba ŋaa a tɩŋ wʋbɔmɔ-la kala Baasa arɩ ʋ nanʋala Ɛla sɩ ŋaa a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaaba, a kpʋkpaarɛ vʋɩyaa wɩaa nɛ. Ŋɩɩ leŋ La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa baanɩŋ sii.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Ɛla sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ. Zimiri dii Iziral kuoruŋ

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ ba buguŋ lɛ aŋ nɩɩ arɩ Zimiri chɛ wombiiŋ nɛ a kpʋ kuoro, ba guu heele bʋl tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa arɩ ba laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ Omiri nɛ ŋaa Iziral kuoro.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Omiri arɩ Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ hɛ ʋ teeŋ lɩɩ Gɩbɛtɔŋ lɛ a mʋ yuo Tɩɩza.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Zimiri sɩ na dɩ ba yuo dii taŋ-la, ʋ fá jʋʋ kuoru dɩa dɩ-duoŋ aŋ joŋ nyiniŋ hɛ, ʋ diiu kpʋ.

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba kala ŋaa a tɩŋ wʋbɔmɔ-la Zimiri sɩ ŋaa La TƖƖNA teeŋ nɛ. Wʋbɔmɔ-la Jerobuam sɩ ŋaa tɩtɩa nɛ ʋ ma ŋaa a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Zimiri sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, arɩ wʋbɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ joŋo ŋaa Ɛla lɛ, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ. Omiri dii Iziral kuoruŋ

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa pɔɩ leree balɩa, dɔnsʋŋ chɩŋ Ginaf nanʋala Tibini harɩŋ a cho dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa kuoro, dɔnsʋŋ ma chɩŋ Omiri harɩŋ a ma cho dɩ ʋ nɛ ŋaa kuoro.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Asa sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ kʋbala lɛ nɛ Omiri dii kuoruŋ Iziral lɛ, a bemba jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩa. Jɩsɩ-la tʋɔŋ, ʋ hɔŋ Tɩɩza lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ balɩdʋ nɛ.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Wʋbɔmɔ-la Nɛbat nanʋala Jerobuam sɩ ŋaa doho tɩtɩa nɛ Omiri ma ŋaa, a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaaba. La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa na baanɩŋ, a tɩŋ ba vʋɩ-tɔɔnʋ-la kpaarɩŋ wɩaa.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Omiri sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Omiri sʋʋ, ba hugu Samarɩa lɛ, ka ʋ nanʋala Ahab dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ. Ahab dii Iziral kuoruŋ

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Asa sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ chori lɛ nɛ Omiri nanʋala Ahab dii kuoruŋ Iziral lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Samarɩa lɛ a beŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ balɩa.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Omiri nanʋala Ahab fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ woruŋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ a kɩɩ kuorusu-la kala sɩ laa ʋ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Jerobuam sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la dʋndʋŋa dee ʋ ŋaa, ʋ-na paala jaa Jɛzɛbɛl nɛ, Sɩdɔŋ kuoro ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛfɩbaal tolo, a suomo kpʋkpaarɛ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Baal vene-la dɩa sɩ hɛ Samarɩa lɛ, ʋ paala saa koruŋ nɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ a kpʋkpaarɛ.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Ahab fa pɛ veŋ-haal-la ma ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daaŋ nɛ. Ʋ chaasa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ woruŋ La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa teeŋ, a leŋ ʋ baanɩŋ sii a kɩɩ Iziral kuorusu-la sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Ahab kuoruŋ bʋa lɛ, Bɛtɛl tɩŋŋaa baal kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hɩɛl nɛ wasa saa taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jeriko. Ʋ sɩ bil taŋ-la gentine, ʋ bii-hɩaŋ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Abɩram sʋba nɛ, ʋ sɩ bɩra dɛrɛ taŋ-la a hɛ ʋ boi-baalaa, ʋ bii-katɩɩ ma ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Segub sʋba nɛ. La TƖƖNA fa to Nuŋ nanʋala Josua lɛ a bʋl wɩɩŋ deeŋ nɛ faafaa kala.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ baa yɩrɛ Ɩlaaja, a lɩɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tɩsɩbɩ sɩ hɛ Gɩlɩad tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ fa bʋla pɩ kuoro Ahab, “La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ weye wɩaa, nɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ tɩma pɩpa, jɩsɩŋ baŋmɛnɛ lɛ, nyalɩŋ bɩ jaŋ nyal koo dɩ duonuŋ nɩɩ, see dɩ mɩ pa wombiiŋ.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩ Ɩlaaja:

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Sii daha, a joŋ sɩaa chaasɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a mʋ faa lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kɛrɩf lɩɩ-libe, a hɛ Jɔdaŋ fuo-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Ŋ jaŋ nyʋnyʋa lɩɩŋ lɩɩ-libe-la sɩɩ pɛllʋ lɛ. Mɩ hɛ gɩlɩŋgaamba nɛ dɩ ba kɛŋ kʋdiilee kʋʋ pɩŋ nɩmɛ.”

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Gɩlɩŋgaamba yie kɛŋ boroboro arɩ nammɩa kʋʋ pʋ chʋchʋɔŋ arɩ dɩdaanɩŋ kala, ka ʋ nyʋnyʋa lɩɩ-libe-la sɩɩ pɛllʋ lɩɩŋ. Yo-haal-la sɩ hɛ Zarɛfaf lɛ

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala lɛ lɩɩ-libe-la sɩɩ pɛllʋ hʋ, a tɩŋ duonuŋ sɩ bɩ tintee-la lɛ ka nɩɩ.

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ Ɩlaaja:

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Guu sii a mʋ hɔŋ Zarɛfaf sɩ hɛ Sɩdɔŋ tinteeŋ lɛ. Mɩ bʋla pɩ yo-haal kʋbala sɩ hɛ lee-la nɛ dɩ ʋ pɩŋ kʋdiilee.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɩlaaja sii mʋ Zarɛfaf. Ʋ sɩ mʋ yi taŋ-la boi-baalɩŋ, ʋ na Zarɛfaf tɩŋŋaa yo-haal kʋbala nɩmɛ dɩ ʋʋ paa daasɩŋ. Ʋ yɩrɛ haal-la a bʋl, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, ŋaa lɩɩŋ mʋa hɛ loŋ lɛ a kaa kʋ pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ nyʋa.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Haal-la sɩɩ mʋ dɩ ʋ ŋaa lɩɩ-la, ʋ bɩra yɩrʋ a bʋl, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ, pɛ kɛŋ boroboro ma mʋa kʋ pɩmɛ.”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Haal-la bʋl, “Ŋ Tɩɩna Wɩa sɩ weye wɩaa, mɩ bɩ kʋdiilii kala kɛnɛ, kʋ-la kala mɩ sɩ kɛnɛ nɛ munuŋ nɩsɩŋ sɩɩŋ a hɛ gbaŋa lɛ arɩ nʋʋŋ ma mʋa loŋ lɛ. Daasɩŋ mʋa nɛ mɩɩ paa daha, dɩ mɩ kaa mʋ dɩa a ŋaa kʋdiile-la mʋa mɩ sɩ kɛnɛ dɩ mɩ dɩ mɩ nanʋala dii, ŋɩɩ harɩŋ, losuŋ nɛ la jaŋ kaa sʋʋ.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɩlaaja bʋla pʋ, “Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛnɩŋ. Ŋ-na mʋ dɩa a ŋaa kʋdiile-la arɩ ŋ sɩ bʋl ŋɩɩ. Ama laa sɩpaaŋ ŋaa muŋ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ a wasɛ boroboro a kaa kʋ pɩmɛ, aŋ-na ŋaa ŋ dɩ ŋ nanʋala ma kɩaa.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Muŋ-la sɩ hɛ gbaŋa-la lɛ bɩ jaŋ dɛrɛ, nʋʋ-la ma sɩ hɛ loŋ lɛ bɩ jaŋ dɛrɛ a kaa mʋ tapʋlɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ duonuŋ nɩɩ tinteeŋ deeŋ lɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Haal-la mʋ a ŋaa wɩɩ-la Ɩlaaja sɩ bʋla pʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɩlaaja arɩ haal-la arɩ ʋ dɩa nɩaa-na kɛŋ kʋdiilee a didii tapʋlɩɩ kala.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA sɩ to Ɩlaaja lɛ a bʋl ŋɩɩ, muŋ-la sɩ hɛ gbaŋa-la lɛ bɩ dɛrɛ, nʋʋ-la ma sɩ hɛ loŋ-la lɛ bɩ dɛrɛ.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala lɛ, yo-haal-la nanʋala wʋwɩɩlɛ. Nyanyalɩɩ-la faasa jʋʋ bile lɛ woruŋ, ʋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Haal-la pɩɛsɛ Ɩlaaja, “Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ, bɛɛ nɛ ŋ ŋaa mɩ lɛ ŋ-la? Ŋ kɔ dɩ ŋ kpʋ mɩ nanʋala nɛ a liisimi mɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ wɩaa?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Ɩlaaja bʋl, “Joŋ bile a pɩmɛ.” Ʋ laa bile haal-la nɩsɩŋ lɛ, a kaa jɩl lusuŋ nyuŋ dɩa-la ʋ sɩɩ jʋʋ, a joŋu bil ʋ kʋpɩnɩŋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
