translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro Jehuas mɩɩra tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋl ŋ-la pɩ Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Amazɩa: “Sɔ-pugu-bie nɛ fa hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ lɛ, a tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ kuolu tɩa ma sɩ hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ tinteeŋ lɛ, ‘Joŋ ŋ tolo pɩ mɩ nanʋala dɩ ʋ jaa.’ Ŋɩɩ nɛ baga kʋŋ ma fa sɩ hɛ Lɛbanɔŋ lɛ kʋ nʋɔsɛ sɔ-pugu-bie-la a bʋrɩgɛ.

english_verse: But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Ama Amazɩa bɩ jegile nɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro Jehuas arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo kʋ yuo Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Amazɩa arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Bɛf Sɛmɛs sɩ hɛ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa yuo dii Juda tɩŋŋaa, ba kala fá mʋ ba dɩɩsɩŋ,

english_verse: He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Ka Jehuas paa sɛlɩmɛ, hɔpʋla arɩ kɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ kaa tɩtɩŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la arɩ dʋa-la kala sɩ hɛ kuoru dɩa lɛ, a pɛ nɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ yuo kɛsɛ lɛ, a kaa mɩɩra mʋ Samarɩa.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he defeated King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Jehuas sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa arɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa laa yɩrɩŋ, a pɛ ʋ sɩ kɛŋ Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Amazɩa yuo laalɩŋ, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa kala lɩɩsɛ ʋ nanʋala Uzia sɩ ŋaa jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩdʋ, ʋ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyɩmma nyuŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath. King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
translation_verse: Ʋ nyɩmma sʋʋŋ harɩŋ lɛ nɛ ʋ bɩra yuo laa taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛlaf a wasa paa saa pɩ Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa. Jerobuam dɔŋɔ ma bɩra dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
translation_verse: Jʋas nanʋala Amazɩa sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ ʋ jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ banɔŋ lɛ nɛ, Jehuas nanʋala Jerobuam ma dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Samarɩa lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ balɩa arɩ kʋbala nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa na ŋɩɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩalɩŋ sɩ ŋaa yosuŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ tɩɩ ba tɩtɩa kala sɩ chaasaa na hɛɛŋ ŋɩɩ nɛ, ka nʋʋ tuo dɩ ʋ pɛ ba lɛ.

english_verse: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
translation_verse: A tɩŋ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ sɩ ʋ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa yɩrɩŋ lɛl wɩaa, ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ to Jehuas nanʋala Jerobuam deeŋ lɛ a laaba ta.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Jerobuam deeŋ sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, arɩ laala-la ʋ sɩ yuo dii arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ yuo laa Damasɩkʋs arɩ Hamaf kala a pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Pɛkahɩa sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ. Pɛka dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Uzia sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mahɩŋ balɩa arɩ fii lɛ nɛ, Mɛnahɛm nanʋala Pɛkahɩa ma dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Samarɩa lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ balɩa.

english_verse: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: Ʋ fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ, arɩ ʋ nyɩmma Amazɩa fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ama ʋ fa bɩ veŋ-kpaarɛ lere-la ŋmoo ta. Nɩaa fa haa kpaarɛ vesiŋ nɛ a nyɩnyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa joŋ dayalɩmɩŋ nɛ a hɛ kuoro Uzia lɛ ʋ mɩɩ-kaanɩŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba lɩɩsʋ kuoru dɩa lɛ, ʋ jʋjʋʋ ʋ dʋndʋŋ dɩa. Ka ʋ nanʋala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Jotam mɩɩra laa ʋ nyuŋ a bibeŋ tintee-la.

english_verse: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Uzia sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Uzia sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi a kpagɛ kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ, Devit tabal-la lɛ. Ka ʋ nanʋala Jotam dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ. Zɛkarɩya dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
translation_verse: Uzia sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ chori lɛ nɛ Jerobuam nanʋala Zɛkarɩya ma dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Samarɩa lɛ a bemba chɛnsɩŋ balɩdʋ.

english_verse: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jabɛs nanʋala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Salum sii chɩŋ Zɛkarɩya lɛ a kpʋʋ nɩaa tʋɔŋ, aŋ laa ʋ nyuŋ dii kuoruŋ.

english_verse: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA fa sɩ bʋla pɩ Jehu sɛnɛ kʋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ: Ʋ fa sɩ, “Ŋ doho nɩaa jaŋ dii Iziral tinteeŋ kuoruŋ naansɩɩŋ bʋnɛsɛ a tɩgɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ.” Salum dii Iziral tinteeŋ kuoruŋ

english_verse: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
translation_verse: Uzia sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ nibi lɛ nɛ Jabɛs nanʋala Salum ma dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Samarɩa lɛ a bemba chɛnɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Uzia sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ nibi lɛ nɛ Gadɩ nanʋala Mɛnahɛm ma dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Samarɩa lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ fii nɛ.

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Mɛnahɛm ma fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Ʋ kuoruŋ bʋa kala lɛ, ʋ fa to Nɛbat nanʋala Jerobuam wʋbɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa nɛ, a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa ba tɩtɩa.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tɩgɩlaf Pɩlɩsa kɔ dɩ ʋ yuo Iziral tinteeŋ. Mɛnahɛm joŋ warɩpʋla bʋɩ balɩa a pʋ, ka dɩ ʋ pɛ ʋ lɛ dɩ ʋ kuoruŋ chaasa kɛŋ doluŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: Jotam fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ a nagɛ ʋ nyɩmma Uzia fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Mɛnahɛm sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: Pɛkahɩa ma fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Ʋ fa to Nɛbat nanʋala Jerobuam wʋbɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa nɛ, a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa ba tɩtɩa.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Pɛka ma fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Ʋ fa to Nɛbat nanʋala Jerobuam wʋbɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa nɛ, a leŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa ma ŋaa ba tɩtɩa.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Pɛka sɩ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ, Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tɩgɩlaf Pɩlɩsa kʋ yuo Iziral tinteeŋ a laa tasɩŋ deemba: Ɩjɔŋ, Abɛl Bɛf Maaka, Janʋa, Kɛdɛs arɩ Hazɔ, a pɛ Gɩlɩad arɩ Galilii arɩ Nafɩtalɩ tinteeŋ kala lɛ, a kɛsɛ ba nɩaa kala kaa mʋ Asiiria tinteeŋ.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Uzia nanʋala Jotam sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara lɛ nɛ Ɛla nanʋala Hosia sii chɩŋ Remalia nanʋala Pɛka lɛ a kpʋʋ, aŋ laa ʋ nyuŋ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Pɛka sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ. Jotam dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Remalia nanʋala Pɛka sɩ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩ-lɩa lɛ nɛ Uzia nanʋala Jotam ma dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ama ʋ fa bɩ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa ŋmoo ta. Nɩaa fa haa kpaarɛ vesiŋ nɛ a nyɩnyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ nɩmɛ. Jotam nɛ fa wasa saa La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la boi-baal-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nyuŋ Boi-baalɩŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Jotam sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Jotam sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ Devit tabal-la lɛ. Ka ʋ nanʋala Ahas dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Remalia nanʋala Pɛka sɩ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩpɛ lɛ nɛ, Jotam nanʋala Ahas ma dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ahas sʋʋ, ba joŋu hugi kuoroo dɩ-huguŋ, Jerusalɛm lɛ. Ka ʋ nanʋala Hezikaaya dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Yuria, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala Ahas sɩ bʋla.

english_verse: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: Ʋ fa to Iziral tinteeŋ kuoroo naabʋɔsʋŋ nɛ. Ʋ paala kɛŋ ʋ nanʋala nɛ a kaa kpaarɛ tɔmʋŋ a nyɩga pʋ, a ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ kɩsʋ La TƖƖNA teeŋ. Wɩalɩŋ tɩtɩa nɛ tinteye-la nɩaa fa ŋɩŋaa tintee-la lɛ, La TƖƖNA kiriba ta ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋ hɔŋ.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Ʋ faa kpaarɛ vʋɩyaa nɛ aŋ nyɩnyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa, dundolluŋ nyuŋ arɩ tɩɩ-lugunuŋ bʋbʋɔsʋŋ kala.

english_verse: While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there. About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ nɛ Siiria kuoro Reziŋ bɩra yuo laa taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Ɛlaf, aŋ kiri Juda nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ hɔŋ nɩmɛ ta. Ka Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa mɩɩra mʋ hɔŋ Ɛlaf lɛ. Arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala ba ha hɛ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ahas tɩŋ tɩndaaraa, ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro Tɩgɩlaf Pɩlɩsa, “Mɩ ŋaa ŋ tɩntɩnnʋ sɩ joŋ mɩ tɩtɩa pɩŋ nɛ. Kʋ laamɛ ta Siiria tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro nɩsɩŋ lɛ, baa yuomi nɛ.”

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Tɩndaara-la sɩɩ mʋ, kuoro Ahas pɛ paa hɔpʋla arɩ sɛlɩmɛ-la kala sɩ hɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ arɩ kuoru dɩa lɛ ba kaa mʋ dii zile pɩ Asiiria kuoro.

english_verse: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
translation_verse: Asiiria kuoro Tɩgɩlaf Pɩlɩsa sɩ laa tɩndaarɩ-la, ʋ dɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo sii mʋ yuo Siiria tinteeŋ. Ba yuo dii ba tabalɩŋ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Damasɩkʋs a kɛsɛ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ ba ŋaa ʋ yosi. Ʋ kaa mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Kɛɛ, aŋ kpʋ kuoro Reziŋ.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Ahas sii mʋ Damasɩkʋs dɩ ʋ cheŋ Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro Tɩgɩlaf Pɩlɩsa. Ʋ sɩ mʋa, ʋ na koruŋ, a tuuri koru-la nagɩsɩŋ kala arɩ ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ jaŋ saaʋ a joŋo pa ba kaa mʋ pɩ Yuria sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara dɩ ʋ laa beŋ aŋ saa ʋ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Yuria laa koru-la nagɩsɩŋ beŋ aŋ saa ʋ dɔŋɔ. Ʋ nagɛ kʋ-la tɩtɩa sɩ hɛ Damasɩkʋs lɛ. Ka kuoro Ahas-na lɩɩ Damasɩkʋs kɔ.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Ahas sɩ kɔ, ʋ mʋ dɩ ʋ na koru-la aŋ pɛ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ ʋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ mʋa, ʋ kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a ŋaa kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, a ŋaa kʋnyʋalaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, aŋ joŋ nii-magɛ dɔŋɔ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pʋsʋŋ chalɩŋ a mɩsɛ koru-la.

english_verse: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ koru-la fa sɩ chɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ sɩpaaŋ a joŋ a kaa mʋ bil Wɩa dɩa wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa, ka koru-falɩɩ-la mɩɩra chɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Yuria, “A chɩŋ lɛɛlɛ a kaa mʋ, ʋ maga dɩ ŋ nyɩnyɩgɛ chʋchʋɔŋ kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ dɩdaanɩŋ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, kuoro kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ ʋ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ tinteeŋ deeŋ lɛ kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ ba mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ arɩ ba kʋnyʋalaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kala koru-falɩŋ deeŋ sɩ yʋga lɛ nɛ. Joŋ pʋsʋ-la kala ba sɩ kpʋa a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ chalɩŋ a mɩsɛ koru-la. Ama leŋ kɔlɩɩŋ koru-la-na pɩmɛ, ʋ nɛ mɩ ma jaŋ kaa chɛ nɩna wɩalɩŋ Wɩa sɩɩ chɛ dɩ mɩ ŋaa.”

english_verse: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
translation_verse: Kuoro Ahas chaarɛ hɔɔ-daaterigeba-la sɩ hɛ torukoba-la lɛ aŋ dʋɔrɛ gbansɩ-la sɩ sagɛ ba nyuŋ, a bɩra dʋɔrɛ taasɩ-gbaŋ-bal-la ma sɩ sagɛ nɛ-belli-la nyuŋ, a joŋo daŋ tabɩɩŋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
translation_verse: A tɩŋ ʋ sɩɩ chɛ Asiiria kuoro tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ, ʋ polli pal-la sɩ tɔ kuoru kpasa, aŋ tɔ wombii-la kuoro sɩ to jʋjʋʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-balɩŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Ahas sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Ahas sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩa lɛ nɛ Ɛla nanʋala Hosia ma dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ. Ʋ hɔŋ Samarɩa lɛ a bemba jɩsɩŋ nibi nɛ.

english_verse: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
translation_verse: Hosia ma fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, ama ʋ bɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ maga.

english_verse: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
translation_verse: Hosia kuoruŋ bʋa lɛ nɛ, Asiiria kuoru kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Salɩmanɛsa kʋ yuo dii Iziral tinteeŋ a fʋgɛba ba tiŋ lampoo pʋpʋ jɩna na-kala.

english_verse: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
translation_verse: Salɩmanɛsa kʋ jɩŋ dɩ Hosia ŋaa zɛmbɛ tɩɩna nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ tɩŋ tɩndaaraa ba mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoru-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ So teeŋ nɛ dɩ ʋ pɛ ʋ lɛ, aŋ bɩra bɩ sɛɩ dɩ ʋ tiŋ lampoo pɩpɩ Asiiria kuoro jɩna na-kala arɩ ʋ fa sɩ vɛnɛɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria kuoro kɛnʋ tɔ bɩnɩŋ dɩa.

english_verse: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Salɩmanɛsa arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo jʋʋ su Iziral tinteeŋ kala, a tɔ Samarɩa hɛ a yuou ŋɩɩ jɩsɩŋ batori.

english_verse: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Hosia sɩ dii kuoruŋ ʋ jɩ-nibi lɛ nɛ, Asiiria kuoro yuo dii Samarɩa a kɛsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala a kaa mʋ Asiiria tinteeŋ. Ʋ kɛmba mʋ a leŋ dɔnsʋŋ hɔŋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hala lɛ, dɔnsʋŋ ma hɔnɔ kpagɛ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Habɔ a hɛ Goza tinteeŋ. Ka dɔnsʋŋ ma hɔŋ tasɩ-la sɩ hɛ Medis tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ lɛ. Wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa mʋ yoŋ-baga

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba kala ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ, a tɩŋ ba sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la a chei ba TƖƖNA Wɩa tʋɔŋ nɛ, Nɩɩ-la sɩ laaba ta Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ka ba vɩaʋ aŋ kpʋkpaarɛ vesiŋ.

english_verse: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
translation_verse: Ba faa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ tɩtɩa tinteye-la nɩaa fa sɩɩ ŋaa nɛ La TƖƖNA kiriba ta tintee-la lɛ ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋ hɔŋ, arɩ wʋbɔmɔ-la Iziral kuoroo sɩ ŋaa dagɛba.

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa lʋara ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba TƖƖNA Wɩa tʋɔŋ ka tɔrɛ nɛ. Ba saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa nɛ ba tasɩŋ kala lɛ, kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ saa kɛrɛ golli arɩ tabiisi-la ba sɩ bɩ kɛrɛ saa golli kala lɛ.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Ba fa bil tabɩaa nɛ, a pɛ Asɩra daasɩŋ dundolluŋ nyuŋ arɩ tɩɩ-lugunuŋ bʋbʋɔsʋŋ kala a kpʋkpaarɛ.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: Vesiŋ dɩ-kpaarɩa-la kala lɛ, ba yie nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ a nagɛ wɩalɩŋ tɩtɩa tinteye-la nɩaa fa sɩɩ ŋaa nɛ tintee-la lɛ La TƖƖNA kiriba ta ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋ hɔŋ. Ba ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la nɛ a leŋ La TƖƖNA baanɩŋ sii.

english_verse: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa sɩ dɩ ba sɩ́ vʋɩyaa kpaarʋ nɛ, ka ba vɩa aŋ kpʋkpaarɛ.

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa to ʋ wʋlaabʋllaa arɩ ʋ sɩɩnaaraa lɛ nɛ a bʋl ŋ-la a chagɩlɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa arɩ Juda nɩaa kala, “Má bɩrɩma lɩɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ lɛ. Má to mɩ wombiee arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ dagɛ ma naabalɩmaba dɩ ba to, arɩ mɩ niiŋ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ to mɩ tɩntɩnna-la sɩ ŋaa mɩ wʋlaabʋllaa lɛ a bʋla pɩma.”

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ama Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa bɩ jegile nɩɩ. Ba nyuŋ fa dolie a nagɛ ba nyɩmmaba-la sɩ bɩ ba TƖƖNA Wɩa wɩaa laa dii nɛ.

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Ba vɩa ʋ wombiiŋ arɩ nii-la ʋ fa sɩ bile pɩ ba nyɩmmaba nɛ arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ fa sɩ kpʋrɩsɛ ba dɩgɩlaa. Ba to vʋɩyaa sɩ bɩ bʋbʋɔ kɛnɛ harɩŋ nɛ, a kʋ ŋaa nɩyaayasɩ. Tinteye-la sɩ golliba wʋŋaalaa nɛ ba chesi. La TƖƖNA fa sɩ dɩ ba sɩ́ ŋɩɩ ŋaa nɛ, ka ba vɩa aŋ ŋaa.

english_verse: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa vɩa ba TƖƖNA Wɩa niiŋ wɩalɩŋ kala nɛ, aŋ mɛ kɩaa balɩa ba nagɛ nɛ-biisiŋ a pɛ Asɩra daaŋ, a bɩra mɛ kɩaa ba nagɛ chɛnwʋlaa a kpʋkpaarɛ ba dɩ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal kala.

english_verse: They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Ba yie kɛsɛ ba hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ba toloo kpʋ a nyɩga pɩpɩ vesiŋ, a vʋvʋgɛ, a joŋ ba tɩtɩa kala hɛ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ lɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, a leŋ ʋ baanɩŋ sii.

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA chaasa na baanɩŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nyuŋ, a kiriba ta ʋ sɩpaaŋ, aŋ leŋ Juda doho nɩaa dʋndʋŋa.

english_verse: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
translation_verse: Juda tɩŋŋaa ma fa bɩ wɩalɩŋ ba TƖƖNA Wɩa sɩ daga to. Ba fa mɩɩra to Iziral tɩŋŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la tɩtɩa nɛ.

english_verse: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA vɩa Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala ta, aŋ dɔgɩsɛba a leŋ ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ sɩ kɛŋ tʋɔhɛɛŋ kɛsɛba a kaa viiri.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ leŋe Iziral tɩŋŋaa pɔrɛ Juda doho nɩaa lɛ ŋɩɩ, ŋɩɩ nɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa leŋ Nɛbat nanʋala Jerobuam ŋaa ba kuoro. Jerobuam leŋ ba vɩa La TƖƖNA, aŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ-balaa.

english_verse: The people kept on sinning like Jeroboam,
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa to Jerobuam naabʋɔsʋŋ a ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la tɩtɩa ʋ sɩ ŋaa nɛ,

english_verse: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
translation_verse: a kaa kɔ bʋa-la lɛ La TƖƖNA sɩ kiriba ta ʋ sɩpaaŋ arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ fa sɩ to ʋ tɩntɩnnaa sɩ ŋaa ʋ wʋlaabʋllaa lɛ a kpʋrɩsɛ ba dɩgɩlaa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria tɩŋŋaa yuo kɛsɛba a kaa mʋ ba tinteeŋ, ba hɔŋ nɩmɛ a kaa kɔ arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala. Asiiria tɩŋŋaa mʋ hɔŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria kuoro kɛsɛ nɩaa tasɩŋ deemba lɛ: Babɩlɔŋ, Kuta, Ava, Hamaf arɩ Safavem a kaa kʋ holli Samarɩa tinteeŋ tasɩ-la lɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ hɔnɔ. Ba mɩɩra laa Samarɩa tinteeŋ tɩɩ a hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩ kʋ buumo hɔŋ nɩmɛ, ba fa bɩ La TƖƖNA ka to. Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA leŋ naachigee kʋ kpʋ ba dɔnsʋŋ.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: Ba tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Asiiria kuoro, “Nɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ kaa kʋ holli Samarɩa tinteeŋ tasɩŋ lɛ, ba bɩ tintee-la vene sɩɩ chɛ wɩalɩŋ jɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ leŋ naachigee kʋ jʋʋ ba tʋɔŋ a kpʋkpʋba.”

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Asiiria kuoro bʋla pɩba, “Má kɛŋ Iziral tɩmma-la la sɩ yuo kɛsɛ, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa dɔŋɔ, kaa mʋ Samarɩa nɩaa teeŋ dɩ ʋ dagɛba ba tintee-la vene wɩaa.”

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa dɔŋɔ, a kaa mɩɩra mʋ Iziral tinteeŋ. Ʋ hɔŋ Bɛtɛl lɛ a dɩdagɛ nɩalɩŋ ŋɩɩ ba sɩ jaŋ dɩdɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: Ama nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɔŋ Samarɩa tintee-la lɛ, tintee na-kala nɩaa ha mɛ ba vesiŋ nɛ a joŋo bil vesiŋ dɩ-kpaarɩa-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa sɩ saa lɛ.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Babɩlɔŋ nɩaa mɛ ba vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sʋkɔf Bɛnɔf, Kuta nɩaa ma mɛ ba vene baa yɩrɛ Nɛgal, Hamaf nɩaa ma mɛ ba vene baa yɩrɛ Asɩma,

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: Ava tɩŋŋaa ma mɛ ba vesiŋ baa yɩrɛ Nibihas arɩ Taatak, Safavem tɩŋŋaa ma mɛ ba vesiŋ baa yɩrɛ Adɩramɛlɛk arɩ Anamɛlɛk a kɛsɛ ba biiriŋ a nyɩga pɩpɩ ba.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: Ba faa chʋɔlɛ La TƖƖNA nɛ, aŋ pɛ kpʋkpaarɛ ba vesiŋ ma a nagɛ ba tinteye-la ba sɩ lɩɩ kɔ naabarɩŋ sɩ dagɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
translation_verse: Arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala, ba haa to ba faafaa wʋŋaalaa nɛ. Ba kʋŋkala bɩ La TƖƖNA dʋndʋŋa nɩɩ dɛnnɛ. Ba bɩ wombie-la ʋ sɩ bile ka to, arɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ daga arɩ ʋ niiri-la arɩ wɩɩ na-kala ʋ sɩ joŋo dagɛ Jekɔb doho nɩaa, nɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ kaa yɩrɛ Iziral.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ La TƖƖNA fa sɩ bil niiŋ ʋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa pɛgɛ, ŋ-la nɛ ʋ bʋl, “Má pɔ ma sɩ́ vesiŋ to koo a kpirimi ba sɩpaaŋ, má sɩ́ ba to koo a kpʋkpaarɛba.

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ama má tuto mɩ dʋndʋŋa, mɩ nɛ Nɩɩ-la sɩ kɛmma kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ arɩ doluŋ. Mɩ nɛ maga ma tuto. Mɩ sɩpaaŋ nɛ maga dɩ ma kpirimi, mɩ nɛ maga dɩ ma kpʋ pʋsʋŋ a sʋl Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩpa.

english_verse: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
translation_verse: Má pɔ ma sɩ́ nii-la mɩ sɩ bile mɩ dɩ ma pɛgɛ yʋ. Má sɩ́ vene kala kpaarʋ.

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: Má tuto mɩ dʋndʋŋa, mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa. Dɩ ma nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, mɩ jaŋ laama ta ma dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɩsɩŋ lɛ.”

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Ama nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɔŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ bɩ jegile nɩɩ, aŋ ha ŋɩŋaa ba naabalɩmaba wʋbɔmɔ-la tɩtɩa.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: Nɩaa deemba faa to La TƖƖNA nɛ, aŋ ha pɛ kpʋkpaarɛ ba vesiŋ ma. Arɩ jɩnɩŋ kala ba biiriŋ arɩ ba nihee ma haa kpaarɛ vesi-la nɛ, arɩ ba nyɩmmaba fa sɩɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you.
translation_verse: Ba nɛ ŋ-la: Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ Hezikaaya nyɩsɛma, ʋ bɩ ma wuo laa ta.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ Hezikaaya teeŋ jegilu. Asiiria kuoro sɩ: Má kɔ mɩ teeŋ dɩ la ŋaa sɩma, ŋɩɩ nɛ ma kʋŋkala jaŋ wuo dii ma tɩtɩa girep nɛnɛɛ aŋ nyʋa ma vilee ma lɩɩŋ,

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: Ma bɩɩna mɩ tɩtɩa doluŋ lɛ nɛ mɩɩ kɔ dɩ mɩ yuo tinteeŋ deeŋ a cheyu ŋɩɩ? La TƖƖNA tɩtɩa nɛ pɩmɛ wombiiŋ dɩ mɩ kʋ yuo ma tinteeŋ a cheyu.”

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
translation_verse: Ʋ fa ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ La TƖƖNA tʋɔŋ nɛ a nagɛ ʋ naabalɩma Devit fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: Hezikaaya fa chei vesiŋ dɩ-kpaarɩa-la nɛ, a yɛrɛ tabɩa-la ma ba fa sɩɩ kpaarʋ, aŋ keri Asɩra daasɩ-la ma lo. Ʋ fa ŋmoo dɩŋ-la ma Mosis fa sɩ kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ libi ba nyɩgɛ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ pʋpʋ a bori nɛ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa faa yɩrɛ dɩŋ-la Nɛhʋsɩtaŋ nɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
translation_verse: Hezikaaya fa laa La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa dii nɛ woruŋ. Juda tinteeŋ kuoroo kala tʋɔŋ, ba kʋŋkala fa tuo a nagʋ, nɩalɩŋ sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ a dii kuoruŋ ʋ lɛ koo nɩalɩŋ sɩ to ʋ harɩŋ a dii kuoruŋ.

english_verse: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
translation_verse: Ʋ fa joŋ ʋ wʋtɩtɩɩ kala hɛ La TƖƖNA lɛ nɛ, a tuto wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ joŋo dagɛ Mosis ʋ ŋmʋnsa bil dɩ nɩaa tuto.

english_verse: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa chɩŋ ʋ harɩŋ nɛ, ʋ wɩɩkala wasɛ. Hezikaaya fa vɩa Asiiria kuoro nɛ a bɩ ʋ niiŋ to.

english_verse: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Ʋ fa yuo dii Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa tabala-la kala ba sɩ saa kɛrɛ golli arɩ tabiisi-la ba sɩ bɩ kɛrɛ saa golli, a kɛŋ ŋɩɩ mʋ yi taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gaza arɩ lere-la sɩ gollu.

english_verse: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
translation_verse: Hezikaaya sɩ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩ-nɛsɛ lɛ, dɩ Ɛla nanʋala Hosia ma sɩ dii kuoruŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ ma jɩ-pɛɩ lɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro Salɩmanɛsa kʋ tɔ Samarɩa hɛ a yuyuou.

english_verse: and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule.
translation_verse: Ʋ yuou ŋɩɩ nɛ jɩsɩŋ batori, aŋ yuo dii. Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dɩ Hezikaaya sɩ dii Juda tinteeŋ kuoruŋ ʋ jɩsɩŋ balɩdʋ lɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ. Hosia ma sɩ dii Iziral tinteeŋ kuoruŋ, ʋ ma jɩ-nibi lɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: The king of Assyria took the Israelites away as prisoners; he forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria kuoro kɛsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala a kaa mʋ Asiiria tinteeŋ. Ʋ kɛmba mʋ a leŋ dɔnsʋŋ hɔŋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hala lɛ, dɔnsʋŋ ma hɔnɔ kpagɛ fuo-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Habɔ sɩ hɛ Gozaŋ tinteeŋ. Ka dɔnsʋŋ ma hɔŋ tasɩ-la kala sɩ hɛ Medis tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them. King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah (
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba kala ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ, a tɩŋ ba sɩ bɩ ba TƖƖNA Wɩa niiŋ to nɛ, aŋ chei nii-la ʋ sɩ bile ʋ dɩ ba pɛgɛ arɩ wɩalɩŋ La TƖƖNA tɩntɩnna Mosis sɩ dagɛba. Ba bɩ wɩalɩŋ jegile nɩɩ koo a toba.

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.
translation_verse: ŋɩɩ deeŋ deeŋ a mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ mɩ sɩ jaŋ kɛmma mʋ lee-la sɩ nagɛ ma tɩtɩa tinteeŋ, a kɛŋ mɩaa ma sɩ jaŋ kaa ŋaa kʋdiilee, girep nɛnɛɛ ma sɩ jaŋ kaa ŋaa sɩnɩŋ, nʋʋŋ tɩɩsɩŋ arɩ tʋʋŋ. Má bagɩsa lɩɩsɛ mɩɩsɩŋ aŋ leŋ sʋʋŋ. Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ Hezikaaya kɛmma yeŋŋi, dɩ ʋ nɛ sɩ, ‘Ma TƖƖNA jaŋ laama ta.’

english_verse: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Laal-baga nɩhɩa-la bʋla pɩba, “Má pɩɛsɛ kuoro Hezikaaya dɩ wɩɩ-la Asiiria kuoru-balɩŋ sɩɩ chɛ ʋ jɩŋ nɛ, ‘Kʋbɛɛ lɛ nɛ ma yɩɛlaa paala hɛ?’

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: Dɩ ma nɛ saa bɩra bʋla pɩmɛ arɩ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa lɛ nɛ ma yɩɛlaa hɛ, ʋ leree arɩ ʋ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ korunuŋ dee Hezikaaya ŋmoo giri ŋɩɩ, aŋ bʋla pɩ Juda arɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa, arɩ ʋ maga dɩ ba dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA Wɩɩsʋllɩ koruŋ deeŋ sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ nɛɛ?

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Hezikaaya sɩ kʋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ banɛsɛ tʋɔŋ nɛ, Asiiria kuoro Sanakɛrɩb arɩ ʋ nɩaa sii kʋ yuo dii Juda tabala-la kala ba sɩ saa kɛrɩsɩŋ golli, a kɛsɛba.

english_verse: Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.” Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hezikaaya tɩŋ ba mʋ bʋla pɩ Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro Sɛnakɛrɩb sɩ hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lakɩs lɛ, “Mɩ cheye nɛ. Bɩra sɩ́ mɩ tinteeŋ yuo. Mɩ jaŋ pɩŋ kʋŋ na-kala ŋ sɩɩ chɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria tinteeŋ kuoro bʋla pɩ Hezikaaya arɩ ʋ jaŋ laa hɔpʋla yuŋuŋ sɩ ŋaa kilo bʋɩ fii arɩ sɛlɩmɛ yuŋuŋ sɩ ŋaa kilo bʋɩ ʋ teeŋ.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hezikaaya paa hɔpʋla-la kala sɩ hɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la arɩ kuoru dɩa kala lɛ a pʋ.

english_verse: He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ nɛ Hezikaaya lɛrɛ sɛlɩmɛ-la kala ba sɩ joŋo taarɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la borusuŋ arɩ boro daasɩŋ kala, a joŋo pa ba kaa mʋ pɩ Asiiria kuoro Sɛnakɛrɩb. Sɛnakɛrɩb fugisi Jerusalɛm tɩŋŋaa

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Asiiria kuoro tɩŋ ʋ nɩaa deemba batori: Ʋ laalɩyuoroo kala nɩhɩaŋ, ʋ tɩntɩnnaa kala nɩhɩaŋ arɩ ʋ laal-baga nɩhɩaŋ ba kɛŋ laalɩyuori daŋ lɩɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lakɩs a mʋ Hezikaaya teeŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ. Laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la arɩ ba nɩaa sɩ kɔ Jerusalɛm, ba chɩŋ pɩl-la sɩ hɛ nyuŋ lɩɩ-libe-la sɩɩ pɛllʋ a hɛ wombii-la sɩɩ mʋ lee-la ba sɩɩ chɛsɛ kɩaa lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ yɩrɛ kuoro Hezikaaya arɩ Ɛlɩakɩm nanʋala Hɩlɩkaaya, nɩɩ-la sɩ ŋaa kuoro dɩa tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ, Sɛbɩna, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋmʋnsɛ ba tenniŋ, a pɛ Asaf nanʋala Jʋab lɛ, nɩɩ-la ma sɩɩ bil ba tenniŋ. Ba kʋ chemba.

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ma sɩ sɩ ma kɛŋ laalɩŋ-yuonuŋ jɩma arɩ doluŋ nɛ, ama ma wʋbʋlɩɩ-la kala ŋaa pɛɩ nɛ. Kʋbɛɛ lɛ nɛ ma joŋ ma yɩɛlaa a daŋ aŋ vɩamɛ?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro lɛ nɛ ma joŋ ma yɩɛlaa daŋ. Ʋ saa nagɛ mɔrʋŋ nɩa sɩ joŋo a kaa ŋaa dantɩga a vɩvɛŋ nɛ. Ʋ jaŋ bori a tʋrɛ ma nɩsaa lɛ a pɩrɛma. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ nagɛ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ joŋ ba yɩɛlaa daŋ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Ma sɩ paala joŋ ma wɩɩkala a daŋ Ijipiti janɩŋ torukoba arɩ ba ja-jɩllaa lɛ ŋɩɩ, ma bɩɩna ma jaŋ wuo yuo dii mɩ nɩhɩaŋ tɩntɩnnaa tʋɔŋ kʋbie naa?

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hɩlɩkaaya nanʋala Ɛlɩakɩm arɩ Sɛbɩna arɩ Jʋa ma bʋla pɩ Asiiria kuoro laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ-la, “Laa sʋlʋŋ, kɛŋ Aramek tɩŋŋaa yikoro bʋl wɩalɩŋ a pɩla, laa nɩɩʋ nɛ, aŋ leŋ Hiburu tɩŋŋaa yikoro. La bɩ chɛ dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ sagɛ kɛrɛ nyuŋ nɩɩ.”

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria kuoro laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ-la ma bʋl, “Ma bɩɩna ma nɩhɩaŋ arɩ ma dʋndʋŋa teeŋ nɛ mɩ nɩhɩaŋ tɩmmɛ dɩ mɩ kʋ bʋl wɩaa deemba? Nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ sagɛ kɛrɛ-la nyuŋ pɛ nɛ. Ma kala jaŋ gʋra dii ma tɩtɩa bɩnɩŋ aŋ nyʋa ma tɩtɩa fɩɩrɩŋ ma.”

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ-la kɛŋ Hiburu yikoro a faasa bʋl, “Má jegile nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ Asiiria kuoro sɩ ŋaa kuoru-balɩŋ sɩ bʋla.

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ Hezikaaya nyɩsɛma dɩ ma joŋ ma yɩɛlaa hɛ ma TƖƖNA lɛ, arɩ ʋ sɩ sɩ ma TƖƖNA bɩ jaŋ sɛɩ joŋ ma tabal-la a pɩ Asiiria kuoro.

english_verse: Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Ma ha na tintee dɔŋ vene dɩ ʋ wuo laa ʋ tinteeŋ Asiiria kuoro nɩsɩŋ lɛɛ?

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Nɩɩ nɛ tasɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hamaf arɩ Apad vesiŋ hɛ? Nɩɩ nɛ tasɩ-la ma ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sɛfavem, Hɛna arɩ Iva vesiŋ hɛ? Ba wuo laa Samarɩa ta nɛ mɩ nɩsɩŋ lɛɛ?

english_verse: None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
translation_verse: Vesiŋ deemba kala tʋɔŋ, ba kʋbɛɛ nɛ wuo laa ʋ tinteeŋ mɩ nɩsɩŋ lɛ? Ɛɛ nɛ saa ma TƖƖNA jaŋ wuo ŋaa a laa Jerusalɛm ta mɩ nɩsɩŋ lɛ?”

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hɩlɩkaaya nanʋala Ɛlɩakɩm sɩ ŋaa kuoru dɩa tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ arɩ Sɛbɩna ma sɩɩ ŋmʋnsɛ ba tenniŋ arɩ Jʋa ma sɩɩ bil ba tenniŋ, kɛŋ ba gɛnnɩŋ kɩɛsɛ aa dagɛ tʋɔ-cheeŋ, aŋ mɩɩra mʋ Hezikaaya teeŋ a bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala Asiiria kuoro laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ-la sɩ bʋla a pʋ.

english_verse: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala Sanakɛrɩb sii a jʋʋ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nɩsɩrɔk dɩa a kpʋkpaarɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ hambolibiisiŋ balɩa, Adɩramɛlɛk arɩ Sarɛza jʋʋ kpʋʋ arɩ tokobiiŋ, aŋ lɩɩ fá mʋ Ararat tinteeŋ. Ka ʋ nanʋala dɔŋɔ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asahadɔŋ dii kuoruŋ.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord.
translation_verse: Kuoro Hezikaaya sɩ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ, ʋ kɛŋ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ kɩɛsɛ aa dagɛ tʋɔ-cheeŋ, aŋ paa tʋɔ-chei gɛnnɩŋ laalɛ a mʋ jʋʋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared. Hezekiah Prays (Isaiah
translation_verse: Nɩɩ nɛ tasɩ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hamaf, Apad, Sɛfavem, koo Hɛna koo Iva kuoroo hɛ?”

english_verse: He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell the prophet Isaiah:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɩŋ Ɛlɩakɩm sɩ ŋaa kuoru dɩa tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ arɩ Sɛbɩna, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋmʋnsɛ ba tenniŋ arɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa ba laalɛ tʋɔ-chei gɛnnɩŋ a mʋ Amos nanʋala Azaaya sɩ ŋaa Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ teeŋ.

english_verse: These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: Ba mʋ bʋla pʋ, “Wɩɩ-la Hezikaaya sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: ‘Jɩnɩŋ la tʋɔŋ kala nɛ cheye, hɛɛŋ jʋʋla nɛ, hɩɩsɩŋ ma diila. La nagɛ haala sɩɩ chɛ ʋ lʋl nɛ aŋ bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ dɩ ʋ lʋl.

english_verse: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
translation_verse: Ŋ bɩ pɔ ŋ Tɩɩna Wɩa jaŋ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ Asiiria kuoro sɩ tɩŋ ʋ laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ ʋ kɔ a tʋʋsɛ Wɩa sɩ weye joŋŋoo. Ŋ Tɩɩna Wɩa sɛnɛ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ nɛ, ʋ jaŋ lɛrɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ bʋlba dɩgɩlɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, sʋl Wɩa pɩ la nɩkaana-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ.’ ”

english_verse: When these leaders went to Isaiah,
translation_verse: Azaaya sɩ nɩɩ kuoro Hezikaaya tɩndaarɩŋ,

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah: I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: ʋ ma bɩra tɩmba, “Má mʋ bʋla pɩ ma nɩhɩaŋ dɩ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la, ‘Sɩ́ leŋe dɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛnɩŋ a mʋ tɩgɛ wɩalɩŋ Asiiria kuoro tɩndaara-la sɩ bʋla a tʋʋsɛ mɩ-na Wɩa joŋŋoo.

english_verse: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma Tɩɩna jaŋ joŋ dɩma kʋbala a hɛ ʋ lɛ, dɩ ʋ nɩɩ ba sɩ a mʋ tɩgɛ ʋ tɩtɩa tinteeŋ lɛ, a sii mʋ nɩmɛ dɩ ba kpʋ.’ ”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Asiiria kuoro laalɩyuori-hɩaŋ-la nɩɩ dɩ Asiiria kuoro lɩɩ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Lakɩs lɛ a mʋ yuyuo Lɩbɩna tabalɩŋ, ʋ mɩɩra mʋ ʋ teeŋ.

english_verse: About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ tɩtɩa lɛ nɛ Asiiria kuoro Sanakɛrɩb nɩɩ dɩ Tɩɩhaka, Kus tɩɩna-la sɩ ŋaa Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa kuoro kɛŋ laalɩyuoroo kʋkɔ dɩ ba yuou nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ ŋmʋnsɛ teniŋ, a tɩŋ ba kaa mʋ pɩ Hezikaaya.

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Ŋ nɩɩ wɩalɩŋ Asiiria kuoro sɩ ŋaa tinteyee kala lɛ nɛ a chei ba kala. Ŋ bɩɩna ŋ-na jaŋ wuo laa ŋ tɩtɩa?

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: Mɩ naabalɩma fa yuo dii tabalaa deemba ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Gozaŋ, Haraŋ, Rɛzɛf arɩ Ɛdɩŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Tɛl Asaa a chei ba kala nɛ. Ba fa kɛŋ vesiŋ nɛ, ka ba kʋŋ bɩ wuo laaba ta.

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Hezikaaya sɩ laa teniŋ tɩndaara-la teeŋ a karɩmɛ, ʋ sii kaa jɩl La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ a kaa jɛrɛ La TƖƖNA sɩpaaŋ,

english_verse: Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said: Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Amos nanʋala Azaaya tɩŋ tɩndaarɩŋ pɩ Hezikaaya: “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la, ‘Ŋ sɩ sʋlmɛ ŋɩɩ a mʋ tɩgɛ Asiiria kuoro Sanakɛrɩb lɛ, mɩ nɩa nɛ.

english_verse: He prayed: Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
translation_verse: aŋ sʋlʋ, “La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa, ŋ sɩ hɔŋ ŋ kuoru kpasa-la sɩ hɛ kɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ a nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa pɛgɛ, ŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ Wɩa, a bibeŋ tinteye-la kala sɩ hɛ dʋnɩa lɛ. Ŋ nɛ ŋaa wɩa-nyuŋ arɩ tinteeŋ.

english_verse: But just look how Sennacherib has insulted you, the living God.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA, jegile nɩɩ aŋ bɩra bee na Sanakɛrɩb sɩ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala a tʋʋsɛ ŋ-na Wɩa sɩ weye joŋŋoo.

english_verse: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.
translation_verse: Wʋtɩtɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA, Asiiria kuoroo chei nɩ-daŋ nɛ, ka ba tinteyee pɩŋ jikpeeŋ.

english_verse: They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped.
translation_verse: Ba paa ba vesi-la sɩ bɩ Wɩa ŋaa a nyɩgɛ nɛ. Daasɩŋ arɩ tabɩaa nɛ nuhuobiinee kaa ŋaaba.

english_verse: But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God. The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA Wɩa, laala ta Asiiria tɩŋŋaa nɩsɩŋ lɛ dɩ dʋnɩa kuoroo arɩ ba nɩaa kala jɩŋ arɩ ŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ Wɩa.” Sanakɛrɩb tele

english_verse: Now this is what I say to that king: The people of Jerusalem hate and make fun of you; they laugh behind your back.
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla a tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ nɛ ŋ-la: Zaayɔŋ nɩaa ka mɔŋ Sɛnakɛrɩb nɛ a sisieri ʋ lɛ. Jerusalɛm nɩaa kɛŋ nyuŋ kpukpegisi nɛ, ka ʋ fɩfá dɩ ʋ laa ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: That same night the Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed
translation_verse: Tɩtaŋ-la tɩtɩa nɛ La TƖƖNA Wɩa tɩndaara mʋ lee-la Asiiria tɩŋŋaa sɩ hɔnɔ, a kpʋ ba laalɩyuoroo bʋɩ zɔlɔ arɩ mahɩŋ banɛsɛ arɩ banɔŋ. Taŋ ka pʋl dɩ lee-la kala suo arɩ sʋʋnʋŋ.

english_verse: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And this is how you bragged about yourself: “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Ŋ leŋe ŋ tɩndaaraa tʋʋsɛ La TƖƖNA joŋŋoo nɛ woruŋ. Ŋ sɩ: Mɩ laalɩŋ janɩŋ torukoba sɩ yʋga ŋɩɩ, ba nɛ mɩ kaa jɩl Lɛbanɔŋ peelee nyu-gbaŋa, a jʋʋ ʋ duuŋ tʋɔŋ a keri ʋ kuolu tɩɩ-duduosuŋ arɩ bʋtʋnsʋŋ tɩɩ-zɔŋŋɔɔ kala lo.

english_verse: I dried up every stream in the land of Egypt, and I drank water from wells I had dug.”
translation_verse: Ŋ sɩ ŋ lu vilee nɛ tintee-wogusuŋ lɛ a nyʋnyʋa lɩɩŋ nɩmɛ. Ŋ sɩ ŋ naachɛɛŋ nɛ ŋ kaa nʋɔsɛ Ijipiti tinteeŋ fuonuŋ kala tɔ ba hɩl.

english_verse: Sennacherib, now listen to me, the Lord. I planned all this long ago. And you don't even realize that I alone am the one who decided that you would do these things. I let you make ruins of fortified cities.
translation_verse: Sanakɛrɩb, ŋ bɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ-na La TƖƖNA sɩ bɩɩna bil faafaa kala dɩ mɩ ŋaa nɩa? Lɛɛlɛ mɩ ŋaaba nɛ. Mɩ nɛ pɩŋ doluŋ ŋ kaa kɛŋ tasɩ-la kala ba sɩ saa kɛrɩsɩŋ golli bɩrɩmɛ ba nagɛ tabɩaa sɩ daŋ dɔŋɔ lɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Their people became weak, terribly confused. They were like wild flowers or tender young grass growing on a flat roof, scorched before it matures.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ lee-la bɩra bɩ dol kala kɛnɛ, ba bugumo nɛ ka hɩɩsɩŋ diiba. Ba fa nagɛ yaŋ sɩ miire ŋmaŋkaaŋ lɛ nɛ, koo yaŋ sɩ nyʋ lusuŋ nyuŋ a bɩ waa, ka hɩlɩŋ leŋ ba hɩl.

english_verse: I know all about you, even how fiercely angry you are with me.
translation_verse: Mɩ jɩŋ ŋ wɩɩkala nɛ, wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa arɩ lee-la ŋ sɩɩ mʋ arɩ baaŋ-la ŋ sɩ kɛnɛ arɩ mɩ.

english_verse: I have seen your pride and the tremendous hatred you have for me. Now I will put a hook in your nose, a bit in your mouth, then I will send you back to where you came from.
translation_verse: A tɩŋ ŋ sɩ faasa kɛŋ baaŋ-la arɩ mɩ arɩ babiibal wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ bʋla mɩ nɩɩ, lɛɛlɛ mɩ jaŋ joŋ hɛmɩŋ tɔɔ gɩrɩgɛ ŋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, a joŋ mɩ koŋ ma a hɛ ŋ niiŋ. Mɩ jaŋ lɛrɩŋ dɩ ŋ mɩɩra joŋ wombii-la ŋ sɩ to kɔ a mʋ.

english_verse: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ ŋaa magɩl a pɩ ŋ-na Hezikaaya nɛ: Jɩna deeŋ ŋ jaŋ dii mɩɩ-tɩarɩŋ, harɩŋ jɩna ma ŋ ha jaŋ dii mɩɩ-tɩarɩŋ. Ama jɩ-tori lɛ, duu kɩaa a kʋŋ, a chɔnsɛ girep tɩɩsɩŋ ma a tɔrɛ ba nɛnɛɛ dii.

english_verse: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.
translation_verse: Juda doho nɩaa nɩkaana-la wɩaa jaŋ chɩŋ woruŋ, a nagɛ tɩa naapoloo sɩ jʋʋ tinteeŋ woruŋ a nɛŋ.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
translation_verse: Nɩaa ha jaŋ ka Jerusalɛm arɩ Zaayɔŋ peel-la lɛ a pɛ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA doluŋ kala Tɩɩna chaasa kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ dɩ mɩ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ.

english_verse: I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa ŋ-la nɛ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA bʋl a mʋ tɩgɛ Asiiria kuoro lɛ: Ʋ bɩ jaŋ wuo kʋ jʋʋ taŋ deeŋ koo a yuo hɛmɩŋ ʋ lɛ. Ʋ laalɩyuoroo bɩ jaŋ wuo golli taŋ deeŋ chu a yuou, ba bɩ jaŋ wuo saa lusuŋ-choluŋ a to nɩmɛ jʋʋ.

english_verse: As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Wombii-la ʋ sɩ to kɔ, ʋ tɩtɩa nɛ ʋ jaŋ bɩra to a mɩɩrɛ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ taŋ deeŋ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: I will protect it for myself and for my servant David. The Death of King Sennacherib (Isaiah
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ pɔ taŋ deeŋ woruŋ a tɩŋ mɩ yɩrɩŋ arɩ mɩ tɩntɩnna kuoro Devit wɩaa.’ ”

english_verse: After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh.
translation_verse: Asiiria kuoro Sanakɛrɩb leŋ laal-la ʋ fa sɩ bɩɩna dɩ ʋ yuo aŋ mɩɩra mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nɩnɩvɛ a hɔŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hezikaaya sʋʋ, ka ʋ nanʋala Manasɛ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_verse: “Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
translation_verse: “Mɩ Tɩɩna, liisi ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ laaŋ dii a toŋ arɩ mɩ tʋɔŋ kala, a ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɔrɛ ŋ tʋɔŋ.” Ʋ bʋl ŋɩɩ aŋ chaasa yel woruŋ.

english_verse: Before Isaiah got to the middle court of the palace,
translation_verse: Ka dɩ Azaaya-na fa mɩɩra lɩɩ kuoru dɩa kaala sɩ hɛ tʋtʋɔbaanɩŋ lɛ, La TƖƖNA fa bʋla pʋ,

english_verse: the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message: Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple.
translation_verse: “Mɩɩra mʋ bʋla pɩ mɩ nɩaa sɩpaalaara Hezikaaya arɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ ŋaa ʋ naabalɩma Devit Wɩa sɩ, ‘Mɩ nɩɩ ŋ sʋla nɛ a na ŋ sɩlɩɩrɩŋ ma. Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ duori. A lɩɩ jɩnɩŋ kaa mʋ tapʋlaa batori chɛɛŋ, ŋ jaŋ mɩɩra jʋʋ mɩ-na Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la.

english_verse: Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
translation_verse: Azaaya fa bʋla pɩ Hezikaaya, “Leŋ dɩ ba tugi tutogo nɛnɛɛ a paa taa mɔpʋla-la.” Ba ŋaa ŋɩɩ ʋ fɩɛlɛ.

english_verse: Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Azaaya bʋl, “Magɩlɩŋ deeŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA jaŋ kaa dagɛ wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ sɩ ʋ jaŋ ŋaa. Ŋ jaŋ cho dɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ daaliimiŋ mʋ sɩpaaŋ naakieliŋ fii koo ŋ jaŋ cho dɩ ʋ mʋ harɩŋ naakieliŋ fii?”

english_verse: “It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
translation_verse: Hezikaaya bʋl, “Ʋ ŋaa mɔlɩɩ nɛ dɩ daaliimiŋ mʋ sɩpaaŋ naakieliŋ fii, ama mɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ mɩɩra mʋ harɩŋ nɛ naakieliŋ fii.”

english_verse: Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway built for King Ahaz. The Lord Is Still with Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Azaaya, Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la ŋmoo niiŋ a pɩ La TƖƖNA, ʋ leŋ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ daaliimiŋ mɩɩra mʋ harɩŋ naakieliŋ fii, lee-la kuoro Ahas lusuŋ-choluŋ sɩ chɩna. Tɩndaara-la sɩ lɩɩ Babɩlɔŋ

english_verse: Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ baal kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Merodak-Baladaŋ nɛ fa ŋaa Babɩlɔŋ kuoro. Ʋ fa ŋaa Baladaŋ nanʋala nɛ. Ʋ sɩ nɩa dɩ Hezikaaya wɩɩla nɛ aŋ duori, ʋ ŋmʋnsɛ teniŋ a joŋ kɩaa pɛ, a tɩŋ nɩaa dɩ ba kaa mʋ dii zile ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
translation_verse: Hezikaaya cheme laa tɩndaara-la, a kɛmba gɔllɔ dagɛ ʋ dʋa-la kala sɩ hɛ ʋ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩɩsɩŋ lɛ: hɔpʋla, sɛlɩmɛ, tegisiŋ, nʋʋ-zɔŋŋɔɔ arɩ ʋ bayuori kɩaa a pɛ kʋŋkala ʋ sɩ kɛnɛ lɛ. Kʋŋkala fa tuo ʋ kuoru dɩa arɩ lee-la kala ʋ sɩɩ beŋ lɛ ʋ bɩ kaa dagɛba.

english_verse: Isaiah asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?” “They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Azaaya Wɩa wʋlaabʋllʋ-la kɔ kuoro Hezikaaya teeŋ a pɩɛsʋ, “Nɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɔ ŋ teeŋ lɩɩ? Wʋbɛɛ nɛ ba kʋ bʋl?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hezikaaya sɩ, “Ba lɩɩ dɩ-bolii nɛ, Babɩlɔŋ nɛ ba lɩɩ.”

english_verse: Then Isaiah told Hezekiah: I have a message for you from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Azaaya bʋla pɩ Hezikaaya, “Jegile nɩɩ wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla:

english_verse: One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left.
translation_verse: Bʋa kʋbala jaŋ yi, kɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ ŋ kuoru dɩa lɛ arɩ kɩalɩŋ ŋ naabalɩmaba sɩ dʋa a kaa kɔ jɩnɩŋ, ba jaŋ chʋŋ ba kala a kaa mʋ Babɩlɔŋ. Kʋŋkala bɩ jaŋ ka. La TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ kɛsɛ ŋ doho nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ arɩ ŋ tɩtɩa bii-lʋlaa a kaa mʋ Babɩlɔŋ a feriba dɩ ba tɩtɩŋ Babɩlɔŋ kuoro dɩa lɛ.”

english_verse: Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told Isaiah, “The message you brought me from the Lord is good.” Hezekiah Dies (
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hezikaaya bʋla pɩ Azaaya, “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla ŋaa wʋzɔŋ nɛ.” Ʋ bʋl ŋɩɩ bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ-na fa bɩɩna La TƖƖNA sɩ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ kala lɛ fɩɛlɩŋ jaŋ hɛ nɩmɛ, wʋwalɩmɩɩ kala bɩ jaŋ jʋʋ-ʋ.

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he made the upper pool and tunnel bring water into Jerusalem, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Hezikaaya sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ ŋaa a laa yɩrɩŋ arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ lu pɩlɩŋ a hɛ lɩɩ-libe lɩɩŋ pɛllɛ kʋʋ jʋʋ ba taŋ tʋɔŋ, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done.
translation_verse: Amɔŋ ma fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, arɩ ʋ nyɩmma Manasɛ fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord God of Israel, will destroy both Jerusalem and Judah! People will hear about it but won't believe it.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ jʋʋ Jerusalɛm arɩ Juda, dɩ nʋʋkala nɛ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la ʋ dɩgɩlaa jaŋ ŋaa zim.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. And he faithfully worshiped the stars in heaven.
translation_verse: Ʋ wasa saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaarɩa-la kala ʋ nyɩmma Hezikaaya fa sɩ ŋmoo giri nɛ, aŋ saa korunuŋ a pɩ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Baal, aŋ pɛ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daaŋ ma, arɩ Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro Ahab fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ. Ʋ fa kpirime aa chʋɔlɛ wɩa-nyuŋ kɩaa kala ma nɛ.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: Ʋ saa fa vʋɩyaa korunuŋ nɛ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ tʋɔŋ, lee-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla arɩ ʋ yɩrɩŋ jaŋ hɛ.

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courts of the temple,
translation_verse: Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la kaalɩsɩ-la balɩa kala lɛ nɛ ʋ saa korunuŋ aa chʋɔlɛ wɩa-nyuŋ kɩaa.

english_verse: and even set up the pole for Asherah there. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own son. He did many sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago the Lord had told David and his son Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: Manasɛ fa joŋ vene-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Asɩra daa-la ʋ sɩ saa a bil Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ nɛ. Ama La TƖƖNA fa bʋla pɩ Devit arɩ ʋ nanʋala Solomoŋ, “Jerusalɛm arɩ mɩ dɩɩ-balɩŋ deeŋ mɩ sɩ lɩɩsa Iziral doho doho kala tʋɔŋ nɛ ba jaŋ zizilmi nɩmɛ a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the commands in the Law of my servant Moses, I will never make them leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: Mɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɩɩ tintee-la lɛ mɩ sɩ joŋo pɩ ba naabalɩmaba, dɩ ba nɛ jaŋ fɩɛlɛ ba sɩaa a to wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩ dagɛba a mʋ tɩgɛ wombie-la kala mɩ tɩntɩnna Mosis sɩ ŋmʋnsa bil dɩ ba tuto.”

english_verse: But the people of Judah disobeyed the Lord. They listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Ama Juda doho nɩaa bɩ La TƖƖNA niiŋ to. Manasɛ leŋe ba yeŋŋi nɛ, a wasa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ a kɩɩ tinteye-la fa sɩ hɛ lee-la La TƖƖNA cheiba ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa kʋ hɔŋ.

english_verse: One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA to ʋ tɩntɩnnaa sɩ ŋaa ʋ wʋlaabʋllaa lɛ a bʋl,

english_verse: King Manasseh has done more disgusting things than the Amorites, and he has led my people to sin by forcing them to worship his idols.
translation_verse: “Juda tinteeŋ kuoro Manasɛ sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ deemba, ba nɛ kɩɩ Amɔrɩ tɩŋŋaa sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔmɔ-la. Ʋ leŋe Juda doho nɩaa kpaarɛ vʋɩyaa nɛ a ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Jerusalem is as sinful as Ahab and the people of Samaria were. So I will wipe out Jerusalem and be done with it, just as someone wipes water off a plate and turns it over to dry.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ Jerusalɛm nɩaa arɩ mɩ fa sɩ dɔgɩsɛ Samarɩa tɩŋŋaa arɩ Iziral kuoro Ahab arɩ ʋ doho nɩaa ŋɩɩ. Mɩ jaŋ kpʋ Jerusalɛm nɩaa kala gbelem gbelem, a nagɛ nɩa sɩ tiisi gbaŋa a tɩɩgɛ lɩɩ-suosoo kala ta aŋ kaa bɩrɩma chu.

english_verse: I will even get rid of my people who survive. They will be defeated and robbed by their enemies.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ vɩa mɩ nɩaa nɩkaana-la ma sɩ bɩ sʋba, aŋ jomba hɛ ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ jaŋ yuo diiba a paa ba kɩaa kaa viiri,

english_verse: My people have done what I hate and have not stopped making me angry since their ancestors left Egypt.
translation_verse: bɛɛ wɩaa ba ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ mɩ sɩɩŋ lɛ, a leŋ mɩ baanɩŋ sii a chɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ ba naabalɩmaba sɩ lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a kaa kɔ arɩ jɩnɩŋ.”

english_verse: Manasseh was guilty of causing the people of Judah to sin and disobey the Lord. He also refused to protect innocent people—he even let so many of them be killed that their blood filled the streets of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Manasɛ ha pɛ kpʋ nɩaa sɩ bɩ wɩɩ cheye a yʋgɛ nɛ a leŋ Jerusalɛm kala ŋaa disiŋ, a pɛ ʋ sɩ leŋe Juda nɩaa ŋaa wʋbɔŋ-la, a ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ La TƖƖNA teeŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his terrible sins, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ Manasɛ sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa, arɩ wʋbɔmɔ-la kala ʋ sɩ ŋaa, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: He died and was buried in Uzza Garden near his palace, and his son Amon became king. King Amon of Judah (
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Manasɛ sʋʋ. Ba joŋu hugi baal kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Uza ŋmaŋkaaŋ lɛ a kpagɛ kuoru dɩa. Ka ʋ nanʋala Amɔŋ dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ. Amɔŋ dii kuoruŋ Juda tinteeŋ lɛ

english_verse: refused to be faithful to the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ʋ vɩa La TƖƖNA nɛ, ʋ naabalɩmaba Wɩa, a bɩ ʋ wombiiŋ to.

english_verse: Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Amɔŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ vʋʋrɛ a kpʋʋ ʋ kuoru dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: He was buried in Uzza Garden. Soon after that, the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon, then they made his son Josiah king. Everything else Amon did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ba joŋu hugi ʋ tɩtɩa bʋa lɛ baal kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Uza ŋmaŋkaaŋ lɛ a kpagɛ kuoru dɩa. Ka ʋ nanʋala Josaaya dii kuoruŋ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ.

english_verse: While Shaphan was at the temple, Hilkiah handed him a book and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.” Shaphan read it,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hɩlɩkaaya, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ bʋla pɩ Safaŋ, nɩɩ-la sɩɩ ŋmʋnsɛ kuoro teniŋ, “Mɩ na teŋ-la lɛ ba sɩ ŋmʋnsɛ Wɩa wombiee hɛ nɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ.” Hɩlɩkaaya joŋ teŋ-la a pɩ Safaŋ ʋ laa karɩmɛ.

english_verse: and ask Hilkiah the high priest to collect from the guards all the money that the people have donated.
translation_verse: “Mʋ Hɩlɩkaaya teeŋ, Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ, a bʋla pʋ dɩ ʋ laa moribie-la ba sɩ kaa kʋ jʋʋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la, kɩalɩŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔ dɩa-la sɩ laa nɩaa teeŋ.

english_verse: Tell Hilkiah to give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. They can use some of the money to pay
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩ Hɩlɩkaaya dɩ ʋ joŋ moribie-la pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ beŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tɩntɩŋŋaa dɩ ba tiŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ wasɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la.

english_verse: the workers, and with the rest of it they can buy wood and stone for the repair work.
translation_verse: Ba tiŋ kapɩntaba arɩ meesimba arɩ dɩɩ-saara-la sɩ pɛ, aŋ yɔɔ daasɩŋ arɩ tabɩɩ-yɛrɛɛ dɩ ba kaa wasɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la.

english_verse: They are honest, so we won't ask them to keep track of the money.
translation_verse: Ama ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba ŋmʋnsɛ moribie-la ba sɩ die niiŋ a bibil, bɛɛ wɩaa ba ŋaa nɩtɩtɩɩba nɛ.”

english_verse: then went back to Josiah and reported, “Your officials collected the money in the temple and gave it to the men supervising the repairs.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Safaŋ mɩɩra mʋ kuoro teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Ŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ laa moribie-la sɩ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ nɛ a joŋo pɩ tɩntɩnnaa arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ beŋ Wɩa dɩa-la tɩntɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it out loud.

translation_verse: Ʋ fa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ La TƖƖNA teeŋ, arɩ Jehoyakim fa sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: It was Zedekiah who finally rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar. The people of Judah and Jerusalem had made the Lord so angry that he turned his back on them. That's why these horrible things were happening.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA baanɩŋ fa chaasa sii Jerusalɛm arɩ Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa nyuŋ nɛ kɩŋkɛŋ, ʋ vɩaba ta. Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dɩ Zedikaaya vɩa Babɩlɔŋ kuoro niiŋ.

english_verse: Each column had been eight meters tall with a bronze cap over one meter high. These caps were decorated with bronze designs—some of them like chains and others like pomegranates.
translation_verse: Kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ libi ba nagɛ jebiee, ba kala fa nagɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ. Ba kʋŋkala leŋiŋ fa ŋaa naakieliŋ chori nɛ. Kɔlɩɩŋ kɩalɩŋ ma sɩ sagɛ jebie-la nyuŋ a nagɛ nyunchuuluŋ, ba leŋiŋ ŋaa naakieliŋ bʋlɩa arɩ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ, ba kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ ŋaa kɩaa sɩ nagɛ kampoi nɛnɛɛ a kpɩɛra golli.

english_verse: near Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar had them killed. Most of the people of Judah had been carried away as captives from their own country. Gedaliah Is Made Ruler of the People Left in Judah (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Rɩbɩla tinteeŋ lee-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hamaf lɛ nɛ kuoro leŋ ba kpʋba. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Juda nɩaa mʋ yoŋ-baga a kagɛ ba tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: As long as Jehoiachin lived, he was paid a daily allowance to buy whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kala Babɩlɔŋ kuoro yie pɩ Jehoyachiŋ moribiee nɛ, bʋa-la kala ʋ sɩ hɛ ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: the Babylonian troops broke through the city wall. That same night, Zedekiah and his soldiers tried to escape through the gate near the royal garden, even though they knew the enemy had the city surrounded. They headed toward the desert,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Babɩlɔŋ laalɩyuoro-la ŋmoo taŋ-la kɛrɛ lo. Zedikaaya arɩ ʋ laalɩyuoroo sii tɩtaŋɩŋ a fá to boi-baal-la sɩ hɛ kɛrɩsɩŋ balɩa pɛgɛ a kpagɛ kuoro ŋmaŋkaaŋ a lɩɩ, arɩ ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ fa sɩ golli tabal-la ma kala. Ba fá to Jɔdaŋ fuo-la dɩɩrɩŋ a mʋ.

english_verse: but the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah, but his soldiers scattered in every direction.
translation_verse: Ama Babɩlɔŋ laalɩyuoro-la kire to ba harɩŋ, a mʋ puuba Jeriko tintee-taalɩ-la lɛ, Zedikaaya laalɩyuoroo kala fá pɩsɛ aŋ kaʋ.

english_verse: Zedekiah was taken to Riblah, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial and found him guilty.
translation_verse: Ba kɛnʋ kaa mʋ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Rɩbɩla, Nebukadineza diiu sarɩya, a joŋ cheeriŋ pʋ.

english_verse: About a month later, in Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king, Nebuzaradan, who was his official in charge of the guards, arrived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nebukadineza sɩ dii kuoruŋ, ʋ jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ nibi, chɛŋ nɔŋ, tapʋl-pɛɩ lɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ Nebuzaradaŋ sɩ ŋaa laalɩyuoro-la sɩɩ pɔ kuoro nɩhɩaŋ, aŋ pɛ ŋaa ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ kɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nebuzaradaŋ leŋ ʋ laalɩyuoroo ŋmoo kɛrɛ-la ba fa sɩ saa golli Jerusalɛm a lo.

english_verse: He led away as prisoners the people left in the city, including those who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradaŋ sɩ ŋaa nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔ kuoro nɩhɩaŋ kɛsɛ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ ka Jerusalɛm lɛ, a kaa mʋ yoŋ-baga a pɛ nɩalɩŋ Nebukadineza fa sɩ laa sɩpaaŋ kɛsɛ mʋ lɛ.

english_verse: Only some of the poorest people were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Ama Nebuzaradaŋ leŋ summo-la dɔnsʋŋ nɛ dɩ ba tɩtɩŋ girep tɩɩsɩŋ bagɩsɩŋ lɛ arɩ bagɩsɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers took the two bronze columns that stood in front of the temple, the ten movable bronze stands, and the large bronze bowl called the Sea. They broke them into pieces so they could take the bronze to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Babɩlɔŋ laalɩyuoro-la ŋmoo kɔlɩɩŋ jebie-la sɩ chɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la sɩpaaŋ giri, a yɛrɛ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ libi ba nagɛ torukoba a kɛŋ naasɩŋ a vɩvɛŋ, a pɛ kɔlɩɩŋ taasɩ-gbaŋ-gugulii-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ mʋga lɛ. Ba sɩ yɛrɛ kɩalɩŋ, ba paa kɔlɩɩ-la kala a kaa mʋ Babɩlɔŋ.

english_verse: They carried off the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, snuffers, and also the dishes for incense,
translation_verse: Ba fa pɛ paa kɩaa deemba ma kaa viiri nɛ: Puposuŋ, safʋlba, kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kaa wasɛ chaaŋ ŋmɛnɩŋ tɩta, gbansɩŋ arɩ kɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ kala ba sɩ kɛŋ kɔlɩɩŋ ŋaa a kaa tɩtɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ.

english_verse: as well as the fire pans and the sprinkling bowls. Nebuzaradan ordered his soldiers to take everything made of gold or silver.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradaŋ fa pɛ paa kɩalɩŋ kala ba sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ sɩ chaasa zɔŋ koo hɔpʋla kaa ŋaa nɛ, kʋmɩsɩrɩ gbansɩŋ arɩ nyiniŋ hɛntɛrɛɛ.

english_verse: The pile of bronze from the columns, the stands, and the large bowl that Solomon had made for the temple was too large to be weighed.
translation_verse: Kɔlɩɩ-la Solomoŋ fa sɩ kaa libi jebie-la balɩa sɩ chɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la sɩpaaŋ, kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ torukoba a kɛŋ naasɩŋ a vɩvɛŋ arɩ taasɩ-gbaŋ-gugulii-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ mʋga, ba fa yʋga kɩɩ magɩsɩŋ nɛ.

english_verse: Next, Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah his assistant, and three temple officials.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradaŋ fa pɛ kɛsɛ Sɛraaya sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ nɛ arɩ Zefanaaya ma sɩɩ tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ, arɩ nɩalɩŋ batori sɩɩ pɔ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la boyee.

english_verse: Then he arrested one of the army commanders, the king's five personal advisors, and the officer in charge of gathering the troops for battle. He also found
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ ha sɩ ka tabal-la lɛ, ʋ kɛsɛ nɩhɩaŋ-la sɩɩ beŋ laalɩyuoroo arɩ nɩaa banɔŋ sɩ bʋl wɩaa chɩchagɩlɛ kuoro. Ʋ fa kɛŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ-la ma sɩɩ dɩɩsɛ tintee-la nɩaa nɛ, a pɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ dɔnsʋŋ mahɩŋ batori sɩ hɛ tabal-la lɛ.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam to rule the few people still living in Judah.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Nebukadineza lɩɩsɛ Ahɩkam nanʋala Gedalia sɩ ŋaa Safaŋ nihiŋ dɩ ʋ bibeŋ nɩkaana-la fa sɩ ka Juda tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: When the army officers and troops heard that Gedaliah was their ruler, the officers met with him at Mizpah. These men were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, and Jaazaniah from Maacah.
translation_verse: Juda tinteeŋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩŋ arɩ ba nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ nɩa arɩ Babɩlɔŋ kuoro lɩɩsɛ Gedalia nɛ dɩ ʋ bibemba, ba sii kɔ ʋ teeŋ Mɩzɩpa lɛ. Nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɔ yɩraa nɛ ŋ-la: Nɛtanɩa nanʋala Ɩsɩmɛl, Karɩa nanʋala Johanaŋ, Tanhʋmɛf nanʋala Sɛraaya sɩ ŋaa Netofa tɩɩna, Jaazanɩa sɩ ŋaa Maaka tɩɩna arɩ ba nɩaa.

english_verse: Gedaliah said to them, “Everything will be fine, I promise. We don't need to be afraid of the Babylonian rulers, if we live here peacefully and do what Nebuchadnezzar says.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Gedalia ŋmɩɛsa pɩ ba dɩ ba nɩaa a bʋl, “Má sɩ́ leŋe dɩ fawʋllʋŋ kɛmma a tɩŋ Babɩlɔŋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la wɩaa. Má hɔŋ Juda tintee-la lɛ a to Babɩlɔŋ kuoro niiŋ, wɩaa jaŋ vɛŋ woruŋ pɩma.”

english_verse: Ishmael was from the royal family. And about two months after Gedaliah began his rule, Ishmael and ten other men went to Mizpah. They killed Gedaliah and his officials, including those from Judah and those from Babylonia.
translation_verse: Chɛŋ-pɛɩ lɛ nɛ Nɛtanɩa nanʋala Ɩsɩmɛl, sɩ ŋaa Ɛlɩsama nihiŋ a ŋaa kuoro doho nʋʋ kɛsɛ baalaa fii ba kɔ Mɩzɩpa, a kpʋ Gedalia arɩ Juda nɩaa arɩ Babɩlɔŋ tɩmma-la kala fa sɩ hɛ ʋ teeŋ.

english_verse: After that, the army officers and all the people in Mizpah, whether important or not, were afraid of what the Babylonians might do. So they left Judah and went to Egypt. Jehoiachin Is Set Free (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ, fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ laalɩyuori-hɩasɩ-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ Mɩzɩpa lɛ, nɩbiisiŋ arɩ nɩbalaa kala, a tɩŋ Babɩlɔŋ tɩŋŋaa wɩaa. Ba lɩɩ fá mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ. Ba lɩɩsɛ Jehoyachiŋ bɩnɩŋ dɩa lɛ

english_verse: Evil-Merodach was kind to Jehoiachin and honored him more than any of the other kings held prisoner there.
translation_verse: Evil-Merodak fa kɛŋ Jehoyachiŋ nɛ woruŋ, a pʋ dɩchɩnɩŋ a kɩɩ kuorusu-la dɔnsʋŋ kala ba fa sɩ kɛsɛ tɔ bɩnɩŋ dɩa Babɩlɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Jehoiachin was even allowed to wear regular clothes, and he ate at the king's table every day.
translation_verse: Kuoro fa leŋe Jehoyachiŋ wuri ʋ dansarɩka gɛnnɩŋ ta nɛ aŋ lɩlaalɛ ʋ tɩtɩa gɛnnɩŋ, a didii kɩaa kuoro dɩa lɛ tapʋlɩɩ kala.

english_verse: Japheth was the father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras, and they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
translation_verse: Jafɛf ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ fa ŋaa: Goma, Magɔg, Madaɩ, Javaŋ, Tubal, Mɛsɛk arɩ Tɩras.

english_verse: Abraham and his slave woman Keturah had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan.
translation_verse: Abɩraham sɩ bil haal-la aŋ bɩ jaa, baa yɩrɛ Ketura. Ʋ hambolibiisiŋ nɛ ŋ-la: Zimiraŋ, Jokisaŋ, Mɛdaŋ, Midiaŋ, Ɩsɩbak arɩ Sʋa. Jokisaŋ ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ Sɛba arɩ Dɛdaŋ.

english_verse: Ethiopia was also the father of Nimrod, the world's first mighty warrior.
translation_verse: Kus nɛ lʋl Nɩmɩrɔd, ʋ sii waa a ŋaa laalɩyuori-duo dʋnɩa lɛ.

english_verse: Egypt was the ancestor of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
translation_verse: Mizirem doho nɩaa nɛ ŋ-la: Lud tɩŋŋaa, Anam tɩŋŋaa, Lɛhab tɩŋŋaa, Nafituhi tɩŋŋaa,

english_verse: Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
translation_verse: Goma ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ fa ŋaa: Asɩkɛnas, Rɩfaf arɩ Togaama.

english_verse: Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
translation_verse: Javaŋ ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ fa ŋaa: Ɛlɩsa, Taasɩs, Kɩtɩm arɩ Rodanim. Ham doho nɩaa

english_verse: Ethiopia was the ancestor of Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah was the ancestor of Sheba and Dedan.
translation_verse: Kus ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ fa ŋaa: Sɛba, Havɩla, Sabɩta, Raama arɩ Sabɩtɛka. Raama ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ: Sɛɛba arɩ Dɛdaŋ.

english_verse: Canaan's oldest son was Sidon; his other son was Heth.
translation_verse: Kɛnaŋ nɛ lʋl Sɩdɔŋ, ʋ bii-hɩaŋ, Hiti tɩŋŋaa,

english_verse: Shem was the ancestor of Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech; they were the ancestors of the kingdoms named after them.
translation_verse: Sɛm hambolibiisiŋ nɛ: Ɛlam, Asu, Afaza, Lud arɩ Aram. Aram ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ: Yus, Hul, Gɛda arɩ Mɛsɛk.

english_verse: Arpachshad was Shelah's father and Eber's grandfather.
translation_verse: Afaza nɛ lʋl Sɛla, ʋ ma sii lʋl Ɛbɛ.

english_verse: the ancestor of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab.
translation_verse: arɩ Ofi, Havɩla arɩ Jobab. Ba kala ŋaa Jɔkɩtaŋ biiriŋ nɛ. Sɛm doho nɩaa a kaa mʋ yi Abɩraham lɛ

english_verse: Abraham was the father of Isaac and Ishmael.
translation_verse: Abɩraham hambolibiisiŋ nɛ ŋ-la: Aɩzɩk arɩ Ɩsɩmɛl.

english_verse: Midian was the father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. Esau's Family (Genesis
translation_verse: Midiaŋ ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ: Ɛfa, Ɛfɛ, Hanɔk, Abɩda arɩ Ɛlɩdaa. Nɩaa deemba kala ŋaa Ketura doho nɩaa nɛ.

english_verse: Abraham's son Isaac was the father of Esau and Jacob.
translation_verse: Abɩraham bie Aɩzɩk ma hambolibiisiŋ nɛ Ɛsɔ arɩ Iziral.

english_verse: Esau was the father of Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Ɛsɔ hambolibiisiŋ yɩraa nɛ: Ɛlɩfas, Rɛwɛl, Jeyus, Jalam arɩ Kora.

english_verse: Reuel was the father of Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. The First Edomites and Their Kings (Genesis
translation_verse: Rɛwɛl hambolibiisiŋ nɛ ŋaa: Nahaf, Zɛra, Sama arɩ Mɩza. Sɛɛ tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Ɛdɔm lɛ

english_verse: Before kings ruled in Israel, Bela son of Beor ruled the country of Edom from its capital of Dinhabah.
translation_verse: Kuoroo deemba nɛ laa sɩpaaŋ dii kuoruŋ Ɛdɔm tinteeŋ lɛ aŋ ka pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa: Bioo nanʋala Bɛla, ʋ fa hɔŋ ba tabalɩŋ Dɩnɩhaba lɛ nɛ a dii kuoruŋ.

english_verse: Seir was the father of Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
