translation_verse: Ba kala pɛ ba sɩpaalaaraa lɛ a ŋmɩɛsɛ, dɩ ba nɛ vɩa nii-la dɩ ŋmɩaŋ-la diiba. Ba ŋmɩɛsa arɩ ba jaŋ fɩɛlɛ ba sɩaa a to wombie-la Wɩa sɩ to ʋ tɩntɩnna Mosis lɛ a joŋo pɩba, a pɛ wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA sɩ daga arɩ ʋ niiriŋ lɛ. Ba sɩ tɔ boŋ-la bʋl wɩɩ-la nɛ ŋ-la,

english_verse: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
translation_verse: Dɩ tintee-wogusu-la nɩaa nɛ kɛŋ mɩaa koo kɩaa dɔnsʋŋ kɔ dɩ ba yallɛ chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ koo tapʋl-zɔŋ kala chɛɛŋ, la bɩ jaŋ yɔɔ. Jɩsɩŋ balɩpɛ na-kala, la jaŋ leŋ dɩ la tinteeŋ pɩna wiesi, aŋ joŋ nɩaa chɩŋŋaa kala ma chɛba.

english_verse: Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Jɩna na-kala, la kʋŋkala jaŋ kɩɛsɛ moribiee mʋa mʋa dɩ ba kaa tɩtɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tɩntɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ kaa yɔɔ boroboro-la sɩɩ daŋ teebʋl nyuŋ, tapʋlɩɩ kala mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa arɩ kʋnyɩgaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa, a pɛ chɛ-wiesii-la Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa lɛ. Chɛŋ-falɩŋ gbielee kɩaa arɩ gbielisi-la dɔnsʋŋ kɩaa, arɩ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kʋzɔmɔ-la, arɩ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ ba sɩ jaŋ ŋaa a pɩɩsɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ta, a pɛ wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ kala sɩ maga dɩ la ŋaa la Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ.

english_verse: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
translation_verse: La-na Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa, Levi doho naa, arɩ la nɩkaanaa kala tɔnsɔ nɛ dɩ la na jɩna na-kala tʋɔŋ bʋa-la lɛ dɩa na-kala nɩaa sɩ maga ba kɛŋ daasɩŋ kɔ dɩ la kaa nyɩgɛ Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa La TƖƖNA Wɩa koru-la nyuŋ, arɩ ba sɩ ŋmʋnsɛ ŋɩɩ hɛ Wɩa wombiiŋ teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
translation_verse: La bɩra sɛyɛ arɩ jɩna kala la jaŋ kɛŋ la baga kʋdii-bumbumba arɩ tɩɩ-nɛŋ bumbuŋ na-kala kɔ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-balɩŋ.

english_verse: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
translation_verse: La jaŋ kɛŋ la hambolibii bumbumba a kɔ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa sɩɩ tɩŋ nɩmɛ teeŋ a joŋo hɛ Wɩa nɩsɩŋ lɛ, la jaŋ kɛŋ la nɛsɩŋ, piesee arɩ bʋʋnaa ma bii-bumbumba kɔ nɩmɛ a joŋo pɩ Wɩa, arɩ ba sɩ ŋmʋnsɛ ŋɩɩ hɛ Wɩa wombiee tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
translation_verse: La ha bɩra jaŋ kɛŋ la mɩɩ-falaa, la tɩɩ-nɛŋ bumbumba, girep nɛnɛɛ sɩ-falɩŋ arɩ la olif nʋʋ-bumbuŋ kaa kɔ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ a joŋo pɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa. La jaŋ kɛŋ la kʋdiilee kpaa leree fii a joŋ kʋbala kaa kʋ pɩ Levi doho nɩaa, bɛɛ wɩaa ba nɩɩ laa kpaalɩŋ fii tʋɔŋ kʋbala deeŋ tasɩ-la kala lɛ la sɩɩ tɩŋ.

english_verse: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara Arɔŋ doho nɩaa tʋɔŋ nɛ maga dɩ ʋ pɛ Levi doho nɩaa lɛ dɩ ba laa kpaalɩŋ fii tʋɔŋ kʋbala deeŋ. Levi doho nɩalɩŋ ma jaŋ laa kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kaa kpaa leree fii a joŋ kʋbala-la a pɩ Wɩa, a ma kaa kpaa leree fii a joŋ kʋbala bil Wɩa dɩa chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩ-biliŋ.

english_verse: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala, maga ba kɩɛsɛ mɩaa, girep nɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ arɩ olif nʋʋŋ nɛ, a kaa mʋ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩa-la lɛ ba sɩɩ bil Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tɩntɩnnɩ kɩaa, arɩ lee-la Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa, boi-pɔɔrɔɔ arɩ yɩɩlɩ yɩɩraa sɩɩ jʋʋ. La bɩ jaŋ vɩa la Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ ta.”

english_verse: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
translation_verse: Tintee-la nɩhɩasɩŋ fa hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ nɛ, ka nɩkaanaa tɔnsɛ dɩ ba lɩɩsɛ nɩbala nɩaa fii kala tʋɔŋ dɩ ba mʋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm, tabal-la sɩ bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ lɛ, ka dɩ nɩaa nibi-la kʋkaanaa ma hɔŋ ba tasɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩaa bɛsɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɛŋ ba tɩtɩa lɩɩ a sɛɩ arɩ ba jaŋ hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
translation_verse: Iziral tinteeŋ ba sɩ kaa kpaa leree sɩpaalaaraa fa hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ nɛ. Iziral tɩŋŋaa dɔnsʋŋ, a pɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa, Levi doho nɩaa, nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ, arɩ Solomoŋ tɩntɩnnaa doho nɩaa fa hɔŋ ba tɩtɩa tinteyee lɛ nɛ Juda tasɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were
translation_verse: a pɛ ʋ naambiiriŋ Gabaɩ arɩ Salaɩ lɛ. Bɛnjamɩŋ ma doho nɩaa fa ŋaa zɔlɔ nibi arɩ mara arɩ chori nɛ a hɔŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
translation_verse: Zikiri nanʋala Jowɛl nɛ fa ŋaa ba tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ tʋɔŋ nɩhɩaŋ, Hasɛnʋa nanʋala Juda ma nɛ fa ŋaa nɩɩ-la sɩ tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ a bibeŋ tabal-la.

english_verse: Four priests settled in Jerusalem. The first was Jedaiah; he was the son of Joiarib and the uncle of Jachin.
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa ma nɛ ŋ-la: Joyarib nanʋala Jedaaya arɩ Jakɩŋ.

english_verse: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
translation_verse: Sɛraaya sɩ ŋaa Hɩlɩkaaya nanʋala, aŋ ŋaa Mesulam ma nihiŋ. Ʋ naabalɩmaba dɔnsʋŋ nɛ fa, Zadɔk, Mɛrayɔf arɩ Ahitub fa sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ.

english_verse: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa ma nɛ ŋ-la: Sɛmaaya sɩ ŋaa Hasub nanʋala, aŋ ŋaa Azirikam ma nihiŋ. Ʋ doho nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ ma nɛ Hasabɩa, arɩ Buni.

english_verse: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
translation_verse: Sabɩtaɩ arɩ Jozabad ma nɛ fa ŋaa Levi doho nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ tɩntɩmɩa-la sɩ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la jeeŋ harɩŋ sɩpaalaaraa.

english_verse: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
translation_verse: Mɩka nanʋala Matanɩa sɩ ŋaa Zabidi nihiŋ, aŋ ŋaa Asaf doho nʋʋ, ʋ nɛ yie laa nɩalɩŋ sɩpaaŋ ba lʋlɔllɛ Wɩa aŋ pɛ chʋhchʋɔlʋ. Bakɩbʋkɩa ma nɛ faa tɩgɛ Matanɩa lɛ. Samʋa nanʋala Abɩda sɩ ŋaa Gala nihiŋ, aŋ ŋaa Jedutuŋ doho nʋʋ ma nɛ faa tɩgʋ lɛ.

english_verse: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
translation_verse: Baala-la fa sɩɩ pɔ boi-baalaa ma nɛ ŋ-la: Akub, Talɩmɔŋ arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ dɔnsʋŋ, ba kala fa ŋaa nɩaa zɔlɔ mahɩŋ batori arɩ fii arɩ balɩa nɛ.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩkaana-la, a pɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa fa hɔŋ ba tɩtɩa ba tinteyee lɛ nɛ Juda tasɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ fa hɛ Jerusalɛm dundolo kʋbala lɛ nɛ baa yɩrɛ Ɔfɛl. Zɩha arɩ Gɛsɩpa nɛ faa bemba.

english_verse: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
translation_verse: Banɩ nanʋala Uzi sɩ ŋaa Hasabaɩ ma nihiŋ nɛ fa ŋaa Levi doho nɩhɩaŋ. Ʋ doho nɩaa nɛ Matanɩa, Mɩka arɩ Asaf. Ba nɛ nyɩŋ-nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ beŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ yɩɩ yɩɩlaa Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ.

english_verse: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
translation_verse: Yɩɩl yɩɩra-la fa to ŋɩɩ Kuoro Devit sɩ daga nɛ, a yɩyɩɩ yɩɩlaa tapʋlɩɩ kala.

english_verse: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
translation_verse: Mɛsɛzabɛl nanʋala Pɛtahɩa sɩ ŋaa Juda nanʋala Zɛra doho nɩaa dɔŋɔ, nɛ faa chagɩlɛ kuoro wɩɩ na-kala sɩ mʋ tɩgɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa lɛ.

english_verse: Enrimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
translation_verse: Ɛŋ Rimoŋ, Zora, Jamʋf,

english_verse: Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah. In fact, they settled the towns from Beersheba in the south to Hinnom Valley in the north.
translation_verse: Zanʋa, Adulam, arɩ ba tabiisi-la dɔnsʋŋ sɩ hɛ Lakɩs arɩ ʋ ŋmaŋkaanɩŋ lɛ, dɔnsʋŋ ma hɛ Azɛka arɩ ʋ tabiisiŋ lɛ. Ba fa hɔŋ Bɛɛsɩba lɛ ŋɩɩ nɛ a mʋ yi Hɩnɔm fuonaaŋ.

english_verse: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
translation_verse: Tasɩŋ deemba lɛ nɛ Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ lɩɩ Geba hɛ: Mɩkɩmas, Aɩja, Bɛtɛl arɩ ʋ tabiisiŋ,

english_verse: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
translation_verse: Anatɔf, Nɔb, Ananɩa,

english_verse: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
translation_verse: Hazɔ, Rama, Gitem,

english_verse: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
translation_verse: Hadid, Zeboim, Nɛbalat,

english_verse: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
translation_verse: Lod, Ono, arɩ kʋŋaarɩ-gɔgɔɔ fuonaaŋ.

english_verse: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩalɩŋ sɩ lɩɩ Juda tinteeŋ ba sɩ kaa kpaa kpaa leree, ba dɔnsʋŋ fa hɔŋ Bɛnjamɩŋ tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩalɩŋ sɩ mɩɩra to Sɩɛlɩtɩɛl nanʋala Zerubabɛl arɩ Jesua harɩŋ a lɩɩ yoŋ-baga kɔ yɩraa nɛ ŋ-la: Sɛraaya, Jɛrɩmaaya, Ɛzɩra,

english_verse: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
translation_verse: Amarɩa, Maluk, Hatus,

english_verse: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
translation_verse: Sɛkanɩa, Rehum, Mɛrɛmɔf,

english_verse: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
translation_verse: Ido, Ginetoŋ, Abija,

english_verse: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
translation_verse: Mɩjamɩŋ, Mʋadɩa, Bɩlɩga

english_verse: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
translation_verse: Sɛmaaya, Joyarib, Jedaaya,

english_verse: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
translation_verse: Salu, Amɔk, Hɩlɩkaaya, Jedaaya. Nɩaa deemba nɛ fa ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ ba tɩntɩnnɩ dɔnsʋŋ Jesua mɩɩsɩŋ bʋa lɛ.

english_verse: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa nɛ ŋ-la: Jesua, Binui, Kadɩmɩɛl, Sɛrɛbɩa, Juda arɩ Matanɩa, a pɛ ʋ dɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ lɛ nɛ faa beŋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ yɩɩ yɩɩlaa a lʋlɔllɛ Wɩa.

english_verse: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
translation_verse: Bakɩbʋkɩa arɩ Uni nɛ ŋaa nɩalɩŋ ba dɩ ba sɩɩ tɩŋ. Ba yie chɩna chaasɛ ba nɛ yɩɩlaa dɩ-yɩɩlɩŋ a laa hɩhɛ.

english_verse: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
translation_verse: Joyakim nyɩmma nɛ fa Jesua, Ɛlɩasɩb ma nyɩmma nɛ Joyakim, Joyada ma nyɩmma nɛ Ɛlɩasɩb,

english_verse: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
translation_verse: Jonataŋ ma nyɩmma nɛ Joyada, Jadʋa ma nyɩmma nɛ Jonataŋ.

english_verse: When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Bʋa-la Joyakim fa sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ, nɩaa deemba nɛ fa ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa dɩa dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ: Sɛraaya dɩa nɩaa tʋɔŋ, Mɛraya nɛ fa ŋaa ba nɩhɩaŋ. Jɛrɩmaaya ma dɩa nɩaa tʋɔŋ, Hananaaya nɛ fa ŋaa ba nɩhɩaŋ.

english_verse: Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah. The Priestly and Levite Families
translation_verse: Hɩlɩkaaya ma dɩa nɩaa tʋɔŋ, Hasabɩa nɛ fa ŋaa ba nɩhɩaŋ. Jedaaya dɩa nɩaa tʋɔŋ, Nɛtanɛl nɛ fa ŋaa ba nɩhɩaŋ.

english_verse: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
translation_verse: Daarus sɩ dii Pɛsɩa tinteeŋ kuoruŋ, bʋa-la lɛ nɛ ba ŋmʋnsɛ Levi doho nɩaa dɩa dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ yɩraa a bil. Nɩaa deemba nɛ fa ŋaa ba nɩhɩasɩŋ: Ɛlɩasɩb, Joyada, Johanaŋ arɩ Jadʋa, a saa pɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa dɩa dɩa yɩraa lɛ.

english_verse: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa dɩa dɩa nɩhɩasɩŋ, a chɩŋ Ɛlɩasɩb nanʋala Johanaŋ lɛ, ba kala nɛ ba ŋmʋnsa hɛ kuoroo wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
translation_verse: Levi doho nɩaa sɩpaalaaraa nɛ fa ŋ-la: Hasabɩa, Sɛrɛbɩa, Kadɩmɩɛl nanʋala Jesua, arɩ ba tɩntɩnnɩ dɔsʋŋ ba sɩ kaa kpaa bugoo, balɩa yie chɩna chaasɛ dɔŋɔ a yɩɩ yɩɩlaa dɩdɛnnɛ Wɩa a lʋlɔllʋ, buguŋ dɔŋɔ yɩɩ dɔŋɔ laa hɩhɛ arɩ Wɩa tɩntɩnna Devit sɩ dagɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ ŋaa boi-pɔɔrɔɔ a pʋpɔ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩɩsɩ-la sɩ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la boi-baalaa niiŋ nɛ ŋ-la: Matanɩa, Bakɩbʋkɩa, Obadaaya, Mesulam, Talɩmɔŋ arɩ Akub.

english_verse: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
translation_verse: Nɩaa deemba kala fa hɛ nɩmɛ nɛ a tɩtɩŋ ba tɩntɩŋŋaa, bʋa-la lɛ Jesua nanʋala Joyakim fa sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ. Ʋ fa ŋaa Jozadak ma nihiŋ nɛ. Bʋa-la tɩtɩa lɛ nɛ Nɛhɩmaaya fa ŋaa ba tinteeŋ nɩhɩaŋ, ka Ɛzɩra ma fa ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara aŋ pɛ ŋaa Wɩa teniŋ kerichi. Ba joŋ Jerusalɛm kɛrɛ-la hɛ Wɩa nɩsɩŋ lɛ

english_verse: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la ba sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ba joŋ Jerusalɛm jebii-la a hɛ La TƖƖNA nɩsɩŋ lɛ, ba yɩrɛ Levi doho nɩaa ba lɩɩ Juda sɛmɛ na-kala nɛ dɩ ba kʋ gbieli arɩ tʋɔtɔrʋŋ a yɩɩ yɩɩlaa a chɩgɩsɛ buguloo, a du chenniŋ arɩ kɔnɛba a dɛnnɛ La TƖƖNA.

english_verse: The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth.
translation_verse: Dɔnsʋŋ lɩɩ Bɛf Gɩlɩgal, Geba arɩ Azɩmavɛf. Yɩɩlɩ yɩra-la fa saa ba tasɩŋ a golli Jerusalɛm nɛ.

english_verse: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
translation_verse: Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa sɩ pɩɩsɛ ba tɩtɩa disiniŋ ta dɛrɛ arɩ ba Wɩɩchʋɔlɛ wombiiŋ sɩ dagɛ ŋɩɩ, ba pɩɩsɛ nɩalɩŋ, boi-baala-la arɩ jebii-la ma disiniŋ ta.

english_verse: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ leŋ Juda nɩaa sɩpaalaaraa jɩl jebii-la nyuŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ lɩɩsɛ yɩɩlɩ yɩraa sɩ yʋga bugoo balɩa dɩ ba lʋlɔllɛ Wɩa. Bugo-la dɔŋɔ jɩl jebii-la nyuŋ a mʋmʋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ, a chaasɛ Nɛ-bɩnɩŋ Boi-baalɩŋ.

english_verse: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them.
translation_verse: Hosaaya arɩ Juda sɩpaalaara-la kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ fa to ba harɩŋ,

english_verse: Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
translation_verse: arɩ Azarɩa, Ɛzɩra, Mesulam,

english_verse: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Juda, Bɛnjamɩŋ, Sɛmaaya, Jɛrɩmaaya,

english_verse: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
translation_verse: a pɛ ba yɩɩl yɩɩrɩ dɔnsʋŋ deemba lɛ: Sɛmaaya, Azarɛl, Mɩlalaɩ, Gɩlalaɩ, Maayɩ, Nɛtanɛl, Juda arɩ Hanani, ba kala fa kori Wɩa tɩntɩnna Devit yɩɩlɩ yɩɩrɩ kɩaa nɛ. Ɛzɩra sɩ ŋaa Wɩa teniŋ kerichi nɛ fa laa ba nɩalɩŋ sɩ kɩɛla sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ mʋ yi Lɩɩ-bulo Boi-baalɩŋ, ba ha mʋmʋ, a mʋ jɩl lusuŋ-chol-sɩa-la ba sɩ to jʋjʋʋ Devit taŋ-la, a joŋ jebii-la ŋɩɩ a mʋ kieli Devit dɩa a mʋ Lɩɩŋ Boi-baal-la sɩ hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ.

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Yɩɩlɩ yɩɩra-la buguŋ dɔŋɔ ma to jebii-la nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ a mʋmʋ. Mɩ ma jɩl jebii-la ba harɩŋ, mɩ dɩ sɩpaalaara-la kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ. La mʋ kieli tabʋʋ-pumoo dɩɩ-leŋii-la a mʋ Je-bii Jalɩɩ-la.

english_verse: Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard,
translation_verse: La lɩɩ nɩmɛ a mʋ Efirem Boi-baalɩŋ, a mʋ Jesana Boi-baalɩŋ, a mʋ Chenfilee Boi-baalɩŋ, a mʋ Hananɛl Dɩɩ-duduoŋ arɩ dɩɩ-leŋii-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Zɔlɔ, a kɛŋ ŋɩɩ mʋ yi Piesee boi-baalɩŋ. La sɩ mʋ yi nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔ leriŋ boi-baalɩŋ, la chɩŋ.

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ yɩɩlɩ yɩɩrɩ bugo-la balɩa sɩɩ lɔllɛ Wɩa chɩŋ ba dɩchɩnaa Wɩa dɩa lɛ. Mɩ ma chɩŋ, mɩ dɩ sɩpaalaara-la kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ,

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: a pɛ nɩaa deemba sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa lɛ: Ɛlɩakɩm, Maasɛya, Mɩnɩamɩŋ, Mɩkaaya, Elionai, Zɛkarɩya arɩ Hananaaya, ba kala kori nyilliŋ.

english_verse: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
translation_verse: Nɩaa deemba ma nɛ pɛ: Maasɛya, Sɛmaaya, Elieza, Uzi, Jehohanaŋ, Malɩkɩja, Ɛlam arɩ Ɛza. Jɛzɩrahɩa nɛ laa yɩɩlɩ yɩɩra-la sɩpaaŋ baa yɩɩ.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la ba kpʋ kɩaa yʋgɛ nɛ woruŋ a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ, aŋ jʋjʋɔsɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa Wɩa leŋe ba tʋɔŋ faasa tɔrɛ nɛ. Haalaa arɩ hambiisiŋ kala nɛ faa jʋɔsʋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ paala hɛ dɩ-bolii ma, ŋ jaŋ wuo nɩɩ nɩaa sɩ jʋɔsa a ŋɩŋaa goŋ Jerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ nɛ ba lɩɩsɛ nɩaa ba bibeŋ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩɩsɩŋ, lee-la nɩaa sɩ yie kɩɛsɛ kɩaa arɩ ba kʋdii falaa kaa kʋʋ bil, a pɛ kpaalɩŋ fii tʋɔŋ kʋbala-la ba sɩ yie joŋo pɩ Wɩa lɛ. Bagɩsɩ-la sɩ golli Jerusalɛm lɛ, ba fa yie kɩɛsɛ kɩaa nɛ a kaa kʋ bil chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩɩsɩ-la lɛ a pɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa a nagɛ Wɩa wombiiŋ ʋ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto sɩ dagɛ ŋɩɩ, bɛɛ wɩaa Juda nɩaa tʋɔŋ fa tɔrɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ tɩŋ Wɩa tɩntɩŋŋaa lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ sɩ maga dɩ ba ŋaa pɩ Wɩa, ŋɩɩ nɛ yɩɩlɩ yɩraa-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ ma sɩɩ pɔ leriŋ tɩŋ ba tɩntɩŋŋaa arɩ kuoro Devit arɩ ʋ nanʋala Solomoŋ sɩ dagɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Kuoro Devit arɩ Asaf mɩɩsɩŋ bʋa lɛ, ba fa kɛŋ nɩaa nɛ sɩ yie laa ba sɩpaaŋ ba yɩɩ yɩɩlaa a dɩdɛnnɛ Wɩa, aŋ lʋlɔllʋ.

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Zerubabɛl arɩ Nɛhɩmaaya ma mɩɩsɩŋ bʋa lɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala yie kɩɛsɛ kɩaa nɛ tapʋlɩɩ kala aa pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ yɩɩ yɩɩlaa arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ pɔ boi-baalaa. Nɩalɩŋ yie joŋ kɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ a pɩ Levi doho nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ, ba ma laa a lɩɩsɛ Arɔŋ doho nɩaa kɩaa pɩba.

english_verse: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la ba faasa karɩmɛ teŋ-la Mosis sɩ ŋmʋnsa ʋ lɩɩ nɛ nʋʋkala nɩɩ. Teŋ-la tʋɔŋ nɛ ba na arɩ ʋ bɩ maga dɩ ba leŋ dɩ Amɔrɩ tɩɩna koo Mʋab tɩɩna kala guoli Wɩa nɩaa tʋɔŋ,

english_verse: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
translation_verse: bɛɛ wɩaa ba fa bɩ kʋdiilee arɩ lɩɩŋ kaa kʋ cheme pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, aŋ mɩɩra joŋ kɩaa kpal Balam ka dɩ ʋ kʋ ŋmɩɛsa hɛ ba lɛ.

english_verse: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma-la sɩ nɩɩ Wɩa wombii-la ʋ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto, ba chaarɛ nɩwogusu-la kala sɩ guoli ba tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
translation_verse: Ka dɩ ba na ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ, ba fa joŋ Ɛlɩasɩb sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara nɛ hɛ ʋ bibeŋ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩɩsɩ-la sɩ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la lɛ. Ʋ dɩ Tobia wɩaa faa jʋʋ nɛ woruŋ.

english_verse: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
translation_verse: Ʋ joŋ dɩɩ-bal kʋbala a pɩ Tobia lee-la ba sɩɩ bil kɩaa deemba: mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩaa, kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ arɩ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la tɩntɩnnɩ kɩaa, a pɛ mɩaa kpaalɩŋ fii tʋɔŋ kʋbala ba sɩ yie joŋo pɩ Wɩa lɛ, arɩ girep nɛnɛɛ sɩ-falɩŋ, nʋʋ-la ba sɩ yie joŋo pɩ Levi doho nɩaa, yɩɩlɩ yɩɩraa arɩ boi-pɔɔrɔɔ, a saa pɛ kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ yie kɩɛsa pɩ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa lɛ.

english_verse: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
translation_verse: Ama bʋa-la lɛ wɩaa deemba kala sɩɩ ŋaa, mɩ fa tuo Jerusalɛm lɛ. Atazɛzɛs sɩ dii Babɩlɔŋ tinteeŋ kuoruŋ ʋ jɩsɩŋ mara arɩ fii arɩ balɩa lɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ, dɩ mɩ mɩɩra mʋ ʋ teeŋ. Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ bʋa kʋbala lɛ, mɩ sʋl wombiiŋ ʋ teeŋ

english_verse: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
translation_verse: a mɩɩra kɔ Jerusalɛm. Mɩ sɩ kɔ nɛ mɩ nɩɩ wʋbɔŋ-la Ɛlɩasɩb fa sɩ ŋaa, ʋ sɩ joŋ dɩa sɩ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la kaalɩsɩŋ lɛ a pɩ Tobɩa.

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: Mɩ tʋɔŋ fa chaasa chei nɛ woruŋ, mɩ paa Tobia kɩaa kala sɩ hɛ dɩa-la tʋɔŋ yuo ta.

english_verse: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ pa wombiiŋ ba pɩɩsɛ dɩɩsɩ-la kala disiniŋ ta, aŋ mɩɩra paa Wɩa dɩa tɩntɩnnɩ kɩalɩŋ kʋ jʋʋ, a pɛ mɩaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ kɩalɩŋ arɩ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋ-la lɛ.

english_verse: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
translation_verse: Mɩ bɩra nɩa arɩ kpaal-la sɩ maga dɩ ba joŋo pɩ Levi doho nɩaa, ba bɩ baa pa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Levi doho nɩalɩŋ arɩ yɩɩlɩ yɩɩra-la kala sɩ maga dɩ ba tɩtɩŋ Wɩa tɩntɩŋŋaa mɩɩra mʋ tɩtɩŋ ba tɩtɩa bagɩsɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bʋl tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la woruŋ a pɩɛsɛba, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma vɩa Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la ta?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ yɩrɛ Levi doho nɩalɩŋ arɩ yɩɩlɩ yɩɩra-la ba mɩɩra kʋ tɩtɩŋ ba tɩntɩŋŋaa.

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ Juda nɩaa kala kɛŋ ba mɩaa, girep nɛnɛɛ sɩ-falɩŋ arɩ nʋʋŋ kpaalɩŋ fii tʋɔŋ kʋbala-la ba sɩ yie joŋo pɩ Wɩa kaa kʋ bil ba chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩɩsɩ-la lɛ.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ lɩɩsɛ Sɛlɛmaaya sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaara, Zadɔk sɩ ŋaa Wɩa teniŋ kerichi arɩ Levi tɩɩna kʋbala baa yɩrɛ Pedaaya, a leŋ ba nɛ bibeŋ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɩɩsɩ-la. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bɩra lɩɩsɛ Hanaŋ sɩ ŋaa Zaku nanʋala, a ŋaa Matanɩa ma nihiŋ ʋ tɩtɩgɛ ba lɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa baalaa deemba fa ŋaa nɩa ba sɩ bene dɩ ba ŋaa nɩtɩtɩɩba nɛ. Ba nɛ fa maga dɩ ba kpɩkpaa kɩalɩŋ nɩaa sɩ kaa kɔ a pɩpɩ ba naambiiriŋ.

english_verse: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
translation_verse: Mɩ Wɩa, liisi mɩ wɩaa sɩ́ wʋzɔmɔ-la kala mɩ sɩ ŋaa a tɩgɛ ŋ dɩa lɛ arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ leŋe ba bɩra ŋɩŋaa nɩmɛ wɩaa yʋ.

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ, mɩ na Juda nɩaa dɩ baa chagɛ girep nɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ, a kɛŋ ba kakusuŋ chʋchʋŋ mɩaa, girep nɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ, girep, tutogi-nambɩlaa arɩ chʋgʋsʋŋ dɔnsʋŋ. Ba chʋŋ kɩaa deemba kala chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ nɛ a kʋʋ jʋʋ Jerusalɛm. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bʋla pɩba dɩ ba sɩ kɩaa yallʋ chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ.

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ Taaya tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ fa yie kɛŋ chenfilee arɩ kɩaa dɔnsʋŋ kʋʋ yallɛ nɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ a pɩpɩ Juda nɩaa.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ ŋaa goŋ Juda sɩpaalaaraa nyuŋ a bʋl, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ wʋbɔŋ nɛ ma ŋɩŋaa ŋ-la a chichei chɛ-wiesii-la kɩsɩŋ lɛ?

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Wʋdosunuŋ deemba dee ma naabalɩmaba ŋaa, la Wɩa joŋ wʋlɔrʋnʋŋ ŋaa la dɩ la tabalɩŋ deeŋ lɛɛ? Lɛɛlɛ ma wasa leŋ Wɩa baanɩŋ sisii Iziral tɩŋŋaa nyuŋ nɛ, a tɩŋ ma sɩɩ chei chɛ-wiesii-la kɩsɩŋ lɛ wɩaa.”

english_verse: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ pa wombiiŋ dɩ ba kɛŋ Jerusalɛm boi-baalaa tɔ dɩdaaŋ-la, ka dɩ taŋ pʋl chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ, a mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩ bala. Mɩ leŋe mɩ nɩaa dɔnsʋŋ chɩŋ boi-baalaa niiŋ nɛ dɩ ba sɩ́ chʋga kala kaa kʋ jʋʋ chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ.

english_verse: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
translation_verse: Bala koo bʋlɩa nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ yallɛ kʋdosunuŋ chʋa Jerusalɛm jeeŋ harɩŋ.

english_verse: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ kpʋrɩsɛ ba dɩgɩlaa aŋ pɩɛsɛba, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma chʋa jeeŋ harɩŋ? Dɩ ma nɛ bɩra ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ, mɩ jaŋ kɛsɛma.” A chɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ a kaa kɔ ba bɩra bɩ chɛ-wiesii-la chɛɛŋ kɔ.

english_verse: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bʋla pɩ Levi doho nɩaa dɩ ba pɩɩsɛ ba disiniŋ ta aŋ mʋ pʋpɔ boi-baalaa dɩ chɛ-wiesii-la ŋaa chɛ-zɔŋ. Mɩ Wɩa ŋ chonuŋ sɩ yʋga wɩaa, tɩŋ wɩɩŋ deeŋ ma wɩaa a fá mɩ nenige.

english_verse: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ nɛ bɩra, mɩ na Juda tɩŋŋaa sɩ jaa Asɩdɔd, Amɔŋ arɩ Mʋab tɩŋŋaa toloo.

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: Ba hambiisiŋ kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ faa bʋl Asɩdɔd tɩŋŋaa yikoro nɛ, koo nɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ yikoro, aŋ bɩ Juda tɩŋŋaa yikoro wuo bʋl.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Mɩ ŋaa goŋ ba nyuŋ a ŋmɩɛsa hɛ ba lɛ. Mɩ ŋmoo nɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ a lɛrɛ ba nyu-pʋnaa churi. Mɩ leŋ ba ŋmɩɛsɛ Wɩa yɩrɩŋ lɛ a bʋl, “La bɩ jaŋ joŋ la toloo a pɩ ba hambolibiisiŋ dɩ ba jaa, koo a jaa ba toloo a pɩ la hambolibiisiŋ koo la tɩtɩa.

english_verse: God dearly loved King Solomon of Israel and made him the greatest king on earth, but Solomon's foreign wives led him into sin.
translation_verse: Ha-jaa doho deeŋ dee bɩ leŋe Iziral tinteeŋ kuoro Solomoŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ? Tinteyee kala tʋɔŋ, kuoru kala fa tuo a magʋ. Wɩa fa chou nɛ woruŋ, a leŋ ʋ ŋaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala kuoro. Ama tintee-wogusuŋ toloo nɛ lɛrʋ mʋ hɛ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ.

english_verse: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɛnɛ magɛ dɩ la bɩra nɩɩ arɩ ma maa ŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ deemba, a bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ arɩ la Wɩa aŋ jɩjaa tintee-wogusuŋ toloo?”

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Ɛlɩasɩb sɩ ŋaa Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa nɩhɩaŋ nanʋala dɔŋɔ nɛ fa Joyada. Ama Joyada hɩɩlɩ-baala nɛ fa Sambalat, Horo tɩɩna-la. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ kiri Joyada ta mɩ teeŋ.

english_verse: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Mɩ Wɩa, liisi ŋɩɩ ba sɩ ŋaa wɩaa a chei wombii-la ba sɩ maga dɩ ba to a ŋaa Wɩɩsʋlʋŋ pɩpɩŋ arɩ nii-la sɩ mʋ tɩgɛ ŋ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa lɛ.

english_verse: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ pɩɩsɛ nɩalɩŋ disiniŋ ta a mʋ tɩgɛ kʋŋkala sɩ ŋaa kʋwogo lɛ, aŋ dagɛ Wɩɩsʋllɩ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ Levi doho nɩaa ba tɩntɩmɩŋ.

english_verse: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_verse: Mɩ bɩra dagɛ nɩalɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ sɩ maga dɩ ba kɛŋ daasɩŋ arɩ ba kʋdii falaa kɔ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ. Mɩ Wɩa, liisi wɩaa deemba kala mɩ sɩ ŋaa aŋ pɛ mɩ lɛ.

english_verse: King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled
translation_verse: Zɛzɛs kuori kpaha fa hɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Susa lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
translation_verse: Ʋ sɩ dii kuoruŋ ʋ jɩ-tori lɛ, ʋ yɩrɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ, Pɛsɩa arɩ Midia laalɩyuori hɩasɩŋ, sɩpaalaaraa arɩ ʋ tinteeŋ nɩbalaa a hɛ dɔŋɔ a ŋaa kʋdiilee ba gbieli.

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Gbiele-la harɩŋ, kuoro Zɛzɛs bɩra leŋ ba ŋaa kʋdiilee ʋ yɩrɛ Susa tabal-la nɩaa kala, nɩbalaa arɩ nɩbiisiŋ kala. Ba kʋ gbieli ʋ kuoru dɩɩ-zɔŋ-la lɩga tʋɔŋ tapʋlaa balɩpɛ.

english_verse: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
translation_verse: Ba kpɩɛrɛ lee-la kala a kɛŋ ŋmɛŋ-vachalɩŋ a vɔɔ patɩɩsaŋ diibelimbine arɩ patɩɩsaŋ pʋllʋŋ kaala-la harɩŋ a mɛrɛ ba sɩ kɛŋ hɔpʋla ŋaa nenii-pɩraa a joŋo hɛ sɛlɩmɛ ba sɩ kaa ŋaa jebiee lɛ. Ka tinteeŋ kala ŋaa tabɩɩ mʋmʋlaa sɩ kɛŋ kpɩɛrɛ dosunuŋ. Sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla ba sɩ kaa ŋaa kpasɩnɩŋ chɩŋ nɩmɛ.

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ yɩra kɛŋ nyʋnyʋalʋsʋŋ ba sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ a ŋaa ba kpɩɛraa bɩ dɔŋɔ naga nɛ a nyʋnyʋa girep nɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ. Kuoro leŋe sɩnɩŋ pʋrɩgɛ nɛ woruŋ gbiele-la lɛ.

english_verse: and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
translation_verse: Kuoro bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnna-la sɩɩ kpaa sɩŋ-la, “Má leŋ dɩ nʋʋkala nyʋa sɩnɩŋ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩɩ chɛ.”

english_verse: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
translation_verse: Baala-la kala fa sɩɩ nyʋa sɩnɩŋ ŋɩɩ, kuoro habidiire Vasiti ma ŋaa kʋdiilee yʋgɛ woruŋ a pɩ haala-la kala sɩ hɛ kuoru dɩa lɛ.

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Tapʋl-pɛɩ chɛɛŋ, dɩ Zɛzɛs nyʋa girep nɛnɛɛ sɩnɩŋ ʋ tʋɔŋ kala tɔrɛ, ʋ bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnna-la balɩpɛ ba sɩ fere, ba yɩraa nɛ Mehuman, Bɩzɩta, Habona, Bigita, Abagɩta, Zeta arɩ Kaakas,

english_verse: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: dɩ ba kɛŋ ʋ habidiire Vasiti kɔ ʋ teeŋ. Kuoro faa chɛ dɩ Vasiti laalɛ ʋ gɛrɩ-zɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ, a chu ʋ kuoru nyunchuulo, a kʋ lɩɩ dɩ kuoro nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ nɩaa kala na ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ zɔmɔ.

english_verse: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
translation_verse: Ama kuoro tɩntɩnna-la sɩ mʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la a pɩ Vasiti, ʋ vɩa dɩ ʋ mʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro na baanɩŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ yɩra pɩɛsɛ yɩraa nɛ ŋ-la, Kaasɩhɛna, Seta, Adɩmata, Taasɩs, Mɛrɛs, Masɛna arɩ Mɛmukaŋ. Ba balɩpɛ nɛ ŋaa Pɛsɩa arɩ Midia tinteeŋ nɩbala-la sɩ kpagɛ kuoro tintee-la lɛ.

english_verse: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
translation_verse: Kuoro pɩɛsɛba, “Mɩ tɩŋ mɩ tɩntɩnnaa nɛ dɩ ba mʋ kɛŋ mɩ habidiire Vasiti kɔ, ba mʋ ʋ vɩa. La naabarɩŋ lɛ bɛɛ nɛ maga dɩ la ŋaaʋ?”

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la dɔŋɔ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɛmukaŋ bʋla pɩ kuoro Zɛzɛs arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ hɩasɩ-la, “Wɩɩ-la kuoro habidiire Vasiti sɩ ŋaa, kuoro dʋndʋŋa dee ʋ hɩɩsɛ, ʋ hɩɩsɛ kuoro tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ, arɩ baal kala sɩ hɛ ʋ tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: Haala-la kala sɩ hɛ la tinteeŋ lɛ jaŋ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la Vasiti sɩ ŋaa, a joŋ ba balaba hɛ sɩɩŋ lɛ. Ba jaŋ bʋl ‘Kuoro Zɛzɛs paala yɩrɛ Vasiti nɛ ʋ vɩa.’

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Ka dɩ wɩa na jʋʋ, kuoro tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la sɩ hɛ Pɛsɩa arɩ Media lɛ, ba haalaa jaŋ nɩɩ wɩɩ-la kuoro haala sɩ ŋaa, ba ma bɩ jaŋ tuto ba balaba niiŋ. Ba bɩra bɩ jaŋ zizil ba balaba ma, dɩ ba balaba baanɩŋ sii ba nyuŋ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa kuoro dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ jaŋ tɔrɛ, leŋ dɩ ba heele bʋl arɩ ŋ habidiire Vasiti maachie bɩra bɩ maga ʋ kɔ kuoro sɩpaaŋ, aŋ ŋmʋnsa hɛ Pɛsɩa arɩ Media tinteeŋ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto teniŋ tʋɔŋ, dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ sɩ bɩ jaŋ dɩsɛ. Ka dɩ la laa ʋ maŋgaazɩa-la a pɩ haal dɔŋ sɩ kpɩaʋ.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Dɩ ba nɛ heele bʋl ŋɩɩ dɩ haalaa kala sɩ hɛ la tinteeŋ lɛ nɩɩ, ba jaŋ chaasa zizil ba balaba, dɩ ba ŋaa summo koo dɩ ba kɛŋ kɩaa.”

english_verse: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
translation_verse: Kuoro Zɛzɛs arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ kala tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ wɩɩ-la Memukan sɩ bʋla lɛ.

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: Kuoro Zɛzɛs ŋmʋnsɛ tenniŋ joŋo kpaa ʋ tinteeŋ tasɩŋ kala. Taŋ-la kala nɩaa sɩɩ bʋl yikoro-la lɛ nɛ, ʋ kaa ŋmʋnsɛ ba teniŋ a pɩba.

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ nɛ bʋa kʋbala lɛ kuoro Zɛzɛs baanɩŋ fɩɛlɛ, ka ʋ ha kɛŋ wɩɩ-la ʋ habidiire Vasiti sɩ ŋaa arɩ nii-la ʋ-na kuoro sɩ bile a tɩgɛ ʋ lɛ wɩaa bɩbɩɩnɛ.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ tɩma pɩpɩ kuoro tapʋlɩɩ kala bʋl, “Kuoro, leŋ dɩ la chɛ hatol-zɔŋŋɔɔ ha sɩ bɩ baalaa jɩŋ a kaa kʋ pɩŋ.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Ŋ jaŋ wuo lɩɩsɛ nɩhɩasɩŋ ŋ tinteeŋ tasɩ-la kala lɛ dɩ ba nɛ chaarɛ hatol zɔmɔ-la kaa kɔ la tabalɩŋ Susa, lee-la ŋ haalaa sɩ hɛ, dɩ ŋ tɩntɩnna ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hagaɩ bafere-la bibemba, aa pɩba nʋʋ-zɔmɔ-la ba sɩ jaŋ tɩtɩsɛ. Ʋ tɩntɩmɩŋ nɛ folo ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Kuoro, hatolo-la nyuŋ ŋ tʋɔŋ sɩ faasa tɔrɛ leŋ dɩ ʋ nɛ laa Vasiti nyuŋ, a ŋaa ŋ habidiire.” Wɩɩŋ deeŋ sɩma pɩ kuoro ʋ kaa tɩŋ.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Bʋa deeŋ lɛ, dɩ Juu tɩŋŋaa baal kʋbala hɛ Susa lɛ baa yɩrɛ Modikaaya. Ʋ ŋaa Bɛnjamɩŋ doho nʋʋ nɛ, ʋ nyɩmma nɛ Jaa, ʋ naabalɩma ma nɛ Sɩmɛɩ, Kɩs nanʋala.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Modikaaya ma fa hɛ nɩalɩŋ Babɩlɔŋ kuoro ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nebukadineza sɩ yuo kɛsɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ a kaa mʋ Babɩlɔŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ, a pɛ Juda kuoro Jehoyachiŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Modikaaya fa kɛŋ naambii nɛ baa yɩrɛ Hadasa, ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ sʋba nɛ aŋ ka Modikaaya dɩɛsʋ. Hadasa yɩrɩŋ dɔŋɔ nɛ Ɛsɩta ʋ zɔmɔ nɛ woruŋ. Ʋ dɩɛsʋ a nagɛ ʋ tɩtɩa tol-lʋlʋŋ nɛ.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Kuoro sɩ pa wombiiŋ dɩ ba chɛ hatol-zɔŋŋɔɔ kɔ ŋɩɩ, ba kɛsɛ hatoloo yʋgɛ woruŋ Ɛsɩta hɛ ba tʋɔŋ ba kaa mʋ Sʋsa kuoro dɩa. Ba joŋ Hagaɩ nɩɩ-la sɩɩ beŋ haalaa dɩa hɛ ʋ bibemba. Ba kɛŋ Ɛsɩta ma kaa kʋ hɛ Hagaɩ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ ʋ bibenu.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Hagaɩ tʋɔŋ fa tɔrɛ Ɛsɩta nyuŋ nɛ woruŋ. Ʋ pʋ nʋʋ-zɔŋŋɔɔ ʋ tɩtɩsɛ, a pʋpʋ kʋdiilee ma woruŋ. Hagaɩ tʋɔsɛ ketiee balɩpɛ kuoro dɩa lɛ a kɛmba kaa mʋ hɛ dɩɩ-zɔŋ lɛ ba tɩma pɩpɩ Ɛsɩta.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Ɛsɩta fa bɩ ʋ dɩ-lɩɩlɩŋ arɩ ʋ doho daga pɩ nʋʋkala. Modikaaya nɛ fa sɩ ʋ sɩ lee-la ʋ sɩ lɩa arɩ ʋ doho daga pɩ nʋʋkala.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-na kala, Modikaaya yie mʋ kaala-la nɛ a daasɛ Ɛsɩta dɩ ʋ na wɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋaa ʋ lɛ arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ naga.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Ka dɩ hantolibie-na jʋʋ kuoro Zɛzɛs dɩa, ʋ maga dɩ ʋ tɩsɛ hazɔŋŋɔɔ nʋʋŋ jɩ-piliŋ nɛ. Ʋ jaŋ tɩsɛ olif nʋʋŋ arɩ tɩɩ-kel zɔŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Mɛɛ chɛnsɩŋ balɩdʋ, a bɩra fo chɛnfɛŋ-sʋɔrʋsʋŋ a tɩsɛ tʋlaalɩɩba arɩ nʋʋ-sʋɔrʋsʋŋ ma chɛnsɩŋ balɩdʋ.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɩɩ jʋʋ kuoro dɩa, ʋ jaŋ wuo joŋ gɛrɩ-la kala koo kpɩɛrɛ-la kala ʋ sɩɩ chɛ haalaa dɩa-la lɛ a laalɛ.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Ʋ jaŋ jʋʋ kuoro teeŋ dɩdaanɩŋ, aŋ mɩɩra kʋ lɩɩ chʋchʋɔŋ a mʋ lee-la haala-la sɩ hɛ. Kuoro kɛŋ bafere kʋbala nɛ baa yɩrɛ Saasɩgas ʋ nɩɩ beŋ haala-la ʋ sɩ bile aŋ bɩ jaa. Dɩ haal-la nɛ kʋ lɩɩ, ʋ bɩra bɩ kuoro teeŋ wuo mɩɩraa mʋ, see dɩ kuoro nɛ cho tɩɩna a yɩrʋ.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Kuoro Zɛzɛs sɩ na Ɛsɩta, ʋ chou a kɩɩ hatolie-la kala ha sɩ bɩ baalaa jɩŋ. Ʋ sɩ chou a kɩɩ hatolie-la kala ŋɩɩ, ʋ joŋ kuoru nyunchuulo, a chuu ʋ laa Vasiti nyuŋ a ŋaa ʋ habidiire.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Kuoro tɩŋ Ɛsɩta wɩaa a leŋ ba ŋaa kʋdiilee, ʋ yɩrɛ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa kala ba kʋ dii. Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ leŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la ŋaa chɛ-wiesii a pɩ ʋ tinteeŋ nɩaa kala, aŋ joŋ kɩaa sɩ kɛŋ yɩrɩŋ ŋaa chɔgɩta pɩ nɩaa. Ba vʋʋra dɩ ba kpʋ kuoro, Modikaaya nɩɩ a bʋl

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Ba sɩ bɩra yɩrɛ hatolie-la kala kʋ hilimi lɩamɩŋ lɛ, dɩ Ɛsɩta naambie Modikaaya lɛɛlɛ ŋaa kuoro dɩa tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩaŋ a hɔŋ kuoro boi-baalɩŋ.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Modikaaya fa sɩ dɩɛsɛ Ɛsɩta a bʋla pʋ arɩ ʋ pʋpɔ dɩ ʋ sɩ́ ʋ doho arɩ ʋ dɩ-lɩɩlɩŋ daga pɩ nʋʋkala ŋɩɩ, ʋ kɛŋ ŋɩɩ Modikaaya sɩ dagʋ a tɩtɩŋ.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ Modikaaya sɩ hɔŋ kuoro boi-baalɩŋ niiŋ ŋɩɩ, kuoro tɩntɩnna kʋbala ba balɩa sɩɩ pɔ kuoro dɩɩsɩŋ, ba yɩraa nɛ Bɩgɩtana arɩ Teres na baanɩŋ kuoro Zɛzɛs nyuŋ a vʋʋrɛ dɩ ba kpʋ.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Modikaaya nɩɩ wɩɩ-la a bʋla pɩ Ɛsɩta kuoro habidiire. Ʋ ma bʋl wɩɩ-la Modikaaya sɩ nɩa a pɩ kuoro.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Kuoro Zɛzɛs to wɩɩ-la naasɩŋ a na dɩ ʋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ, ʋ ŋaa ba lieŋi ʋ tɩntɩnna-la balɩa. Ka ʋ leŋ ba ŋmʋnsɛ wɩɩ-la kala hɛ ba wʋŋaalaa teniŋ tʋɔŋ ʋ sɩɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba sɩ bala, bʋa kʋbala lɛ kuoro Zɛzɛs joŋ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ ma kala hɩasɩŋ a pɩ baal kʋbala ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hamaŋ, ʋ nyɩmma nɛ Hamɛdata a ŋaa Agag doho nʋʋ.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩ-la kala sɩɩ hɔŋ kuoro dɩa boi-baalɩŋ dɩ ba kpirime zizil Hamaŋ. Ba kala sɛɩ a kpikpirimi, ka Modikaaya-na vɩa.

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Kuoro tɩntɩnnɩ hɩasɩ-la dɔnsʋŋ sɩɩ hɔŋ kuoro dɩa boi-baalɩŋ pɩɛsɛ Modikaaya, “Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ vɩa dɩ ŋ to nii-la kuoro sɩ bile?”

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ na-kala ba yie bʋla pɩ Modikaaya wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩɩ ŋaa, ka ʋ bɩ kaa tɩtɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba bʋl wɩɩ-la pɩ Hamaŋ dɩ ba naa, ʋ jaŋ sɛɩ Modikaaya sɩ kɛŋ ʋ mɛlɛ-la, bɛɛ wɩaa Modikaaya bʋla pɩba arɩ ʋ na ŋaa Juu tɩɩna nɛ.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Hamaŋ sɩ na dɩ Modikaaya bɩ sɛɩ dɩ ʋ kpirimi ʋ sɩpaaŋ koo ʋ zilu, ʋ na baanɩŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: Hamaŋ sɩ kʋ jɩŋ dɩ Modikaaya ŋaa Juu tɩɩna nɛ, ʋ beŋ dɩ ʋ nɛ kpʋ ʋ dʋndʋŋa, ŋɩɩ ha bɩ magɛ. Ʋ lɛɛlɛ chɩchɛ wombiiŋ dɩ ʋ kpʋ Juu tɩŋŋaa kala sɩ hɔŋ kuoro Zɛzɛs tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Kuoro Zɛzɛs sɩ dii kuoruŋ, jɩsɩŋ fii arɩ balɩa tʋɔŋ chɛŋ bumbuŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nɩsaŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ, Hamaŋ bʋl dɩ ba tɔnsɛ dɩ ʋ na tapʋlɩɩ-la arɩ chɛnɛ-la sɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩ bɩɩna dɩ ʋ ŋaa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba lɩɩsɛ chɛŋ-fii arɩ balɩa-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Adaa, ʋ tʋɔŋ tapʋlaa fii arɩ batori chɛɛŋ.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hamaŋ sii mʋ kuoro Zɛzɛs teeŋ a bʋla pʋ, “Nɩa kʋbala ba nɛ gɔllɔ hɔŋ ŋ tinteeŋ kala lɛ, ŋ nɩaa tʋɔŋ. Ba naabarɩŋ arɩ ŋ nɩaa naabarɩŋ bɩ dɔŋɔ naga. Ba-na bɩ ŋ niiŋ wɩaa kaa tɩtɩŋ. Kuoro, ŋ bɩ maga dɩ ŋ leŋ dɩ ba hɔŋ ŋ nɩaa tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Kuoro dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ jaŋ tɔrɛ, pɩ wombiiŋ dɩ ba kpʋ nɩalɩŋ. Dɩ ŋ nɛ ŋaa ŋɩɩ, mɩ jaŋ wuo na warɩpʋla bʋɩ-fii a hɛ ŋ kuoru dɩa moribiee lɛ dɩ ba kaa wasɛ la tinteeŋ.”

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Zɛzɛs lɩɩsɛ ʋ nenii-pɩrɩ-la ʋ sɩ kaa magɩlɛ ʋ teniŋ a pɩ Agag doho nɩaa Hamɛdata nanʋala Hamaŋ, jʋʋ tɩŋŋaa dʋndɔŋ-la,

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: aŋ bʋla pʋ, “Nɩalɩŋ arɩ ba moribiee kala hɛ ŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ, ŋaa ba ŋɩɩ kala ŋ sɩɩ chɛ.”

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Chɛŋ-bumbuŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Nɩsaŋ tapʋlaa fii arɩ batori chɛɛŋ, Hamaŋ yɩrɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ ŋmʋnsɛ kuoro teniŋ, dɩ ba kɛŋ ba tinteeŋ yikoro na-kala a ŋmʋnsɛ tenniŋ a pɩ ba tinteeŋ sɩpaalaaraa arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba ŋmʋnsɛ tenni-la kuoro yɩrɩŋ lɛ a kɛŋ nenii-pɩrɩ-la kuoro sɩ kaa magɩlɛ ʋ tenniŋ a magɩlɛ.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Ba joŋ tenni-la pɩ tɩndaaraa ba kaa gɔllɔ kpaa ba tinteeŋ tasɩŋ kala. Ŋ la nɛ ba bʋl a hɛ tenni-la lɛ: Chɛnɛ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Adaa tapʋlaa fii arɩ batori chɛɛŋ, má kpʋ Juu tɩmma-la kala sɩ hɛ tintee-la lɛ baalaa arɩ haalaa, nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ hambiisiŋ aŋ paa ba kɩaa kala.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro pɩ wombiiŋ tɩndaaraa gɔllɔ bʋl wɩɩ-la pɩ ba tinteeŋ nɩaa kala, ʋ leŋ ba heele pɩ ba tabalɩŋ Sʋsa nɩaa ma kala. Ka ʋ dɩ Hamaŋ hɔnɔ nyʋnyʋa kɩaa, ka Susa kala hosi.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Modikaaya sɩ nɩɩ teŋ-la ba sɩ ŋmʋnsa wɩaa, ʋ kɛŋ ʋ gɛnnɩŋ kɩɛsɛ aŋ ŋaa tʋɔrʋŋ bʋgɛ, a laalɛ tʋɔ-chei gɛrɩŋ a faasaa ŋmoo niiŋ.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: Ʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ a wuo mʋ kuoro dɩa boi-baalɩŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba bɩ jaŋ sɛɩ dɩ nʋʋkala sɩ laalɛ tʋɔ-chei-gɛrɩŋ jʋʋ kuoro kaala.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Lee-la na-kala kuoro tɩndaarɩ-la sɩ yie ba karɩmɛ, Juu tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ kala tʋɔŋ yie chei nɛ ba yiyel a bɩ kɩaa ka dii. Ba jesiŋ kala laalɛ tʋɔ-chei gɛnnɩŋ aŋ bʋgɛ tʋɔrʋŋ.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Ɛsɩta ketiee arɩ baferisi-la sɩɩ benu sɩ kʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la Modikaaya sɩ ŋaa pʋ, ʋ tʋɔŋ faasa chei. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ tɩa gɛnnɩŋ dɩ ba kaa mʋ pʋ dɩ ʋ laalɛ aŋ wuri tʋɔ-chei gɛnnɩ-la, ama Modikaaya vɩa.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛsɩta yɩrɛ bafere-la dɔŋɔ ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Hatak kuoro sɩ leŋe ʋ bibenu dɩ ʋ lɩɩ pɩɛsɛ Modikaaya na wɩɩ-la sɩɩ walɩmʋ.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Hatak lɩɩ na Modikaaya kuoro dɩa boiŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Modikaaya bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala sɩ ŋaa a pʋ, aŋ dagɛ moribiee niiŋ ma Hamaŋ sɩ daga arɩ ʋ jaŋ joŋo time hɛ kuoro dɩa moribiee lɛ, dɩ ba nɛ kpʋ Juu tɩŋŋaa kala sɩ hɛ kuoro Zɛzɛs tinteeŋ lɛ,

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: aŋ joŋ teŋ-la ba sɩ ŋmʋnsa a pa wombiiŋ dɩ ba kpʋ Juu tɩŋŋaa kala Susa lɛ dɔŋɔ pɩ Hatak dɩ ʋ kaa jʋʋ pɩ Ɛsɩta aŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la a pʋ aŋ sʋlʋ dɩ ʋ jʋʋ sʋl kuoro dɩ ʋ fa ʋ dɩ ʋ nɩaa nenige.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Hatak mɩɩra jʋʋ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala Modikaaya sɩ bʋla a pɩ Ɛsɩta.

english_verse: She answered, “Tell Mordecai
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛsɩta bʋl, “Mʋ bʋla pɩ Modikaaya,

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: wɩɩ nɛ ba bʋla bil a mʋ tɩgɛ dɩ nʋʋ nɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ na Kuoro lɛ, ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ arɩ ʋ nɩaa kala jɩŋ wɩɩŋ deeŋ lɛ. Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ jʋa dɩ ʋ na kuoro ka kuoro bɩ tɩɩna yɩra, ba jaŋ kpʋ. Wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ laa tɩɩna ta nɛ dɩ kuoro nɛ kɛŋ ʋ sɛlɩmɛ dantɩga a liesi tɩɩna. Mɩ ma tapʋlaa Mara arɩ fii nɛ ŋ-la kuoro ha sɩ bɩ mɩ yɩra.”

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Hatak sɩ mʋ bʋl wɩɩ-la Ɛsɩta sɩ bʋla a pɩ Modikaaya,

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Modikaaya bɩra tɩŋ ʋ mʋ bʋla pɩ Ɛsɩta, “Sɩ́ bɩɩna bʋl ŋ sɩ hɛ kuoro dɩa lɛ wɩaa dɩ ba nɩɩ kpʋ Juu tɩŋŋaa ŋ jaŋ fori.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩ sii bʋla laala ta lɛlɛ, Wɩa jaŋ wuo to wombiiŋ a laala ta, ama ŋ dɩ ŋ nyɩmma dɩa nɩaa jaŋ sʋʋ. Ŋ bɩ pɔ wɩɩŋ deeŋ wɩaa nɛ tɩɩ ŋ ŋaa kuoro habidiire dɩ ŋ laa ŋ nɩaa ta.”

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛsɩta tɩŋ tɩndaarɩŋ pɩ Modikaaya a bʋl,

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: “Kɛŋ Juu tɩmma-la kala sɩ hɛ Susa tinteeŋ lɛ hɛ dɔŋɔ a bʋla pɩba dɩ ba vɔɔ niiŋ wɩɩhɛyɛ arɩ tɩtaŋɩŋ kala tapʋlaa batori a sʋl Wɩa pɩmɛ. Mɩ dɩ mɩ ketiee ma jaŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ tɩtɩa. Ʋ ŋɩɩ harɩŋ mɩ jaŋ jʋʋ kuoro teeŋ, dɩ ʋ nɛ paala magɛ dɩ mɩ sʋʋ ma, mɩ jaŋ sʋʋ.”

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Modikaaya ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala Ɛsɩta sɩ dagʋ.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Tapʋl-tori chɛɛŋ, Ɛsɩta sii laalɛ ʋ kuoru-gɛnnɩŋ a mʋ jʋʋ kuoro zawʋra, ʋ jʋa dɩ kuoro hɔŋ ʋ kuoru kpasa nyuŋ a chaasɛ boiŋ niiŋ.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: Kuoro sɩ na ʋ habidiire Ɛsɩta, dɩ ʋ kʋ jʋʋ chɩŋ ʋ sɩpaaŋ, ʋ tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ, ʋ kɛŋ ʋ kuoru dantɩga ba sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ ŋaa a liesi Ɛsɩta. Ɛsɩta mʋ yiu a digi dantɩga-la niiŋ lɛ.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro pɩɛsɛ, “Mɩ habidiire Ɛsɩta, bɛɛ nɛ ŋ chɩchɛ daha? Bʋl, dɩ ʋ nɛ maga dɩ mɩ kɛŋ mɩ tinteeŋ kala kpaa leree balɩa dɩ ŋ kɛŋ dɔŋɔ ma, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ pɩŋ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ɛsɩta bʋl, “Kuoro, dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ jaŋ tɔrɛ, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa kʋdiilee jɩnɩŋ dɩ ŋ kɛŋ Hamaŋ kɔ dɩ ma kʋ dii kɩalɩŋ aŋ gbieli.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bʋla pɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa, “Má mʋ lɩma a kɛŋ Hamaŋ kɔ dɩ la mʋ Ɛsɩta yɩra-la.” Kuoro arɩ Hemaŋ mʋ Ɛsɩta kʋdiile-la dɩ-diiliŋ.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ba sɩ hɔnɔ nyʋnyʋa tɩɩ-nɛnɛ sɩnɩŋ, kuoro bɩra pɩɛsɛ Ɛsɩta, “Bɛɛ nɛ ŋ chɛ dɩ mɩ ŋaa pɩŋ? Dɩ ŋ nɛ paalaa chɛ dɩ mɩ kɛŋ mɩ tinteeŋ a kpaa leree balɩa, dɩ ŋ kɛŋ dɔŋɔ ma, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ sɛnɛ chomi a cho dɩ ŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩɩ chɛ, ŋɩɩ na ŋ dɩ Hamaŋ chie bɩra kɔ daha a dii kʋdiilee, bʋa-la lɛ nɛ mɩ jaŋ dagɛ kʋla mɩ sɩɩ chɛ. Hamaŋ vʋʋra dɩ ʋ kpʋ Modikaaya

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Hamaŋ sii kʋdiile-la leriŋ tapʋlɩɩ-la ʋ tʋɔŋ kala tɔrɛ woruŋ. Ama ʋ sɩ mʋ na dɩ Modikaaya chɩŋ kuoro dɩa boiŋ niiŋ aŋ bɩ ʋ chʋɔla ʋ baanɩŋ faasa sii.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Ama Hamaŋ kɛŋ ʋ tɩtɩa, ʋ bɩ wɩɩkala bʋla aŋ mʋ dɩa. Ʋ sɩ mʋa, ʋ yɩrɛ ʋ nandɔnsʋŋ hɛ dɔŋɔ arɩ ʋ haala Zeresi,

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: a suomo bigisi ʋ tɩtɩa lɛ a pɩpɩba, ʋ dʋa sɩ magɛ ŋɩɩ arɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ biiriŋ sɩ maga arɩ ŋɩɩ kuoro sɩ zilu a pʋ hɩasɩŋ a leŋ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ arɩ sɩpaalaaraa kala zizilu.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Hamaŋ bɩra bʋl, “Ŋɩɩ ma dʋndʋŋa dee Ɛsɩta yɩrɛ mɩ dɩ kuoro dʋndʋŋa nɛ la mʋ dii kɩaa, aŋ ka ʋ ha bɩra bʋl la chie kɔ.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Wɩaa deemba kʋŋkala bɩ mɩ tʋɔŋ tɔrɔ a tɩŋ mɩ sɩ yie na Modikaaya Juu tɩɩna-la dɩ ʋ hɔŋ kuoro dɩa boiŋ niiŋ.”

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtaŋɩŋ kuoro walɩmɛ doŋ pɩnɩŋ lɔl aŋ leŋ ba joŋ teŋ-la lɛ ba sɩ ŋmʋnsɛ wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ dii kuoruŋ a ŋaa a hɛ, a kaa kʋ lɩɩ karɩma pʋ.

english_verse: When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king,
translation_verse: Teŋ-la tʋɔŋ nɛ ba na arɩ Modikaaya wuoli Bigata arɩ Tɛrɛs bʋbʋɔŋ, tɩntɩnna-la balɩa fa sɩɩ pɔ kuoro boiŋ niiŋ, sɩ vʋʋra dɩ ba kpʋ kuoro Zɛzɛs.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro pɩɛsɛ, “Modikaaya sɩ ŋaa wɩɩŋ deeŋ, bɛɛ kʋŋ wʋzɔŋ nɛ ma joŋo siilu?” Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro dɩa tɩntɩnna-la bʋla pʋ, “Ba bɩ wɩɩkala ŋaa pʋ.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro pɩɛsɛ, “Mɩ tɩntɩnnɩ hɩa bɛɛ ba nɛ hɛ daha.” Bʋa la lɛ dɩ Hamaŋ kʋ jʋʋ dɩ ʋ bʋla pɩ kuoro dɩ ʋ leŋ ba kɛŋ Modikaaya ka mʋ lieŋi jebii-duduoŋ-la lɛ ʋ sɩ saa.

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro-dɩa tɩntɩnna-la bʋl, “Hamaŋ nɛ chɩŋ kaala tʋɔŋ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ Kuoro bʋl, “Ma kɛnʋ ka kɔ.”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Hamaŋ sɩ kʋ jʋʋ, kuoro pɩɛsʋ, “Bɛɛ kʋŋ nɛ maga dɩ mɩ joŋo dii zile nɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ cho dɩ mɩ dii zile ʋ lɛ?” Hamaŋ bɩɩnɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ lɛ, “Kʋbɛɛ nɛ saa bɩra hɛ nɩmɛ kuoro chɩchɛ ʋ ŋaa Zile ʋ lɛ, dɩ mɩ dee?”

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩ kuoro, “Nɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ ŋaa zile ʋ lɛ,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: leŋ dɩ ba joŋ ŋ kuoru gɛnnɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ laalʋ dɔŋɔ, a kɛŋ ŋ janɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ jɩl dɔŋɔ, a joŋ ŋ kuoru nyu-bɛlɛ a bɛ jaaba-la nyuŋ.

english_verse: Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
translation_verse: Leŋ dɩ ŋ nɩhɩasɩ-la dɔŋɔ joŋ kuoru gɛrɩ-la a laalɛ nɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ zil dɩ ʋ jɩl jɔɔ-la. Ka nɩhɩaŋ-la laa jaaba-la sɩpaaŋ a bʋbʋl, ‘Má na nɩɩ-la kuoro sɩɩ zil nɛ ŋ-la.’ ” Ʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ a kɛnʋ ba gɔllɛ jaŋ kala.

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bʋla pɩ Hamaŋ, “Guu mʋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ ŋ sɩ bʋla. Joŋ kuori-gɛrɩ-la arɩ jɔɔ-la a kaa mʋ pɩ Modikaaya Juu tɩɩna la sɩ hɔŋ kuoro dɩa boiŋ niiŋ. Sɩ́ wɩalɩŋ kʋŋkala ŋ sɩ daga vɩa.”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Hamaŋ joŋ kuoru-gɛrɩŋ a laalɛ Modikaaya, a leŋ ʋ jɩl jaaba ʋ kɛnʋ gɔllɛ jaŋ-la kala, aŋ bʋbʋl, “Má na nɩɩ-la kuoro sɩ zile.”

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Hamaŋ sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ dɛrɛ, Modikaaya mɩɩra mʋ hɔŋ kuoro-dɩa boiŋ niiŋ, ka hɩɩsɩŋ kɛŋ Hamaŋ ʋ kɛŋ nyuŋ gʋrɛ a fá mʋ dɩa.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Hamaŋ mʋ a bʋl wɩɩ-la kala sɩ ŋaa ʋ lɛ a pɩ ʋ haala Zɛrɛs arɩ ʋ nandɔnsʋŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ haala arɩ ʋ nandɔsʋ-la sɩ dagʋ bʋla pʋ, “Dɩ Modikaaya nɛ ŋaa Juu tɩɩna, ŋ wʋwalɩmaa dɩ-suomuŋ nɛ ŋ-la, ŋ lɛlɛ nɛ.”

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Ba fa ha sɩɩ bʋl wɩaa ŋɩɩ, dɩ kuoro tɩntɩnnaa kʋ jʋʋ kɛŋ Hamaŋ a lɛrɛ mʋ Ɛsɩta kʋdiile-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa dɩ-diiliŋ.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro arɩ Hamaŋ arɩ kuoro habidiire Ɛsɩta hɔŋ dɩ ba dii kʋdiilee

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: ba sɩ hɔnɔ a nyʋnyʋa kʋnyʋalaa lɩamɩŋ lɛ nɛ kuoro bɩra pɩɛsɛ, “Ɛsɩta, bɛɛ nɛ ŋ chɩchɛ? Bʋl mɩ jaŋ ŋaa pɩŋ. Dɩ ʋ nɛ paala magɛ dɩ mɩ kɛŋ mɩ tinteeŋ kaa kpaa leree balɩa, dɩ ŋ joŋ dɔŋɔ ma, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa ŋɩɩ pɩŋ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Ɛsɩta bʋl, “Kuoro dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ tɔrɛ mɩ nyuŋ, ŋ cho dɩ ŋ pɛ mɩ lɛ, laa mɩ dɩ mɩ nɩaa mɩɩsɩŋ pɩla. Wɩɩ-la kala mɩ sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ŋ ŋaa pɩmɛ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Mɩ dɩ mɩ nɩaa kala nɛ ba joŋo yallɛ dɩ ba kpʋ. Dɩ ba nɛ fa kɛsɛ la yallɛ arɩ yosuŋ mɩ fa bɩ jaŋ walɩmɩŋ. Ama baa chɛ dɩ ba kpʋla nɛ.”

english_verse: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoru Zɛzɛs pɩɛsɛ Ɛsɩta, “Kʋbɛɛ nɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wʋdoho deeŋ? Nɩɩ nɛ tɩɩna hɛ?”

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Ɛsɩta bʋl, “La dʋndɔmɔ nɛ ŋaa Hamaŋ, babɔmʋŋ deeŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ Hamaŋ kuoro arɩ Ɛsɩta sɩpaaŋ.”

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro na baanɩŋ a guu sii, aŋ leŋ ʋ tɩɩnɛnɛɛ sɩŋ-la ʋ fa sɩɩ nyʋa ta aŋ mʋ jʋʋ lɩga-la ba sɩ lɩga golli ʋ kuori dɩa. Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ Hamaŋ jɩŋ arɩ kuoro jaŋ ŋaaʋ wʋbɔŋ. Hamaŋ mɩɩra ka harɩŋ a sʋsʋl kuoro habidiire Ɛsɩta dɩ ʋ laa ʋ mɩɩsɩŋ pʋ.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Kuoro sɩ mɩɩra lɩɩ lɩga-la lɛ a kʋ jʋʋ dɩa-la lɛ ba fa sɩ hɔnɔ dii kɩaa, dɩ Hamaŋ tuu kpirimi Ɛsɩta sɩpaaŋ a sʋsʋlʋ dɩ ʋ fá ʋ nenige. Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro kpɩa a bʋl, “Baala deeŋ paala chɩchɛ dɩ ʋ gurigi mɩ habidiire nɛ mɩ kuoru dɩa lɛ koo?” Kuoro sɩ bʋl wɩɩŋ deeŋ dɩdɛrɛ, dɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnaa guu tɔ Hamaŋ sɩaa.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Lɩma lɩma dɩ ba kɛŋ Hamaŋ a lieŋu jebii-la ʋ sɩ saa dɩ ʋ lieŋi Modikaaya lɛ, ka kuoro baanɩŋ na fɩɛlɛ.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa nɛ kuoro Zɛzɛs laa Juu tɩŋŋaa dʋndɔŋ-la Hamaŋ kɩaa kala a pɩ Ɛsɩta. Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛsɩta bʋla pɩ kuoro arɩ Modikaaya ŋaa ʋ naambii nɛ. Kuoro leŋ Modikaaya ŋaa ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Kuoro joŋ nenii-pɩrɩ-la ʋ fa sɩ joŋo pɩ Hemaŋ a pɩ Modikaaya. Ɛsɩta joŋ Modikaaya hɛ ʋ bibeŋ Hamaŋ dʋa-la ba sɩ kaa laa.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Ɛsɩta bɩra sii mʋ dɩ ʋ bʋl wɩaa kuoro teeŋ. Bʋa deeŋ-na lɛ ʋ mʋ kpirimi ʋ naadʋsʋŋ nyuŋ nɛ a sʋlʋ aŋ yiyel a bʋl, “Mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ kuoro giri wʋbɔŋ-la Hamaŋ Agag tɩɩna-la fa sɩ bɩɩna dɩ ʋ ŋaa, a kpʋ Juu tɩŋŋaa kala.”

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ aŋ bʋl, “Kuoro dɩ ŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ jaŋ tɔrɛ, dɩ ŋ nɛ chaasa chomi, mɩɩ sʋlʋŋ ŋmʋnsɛ tenniŋ a tɩa dɩ ba kaa gɔllɛ kpaa ŋ tinteeŋ nɩaa kala a giri wʋbɔŋ-la Hamɛdata nanʋala Hamaŋ, Agag tɩɩna-la sɩ ŋmʋnsɛ pɩ ŋ tinteeŋ nɩaa dɩ ba kpʋ Juu tɩmma-la kala sɩ hɛ ŋ tinteeŋ lɛ ta.

english_verse: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
translation_verse: Mɩ sɛnɛ jaŋ wuo bibeŋ ŋ-la ka dɩ ba kpʋ mɩ naambiiriŋ kala? Mɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa ŋɩɩ.”

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro Zɛzɛs mɩɩra bʋla pɩ Ɛsɩta arɩ Modikaaya Juu tɩɩna-la, “Mɩ paala leŋ ba lieŋi Hamaŋ nɛ ka mɩ laa ʋ dʋa pɩ Ɛsɩta, a tɩŋ wʋbɔŋ-la ʋ sɩ bɩɩna a tɩgɛ Juu tɩŋŋaa kala wɩaa.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Mɩ pɩŋ wombiiŋ nɛ lɛɛlɛ dɩ ŋ chɩŋ Juu tɩŋŋaa kala naasɩŋ lɛ a ŋmʋnsɛ teniŋ dɔŋɔ mɩ-na kuoro yɩrɩŋ lɛ sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ba sɩ́ Juu tɩŋŋaa kpʋ, a kɛŋ mɩ nenii-pɩrɩ-la mɩ sɩ kaa magɩlɛ tenniŋ a magɩlɛ dɩ nʋʋkala sɩ́ wuo kaa bɩrɩmɛ.”

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Modikaaya ŋmʋnsɛ tenni-la kuoru Zɛzɛs yɩrɩŋ lɛ nɛ a joŋ nenii-pɩrɩ-la kuoro sɩ kaa magɩlɛ ʋ tenniŋ a magɩlɛ, dɩ tɩndaaraa laa tenni-la a jɩl kuoro janɩ-la sɩ faasa fá, a kaa gɔllɔ kpaa.

english_verse: In these letters the king said: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies. A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
translation_verse: Teŋ-la ŋaa nii nɛ kuoro bil dɩ ba karɩma pɩ ʋ tinteeŋ taŋ na-kala nɩaa dɩ ba jɩŋ, dɩ Juu tɩŋŋaa wuo kɛŋ ba tɩtɩa hɛ dɔŋɔ a ŋaa siri dɩ tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ yie dɩ ba yuo ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Modikaaya lɩɩ kuoro teeŋ a laalɛ kuoru-gɛrɩŋ sɩ nagɛ diibelimbine a tagɩsɛ kʋpulluŋ, a chu kuoru nyunchuulo ba sɩ kɛŋ sɛlɩmɛ ŋaa, a ha bɩra laalɛ gɛrɩŋ dɔŋɔ ma sɩ ŋaa gɛrɩpɛ vachalɩŋ gɛrɩ-fʋfʋlʋŋ a daŋ. Ka Susa nɩaa tʋɔŋ kala tɔrɛ ba jʋjʋɔsɛ.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Fawʋllʋŋ bɩra bɩ Juu tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ kɛnɛ, ka ba yaraa fɩɛlɛ ba tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ ba jʋjʋɔsɛ.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Tintee-na kala arɩ taŋ na-kala lɛ tɩndaara-la sɩ kɛŋ nii-la kuoro sɩ bile teniŋ a mʋ karɩma pɩba, Juu tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ tʋɔŋ yie tɔrɛ nɛ, tapʋlɩɩ-la ŋaa tapʋl-zɔŋ ba gbigbieli. Nɩwogusuŋ dɔnsʋŋ yʋgɛ a joŋ ba tɩtɩa arɩ ba ma ŋaa Juu tɩmma, bɛɛ wɩaa fawʋllʋŋ kɛmba nɛ a tɩŋ Juu tɩmma-la wɩaa.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Chɛŋ fii arɩ balɩa-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Adaa tapʋlaa fii arɩ batori chɛɛŋ, tapʋlɩɩ-la kuoro sɩ daga dɩ Juu tɩŋŋaa yuo ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ sɩ yie, Juu tɩŋŋaa dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ fa kɛŋ yɩɛlaa arɩ ba jaŋ wuo yuo dii Juu tɩŋŋaa, ama Juu tɩŋŋaa wuo yuo dii nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ bɛrɛba.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Kuoro Zɛzɛs tinteeŋ tasɩ-la kala lɛ, Juu tɩŋŋaa hilimi a ŋaa siri dɩ ba yuo ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ. Fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ nɩwogusu-la ba kʋŋkala bɩ wuo lɩɩ cheŋ Juu tɩmma-la.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Kuoro tinteeŋ sɩpaalaaraa, ʋ kuoru-biisiŋ arɩ ʋ tɩntɩnnɩ-hɩasɩŋ kala sii chɩŋ Juu tɩŋŋaa harɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba faa fa Modikaaya nɛ.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Modikaaya lɛɛlɛ kʋ ŋaa nɩbal kuoro dɩa lɛ, ʋ yɩrɩŋ teeli tintee-la kala kuoro sɩɩ beŋ, ʋ doluŋ faasa pʋŋa pɛ.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Juu tɩŋŋaa paa ba tokobiee a kpʋ ba dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ ŋɩɩ kala ba sɩɩ chɛ.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la tɩtɩa nɛ ba dagɛ nɩalɩŋ Juu tɩŋŋaa sɩ kpʋa Susa lɛ niiŋ a pɩ kuoro.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro bʋla pɩ ʋ habidiire Ɛsɩta, “Susa dʋndʋŋa lɛ Juu tɩŋŋaa kpʋ nɩaa zɔɔ-banɔŋ nɛ, a pɛ Hamaŋ biiriŋ fii lɛ. Dɩ nɩaa nɛ magɛ ŋ-la dɩ ba kpʋ daha dʋndʋŋa, nɩaa magɛ ɛɛ nɛ ba jaŋ kpʋ mɩ tinteeŋ kala lɛ? Wɩɩ dɔŋ nɛ bɩra hɛ nɩmɛ ŋ chɛ dɩ mɩ ŋaa? Bʋl, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Ɛsɩta bʋl, “Kuoro dɩ ʋ nɛ jaŋ tɔrɛ ŋ tʋɔŋ, chie bɩra pɩ Juu tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Susa lɛ wombiiŋ dɩ ba yuo laa ba tɩtɩa arɩ ba sɩ ŋaa ŋɩɩ jɩnɩŋ. Leŋ dɩ ba paa Hamaŋ biiri-la fii ba sɩ kpʋa kʋsʋʋnʋŋ a sagɛ lee-la nʋʋkala sɩ jaŋ nɩnaba.”

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kuoro pa wombiiŋ ba ŋaa wɩɩ-la Ɛsɩta sɩɩ chɛ a paa Hamaŋ biiri-la fii kʋsʋʋnʋŋ sagɛ Susa lɛ.

english_verse: Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed
translation_verse: Chɛnɛ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Adaa tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɛsɛ chɛɛŋ, Juu tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Susa lɛ bɩra sii hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ a kpʋ nɩaa zɔɔ-batori ama ba bɩ ba dʋa paa.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Juu tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ Susa lɛ ma kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ Adaa chɛnɛ-la tapʋl fii arɩ batori arɩ tapʋl fii arɩ banɛsɛ chɛɛŋ nɛ, aŋ ma sii wiesi tapʋl fii arɩ banɔŋ chɛɛŋ a dii kʋdiilee aŋ gbieli.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Ŋ-la nɛ tɩɩ Juu tɩmma-la sɩ hɛ tabiisiŋ lɛ joŋ chɛnɛ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Adaa tapʋlaa fii arɩ banɛsɛ chɛɛŋ ʋ ŋaa tʋɔŋ tɔrɛ tapʋlɩɩ ba yie dii kɩaa aŋ gbigbieli aŋ pɛ ŋaa kʋdiilee pɩpɩ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
