english_verse: He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.” The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
translation_verse: Má kpʋ banɩhɩasɩŋ, bapʋɔsaa, hatoloo, naamba arɩ hambiisiŋ. Ama má sɩ́ nʋʋkala sɩ kɛŋ magɩl-la digu. Má suomi mɩ dɩa lɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba suomi sɩpaalaara-la sɩ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ bʋla pɩba, “Má ŋaa disiniŋ hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-balɩŋ lɛ, a paa sʋʋnʋŋ su ʋ kaalɩsɩ-la kala. Má mʋ a ŋaa ŋɩɩ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba lɩɩ a suomo kpʋkpʋ nɩaa tabal-la kala lɛ.

english_verse: I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
translation_verse: Ba fa sɩɩ kpʋ nɩaa ŋɩɩ, ka mɩ chɩŋ mɩ dʋndʋŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ tele chu a ŋmoo niiŋ a pɩɛsɛ, “Ou, La TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ, ŋ baanɩŋ chaasa sii Jerusalɛm nyuŋ nɛ ŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ŋ kpʋ nʋʋ na-kala sɩ hɛ Iziral lɛɛ?”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa bʋl, “Iziral arɩ Juda nɩaa chaasa ŋaa wʋbɔŋ bal nɛ, ba kpʋ nɩaa yʋgɛ nɛ tintee-la lɛ, ka Jerusalɛm kala su arɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ. Ba yie bʋl, ‘La TƖƖNA vɩa la tinteeŋ ta nɛ, ʋ bɩ laa na.’

english_verse: And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, mɩ bɩ jaŋ kɔ dɩ mɩ fá ba nisusuŋ koo a lemba, ama mɩ jaŋ joŋ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ ŋaa a tiŋ ba lɛ.”

english_verse: Just then, the man in the linen robe returned and said, “I have done what you commanded.”
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ baal-la fa sɩ laalɛ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ gɛrɩŋ, ka kʋ-la ba sɩ kaa ŋmʋŋmʋnsɛ kɩaa hɛ ʋ sɛmɛ mɩɩra kɔ a bʋl, “Mɩ ŋaa wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ sɩ mɩ ŋaa nɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, “Walk among the four wheels beside the creatures and pick up as many hot coals as you can carry. Then scatter them over the city of Jerusalem.” I watched him as he followed the Lord's instructions.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋla pɩ baal-la sɩ laalɛ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ gɛrɩŋ, “Jʋʋ kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba-la pɛgɛ, a chaanɛ nyiŋ-halaa su ŋ nɩsaa. Joŋ nyiŋ-hala-la a yuo jaasɛ taŋ-la kala lɛ.” Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bibenu ka ʋ jʋʋ.

english_verse: The winged creatures were standing south of the temple when the man walked among them. A cloud filled the inner courtyard,
translation_verse: Kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ fa chɩŋ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ nɛ ka baal-la jʋʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaanɩŋ kʋ tɔ tʋɔŋ kaala-la kala.

english_verse: and the brightness of the Lord's glory moved from above the creatures and stopped at the entrance of the temple. The entire temple was filled with his glory, and the courtyard was dazzling bright.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA tʋla sii kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ nyuŋ a mʋ chɩŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la boiŋ nii-jʋʋlʋŋ lɛ. Duoŋ-bɩlɩmbaaŋ-la tuu su Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la, La TƖƖNA tʋla su kaala-la kala.

english_verse: The sound of the creatures' wings was as loud as the voice of God All-Powerful and could even be heard in the outer courtyard.
translation_verse: Kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ, ba kɩŋkɛnsɩ-la faa dɔŋ nɛ a nagɛ Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ yikoro, dɩ ŋ nɛ paala hɛ Wɩa dɩɩ-bal-la harɩŋ kaala-la tʋɔŋ ma, ŋ haa nɩɩ ba dɔmɔ nɛ.

english_verse: One of the four creatures reached its hand into the fire among them and gave him some of the hot coals. The man took the coals and left.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ dɔŋɔ joŋ ʋ nɩsɩŋ hɛ nyiŋ-la sɩ hɛ ba pɛgɛ tʋɔŋ a chaanɛ nyiŋ-halaa hɛ baal-la sɩ laalɛ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ gɛrɩŋ nɩsaa lɛ. Baal-la laa nyiŋ-hala-la a kaa lɩɩ.

english_verse: I noticed again that each of the four winged creatures had what looked like human hands under their wings,
translation_verse: Kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ bʋbʋɔŋ, nɩsaa nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ a nagɛ nuhuobiine nɩsaa.

english_verse: Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it,
translation_verse: Gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba-la banɛsɛ kala fa nagɛ dɔŋɔ nɛ, a gɩrɩgɛ dɔŋɔ lɛ.

english_verse: I also noticed that the wheels and the creatures' bodies, including their backs, their hands, and their wings, were covered with eyes.
translation_verse: Ba yaraa kala, ba harɩŋ, ba nɩsaa, ba kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ arɩ gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba-la kala fa kɛŋ sɩaa nɛ.

english_verse: And I heard a voice calling these “the wheels that spin.”
translation_verse: Mɩ nɩɩ yikoro sɩ yɩrɛ gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba-la: “Gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba sɩɩ villu.”

english_verse: Each of the winged creatures had four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a human, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle.
translation_verse: Kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ fa kɛŋ sɩaa nɛ ba sɛsɩŋ banɛsɛ kala lɛ. Sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ sɩaa nagɛ nɛ-bele sɩaa nɛ, sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ sɩaa nagɛ nuhuobiine sɩaa, sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ ma sɩaa nagɛ naachigiŋ sɩaa, ka sɛmɛ dɔŋɔ ma sɩaa nagɛ kachuuŋ sɩaa.

english_verse: These were the same creatures I had seen near the Chebar River. They controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels stayed beside them.
translation_verse: Dɩ kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ nɛ chɩna, gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba-la ma yie chɩŋ nɛ, dɩ ba nɛ sie, ba ma yie sii to nɛ, bɛɛ wɩaa kɩalɩŋ sɩ weye dɩma fa hɛ gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba-la lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: Then I watched the brightness of the Lord's glory move from the entrance of the temple and stop above the winged creatures.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tʋla-la bɩra sii ʋ dɩɩ-bal-la boiŋ nii-jʋʋlʋŋ lɛ a kʋ chuguli kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: They spread their wings and flew into the air with the wheels at their side. They stopped at the east gate of the temple, and the Lord's glory was above them.
translation_verse: Mɩ bibeŋ, ka kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ kɛŋ ba kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ jɛrɛ a sii jɩl wɩa-nyuŋ, gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba-la ma tuto. Ba mʋ chɩŋ La TƖƖNA dɩɩ-bal-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ boi-baalɩŋ lɛ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa tʋla ma mʋ chuguli ba nyuŋ.

english_verse: I knew for sure that these were the same creatures I had seen beneath the Lord's glory near the Chebar River.
translation_verse: Kɩaa deemba sɩ weye nɛ mɩ fa na Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa bʋbʋɔŋ ŋɩɩ, Keba fuo-la sɛmɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ jɩŋ arɩ kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ nɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: They had four wings with hands beneath them, and they had the same four faces as those near the River. Each creature moved straight ahead without turning.
translation_verse: Ba sɩaa fa nagɛ kɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ na Keba fuo-la sɛmɛ nɛ. Ba faa vɛŋ nɛ tegi tegi.

english_verse: and I told them everything the Lord had shown me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ bʋl wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA fa sɩ joŋo dagɛmɛ a pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ yoŋ-baga lɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, these men are making evil plans and giving dangerous advice to the people of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA fa bʋla pɩmɛ, “Nuhuobiiŋ, baalaa deemba nɩɩ vʋʋrɛ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ aŋ dɩdagɛ nɩaa nɩbɔŋ wɩaa tabalɩŋ deeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: They say things like, ‘Let's build more houses. This city is like a cooking pot over a fire, and we are the meat, but at least the pot keeps us from being burned in the fire.’
translation_verse: Ba pɩɛsɛ dɔŋɔ, ‘Bʋa deeŋ lɛ dee bɩ maga dɩ la saa dɩɩsɩŋ? Tabalɩŋ deeŋ ŋaa pupoiŋ nɛ, ka la ma nagɛ nammɩa a hɛ ʋ tʋɔŋ, ama ʋ ha tɔla nɛ dɩ nyiniŋ sɩ́ la dii.’

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of me and told me to tell these leaders: I, the Lord God, know what you leaders are saying.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ Wɩa Dɩma-la kʋ jʋʋmɛ a bʋla pɩmɛ dɩ mɩ bʋla pɩba, “Wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Iziral tɩmma, mɩ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la ma sɩɩ bʋl arɩ wɩɩ-la ma sɩɩ bɩɩnʋ nɛ.

english_verse: You have murdered so many people that the city is filled with dead bodies!
translation_verse: Nɩ-daŋ nɛ ma kpʋ tabalɩŋ deeŋ lɛ, ʋ womporunuŋ kala su arɩ sʋʋnʋŋ.

english_verse: This city is indeed a cooking pot, but the bodies of those you killed are the meat. And so I will force you to leave Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Sʋʋnʋ-la ma sɩ joŋo yuo ta nɛ ŋaa nammɩa-la, tabal-la ma nɛ ŋaa pupoiŋ, ama mɩ jaŋ kirima ta dɩ ma lɩɩ ʋ lɛ.

english_verse: and I'll send armies to attack you, just as you fear.
translation_verse: Maa fá laalɩŋ nɛ, laalɩŋ nɛ saa mɩ jaŋ joŋo hɛ ma lɛ. Ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: Then you will be captured and punished by foreign enemies.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ kirima ta dɩ ma lɩɩ tabal-la lɛ a jomma hɛ nɩwogusuŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ a dɔgɩsɛma.

english_verse: You will be killed in your own country, but not before you realize that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ kpʋma laalɩŋ lɛ, mɩ jaŋ dii ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa sarɩya ma tɩtɩa tinteeŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: You leaders claim to be meat in a cooking pot, but you won't be protected by this city. No, you will die at the border of Israel.
translation_verse: Tabalɩŋ deeŋ bɩra bɩ jaŋ ŋaa ma pupoiŋ ka dɩ ma ma ŋaa nammɩa a hɛ ʋ lɛ, mɩ jaŋ dii ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa sarɩya ma tɩtɩa tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: You will realize that while you were following the laws of nearby nations, you were disobeying my laws and teachings. And I am the Lord!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ-na nɛ ma TƖƖNA, ka ma bɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ daga arɩ mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile to, aŋ mɩɩra tuto tinteye-la sɩ gollima wʋŋaalaa.”

english_verse: Before I finished speaking, Pelatiah dropped dead. I bowed down and cried out, “Please, Lord God, don't kill everyone left in Israel.” A Promise of Hope
translation_verse: Mɩ fa ha sɩɩ bʋl wɩaa Wɩa doluŋ lɛ ŋɩɩ, Bɛnaaya nanʋala Pɛlatɩa tele sʋʋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ tele kɛŋ mɩ sɩaa chu tinteeŋ, aŋ ŋmoo niiŋ bogi bogi a pɩɛsɛ, “La TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ, ŋ jaŋ kpʋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩkaanaa kalaa?”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in Jerusalem claim that you and the other Israelites who were taken to Babylonia are too far away to worship me. They also claim that the land of Israel now belongs only to them.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, ŋ naambiiriŋ arɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kala sɩ hɛ yoŋ-baga lɛ, ma wɩaa nɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ bʋl, ‘Ba dɩ La TƖƖNA pɛgɛ bolie nɛ, La TƖƖNA joŋ tinteeŋ deeŋ pɩla nɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa la kʋŋ.’ La TƖƖNA sɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa jaŋ mɩɩra kɔ

english_verse: But here is what I want you to tell the Israelites in Babylonia: It's true that I, the Lord God, have forced you out of your own country and made you live among foreign nations. But for now, I will be with you wherever you are, so that you can worship me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ yoŋ-baga lɛ, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Mɩ nɛ fa leŋe ba mʋ tintee-wogusuŋ a kɛmba pɩsa hɛ tinteyee sɩ bolie lɛ, ama mɩ hɛ ba teeŋ nɛ a pɔba tinteye-la kala lɛ ba sɩ mʋa.’

english_verse: When that happens, I want you to clear the land of all those idols I hate so much.
translation_verse: Dɩ ba nɛ mɩɩra kɔ, ba jaŋ chei tɔŋŋɔɔ sɩ ŋaa disiŋ kɩaa arɩ vesiŋ mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ kala sɩ hɛ tintee-la lɛ.

english_verse: Then I will take away your stubbornness and make you eager to be completely faithful to me. You will want to obey me
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ba kɛŋ tʋɔ-bala a tutomi, a pɩba dɩŋ-falɩŋ. Mɩ jaŋ lɩɩsɛ tʋɔ-dol-la sɩ nagɛ tabɩɩŋ a hɛ ba lɛ ta, aŋ pɩba tʋɔ-la sɩ pʋnyɛ.

english_verse: and all my laws and teachings. You will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba jaŋ to mɩ wʋdagaa a fɩɛlɛ ba sɩaa a to mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto. Ba jaŋ ŋaa mɩ nɩaa, dɩ mɩ ma ŋaa ba Wɩa.

english_verse: But those who worship idols will be punished and get what they deserve. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord's Glory Leaves Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ama nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ to tɔŋŋɔɔ sɩ ŋaa disiŋ kɩa arɩ vesiŋ mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ, mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛba a tɩŋ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ ŋaa wɩaa. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.”

english_verse: After the Lord had finished speaking, the winged creatures spread their wings and flew into the air, and the wheels were beside them. The brightness of the Lord's glory above them
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ kɩalɩŋ sɩ nagɛ Wɩa tɩndaaraa a kɛŋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ, gɩrɩŋgɩrɩmba hɛ ba sɛsɩŋ lɛ file jɩl wɩa-nyuŋ, ka Iziral tɩŋŋaa Wɩa tʋla chuguli ba lɛ.

english_verse: left Jerusalem and stopped at a hill east of the city.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA tʋla-la faa sii tabal-la lɛ a mʋ chɩŋ peeliŋ nyuŋ, tabal-la wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ.

english_verse: Then in my vision, the Lord's Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to the other exiles in Babylonia. The vision faded away,
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ mɩ fa sɩ na arɩ duosoo tʋɔŋ, Wɩa Dɩma-la jommi kaa mʋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ yoŋ-baga lɛ Babɩlɔŋ tinteeŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ wɩalɩŋ mɩ fa sɩ na a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ lɛl.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, you are living among rebellious people. They have eyes, but refuse to see; they have ears, but refuse to listen.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, ŋ hɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ. Ba kɛŋ sɩaa nɛ a magɛ dɩ ba nɩna, ama ba bɩ na, a kɛŋ dɩgɩlaa a magɛ dɩ ba nɩnɩɩ ka ba bɩ nɩɩ, bɛɛ wɩaa ba ŋaa nɩa sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ nɛ.

english_verse: So before it gets dark, here is what I want you to do. Pack a few things as though you were going to be taken away as a prisoner. Then go outside where everyone can see you and walk around from place to place. Maybe as they watch, they will realize what rebels they are.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, nuhuobiiŋ, leŋ dɩ ba naŋ ka dɩ ŋ paa ŋ kɩaa wɩɩhɛyɛ a lɩɩ mʋmʋ yoŋ-baga. Lɩɩ lee-la ŋ sɩ hɛ a lɩɩ mʋ lee dɔŋ. Ba ŋaa nɩa sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ nɛ, kapo ba jaŋ jɩŋ wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa bʋbʋɔŋ.

english_verse: After you have done this, return to your house. Later that evening leave your house as if you were going into exile.
translation_verse: Kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ paa dɩ ŋ kaa mʋ yoŋ-baga kʋ lɩɩ dɩ-jalɩŋ wɩɩhɛyɛ ka dɩ ba bibeniŋ. Leŋ dɩ ba naŋ dɩdaanɩŋ ka dɩ ŋ lɩɩ a nagɛ nɩaa sɩɩ mʋ yoŋ-baga.

english_verse: Dig through the wall of your house and crawl out, carrying the bag with you. Make sure everyone is watching.
translation_verse: Ba sɩɩ beniŋ ŋɩɩ, ta jeeŋ luri a paa ŋ kɩaa kaa to nɩmɛ lɩɩ.

english_verse: Lift the bag to your shoulders, and with your face covered, take it into the darkness, so that you cannot see the land you are leaving. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Leŋ dɩ ba naŋ ka dɩ ŋ joŋ kɩalɩŋ baasɛ a kaa lɩɩ sɩɩ-dɩsaa. Joŋ kʋŋ tɔ ŋ sɩaa dɩ ŋ sɩ́ tintee-la lɛ ŋ sɩɩ lɩɩ na. Wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa jaŋ ŋaa magɩl a pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa.”

english_verse: I did everything the Lord had said. I packed a few things. Then as the sun was going down, and while everyone was watching, I dug a hole through one of the walls of my house. I pulled out my bag, then lifted it to my shoulders and left in the darkness.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ kala La TƖƖNA fa sɩ sɩ mɩ ŋaa. Wɩɩhɛyɛ mɩ paa mɩ kɩaa kʋ lɩɩ dɩ mɩ mʋ yoŋ-baga. Dɩdaanɩŋ mɩ ta jeeŋ luri a paa mɩ kɩaa baasɛ a lɩɩ sɩɩ-dɩsaa ka ba bibeŋ.

english_verse: The next morning, the Lord
translation_verse: Chʋchʋɔŋ La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩmɛ:

english_verse: reminded me that those rebellious people didn't even ask what I was doing.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, Iziral tɩmma-la sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ bɩŋ wɩɩ pɩɛsa arɩ bɛɛ nɛ ŋ ŋɩŋaa ŋɩɩ?

english_verse: So he sent me back to tell them: The Lord God has a message for the leader of Jerusalem and everyone living there!
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩba, Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ joŋo dagɩŋ mʋʋ tɩgɛ sɩpaalaarʋ-la sɩɩ beŋ Jerusalɛm arɩ nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: I have done these things to show them what will happen when they are taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Bɩra bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ‘Wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ ŋaa, ba ŋaa magɩl nɛ a pɩba.’ Ŋɩɩ mɩ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa, ŋɩɩ nɛ jaŋ ŋaa ba ma lɛ. Ba jaŋ kɛsɛba kaa mʋ yoŋ-baga.

english_verse: The leader of Jerusalem will lift his own bag to his shoulders at sunset and leave through a hole that the others have dug in the wall of his house. He will cover his face, so he can't see the land he is leaving.
translation_verse: Jerusalɛm sɩpaalaara jaŋ paa ʋ kɩaa baasɛ a lɩɩ sɩɩ-dɩsaa, ba jaŋ ta jeeŋ luro pʋ dɩ ʋ to nɩmɛ lɩɩ. Ʋ jaŋ tɔ ʋ sɩaa dɩ ʋ sɩ́ tintee-la lɛ ʋ sɩɩ lɩɩ na.

english_verse: The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ yuo mɩ jóŋ a kɛnʋ, mɩ jaŋ kɛnʋ mʋ Babɩlɔŋ, Chalɩdɩ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ. Ʋ bɩ jaŋ na lee-la, ama nɩmɛ nɛ ʋ jaŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ ŋmoo nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ ʋ teeŋ pɩsɛ, nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ dagʋ arɩ laalɩyuoro-la sɩɩ pɔʋ, a kire to kpʋba arɩ tokobiiŋ.

english_verse: The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things.
translation_verse: Dɩ mɩ nɛ ŋmoo Jerusalɛm nɩaa pɩsa hɛ tintee-wogusuŋ lɛ, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ba TƖƖNA.

english_verse: Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way. A Sign of Fear
translation_verse: Ama mɩ jaŋ leŋ ba nɩaa baŋmɛnɛ, mɩ bɩ jaŋ kpʋ ba kala laalɩŋ lɛ, losuŋ arɩ nyanyal bɔŋŋɔɔ ma bɩ jaŋ kpʋ ba kala. Dɩ ba nɛ mʋ tinteye-la, dɩ ba wuo liisi wʋkɩsɩa-la kala ba sɩ ŋaa. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋaa ba TƖƖNA.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, didii ŋ kʋdiilee aŋ chichel, aŋ nyʋnyʋa lɩɩŋ ma arɩ fawʋllʋŋ aŋ chichel.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent.
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩ tintee-la nɩaa: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla tɩgɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm arɩ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ ŋ-la: Ba jaŋ dii ba kʋdiilee arɩ fawʋllʋŋ, a nyʋa lɩɩŋ ma arɩ tʋɔ-cheeŋ. Nɩaa jaŋ chei ba tinteeŋ dɩ ʋ pɩŋ hoi, a tɩŋ ba nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɔŋ lee-la sɩ ŋaa yuo-hɛɛrɛɛ wɩaa.

english_verse: Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord. The Words of the Lord Will Come True
translation_verse: Tasɩ-la lɛ nɩaa sɩ hɔnɔ jaŋ pɩŋ jikpeeŋ, dɩ tintee-la kala pɩŋ hoi. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ba TƖƖNA.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.”
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, bɛɛ kʋŋ namaga nɛ maa magɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ ŋ-la, ‘Tapʋlaa bala a yʋgɛ nɛ ka wɩalɩŋ kala Wɩa sɩ joŋo dagɛ nɩaa a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ bɩ ŋaa.’

english_verse: Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true!
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa bʋla pɩba, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Mɩɩ chɛ dɩ mɩ giri namaga-la ta nɛ, ba bɩra bɩ jaŋ magʋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ.’ Bɩra bʋla pɩba, ‘Tapʋlaa kpaga nɛ, wɩɩ na-kala mɩ fa sɩ joŋo dagɛ nɩaa a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ jaŋ kʋ ŋaa.

english_verse: I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ama mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA jaŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩɩ chɛ, ʋ jaŋ sɛnɛ ŋaa, ʋ bɩ dieni. Ma ŋaa nɩa sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ nɛ. Ma mɩɩsɩŋ lɛ, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ bʋla, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩ, ‘Wɩalɩŋ Wɩa sɩ joŋo dagɛ Ɛzɩkɩɛl a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ ŋaa jɩ-dandaŋ wɩɩ nɛ, lɛɛlɛ dee. Wɩalɩŋ ma ʋ sɩ bʋla Wɩa doluŋ lɛ ŋaa maachie wɩaa nɛ.’

english_verse: So tell them that my words will soon come true, just as I have warned. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa bʋla pɩba, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ bʋla kʋŋkala bɩ jaŋ dieni. Mɩ wʋbʋlaa kala jaŋ kʋ ŋaa, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, bʋl wɩaa mɩ doluŋ lɛ a hɛ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ nyɩɛ wɩaa arɩ ba ŋaa mɩ wʋlaabʋllaa nɛ a hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ a bʋbʋl wɩaa naabʋɔsʋŋ deemba lɛ. Bʋla pɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ bʋl ba tɩtɩa tʋɔbɩɩnaa wɩaa: ‘Má jegile nɩɩ wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA sɩ bʋla.’

english_verse: Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city.
translation_verse: Iziral tɩmma, ma wʋlaabʋllaa nagɛ jolluŋ sɩ hɛ jikpeeniŋ lɛ nɛ.

english_verse: They don't warn the people about coming trouble or tell them how dangerous it is to sin against me.
translation_verse: Ba bɩ chɩna pɔ jee-la lere-la sɩ tele, a bɩ jee-la paa wasa saa ma dɩ Iziral tinteeŋ chɩŋ kpaŋkpaŋ dɩ La TƖƖNA tapʋlɩɩ-la nɛ yie dɩ laalɩŋ sii.

english_verse: Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true.
translation_verse: Wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ na a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ, arɩ ba vʋgʋrʋ wɩaa ŋaa wʋnyɩɛrɩŋ nɛ. Ba sɩ, ‘La TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla,’ ka mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA bɩ ba tɩma, ka ba ha bɩɩnɛ arɩ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩ bʋla jaŋ kʋ ŋaa wʋtɩtɩɩ.

english_verse: They say they're preaching my messages, but they are full of lies—I did not speak to them!
translation_verse: Ba nyɩɛ wɩaa arɩ ma na wɩaa a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ nɛ a vʋga nyɩɛ wɩaa ma, bʋa-la lɛ ba sɩ sɩ, ‘La TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla,’ ka mɩ bɩ wɩɩ bʋla.

english_verse: I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ ma nɩalɩŋ sɩ nyɩɛ wɩaa arɩ maa na wɩaa a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ nɛ, a vʋgaa nyɩɛ wɩaa. Ma bɩra bɩ jaŋ guoli mɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ yie hilime vʋvʋʋrɛ wɩaa tʋɔŋ, koo dɩ ba ŋmʋnsɛ ma yɩraa hɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ koo ma jʋʋ Iziral tinteeŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ.

english_verse: Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint.
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩ nyɩɛ wɩaa a leŋ mɩ nɩaa yeŋŋi yie bʋl, ‘Fɩɛlɩŋ hɛ nɩmɛ nɛ,’ ka fɩɛlɩŋ tuo. Mɩ nɩaa saa jeeŋ sɩ bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ nɛ, nɩalɩŋ sɩ nyɩɛ wɩaa arɩ ba ŋaa mɩ wʋlaabʋllaa kʋ ŋaa tʋɔrʋŋ bʋgɛ.

english_verse: People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
translation_verse: Dɩ jee-la sɩ bɩ doluŋ kɛnɛ nɛ tele, nɩaa jaŋ pɩɛsɛma, ‘Tʋɔrʋ-la ma sɩ joŋo bʋgɛ jee-la hɛ nɩa?’

english_verse: That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Mɩ jaŋ faasa na baanɩŋ a leŋ dɩ pel-duoŋ lu dɩ duonuŋ lɔgɔ jaasɛ, dɩ duoŋ-tabɩaa tele yagɛ jee-la lo.

english_verse: The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ yigi jee-la ma sɩ joŋ tʋɔrʋŋ bʋgɛ a lo, a yɛrɛ ʋ kala muno muno ka dɩ ʋ gentine nyɩɩsɛ, dɩ jee-la nɛ tele, ʋ jaŋ kpʋ ma kala. Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead,
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ joŋ mɩ baanɩŋ fɩɩsɛ jee-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ joŋ tʋɔrʋŋ bʋgʋ kala nyuŋ a cheiba. Mɩ jaŋ bʋla pɩma: Jee-la arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ joŋ tʋɔrʋŋ bʋgʋ kala lɛlɛ nɛ.

english_verse: because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Women Who Wear Magic Charms The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nɩalɩŋ sɩ nyɩɛ wɩaa arɩ ba ŋaa mɩ wʋlaabʋlla nɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ, a bʋla pɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa arɩ ba na wɩaa a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ dɩ fɩɛlɩŋ hɛ ʋ lɛ nɛ, ka fɩɛl kala tuo. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination.
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA sɩ, “Nuhuobiiŋ, joŋ sɩaa chaasɛ haala-la sɩ hɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ a nyɩɛ wɩaa arɩ ba ŋaa mɩ wʋlaabʋlla nɛ aŋ bʋbʋl ba tɩtɩa tʋɔbɩɩnaa wɩaa. Bʋl wɩaa mɩ doluŋ lɛ a hɛ ba lɛ,

english_verse: Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies.
translation_verse: a bʋla pɩba, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Hɛɛŋ jaŋ jʋʋ haala-la sɩ yɛrɛ chichiribi kɩalɩŋ ba sɩ kaa bugumi nɩaa a vɔɔ ba nachɩgɩsɩŋ, aŋ yɛrɛ nyu-kpal-duduosuŋ ma ba sɩ kaa bɛrɛɛ kɛsɛ nɩaa a vɔɔ nyusuŋ. Ma bɩɩna ma jaŋ wuo bɛrɛ kɛsɛ mɩ nɩaa dɩ ba sʋʋ, aŋ ka dɩ ma-na kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ koo?

english_verse: They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
translation_verse: Ma chei mɩ yɩrɩŋ nɛ mɩ nɩaa tʋɔŋ, aŋ laa mɩaa nɩsɩŋ sɩɩŋ arɩ boroboro biisiŋ mʋa. Ma nyɩɛ wɩaa pɩ mɩ nɩaa nɛ ba laa wʋnyɩɛrɩ-la dii, ka ma kpʋ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ maga dɩ ba sʋʋ, aŋ leŋ nɩalɩŋ fa sɩ maga dɩ ba sʋʋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Mɩ bɛrɛ chichiribi kɩalɩŋ ma sɩ kaa bɛrɛɛ kɛsɛ nɩaa a nagɛ ba ŋaa diibiisiŋ nɛ, mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ kɩalɩŋ kɛrɛ ma nɩsaa lɛ, aŋ laa nɩalɩŋ ma sɩ bɛrɛ kɛsɛ a nagɛ ba ŋaa diibiisiŋ nɛ a ta.

english_verse: I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ ma nyu-kpal-duduosu-la puri aŋ laa mɩ nɩaa ta ma nɩsaa lɛ, dɩ ma bɩra sɩ́ doluŋ kɛŋ ba lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin.
translation_verse: Ma nyɩɛ wɩaa a ŋaa tʋɔpʋl tɩmma-la mɩ sɩ bɩ chɛ mɩ leŋ dɩ ba tʋɔŋ chei, nandaasɩŋ yʋɔrɛ nɛ, aŋ leŋ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ nyuŋ nyaasɛ dɩ ba sɩ bɩrɩma lɩɩ ba wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ a laa ba mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: I will no longer let these women give false messages and use magic, and I will free my people from their control. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, ma bɩra bɩ jaŋ nyɩɛ wɩaa arɩ maa na wɩaa a nagɛ duosoo tʋɔŋ nɛ, koo a ŋaa vʋgʋra. Mɩ jaŋ laa mɩ nɩaa ta ma nɩsɩŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA.’ ”

english_verse: One day, some of Israel's leaders came to me and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala Iziral tɩŋŋaa nɩhɩasɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ sii kɔ mɩ teeŋ la hɔŋ.

english_verse: While they were there, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩmɛ:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these men have started worshiping idols, though they know it will cause them to sin even more. So I refuse to give them a message!
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, nɩaa deemba joŋ vʋɩyaa kpaarɩŋ nɛ hɛ ba nyuŋ lɛ, a leŋ nɩbɔŋ wɩaa kɛrɛba. Ɛɛ nɛ saa ba jaŋ pɩɛsɛmɛ dɩ mɩ dagɛba wɩaa?

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that if they sin by worshiping idols and then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will give them the answer their sins deserve.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩmma-la, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ba TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Iziral tɩɩna kala nɛ joŋ vʋɩyaa kpaarɩŋ hɛ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ, a leŋ nɩbɔŋ wɩaa kɛrʋ, aŋ sii mʋ Wɩa wʋlaabʋlla teeŋ dɩ ʋ pɩɛsa na wɩɩ mɩ teeŋ, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA tɩtɩa nɛ jaŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ a mʋ tɩgɛ ʋ vʋɩ-kpaarɩ-daŋ-la lɛ a pʋ.

english_verse: When they hear my message, maybe they will see that they need to turn back to me and stop worshiping those idols.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ jaŋ ŋaa a kɛŋ Iziral tɩmma-la kala sɩ vɩamɛ aŋ kpʋkpaarɛ vʋɩyaa tʋɔbɩɩnaa bɩrɩmɛ dɩ ba tutomi.’

english_verse: Now, Ezekiel, tell everyone in Israel: I am the Lord God. Stop worshiping those idols I hate so much and come back to me.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Má bɩrɩma lɩɩ ma wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ. Má leŋ ma vʋɩya-la arɩ wʋkɩsɩa-la kala ma sɩɩ ŋaa.

english_verse: Suppose one of you Israelites or a foreigner living in Israel rejects me and starts worshiping idols. If you then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will answer
translation_verse: Dɩ Iziral tɩɩna koo dɩ nʋhʋɔrʋ sɩ hɔŋ ma tʋɔŋ nɛ vɩamɛ aŋ joŋ vʋɩyaa kpaarɩŋ hɛ ʋ nyuŋ lɛ, a leŋ nɩbɔŋ wɩaa kɛrʋ, aŋ sii mʋ mɩ wʋlaabʋlla teeŋ dɩ ʋ pɩɛsa na wɩɩ mɩ teeŋ, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA tɩtɩa nɛ jaŋ bʋl wɩɩ-la sɩ hɛ nɩmɛ a pʋ.

english_verse: by turning against you. I will make you a warning to anyone who might think of doing the same thing, and you will no longer belong to my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord and that you have sinned against me.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ tɩɩna a leŋ dɩ ŋɩɩ ŋaa wɩɩ a chagɩlɛ nʋʋkala sɩɩ chɛ dɩ ʋ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ tɩtɩa tɩɩna sɩ ŋaa, dɩ ba liisi ʋ wɩaa a bʋbʋl. Mɩ jaŋ keri tɩɩna ta mɩ nɩaa tʋɔŋ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA.

english_verse: If a prophet gives a false message, I am the one who caused that prophet to lie. But I will still reject him and cut him off from my people,
translation_verse: Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ nyɩsɛ mɩ wʋlaabʋllʋ hɛ dɩ ʋ nyɩɛ bʋl wɩaa mɩ doluŋ lɛ, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA tɩtɩa nɛ nyɩsʋ ŋɩɩ. Ama mɩ jaŋ lɩɩsɛ mɩ nɩsɩŋ liesu a cheyu a lɩɩsʋ ta mɩ nɩaa Iziral tɩŋŋaa tʋɔŋ.

english_verse: and anyone who goes to that prophet for a message will be punished in the same way.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛ nɩɩ-la sɩ mʋ mɩ wʋlaabʋllʋ-la teeŋ dɩ ʋ pɩɛsa na wɩaa arɩ mɩ wʋlaabʋllʋ-la kala a magɛ dɔŋɔ.

english_verse: I will do this, so that you will come back to me and stop destroying yourselves with these disgusting sins. So turn back to me! Then I will be your God, and you will be my people. I, the Lord God, make this promise. Judgment on a Sinful Nation
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ jaŋ leŋ dɩ Iziral nɩaa bɩra sɩ́ mɩ vɩa, koo a ŋaa wʋbɔŋ a kɛŋ disiniŋ. Ba jaŋ ŋaa mɩ nɩaa, dɩ mɩ ma ŋaa ba Wɩa. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.’ ” Sarɩya-la nʋʋ sɩ bɩ jaŋ wuo fa kagɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩmɛ, ʋ sɩ:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, suppose an entire nation sins against me, and I punish it by destroying the crops and letting its people and livestock starve to death.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, dɩ tinteeŋ nɩa nɛ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ a bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ mɩ teeŋ, mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛba a leŋ dɩ ba kʋduuloo chei ka dɩ losuŋ jʋʋba, dɩ nuhuobiine arɩ pʋsʋŋ kala sʋʋ.

english_verse: Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
translation_verse: Dɩ nɩaa deemba batori, Nowa, Danɩɛl arɩ Job nɛ fa paala hɛ tintee-la lɛ ma, ba tʋɔpʋla jaŋ wuo laa ba tɩtɩa mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ, ama nʋʋkala dee. La TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert.
translation_verse: Koo dɩ baga kʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ mɩ leŋ ba jʋʋ tintee-la a kpʋ nɩaa, ka dɩ ʋ pɩŋ hoi nʋʋkala bɩ nɩmɛ wuo to bɩbal a tɩŋ baga kʋbɔmɔ-la wɩaa.

english_verse: As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ ŋmɩɛsa, dɩ baalaa deemba batori nɛ fa paala hɛ ʋ lɛ ma, ba bɩ ba tɩtɩa hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ba toloo ma mɩɩsɩŋ wuo laa. Ba tɩtɩa mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ ba fa jaŋ wuo laa, ka dɩ tintee-la pɩŋ hoi.

english_verse: Or suppose I send an enemy to attack a sinful nation and kill its people and livestock.
translation_verse: Koo dɩ laalɩyuoroo nɛ mɩ kaa kʋ jʋʋ tintee-la aŋ bʋl, ‘Má gɔllɛ tintee-la kala, a kpʋ ʋ nɩaa arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ kala,’

english_verse: If these three men were in that nation when I punished it, not even their children would be spared. Only the three men would live.
translation_verse: mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ ŋmɩɛsa, dɩ baalaa deemba batori nɛ fa paala hɛ tintee-la nɩaa tʋɔŋ ma, ba bɩ ba tɩtɩa hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ba toloo mɩɩsɩŋ wuo laa. Ba tɩtɩa mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ ba fa jaŋ wuo laa.

english_verse: And suppose I am so angry that I send a deadly disease to wipe out the people and livestock of a sinful nation.
translation_verse: Koo dɩ nyanyal-bɔŋ sɩɩ kpʋ nɩaa nɛ mɩ na baanɩŋ a joŋo hɛ tintee-la lɛ, dɩ ʋ kpʋkpʋ tintee-la nɩaa arɩ ba pʋsʋŋ kala,

english_verse: Again, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living there, I, the Lord, promise that the children of these faithful men would also die. Only the three of them would be spared.
translation_verse: mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ ŋmɩɛsa: Dɩ Nowa, Danɩɛl arɩ Job nɛ fa paala hɛ tintee-la nɩaa tʋɔŋ ma, ba bɩ jaŋ wuo laa ba tɩtɩa hambolibie koo ba tolo mɩɩsɩŋ. Ba tʋɔpʋla jaŋ laa ba tɩtɩa mɩɩsɩŋ nɛ.

english_verse: I am the Lord God, and I promise to punish Jerusalem severely. I will send war, starvation, wild animals, and deadly disease to slaughter its people and livestock.
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩɩ bʋl nɛ ŋ-la: Ʋ jaŋ ŋaa wʋlɔrʋ a pɩ Jerusalɛm nɩaa dɩ mɩ nɛ joŋ wɩaa deemba banɛsɛ dɔgɩsɛba: laalɩŋ, losuŋ, baga kɩaa arɩ nyanyal bɔŋŋɔɔ, dɩ ba kpʋ ʋ nɩaa arɩ ʋ pʋsʋŋ.

english_verse: And those who survive will be taken from their country and led here to Babylonia. Ezekiel, when you see how sinful they are, you will know why I did all these things to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Arɩ ŋɩɩ kala, ba hambolibiisiŋ arɩ ba toloo dɔnsʋŋ ha jaŋ ka dɩ ba kɛmba lɩɩ ba tinteeŋ lɛ a kaa kɔ ma teeŋ Babɩlɔŋ lɛ. Dɩ ma nɛ na mɛl-bɔŋ-la ba sɩ kɛnɛ arɩ wɩalɩŋ ba sɩɩ ŋaa, ma tʋɔŋ jaŋ pɩŋ dɩ-bala a mʋ tɩgɛ wʋlɔrʋnʋ-la mɩ sɩ joŋo ŋaa Jerusalɛm nɩaa lɛ.

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩmɛ, ʋ sɩ:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, what happens to the wood of a grapevine after the grapes have been picked? It isn't like other trees in the forest,
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, ɛɛ nɛ girep sɩ ŋaa tɩɩbɛ ʋ daaŋ jaŋ ŋaa a kpɩa duuŋ tɩa na-kala tɩɩ-naakeliŋ?

english_verse: because the wood of a grapevine can't be used to make anything, not even a small peg to hang things on.
translation_verse: Ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ tɩɩbɛ daaŋ ŋaa kʋŋ? Ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ ʋ daaŋ ŋaa daapɛsɩŋ a joŋ kɩaa sagɛɛ?

english_verse: It can only be used as firewood. But after its ends are burnt and its middle is charred, it can't be used for anything.
translation_verse: Nyiniŋ dʋndʋŋa nɛ ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛnʋ hɛ. Dɩ nyiniŋ nɛ dii ʋ niiriŋ balɩa kala aŋ ka ʋ tʋtʋɔbaanɩŋ fisi, ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛnʋ ŋaa kʋŋ dɔŋ?

english_verse: The wood is useless before it is burned, and afterwards, it is completely worthless.
translation_verse: Dɩ ŋ nɛ bɩ ʋ kʋpilimiŋ wuo kaa ŋaa kʋŋ, ɛɛ nɛ ŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ ʋ kʋfisii-la kaa ŋaa kʋŋ sɩ kɛŋ bʋbʋɔŋ?

english_verse: I will punish the people of Jerusalem with fire. Some of them have escaped one destruction, but soon they will be completely burned. And when that happens, you, Ezekiel, will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsɛba, ba loo lɩɩ nyiniŋ tʋɔŋ nɛ, ama nyiniŋ nɛ ha jaŋ diiba. Dɩ mɩ nɛ dɔgɩsɛba, ŋɩɩ nɛ ba jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ba TƖƖNA.

english_verse: I will make their country an empty wasteland, because they have not been loyal to me. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ba tinteeŋ pɩŋ hoi, bɛɛ wɩaa ba bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ mɩ teeŋ, mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, remind the people of Jerusalem of their disgusting sins
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, chaasa dagɛ wʋkɩsɩa-la Jerusalɛm sɩɩ ŋaa a pʋ,

english_verse: and tell them that I, the Lord God, am saying: Jerusalem, you were born in the country where Canaanites lived. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
translation_verse: bʋla pʋ, wɩɩ-la La TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla pɩ Jerusalɛm nɛ ŋ-la: Ba lʋl ŋ naabalɩma Kɛnaŋ tɩŋŋaa tinteeŋ lɛ nɛ, ŋ nyɩmma fa ŋaa Amɔrɩ tɩɩna nɛ, ka ŋ naaŋ ma ŋaa Hiti tɩɩna.

english_verse: When you were born, no one cut you loose from your mother or washed your body. No one rubbed your skin with salt and olive oil, and wrapped you in warm blankets.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la ba sɩ lʋlʋŋ, ba fa bɩŋ kawul-jʋa kere, koo a foŋ lɩɩŋ koo a ŋaa yɩsɩŋ tɩsɩŋ koo a joŋ gɛrɩŋ pilimiŋ.

english_verse: Not one person loved you enough to do any of these things, and no one even felt sorry for you. You were despised, thrown into a field, and forgotten.
translation_verse: Nʋʋkala bɩŋ nenige koo nisusuŋ fá a ŋaa wɩaa deemba kʋŋ ŋ lɛ. Ba fa mɩɩra joŋuŋ yuo ta ŋmaŋkaaŋ nyuŋ nɛ. Tapʋlɩɩ-la ba sɩ lʋlʋŋ, ba kɛnɩŋ ŋmoo gbɛɛŋ nɛ.

english_verse: I saw you lying there, rolling around in your own blood, and I couldn't let you die.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ kʋʋ bal a naŋ dɩ ŋ pɩŋ ŋ tɩtɩa chalɩŋ lɛ a yuyuo naasɩŋ, ŋ fa sɩ pɩŋ chal-la lɛ ŋɩɩ mɩ bʋla pɩŋ: Kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: I took care of you, like someone caring for a tender, young plant. You grew up to be a beautiful young woman with mature breasts and hair, but you were still naked.
translation_verse: Mɩ nɛ leŋe ŋ waa a nagɛ tɩa sɩ hɛ ŋmaŋkaaŋ lɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ waa a ŋaa hatol-zɔŋ, a kpʋrɛ yɩlaa, ŋ nyu-pʋnaa waa a duomi, ama ŋ fa kɛŋ yarɩ-biree nɛ.

english_verse: When I saw you again, you were old enough to have sex. So I covered your naked body with my own robe. Then I solemnly promised that you would belong to me and that I, the Lord God, would take care of you.
translation_verse: Harɩŋ mɩ bɩra kʋʋ bal, a naŋ dɩ ŋ waa a magɛ baalaa chɛnɩŋ. Mɩ joŋ mɩ gɛrɩŋ a tɔ ŋ yarɩ-bire-la, aŋ chaasa bʋla pɩŋ arɩ mɩ jaŋ jaaŋ, ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ dɩŋ bil niiŋ pɩ dɔŋɔ ŋ ŋaa mɩ kʋŋ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: I washed the blood off you and rubbed your skin with olive oil.
translation_verse: Mɩ ŋaa lɩɩŋ fo ŋ chal-la ta aŋ tɩsɩŋ nʋʋŋ,

english_verse: I gave you the finest clothes and the most expensive robes, as well as sandals made from the best leather.
translation_verse: a joŋ gɛrɩ-la ba sɩ sʋa ʋ zɔŋ a laalɩŋ, a joŋ teniŋ nɛntɛŋŋɛɛ hɛŋ. Mɩ joŋ gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlʋŋ gɛnnɩŋ arɩ gɛnnɩ-la yalɩŋ sɩ hɛyɛ nɛ a kaa kpɩɛrɩŋ.

english_verse: Your jewelry was gold and silver, and your clothes were made of only the finest material and embroidered linen. Your bread was baked from fine flour, and you ate honey and olive oil. You were as beautiful as a queen,
translation_verse: Sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla nɛ mɩ kaa kpɩɛrɩŋ, ŋ gɛnnɩŋ ma nɛ fa gɛrɩpɛ fʋfʋlaa arɩ gɛrɩ-la yalɩŋ sɩ hɛyɛ arɩ gɛrɩ-la ba sɩ sʋa ʋ zɔŋ. Ŋ kʋdiilee ma nɛ fa ŋaa munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ, tʋʋŋ arɩ olif nʋʋŋ. Ŋ ŋaa hazɔŋ nɛ woruŋ a ŋaa ha-kuoru.

english_verse: and everyone on earth knew it. I, the Lord God, had helped you become a lovely young woman.
translation_verse: Ŋ yɩrɩŋ teeli tinteyee a tɩŋ ŋ sɩ zɔmɔ wɩaa, bɛɛ wɩaa tʋla-la mɩ sɩ joŋo pɩŋ nɛ leŋe ŋ chaasa zɔŋ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: You learned that you were attractive enough to have any man you wanted, so you offered yourself to every passerby.
translation_verse: Ama ŋ mɩɩra joŋ ŋ yɩɛlaa kala hɛ ŋ zɔmʋŋ lɛ nɛ, ŋ yɩrɩŋ sɩɩ sii ŋɩɩ mɩɩra leŋ ŋ ŋɩŋaa hachɔrʋŋ wɩaa. Ŋ ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ nɛ a joŋ ŋ zɔmʋŋ a pɩpɩ nʋʋkala sɩ kʋʋ bal.

english_verse: You made shrines for yourself and decorated them with some of your clothes. That's where you took your visitors to have sex with them. These things should never have happened!
translation_verse: Ŋ mɩɩra joŋ ŋ gɛrɩ-zɔmɔ-la dɔnsʋŋ a kpɩɛrɛ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa nɛ, lere-la ŋ sɩɩ ŋaa ŋ hachɔrʋŋ wɩaa. Wʋdosunuŋ deemba saa bɩ maga dɩ baa ŋaa, ŋɩɩ bɩ maga dɩ ʋ ŋaa.

english_verse: You made idols out of the gold and silver jewelry I gave you, then you sinned by worshiping those idols.
translation_verse: Ŋ bɩra joŋ kpɩɛrɩ-zɔmɔ-la ba sɩ kɛŋ mɩ sɛlɩmɛ arɩ hɔpʋla ŋaa mɩ joŋo pɩŋ, a kaa libi tɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ ba nagɛ baala ŋ kaa ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ wɩaa.

english_verse: You dressed them in the clothes you got from me, and you offered them the olive oil and incense I gave you.
translation_verse: Ŋ joŋ gɛnnɩ-la ba sɩ sʋa ba zɔŋ mɩ joŋo pɩŋ a laalɛ tɔmɔ-la nɛ, a joŋ mɩ olif nʋʋ-la arɩ kʋsʋɔrʋsʋŋ a pɩpɩba.

english_verse: I supplied you with fine flour, olive oil, and honey, but you sacrificed it all as offerings to please those idols. I, the Lord God, watched this happen.
translation_verse: Kʋdiile-la ma mɩ sɩ joŋo pɩŋ dɩ ŋ dii, munuŋ sɩ bɩɩ nʋgʋgʋ, olif nʋʋŋ arɩ tʋʋ-la, ŋ joŋ ba ma a pɩpɩ tɔmɔ-la nɛ, wɩɩ-la ŋ sɩ ŋaa nɛ ŋɩɩ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: But you did something even worse than that—you sacrificed your own children to those idols!
translation_verse: Ŋ joŋ ŋ hambolibiisi-la arɩ hantolibiisi-la ŋ sɩ lʋla pɩmɛ a kpaarɛ tɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ. Hachɔrʋŋ wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ ŋaa bɩ magaa?

english_verse: You slaughtered my children, so you could offer them as sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ŋ kɛsɛ mɩ biiriŋ nɛ a kaa kpaarɛ tɔŋŋɔɔ.

english_verse: You were so busy sinning and being a prostitute that you refused to think about the days when you were young and were rolling around naked in your own blood.
translation_verse: Wʋkɩsɩa-la arɩ hachɔrʋŋ wɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ ŋaa, ŋ bɩ liise yi tapʋlɩa-la ŋ fa sɩ ŋaa bii-mulo lɛ, a kɛŋ yarɩ-biree a pɩŋ ŋ tɩtɩa chalɩŋ lɛ a yuyuo naasɩŋ.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord God, say you are doomed! Not only did you do these evil things,
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla, wɩɩŋ puuŋ nɛ. A pɛ nɩbɔŋ wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa lɛ,

english_verse: but you also built places on every street corner
translation_verse: ŋ ha saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa nɛ a pɩ ŋ tɩtɩa, lere-la kala nɩaa sɩɩ hɔŋ lɛ.

english_verse: where you disgraced yourself by having sex with anyone who walked by. And you did that more and more every day!
translation_verse: Womporii na-kala nyuŋ nɛ ŋ saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa a chei ŋ zɔmʋŋ, a joŋ ŋ tɩtɩa a pɩ nʋʋ na-kala sɩ to lee-la bɩbal, ŋ hachɔrʋŋ wɩaa pʋŋa pɩpɛ.

english_verse: To make me angry, you even offered yourself to Egyptians, who were always ready to sleep with you.
translation_verse: Ŋ ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ wɩalɩŋ nɛ a joŋ ŋ tɩtɩa pɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa sɩ hɔnɔ kpagɩŋ. Nɩalɩŋ sɩ cho wʋlɩɩlɩŋ kɛnɩŋ pɩpɩŋ a leŋ mɩ baanɩŋ sii.

english_verse: So I punished you by letting those greedy Philistine enemies take over some of your territory. But even they were offended by your repulsive behavior.
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ, mɩ chɩna dɩ mɩ dɔgʋsʋŋ nɛ a keri ŋ tinteeŋ ta. Mɩ joŋuŋ hɛ ŋ dʋndɔŋŋɔɔ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩmma-la sɩ kɛŋ tʋɔ-luŋuŋ nɩsɩŋ lɛ nɛ. Ŋ hachɔrʋŋ wʋŋaalaa leŋe hɩɩsɩŋ kɛmba nɛ.

english_verse: You couldn't get enough sex, so you chased after Assyrians and slept with them. You still weren't satisfied,
translation_verse: Ŋ kɛŋ ŋ hachɔrʋŋ wɩalɩŋ yi Asiiria tɩŋŋaa ma nɛ, a leŋ ba kɛnɩŋ pɩpɩŋ a tɩŋ baalaa sɩ bɩŋ ka vɔgɛ wɩaa. Ka ŋ ha paala bɩ vɔgɔ.

english_verse: so you went after Babylonians. But those merchants could not satisfy you either.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ŋ bɩra kɛŋ ŋ hachɔrʋŋ wɩalɩŋ kire to Babɩlɔŋ tɩŋŋaa ma harɩŋ, tintee-la nɩaa sɩ ŋaa bayallaa, ama ŋ ha bɩ vɔgɔ.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, say that you were so disgusting that you would have done anything to get what you wanted.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla: Ŋ tʋɔŋ nyaa ɛɛ nɛ, ŋ ŋaa wɩaa deemba a nagɛ hachɔrʋŋ sɩ bɩ hɩɩsɩŋ ka fá.

english_verse: You had sex on every street corner, and when you finished, you refused to accept money. That's worse than being a prostitute!
translation_verse: Ŋ sɩ saa vesiŋ dɩ-kpaaraa womporii na-kala nyuŋ, aŋ saa vʋɩyaa lee-la taŋ nɩaa sɩɩ hɔŋ, ŋ fa bɩ hachɔrʋŋ naga, bɛɛ wɩaa ŋ bɩ moribiee ka laa.

english_verse: You are nothing but an unfaithful wife who would rather have sex with strangers than with your own husband.
translation_verse: Ŋ ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ nɛ, a cho nʋhʋɔraa ba kɛnɩŋ pɩpɩŋ, aŋ vɩa ŋ bala.

english_verse: Prostitutes accept money for having sex, but you bribe men from everywhere to have sex with you.
translation_verse: Hachɔrʋŋ na-kala yie laa time nɛ, ama ŋ-na yie mɩɩra joŋ kɩaa a pɩ ŋ hɩɩlaba sɩ lɩɩ lee na-kala nɛ a kpalba, ka ba kɛnɩŋ pɩpɩŋ.

english_verse: You're not like other prostitutes. Men don't ask you for sex—you offer to pay them! Jerusalem Must Be Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ŋ-na bɩ hachɔrʋmɔɔ dɔnsʋŋ naga, baal kala bɩ kire to ŋ harɩŋ dɩ ʋ kɛnɩŋ pɩŋ, ama ŋ nɛ yie mɩɩra timba ka ba pɩnɩŋ, ŋ-na bɩ kʋŋkala ka laa.

english_verse: You chased after lovers, then took off your clothes and had sex. You even worshiped disgusting idols and sacrificed your own children as offerings to them.
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ŋ TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Ŋ wuri ŋ gɛnnɩŋ nɛ aŋ ka ŋ yarɩ-biree a nagɛ hachɔrʋŋ a joŋ ŋ tɩtɩa pɩ ŋ hɩɩlaba arɩ ŋ vʋɩyaa kala, aŋ kɛsɛ ŋ biiriŋ kpaarɛ tɔŋŋɔɔ sɩ ŋaa disiŋ kɩaa mɩɩ kɩsɛ.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will gather every one of your lovers, those you liked and those you hated. They will stand around you, and I will rip off your clothes and let all of those lovers stare at your nakedness.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, mɩ jaŋ kɛŋ ŋ hɩɩlaba-la kala sɩma ŋ sɩ nɩa kʋ hɛ dɔŋɔ, nɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ cho arɩ nɩalɩŋ ŋ sɩ bɛrɛ. Mɩ jaŋ kɛmba kʋ golluŋ aŋ wuri ŋ gɛnnɩŋ ba sɩpaaŋ aŋ leŋ dɩ ba na ŋ yarɩ-biree.

english_verse: I will find you guilty of being an unfaithful wife and a murderer, and in my fierce anger I will sentence you to a violent death!
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ joŋ cheeriŋ pɩŋ a dɔgʋsʋŋ a tɩŋ ŋ sɩ ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ arɩ nɩkpʋʋrʋ wɩaa. Mɩ jaŋ na baanɩŋ kɩŋkɛŋ ŋ nyuŋ, a leŋ dɩ ba kpʋŋ.

english_verse: Then I will hand you over to your lovers, who will tear down the places where you had sex. They will take your clothes and jewelry, leaving you naked and empty-handed.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ joŋuŋ hɛ ŋ hɩɩlaba nɩsɩŋ lɛ, ba jaŋ ŋmoo ŋ vesiŋ dɩ-kpaara-la ŋ sɩ kaa ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ wɩaa lo. Ba jaŋ wuri ŋ gɛnnɩŋ arɩ ŋ kpɩɛra-la, aŋ ka dɩ ŋ kɛŋ yarɩ-biree.

english_verse: Your lovers and an angry mob will stone you to death; they will cut your dead body into pieces
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ kɛŋ nɩ-daŋ kʋ golluŋ a yagɩŋ arɩ tabɩaa, aŋ keriŋ muno muno arɩ ba tokobiee.

english_verse: and burn down your houses. Other women will watch these terrible things happen to you. I promise to stop you from being a prostitute and paying your lovers for sex.
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ nyɩgɛ ŋ dɩɩsɩŋ aŋ dɔgʋsʋŋ, ka dɩ haalaa yʋgɛ a bibeŋ. Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ŋ hachɔrʋŋ wɩalɩŋ dɛrɛ, ŋ bɩra bɩ jaŋ titiŋ ŋ hɩɩlaba-la.

english_verse: Only then will I calm down and stop being angry and jealous.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ mɩ yarɩ-bieri baaŋ-la mɩ sɩ na ŋ nyuŋ jaŋ fɩɛlɛ. Mɩ bɩra bɩ jaŋ na baanɩŋ ŋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: You made me furious by doing all these disgusting things and by forgetting how I took care of you when you were young. Then you made things worse by acting like a prostitute. You must be punished! I, the Lord God, have spoken. Jerusalem's Two Sisters The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ŋ sɩ bɩ liise yi wɩalɩŋ mɩ fa sɩ ŋaa pɩŋ ŋ hambiiriŋ lɛ wɩaa, aŋ ŋaa wɩaa deemba kala a leŋ mɩ baanɩŋ sii, ŋɩɩ nɛ tɩɩ mɩ leŋ wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa nyʋa ŋ nyuŋ lɛ ŋɩɩ. Mɩ-na ŋ TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ pɩɛsɩŋ nɛ: Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ŋ ŋaa hachɔrʋŋ wɩaa a pɛ disiŋ wɩalɩŋ kala mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ lɛ?

english_verse: People will use this saying about you, Jerusalem: “If the mother is bad, so is her daughter.”
translation_verse: Nʋʋ na-kala sɩɩ magɛ namagaba jaŋ magɛ namaga deeŋ a tɩgɛ ŋ-na Jerusalɛm lɛ: Naaŋ sɩ nagɛ ŋɩɩ, ŋɩɩ nɛ tolo ma nagɛ.

english_verse: You are just like your mother, who hated her husband and her own children. You are also like your sisters, who hated their husbands and children. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite.
translation_verse: Ŋ sɛnɛ laa ŋ naaŋ wɩɩŋ nɛ. Ŋ naaŋ vɩa ʋ bala arɩ ʋ biiriŋ nɛ. Ŋ nagɛ ŋ naambiiriŋ nɛ, ba vɩa ba balaba arɩ ba biiriŋ nɛ. Ŋ naaŋ fa ŋaa Hiti tɩɩna nɛ, ŋ nyɩmma ma fa ŋaa Amɔrɩ tɩɩna.

english_verse: Your older sister was Samaria, that city to your north with her nearby villages. Your younger sister was Sodom, that city to your south with her nearby villages.
translation_verse: Ŋ malɩma nɛ fa taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Samarɩa, a hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nagʋa dɩɩrɩŋ arɩ ʋ tabiisiŋ. Ŋ ŋaana ma nɛ taŋ-la ba sɩɩ yɩrɛ Sodom, a hɛ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ nadiiŋ dɩɩrɩŋ arɩ ʋ ma tabiisiŋ.

english_verse: You followed their way of life and their wicked customs, and soon you were more repulsive than they were.
translation_verse: Ba naabʋɔsʋŋ dʋndʋŋa dee ŋ to a chesiba wʋkɩsɩa-la ba sɩ ŋaa, ama ʋ bɩ diene ka ŋ wʋŋaalaa paala bɔmɔ kɩɩba.

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, the people of Sodom and its nearby villages were never as sinful as you.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ŋ TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ weye bʋla, ŋ naambie Sodom arɩ ʋ tabiisiŋ bɩ wʋbɔmɔ-la ŋ dɩ ŋ tabiisiŋ sɩ ŋaa, ŋaa.

english_verse: They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
translation_verse: Ba fa kɛŋ sɩɩ-duoŋ a ŋaa disiŋ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ nɛ. Ŋɩɩ wɩaa nɛ mɩ cheiba, ma na ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent.
translation_verse: Samarɩa bɩ wʋbɔmɔ-la ŋ sɩ ŋaa kpaa magɛ dɔŋɔ ma ŋaa. Ŋ nɛ ŋaa wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ a kɩɩba, ŋ wʋŋaalaa leŋe ŋ naambiiriŋ Sodom arɩ Samarɩa mɩɩra nagɛ arɩ ba-na ŋaa tʋɔpʋl tɩmma nɛ.

english_verse: So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins. Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed The Lord said to Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Leŋ dɩ hɩɩsɩŋ kɛnɩŋ, ŋ wʋŋaalaa daga arɩ ŋ naambiiri-la bɩ wʋbɔŋ ŋaa. Ŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ nɛ yʋga kɩɩ ba wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ, ba-na mɩɩra nagɛ tʋɔpʋl tɩmma nɛ. Gʋrʋ nyuŋ a leŋ dɩ hɩɩsɩŋ kɛnɩŋ, ŋ leŋe ŋ naambiiriŋ mɩɩra nagɛ tʋɔpʋl tɩmma nɛ.

english_verse: Someday I will bless Sodom and Samaria and their nearby villages. I will also bless you, Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ama tapʋlɩɩ kʋbala, mɩ jaŋ pɛ ŋ naambiiriŋ Sodom arɩ Samarɩa arɩ ba tabiisiŋ lɛ dɩ ba bɩra kuori, aŋ pɛ ŋ ma lɛ dɩ ŋ kuori.

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you.
translation_verse: Hɩɩsɩŋ jaŋ kɛnɩŋ a tɩŋ ŋ wʋŋaalaa wɩaa, hɩɩsɩ-la sɩ jaŋ kɛnɩŋ daga arɩ ŋ naambiiri-la wʋŋaalaa kpɩa ŋ kɩaa nɛ.

english_verse: When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
translation_verse: Ŋ naambiiriŋ Sodom arɩ Samarɩa arɩ ba tabiisiŋ jaŋ bɩra kuori a nagɛ ŋɩɩ ba fa sɩ naga. Ŋ dɩ ŋ tabiisiŋ ma jaŋ bɩra kuori a nagɛ ma fa sɩ nagɛ ŋɩɩ.

english_verse: Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom.
translation_verse: Bʋa-la lɛ ŋ fa sɩɩ dagɛ ŋ tɩtɩa, ŋ bɩ ŋ naambie Sodom kaa tɩtɩŋ,

english_verse: But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks.
translation_verse: a mʋ yi bʋa-la lɛ ŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ sɩ kʋ lɩɩ pʋlʋmʋŋ nʋʋkala jɩŋ. Ama lɛɛlɛ Ɛdɔm tɩŋŋaa arɩ tabiisi-la sɩ kpagɛba arɩ Fɩlɩsɩtɩa tɩŋŋaa ka sieri ŋ lɛ nɛ, nɩalɩŋ kala sɩ golluŋ a bɩ ŋ wɩaa cho.

english_verse: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ dɔgʋsʋŋ a tɩŋ hachɔrʋŋ wɩalɩŋ arɩ wʋkɩsɩa-la ŋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
translation_verse: Ama mɩ-na ha jaŋ liise yi nii-la mɩ fa sɩ bile mɩ dɩŋ pɛgɛ ŋ hatulluŋ kala lɛ, mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ nii-la chɩŋ kpaŋkpaŋ a kaa mʋ wuu.

english_verse: When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ ŋ jaŋ liise yi wʋbɔmɔ-la ŋ sɩ ŋaa lɛ, dɩ hɩɩsɩŋ kɛnɩŋ. Dɩ mɩ nɛ mɩɩra joŋ ŋ naambiiriŋ pɩŋ, nɩalɩŋ sɩ hɩaŋ arɩ nɩalɩŋ ŋ ma sɩ hɩa. Mɩ jaŋ jomba pɩŋ a leŋ dɩ ba nagɛ ŋ toloo, ama ʋ bɩ naga arɩ nii-la sɩ hɛ mɩ dɩŋ pɛgɛ wɩaa nɛ tɩɩ.

english_verse: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ nii-la sɩ hɛ mɩ dɩŋ pɛgɛ chɩŋ kpaŋkpaŋ, dɩ ŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ŋ TƖƖNA.

english_verse: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Dɩ mɩ nɛ joŋ wɩalɩŋ kala ŋ sɩ ŋaa a chɛŋ, ŋ jaŋ liise yi wʋbɔmɔ-la ŋ sɩ ŋaa lɛ, dɩ hɩɩsɩŋ kɛnɩŋ kɩŋkɛŋ dɩ ŋ bɩra bɩ ŋ niiŋ wuo suri. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, magɛ namaga deeŋ a pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa,

english_verse: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
translation_verse: a leŋ dɩ ba jɩŋ wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩɩ bʋl: Kachuu-bal kʋbala nɛ fa hɛ nɩmɛ ʋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ dol woruŋ, ʋ pʋnaa ma duomi a tɔ ʋ yaraa aŋ zɔŋ woruŋ a ŋaa dabaŋ dabaŋ. Ʋ sii file mʋ Lɛbanɔŋ, a kɛŋ kuolo nyu-gbaŋa naakeliŋ bori,

english_verse: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
translation_verse: a kaa mʋ tintee-la nɩaa sɩ ŋaa bayalaa, a joŋo chɔnsɛ ba tabalɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
translation_verse: Kachuu-la bɩra churi tɩɩ-nyʋʋlʋ-bie kʋbala Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ a joŋo chɔnsɛ tintee-la sɩ sɩma lɛ a kpagɛ lɩɩŋ sɩ yʋga leriŋ.

english_verse: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
translation_verse: Tɩa-la tɔsɛ a jɛrɛ. Baa yɩrɛ tɩa-la girep nɛ. Ʋ naakelee mɩɩra chaasɛ kachuu-la, ka ʋ naapoloo hɛ ʋ bʋbʋɔŋ. Tɩa-la tɔsɛ naakel-duoruŋ a kɛŋ pɩpaarɩŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
translation_verse: Ama kachuuŋ dɔŋɔ ma fa hɛ nɩmɛ a yʋgɛ woruŋ ʋ kɩŋkɛnsɩŋ dol, ʋ pʋnaa ma yʋgɛ a tɔ ʋ yaraa. Girep tɩɩbɛ-la kɛŋ ʋ naapoloo arɩ ʋ naakelee jɛrɛ lɩɩ lee-la ba sɩ chɔnsʋ a chaasɛ kachuuŋ deeŋ, a chɩchɛ lɩɩŋ.

english_verse: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
translation_verse: Ama ba fa paala chɔnsɛ girep tɩɩbɛ-la tintee-la sɩ sɩma lɛ nɛ, lee-la lɩɩŋ sɩ yʋga, dɩ ʋ wuo waa a chaarɛ naakelee, a nɛŋ nɛnɛɛ a zɔŋ woruŋ.

english_verse: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩ Iziral tɩŋŋaa, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ pɩɛsa nɛ ŋ-la: Ŋ bɩɩna girep tɩɩbɛ-la jaŋ wei? Bumbuŋ kachuu-la bɩ jaŋ churi ʋ dɩ ʋ naapoloo a pʋrɛ ʋ nɛnɛɛ ta dɩ tɩa-la hɩl? Ʋ dɩ ʋ pɩpaa falɩa-la kala jaŋ hɩl. Nɩpʋgʋŋ ma paala jaŋ wuo kɛŋ ʋ dɩ ʋ naapoloo kala lɛrɛ churi, nɩ-daŋ dee.

english_verse: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
translation_verse: Dɩ ba nɛ paala joŋ girep tɩɩbɛ-la wasa chɔnsɛ ma, ʋ bɩ jaŋ waa. Dɩ pel-lɩmɩŋ nɛ lɩɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ kʋ ŋmobu, ʋ jaŋ sʋʋ lee-la ʋ fa sɩ chɩna.’ ”

english_verse: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Pɩɛsɛ Iziral nɩaa deemba sɩ vɩa mɩ niiŋ, ‘Ma bɩ wɩaa deemba bʋbʋɔŋ jɩŋ?’ Bʋla pɩba: ‘Babɩlɔŋ kuoro nɛ sii mʋ Jerusalɛm a yuo kɛŋ ʋ kuoro arɩ ʋ nɩhɩasɩŋ a kɛmba mɩɩra mʋ Babɩlɔŋ.

english_verse: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ ʋ lɩɩsɛ Juda kuoro dɩa nɩaa dɔŋɔ ba pɛ niiŋ, ʋ leŋ ʋ ŋmɩɛsɛ arɩ ʋ jaŋ tutou. Ʋ fa pɛ kɛsɛ tintee-la sɩpaalaaraa ma nɛ,

english_verse: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
translation_verse: dɩ ŋɩɩ leŋ dɩ Juda tinteeŋ nɩaa tutou, aŋ bɩra sɩ́ doluŋ kɛŋ a wuo beŋ ba tɩtɩa.

english_verse: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
translation_verse: Ama Juda kuoro nɩɩ-la kʋ magɛ ŋɩɩ, a vɩa dɩ ʋ to Babɩlɔŋ kuoro niiŋ aŋ tɩŋ nɩaa dɩ ba mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ a kɛsɛ janɩŋ arɩ laalɩyuori-daŋ kɔ. Kuoro deeŋ jaŋ wuo na wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩɩ chɛɛ? Ʋ jaŋ wuo fori wɩaa deemba lɛɛ? Ʋ jaŋ wuo chei nii-la ba sɩ pɛ aŋ fori?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ ŋmɩɛsa: Juda kuoro jaŋ sʋʋ Babɩlɔŋ lɛ, tintee-la kuoro sɩ leŋe ʋ dii kuoruŋ aŋ bɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ ŋmɩɛsa kaa tɩŋ, a chei nii-la ʋ dɩ ʋ sɩ pɛ.

english_verse: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
translation_verse: Dɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ kuoro arɩ ʋ laalɩyuori-duoru-la arɩ ʋ nɩ-daŋ-la nɛ pɛ Juda tinteeŋ kuoro lɛ a yuo laalɩŋ ma, ba bɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa wɩɩkala dɩ Babɩlɔŋ tɩŋŋaa nɛ saa vaŋkumba dɩ ba to ba lɛ a jʋʋ kpʋ ba nɩ-daŋ-la sɩ hɛ Jerusalɛm lɛ.

english_verse: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
translation_verse: Juda tinteeŋ kuoro bɩ ŋɩɩ ʋ sɩ ŋmɩɛsa kaa tɩŋ, aŋ chei nii-la sɩ hɛ ba pɛgɛ. A tɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa deemba kala, ʋ bɩ jaŋ fori.’

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa, wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Mɩ ŋmɩɛsa, mɩ jaŋ dɔgɩsʋ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋmɩɛsɛ mɩ yɩrɩŋ lɛ aŋ bɩ kaa tɩŋ, aŋ chei nii-la sɩ hɛ mɩ dɩ ʋ pɛgɛ.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ hɛ bɛrɛ a kɛnʋ. Mɩ jaŋ kɛnʋ mʋ Babɩlɔŋ a dɔgɩsʋ nɩmɛ a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ mɩ teeŋ.

english_verse: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ba jaŋ kpʋ ʋ laalɩyuoro-la kala sɩ jɩŋ laalɩŋ yuonuŋ, aŋ ka nɩkaanaa fá pɩsɛ lee-kala. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla.

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Mɩ tɩtɩa jaŋ keri kuolu tɩa-la nyu-gbaŋa naakeliŋ sɩ tɔsɔ, mɩ jaŋ bori naakel-pɔrʋ-la a joŋo chɔnsɛ peel-la sɩ leŋie kɩŋkɛŋ nyuŋ.

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: Iziral peel-la sɩ leŋie nyu-gbaŋa nɛ mɩ jaŋ chɔnsʋ, ʋ jaŋ kel woruŋ a nɛŋ nɛnɛɛ a bɩrɩmɛ kuolu tɩɩ-zɔŋ. Diibii doho kala jaŋ sʋa ba dɛllɩŋ ʋ lɛ, ba jaŋ sagɛ ʋ naakele-la lɛ a wiwiesi ʋ fɩɛlɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Tɩɩsɩŋ kala sɩ hɛ baga lɛ jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ-na ba TƖƖNA jaŋ wuo ŋaa dɩ tɩɩ-duduosuŋ kui, a ŋaa tɩɩ-kuunuŋ ma duomi. Mɩ jaŋ wuo ŋaa tɩɩsɩ-la pɩpaarɩŋ sɩ lɛyɛ hɩl, a ŋaa tɩɩsɩ-la ma pɩpaarɩŋ sɩ hɩla lɛɩ. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA nɛ bʋla, mɩ jaŋ ŋaa wɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ bʋla.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Namaga deeŋ ma sɩ yie magɛ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ bʋbʋɔŋ nɛ bɛɛ? ‘Nyɩmmaba nɛ chaŋ girep nɛŋ huoruŋ, aŋ ka ba biiriŋ nyɩlaa mɩɩra nyal.’

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ ŋmɩɛsa, ma bɩra bɩ jaŋ magɛ namaga deeŋ Iziral tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Mɩ nɛ tɩɩ nuhuobiiŋ kala, nyɩmmaba, naamba arɩ ba biiriŋ kala. Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔmʋŋ nɛ jaŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: Leŋ la joŋ arɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna nɛ hɛ nɩmɛ, a ŋaa nʋʋ sɩ kɛŋ wʋtɩtɩɩ a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ.

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩ vesiŋ kʋdiilee ka dii peelee nyuŋ, koo a kpʋkpaarɛ vʋɩya-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩɩ kpaarʋ. Ʋ bɩ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna haala kaa pɩpɩŋ, koo a kɛŋ haala pɩŋ bʋa-la lɛ ʋ sɩ hɛ tɩŋa.

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩ kɩaa joŋo chɩŋ nɩaa aŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ba tiŋ nyʋʋrʋŋ yʋgɛ. Ʋ bɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ka ŋaa, dɩ nɩaa nɛ kɛŋ kaalɛrɛ, ʋ yie bʋl wɩɩ-la ʋ bʋa lɛ nɛ a pɩba.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: La joŋ arɩ baala deeŋ nɛ kɛŋ hambolibie sɩ ŋaa yuo-hɛɛrʋ, a kpʋkpʋ nɩaa, a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa deemba

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: ʋ nyɩmma sɩ bɩ ŋaa aŋ ka, a didii vesiŋ kʋdiilee peelee nyuŋ, a kɛŋ ʋ dɔŋɔ tɩɩna haala pɩpɩŋ.

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: Ʋ yie nyagɛ summoo arɩ nɩalɩŋ sɩ bɩ ba tɩtɩa lɛ wuo pɛ bil, a kɛŋ nɩaa kɩaa lɩlaa arɩ doluŋ. Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ dii ʋ chɩmɩŋ aŋ joŋ kʋŋ bil bʋbʋɔŋ, ʋ bɩra bɩ kʋ-la joŋo pɩpɩ tɩɩna. Ʋʋ kpaarɛ tɔŋŋɔɔ a ŋɩŋaa wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ.

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ʋ yie joŋ kɩaa chɩŋ nɩaa aŋ leŋ ba tiŋ nyʋʋrʋŋ yʋgɛ. Nɩdoho deeŋ jaŋ wuo kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ? Ʋ bɩ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ, bɛɛ wɩaa ʋ ŋaa wɩaa deemba kala mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ nɛ. Ʋ maga dɩ ba kpʋʋ nɛ, ʋ tɩtɩa nɛ chɛ ʋ sʋʋŋ.

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ baala deeŋ ma nɛ kɛŋ hambolibie, dɩ bile na wʋbɔmɔ-la kala ʋ nyɩmma fa sɩ ŋaa, aŋ bɩ baa ŋaa:

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: Ʋ bɩ vesiŋ kʋdiilee ka dii peelee nyuŋ, koo a kpʋkpaarɛ vʋɩya-la Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩɩ kpaarʋ. Ʋ bɩ ʋ dɔŋɔ haala kaa pɩpɩŋ.

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: Ʋ lɩɩsɛ ʋ nɩsɩŋ wʋbɔŋ kala lɛ nɛ, a bɩ kɩaa joŋo chɩŋ nɩaa aŋ chɩchɛ dɩ ba tiŋ nyʋʋrʋŋ yʋgɛ. Ʋʋ to mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ daga nɛ. Ʋ bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ a tɩŋ ʋ nyɩmma wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ wɩaa, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: Ama ma pɩɛsa, ‘Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ bile bɩ maga dɩ ʋ na hɛɛŋ a tɩŋ ʋ nyɩmma wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ wɩaa?’ A tɩŋ bile sɩ ŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ arɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ, a fɩɛlɛ ʋ sɩaa a to mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto, ʋ sɛnɛ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Nɩɩ-la kala sɩ ŋaa wʋbɔmʋŋ nɛ jaŋ sʋʋ. Bie bɩ jaŋ na hɛɛŋ a tɩŋ ʋ nyɩmma arɩ ʋ naaŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ wɩaa. Nyɩmmaba bɩ jaŋ na hɛɛŋ a tɩŋ ba biiriŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ wɩaa. Tʋɔpʋl tɩŋŋaa kala jaŋ laa ba tʋɔpʋl wʋŋaalaa time, dɩ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ ma laa ba nɩbɔŋ wʋŋaalaa time.

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɛ leŋ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ aŋ tuto mɩ wombiee mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto, a ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ arɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Mɩ jaŋ joŋ wʋbɔmɔ-la kala ʋ fa sɩ ŋaa a chɛʋ, aŋ ka dɩ ʋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ a tɩŋ tʋɔpʋl wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ pɩɛsa: Ma bɩɩna mɩ cho dɩ nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ sʋsʋʋ nɛɛ? Mɩ yie cho dɩ ba bɩrɩma lɩɩ ba wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋaanɩŋ lɛ nɛ a kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna nɛ leŋ tʋɔpʋl wɩaa ŋaanɩŋ aŋ mɩɩra ŋɩŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩɩ kɩsʋ ka nɩbɔŋŋɔɔ ŋɩŋaa, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ? Aɩ, mɩ jaŋ yʋ tʋɔpʋl wɩalɩŋ kala ʋ sɩ ŋaa, a tɩŋ ʋ sɩ bɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ kɛnɛ arɩ mɩ aŋ ŋaa wʋbɔŋ wɩalɩŋ, ʋ jaŋ sʋʋ.

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Dɩ tʋɔpʋl tɩɩna nɛ leŋ tʋɔpʋl wɩaa ŋaanɩŋ aŋ ŋɩŋaa wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ, ʋ jaŋ sʋʋ, a tɩŋ wʋbɔmɔ-la ʋ sɩ ŋaa wɩaa.

english_verse: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Ama dɩ nɩbɔmʋŋ nɛ leŋ nɩbɔŋ wɩaa ŋaanɩŋ aŋ ŋɩŋaa wɩaa ba bʋa lɛ arɩ wʋtɩtɩɩ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Dɩ ʋ nɛ bee na arɩ wɩalɩŋ ʋ sɩɩ ŋaa ba bʋa lɛ dee, a leŋ wʋbɔmɔ-la ŋaanɩŋ, ʋ bɩ jaŋ sʋʋ, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa ma Iziral tɩmma, mɩ jaŋ dii ma kʋŋkala sarɩya a magɛ ŋɩɩ ma sɩ ŋaa wɩaa. Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla. Má bɩrɩma lɩɩ wʋbɔmɔ-la kala ma sɩɩ ŋaa lɛ, a sɩ́ leŋe dɩ wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ cheima.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Má lɩɩsɛ ma tɩtɩa wʋbɔmɔ-la ma sɩɩ ŋaa lɛ, aŋ ka dɩ mɩ pɩma tʋɔ-falɩŋ arɩ dɩŋ-falɩŋ. Bɛɛ nɛ tɩɩ ma Iziral tɩŋŋaa cho dɩ ma sʋba?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ nɛ bʋla, mɩ bɩ cho dɩ nʋʋkala sʋba, má bɩrɩma lɩɩ ma wʋbɔŋŋɔɔ lɛ a kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: Ta jembiiŋ a pɩ Iziral sɩpaalaaraa balɩa

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
translation_verse: a bʋl: “Ma naaŋ fa ŋaa naachigi-duo nɛ a guoli naachigi-belliŋ tʋɔŋ. Ʋ yie hɛ ba tʋɔŋ nɛ a dɩdɩɛsɛ ʋ biiriŋ.

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Ʋ dɩɛsɛ ʋ biiri-la dɔŋɔ ʋ ŋaa naachigi-duo. Ʋ gʋnnʋ kɩaa kpʋ diiniŋ, ʋ didii nuhuobiinee.

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Tinteyee nɩaa nɩɩ ʋ wɩaa, a bɛrɛ kɛnʋ ba buotuoŋ lɛ. Ba kɛŋ gbɩamba nɛ kɛnʋ a lɛrʋ kaa mʋ Ijipiti tinteeŋ.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Naachigi naaŋ-la sɩ na dɩ ʋ yɩɛlaa kala dɛrɛ ʋ bile lɛ, ʋ bɩra dɩɛsɛ ʋ biiri-la dɔŋɔ, ʋ ma bɩrɩmɛ naachigi-duo.

english_verse: He destroyed fortresses and ruined towns; his mighty roar terrified everyone.
translation_verse: Ʋ chei tinteye-la sɩ kpagʋ nɩaa dɩ-duoruŋ, ka ba tabalaa pɩŋ jikpeeŋ. Ʋ huoso leŋ fawʋllʋŋ kɛŋ nʋʋkala sɩ hɛ tintee-la lɛ.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ tinteye-la nɩaa vʋʋrɛ a sii chɩŋ ʋ lɛ dɩ ba yuou, nɩaa lɩɩ sɛmɛ na-kala a kʋ gollu chu. Ba yuo ba jomba a bɛrɛ kɛnʋ.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Ba bɩra kɛŋ gbɩamba nɛ a kɛŋ ʋ ma, a lɛrʋ mʋ hɛ kʋa ba sɩ kpaasa tɔ lɛ, a kɛnʋ kaa mʋ Babɩlɔŋ kuoro teeŋ, ba kɛnʋ tɔ dɩa. Ŋɩɩ lɛ nɛ ba bɩra bɩ ʋ huoso nɩa Iziral peelee nyuŋ.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: Ŋ naaŋ fa nagɛ girep tɩɩbɛ nɛ a hɛ girep tɩɩsɩŋ baga lɛ, ba chɔnsʋ kpagɛ lɩɩŋ niiŋ. Lɩɩŋ fa sɩ yʋga ŋɩɩ ʋ kel a nɛŋ nɛnɛɛ yʋgɛ.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: Ʋ naakelee fa kɛŋ doluŋ nɛ a magɛ dɩ ba kaa ŋaa kuoru dantɩga. Ʋ nɛ fa duomo kɩɩ tɩɩsɩ-la dɔnsʋŋ kala a kɛŋ naakelee woruŋ.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Ama ba na baanɩŋ a kɛnʋ churi a joŋo yuo ta tinteeŋ. Pel-lɩmɩŋ lɩɩ wɩɩpɔsʋŋ dɩɩrɩŋ a kʋ leŋ ʋ hɩl, ʋ nɛnɛɛ kala yuori. Ʋ naakel duoru-la kala hɩl, nyiniŋ joŋo dii.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Lɛɛlɛ ba chɔnsʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ nɛ, lee-la sɩ hɩla, lɩɩŋ tuo.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Nyiniŋ chol ʋ gentine a joŋ ʋ naakelee arɩ ʋ nɛnɛɛ dii. Naakel-duo kala bɩra tuo a magɛ dɩ ba kaa ŋaa kuoru dantɩga. Jembii-la nɛ ŋɩɩ a magɛ dɩ ba tɩtaʋ yoho lɛ.”

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: La fa sɩ hɛ yoŋ-baga lɛ jɩsɩŋ balɩpɛ, chɛŋ-nɔŋ tʋɔŋ tapʋl-fii chɛɛŋ, Iziral tɩŋŋaa sɩpaalaaraa dɔnsʋŋ sii kɔ mɩ teeŋ dɩ ba pɩɛsɛ La TƖƖNA na wɩɩ-la ʋ sɩɩ chɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ba kʋ hɔŋ mɩ sɩpaaŋ.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ nɛ La TƖƖNA bʋl wɩaa pɩmɛ, ʋ sɩ:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: “Nuhuobiiŋ, bʋla pɩ Iziral sɩpaalaara-la, ‘Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ pɩɛsa nɛ ŋ-la: Ma kɔ dɩ ma pɩɛsɛmɛ a na wɩaa nɛɛ? Mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ ŋmɩɛsa, mɩ bɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ ma pɩɛsɛmɛ na wɩɩkala.’

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Nuhuobiiŋ, ŋ jaŋ diiba sarɩyaa? Ŋɩɩ-na liisiba a mʋ tɩgɛ wʋkɩsɩa-la ba naabalɩmaba sɩ ŋaa lɛ.

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: Bʋla pɩba: Wɩɩ-la mɩ-na ma TƖƖNA Wɩɩjarɩbakɔ sɩ bʋla nɛ ŋ-la: Tapʋlɩɩ-la mɩ sɩ lɩɩsɛ ba-na Iziral tɩŋŋaa, mɩ fa chaasa ŋmɩɛsa pɩ ba-na Jekɔb doho nɩaa nɛ aŋ kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa dagɛba Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ. Mɩ fa ŋmɩɛsa pɩba a bʋl, ‘Mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa.’

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Tapʋlɩɩ-la mɩ ŋmɩɛsa pɩba arɩ mɩ jaŋ kɛmba lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a kaa kɔ tintee-la mɩ sɩ chɛ bil ba lɛ, tintee-la sɩ sɩma a kɛŋ kɩaa woruŋ. Ʋ nɛ zɔmɔ kɩɩ tintee kala.”

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: Mɩ fa bɩra bʋla pɩba, “Má kʋŋkala joŋ tɔŋŋɔɔ sɩ ŋaa disiŋ kɩa ma sɩ cho ta, má sɩ́ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa tɔŋŋɔɔ to a ŋaa disiniŋ hɛ ma tɩtɩa lɛ. Mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa.

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama ba vɩa mɩ niiŋ nɛ a bɩ jegile nɩɩ mɩ teeŋ. Ba bɩ tɔmɔ-la sɩ ŋaa disiŋ kɩa ka ba choba joŋo ta, ba bɩra bɩ Ijipiti tɩŋŋaa tɔŋŋɔɔ ma leŋe. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ sɩ mɩ jaŋ na baanɩŋ ba nyuŋ a ŋaa baaŋ wɩaa ba lɛ Ijipiti tintee-la lɛ.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama a tɩŋ mɩ yɩrɩŋ wɩaa, mɩ fa ŋaa wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ yɩrɩŋ sɩ́ chei nɛ, dɩ tinteye-la nɩaa tʋɔŋ ba sɩ guolo na, nɩalɩŋ tʋɔŋ mɩ sɩ kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa dagɛ Iziral tɩŋŋaa aŋ kɛmba kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: Ŋɩɩ wɩaa mɩ fa kɛmba kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ a kɛmba kaa jʋʋ tintee-hɩlɩŋ.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: Mɩ fa joŋ mɩ wɩaa dagɛba nɛ a leŋ ba jɩŋ mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto. Dɩ nʋʋ nɛ sɛɩba a kɛmba tɩtɩŋ, ʋ jaŋ kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: Mɩ fa bɩra joŋ mɩ chɛ-wiesii-la ma pɩba nɛ dɩ ba tuto. Ʋ ŋaa magɩl a hɛ mɩ dɩ ba pɛgɛ, dɩ ŋɩɩ leŋ dɩ ba jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ba TƖƖNA sɩ leŋe ba bɩ disiniŋ kɛnɛ.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: Ama Iziral tɩŋŋaa fa ha vɩa mɩ niiŋ nɛ tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ. Ba fa vɩa mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ dagɛba nɛ, wɩalɩŋ nʋʋ sɩ jaŋ to a kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ. Ba fa chaasa chei mɩ chɛ-wiesii-la nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ sɩ mɩ jaŋ faasa na baanɩŋ ba nyuŋ a cheiba tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama a tɩŋ mɩ yɩrɩŋ wɩaa, mɩ fa ŋaa wɩɩ-la sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ yɩrɩŋ sɩ́ chei nɛ tinteye-la nɩaa sɩpaaŋ, nɩalɩŋ sɩɩ beŋ ka mɩ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: Mɩ fa bɩra ŋmɩɛsa pɩba tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ, arɩ mɩ bɩ jaŋ kɛmba kaa jʋʋ tintee-la mɩ fa sɩ sɩ mɩ jaŋ joŋo pɩba, tintee-la sɩ sɩma a kɛŋ kɩaa woruŋ. Ʋ nɛ zɔmɔ kɩɩ tintee kala.

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: Mɩ fa bʋl ŋɩɩ pɩba a tɩŋ ba sɩ vɩa mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ba tuto arɩ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ dagɛba nɛ. Ba fa chei mɩ chɛ-wiesii-la nɛ aŋ tuto ba tɔŋŋɔɔ.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: Ama mɩ fa ha fá ba nenige nɛ a bɩ ba cheye koo a kpʋba tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ.

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: Tintee-hɩlɩɩ-la lɛ, mɩ fa bʋla pɩ ba biiriŋ, ‘Má pɔ ma sɩ́ ma nyɩmmaba wʋdagaa to koo a to ba wombiee koo a to ba tɔmɔ-la a ŋaa disiniŋ hɛ ma tɩtɩa lɛ.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa, má to mɩ niiŋ wɩalɩŋ mɩ sɩ dagɛma, a fɩɛlɛ ma sɩaa to mɩ wombie-la mɩ sɩ bile dɩ ma tuto.

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Má to mɩ chɛ-wiesii-la, ʋ ŋaa tapʋl-zɔŋ nɛ, dɩ ŋɩɩ ŋaa magɩl a hɛ mɩ dɩ ma pɛgɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ ma jaŋ jɩŋ arɩ mɩ nɛ ma TƖƖNA Wɩa.

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: Ama biiri-la ma fa vɩa mɩ niiŋ nɛ: Ba bɩ mɩ wombiee arɩ mɩ niiŋ wɩalɩŋ dɔnsʋŋ mɩ fa sɩ dagɛba to, wɩalɩŋ nʋʋ sɩ jaŋ to a kɛŋ mɩɩsɩŋ. Ba fa chaasa chei mɩ chɛ-wiesii-la nɛ. Ŋɩɩ nɛ mɩ fa sɩ mɩ jaŋ faasa na baanɩŋ ba nyuŋ a cheiba tintee-hɩlɩŋ lɛ.

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama a tɩŋ mɩ yɩrɩŋ wɩaa, mɩ fa kɛŋ mɩ tɩtɩa nɛ dɩ mɩ sɩ́ wɩɩ ŋaa sɩ jaŋ leŋ dɩ mɩ yɩrɩŋ chei tinteye-la nɩaa sɩpaaŋ, nɩalɩŋ fa sɩɩ beŋ ka mɩ kɛŋ Iziral tɩŋŋaa kaa lɩɩ Ijipiti tinteeŋ lɛ.
